Summary

As of the 2026-10-24 commit (6258a15, Gen4+49), X For You gathers the latest in-network posts from Thunder and OON candidates from Phoenix retrieval, SimClusters, and a popular posts source that has been on by default since 2026-10-07, while the legacy tweet-mixer and SID retrieval sources are off by default. Phoenix, a Grok-based Transformer, predicts per-action engagement probabilities for each candidate, and since 2026-09-24 the shared crate xai-value-model applies an author-diversity decay and an OON multiplier to the weighted sum of these probabilities. There are 22 filters before scoring and 5 after selection, and the sorted candidates then pass through VMRanker DPP slate re-ranking (θ=0.65, K=150, skipped for topic requests) and blending of ads and follow recommendations.

Released source up to Gen4 — read this first to keep the rest straight

X's recommendation code release is divided into four generations. Gen1 is Scala/Java and Gen2 is Scala, both from the Twitter repo, while Gen3 and Gen4 are Rust/Python code from the xAI repo. From Gen4 on, the weight parameter mirror, the safety pipeline, and the training code were also released verified.

Generation Repo Released Language Status
Gen1 twitter/the-algorithm @ ef4c5eb…72eda9a 2023-03-31 ~ 2023-07-07 Scala/Java 99% of the "Twitter algorithm" analyses circulating in the world look at this generation
Gen2 same repo @ c54bec0 2025-09-03 Scala 988 files, +65,319/−3,195. Introduced tweet-mixer; Grok and Phoenix entered
Gen3 xai-org/x-algorithm @ aaa167b·e414c17·0bfc279 2026-01-20·2026-05-15 Rust/Python Complete rewrite. Zero code duplication with Gen1 and Gen2. 216 files in total (79 initially, 137 added and 50 modified in e414c17 (including 59 grox), and 1 LFS pointer replaced in 0bfc279)
Gen4 same repo @ 47c1bcd (.gitattributes cleanup in a389166) 2026-08-13 Rust/Python +363,246/−11,640 (300+ files). Introduced the weight params mirror and 15 visibility-filtering and labeling sub-repos, included phoenix/ training code and synthetic data, revived SimClusters, and began the practice of documenting parameter diffs in docs/BIDIRECTIONAL_BOOST_CHANGE.md

A direct check of the git log on 2026-09-10 showed that xai-org/x-algorithm had 18 commits (+1 from the previous day: 49815da) and that twitter/the-algorithm was unchanged at 31 commits verified.

These notes number the xai-org/x-algorithm commits that came after the Gen4 release (47c1bcd, 2026-08-13) sequentially, starting from Gen4+1. Per-commit details are in the change log at the end of the file.

Four facts matter most:

  1. There is a 26-month gap between Gen1 and Gen2. There was not a single commit between 2023-07-07 and 2025-09-03 verified.

  2. Gen2 deleted nothing. There were 0 deletions and 0 renames. The 2023 file set of 6,906 files is a proper subset of the 2025 file set of 7,667 files. In other words, cr-mixer/, navi/, ann/, simclusters-ann/, src/, product-mixer/, and others remain exactly as they were, with not a single byte changed since 2023-04. The only top-level paths the 2025 commit touched are home-mixer/, tweet-mixer/, and README.md, with 603, 384, and 1 files respectively verified.

    • The command used for the check is git show --name-only --pretty='' c54bec0 | awk -F/ '{print $1}' | sort | uniq -c.

    A file in the repo does not mean the code is in use now. Deprecation shows up only as a line removed from the README, not as a file deletion. cr-mixer is exactly such a case. The only documentation change in the 2025 commit replaced the service name in the README's cr-mixer row with tweet-mixer and left the wording as is verified — git show c54bec0 -- README.md.

  3. Gen3 is a separate repo. The first 3 commits of xai-org/x-algorithm (aaa167b→e414c17→0bfc279) rewrote the code and added grox/, reaching 216 files verified.

  4. Gen4 changed the nature of Gen3. Through Gen3, only the shape of the logic was released, while values, wiring, and safety rules were not public, but Gen4 released the following three things verified — README.md #latest-update--august-13th-2026.

    • Released a production cron mirror of the weights and constants as home-mixer/params/param.rs verified — same README.
    • Released the entire safety pipeline through visibility-filtering/ and 15 labeling sub-repos verified — same README.
    • Made the system runnable end to end by including training code and synthetic data in phoenix/ verified — same README.

    The detailed analysis is in daily/2026-08-15.md.

Glossary

Name Meaning Code location Evidence section

canon Refers to this document (the X canon). 'The earlier canon version' means an earlier version of this document — Generation comparison
cron mirror A parameter file published in the repo that syncs production feature-switch defaults daily. The time of the last sync is written in the file header home-mixer/params/param.rs Weights
home-mixer The service that receives For You and Following feed requests. The candidate source, scorer, filter, and blender code lives under it home-mixer/ Feed surfaces
Thunder An index that holds the latest in-network posts in memory (2-day retention). Newly built in 2026 thunder/ Candidate generation — current
Phoenix A Transformer ported from Grok-1. It puts the user history and the candidates into one sequence and predicts engagement probabilities for each candidate. There is also Phoenix retrieval, which finds OON candidates phoenix/ Phoenix
OON out-of-network. Posts from accounts the viewer does not follow. The OON multiplier applies in score calculation OonWeightFactor Candidate allocation
SID semantic ID. An ID that represents a post as a sequence of codewords in a coarse → fine hierarchy SidSource, sid_k1 / sid_k2 / sid_k3 Candidate generation — current, Phoenix
VQV video quality view. X's behavior label for whether a video was actually watched for at least a set time. It belongs to the Attention category among the Phoenix prediction heads VqvWeight Phoenix
VMRanker (VM-Ranker) The slate re-ranking service. It keeps the legacy name but is responsible for DPP slate re-ranking home-mixer/scorers/vm_ranker.rs, vm-ranker/ Diversity
DPP Determinantal Point Process. One of the diversity mechanisms; it selects candidates by optimizing them as a set DppTheta, DppMaxSelectedRank in vm-ranker/params.rs. In the Gen4 home-mixer param, VMRankerDppTheta, VMRankerDppMaxSelectedRank Diversity, commit summary table
VF (visibility-filtering) The last stage of the Labeling Path. For each post it issues a verdict on whether it may be shown to this viewer, and home-mixer drops or keeps the candidate according to that verdict visibility-filtering/, home-mixer/filters/vf_filter.rs Safety
grox A Grok-based nearline annotation pipeline. It produces slop scores, safety labels, topics, reply scores, and multimodal embeddings grox/ Grox
PTOS (PtOS) The layer in the grox safety pipeline that determines violation categories based on policy grox/flows/ptos/ Grox → PtOS
Strato An internal X system. The code looks up or stores safety annotations, AI trends, and reply ranking scores through Strato StratoVfClient, grox/flows/reply_spam/strato_loader.py Grox → PtOS
TES Tweet Entity Service. X's internal tweet metadata lookup service TesHydrator, TESClient TesHydrator cache removal in the change log
shadow traffic A path that picks some real requests and also sends them to an experimental Phoenix cluster for scoring, keeping those scores only in logs. It does not affect serving results home-mixer/util/shadow.rs, PhoenixExperimentsSideEffect Open questions
served type A label showing which source path a candidate came in through (for example in-network, SimClusters, Phoenix retrieval) served_type, ServedType Filters
side effect A home-mixer pipeline stage that runs after candidate selection and leaves only logs or metrics without changing the response home-mixer/side_effects/ Diversity
UTH (Under the Hood) A transparency tool where users look up the visibility-impacting labels attached to their own account and posts. A daily batch collects them and the serving layer aggregates them under-the-hood/ Under the Hood

Feed surfaces

This document mainly covers For You, the feed surface the algorithm recommends. The vertical video carousel inside For You was introduced, off by default, in the 2026-10-08 commit (Gen4+38) verified (Gen4+38 in the change log); in the 2026-10-15 commit (Gen4+42), a VQV prediction term from the immersive surface model was added to the carousel ranking score, but its default weight is 0.0, so default behavior is unchanged verified (Gen4+42 in the change log). Since the 2026-10-17 commit (Gen4+44), the three dedup checks inside the carousel are on by default, and the carousel is not inserted when the same response has a Who-to-Follow module verified (Gen4+44 in the change log). Since the 2026-10-20 commit (Gen4+45), the carousel excludes videos whose media already appears in the top 35 of the main feed, and the carousel itself is still off by default as of that commit verified (daily 2026-10-21); the video-only path implemented in Thunder is turned on by a separate surface that is not public (Reels equivalent) inferred.

  • For You is the algorithm-recommended feed this document mainly covers, and its gRPC methods are get_for_you_feed and get_for_you_feed_urt verified 2026 — home-mixer/server.rs:273-346
  • A vertical video carousel module, which places 3–5 vertical videos in the 6th slot of the For You feed, was introduced off by default in the 2026-10-08 commit (Gen4+38) verified — home-mixer/util/video_carousel.rs
    • Off by default means EnableVideoCarousel = false in home-mixer/params/param.rs.
    • It is enabled only on For You requests and appears again only after 60 minutes (VideoCarouselFatigueMinutes) have passed since the last carousel impression.
    • The slot is the 6th position in the feed (VideoCarouselPosition). A vertical video is one whose width-to-height ratio is below 1.0.
    • Since the 2026-10-15 commit (Gen4+42), the ranking score is the video_open weight plus the VQV prediction weight of the immersive surface model (GalleryPage). Because the VQV weight defaults to 0.0, default behavior is still ordering by video_open verified — home-mixer/util/video_carousel.rs:104-123.
    • Since the 2026-10-17 commit (Gen4+44), the three dedup checks inside the carousel (same author, first 3 SID levels matching, multimodal embedding cosine of 0.72 or higher) are on by default verified — params/param.rs:1095-1112.
      • From the same commit, the carousel is not inserted when the same response has a Who-to-Follow module (no parameter) verified — selectors/blender_selector.rs:50, 156-161.
      • The carousel itself (EnableVideoCarousel) is still off by default in the 2026-10-22 commit (989fb91) verified — params/param.rs:1120-1125.
    • Since the 2026-10-20 commit (Gen4+45), the carousel skips videos that have the same media ID or MD5 hash as the top 35 of the main feed, and videos with the same media as one picked earlier within the carousel (no parameter) verified — util/video_carousel.rs:52-108.
      • The main feed range is cut at the same boundary as the carousel candidate pool (RESULT_SIZE) — filters/video_carousel_filter.rs:26-29. Details are in daily 2026-10-21.
    • The side effect that logs the position and score of carousel videos to Kafka in responses where the carousel was actually served was introduced in the 2026-10-21 commit (Gen4+46), and its switch has been on by default since the 2026-10-22 commit (989fb91) verified — side_effects/video_carousel_candidates_kafka_side_effect.rs, params/param.rs:1162-1167. Because the carousel itself is off by default, this log is also written only for requests where the carousel is on. Details are in daily 2026-10-22.
    • Since the 2026-10-22 commit (Gen4+47), the carousel is not inserted into requests that fetch more by scrolling down (BOTTOM cursor) verified — util/video_carousel.rs:11-23.
    • At introduction (Gen4+38, 2026-10-08), vertical videos were grouped in order of predicted video_open probability.
    • The detailed selection path is in Gen4+38 in the change log.
  • Following handles only in-network posts and, as of the 2026-10-17 commit (862a123), has a gRPC service and candidate pipelines separate from For You verified — home-mixer/lib.rs
    • The services are FollowingFeedService and RankedFollowingFeedService, and the pipelines are following_candidate_pipeline.rs, ranked_following_candidate_pipeline.rs, and reverse_chron_posts_pipeline.rs. The Gen4 release (47c1bcd) already had the same structure verified — home-mixer/server.rs:522-680, home-mixer/candidate_pipeline/
    • Both Following services set in_network_only to true after building the query verified — home-mixer/server.rs:555, 658
    • Important: Even for a For You request, if the user has allow_for_you_recommendations = false, the server demotes the request to in_network_only verified — home-mixer/server.rs:96-97
    • The product_surface value passed to Phoenix also splits into HomeTimelineRankedFollowing and HomeTimelineRanking depending on this flag verified — home-mixer/scorers/phoenix_scorer.rs:86-90.
    • Gen3 (0bfc279) had no Following-specific service and was split only by the in_network_only flag of the same pipeline verified — home-mixer/server.rs:75-76
    • In the 2026-08-18 commit (Gen4+3), a VF hydrator dedicated to reverse-chron (Following) was branched off verified — home-mixer/candidate_hydrators/vf_following_candidate_hydrator.rs
      • The new hydrator is a new file of 95 lines.
      • Another evidence location is home-mixer/candidate_pipeline/reverse_chron_posts_pipeline.rs:141-144.
      • Previously, For You and Following used the same VFCandidateHydrator.
      • The new hydrator is connected only to the Following pipeline.
      • The should_drop_ancillary helper is reused from the existing file as pub(crate).
      • The new hydrator returns only the VF lookup results (visibility_reason, drop_ancillary_posts) and resets the remaining candidate fields with ..Default::default().
      • In other words, the Following pipeline's hydration output shrank to the two VF results, and the remaining fields are filled by other hydrators.
      • VF's SafetyLevel remains TimelineHome. Following and For You share the safety level.
      • Why it matters: With this commit, the hydration field sets of For You and Following were explicitly split; this is an optimization direction that avoids spending logic and resources on candidate fields Following does not use inferred
  • A topic feed is a request carrying topic_ids; if there are 7 or more topic ids (> 6), it is treated as a "bulk topic request" and the candidate sources differ verified 2026 — home-mixer/models/query.rs:201-203
  • Video surface: Thunder has a dedicated video ring buffer and an is_video_request path that are fully implemented, but the only public caller hardcodes is_video_request: false verified(code) — thunder/thunder_service.rs:287
    • Another evidence location is home-mixer/sources/thunder_source.rs.
    • Because the implementation is complete and not a stub, a separate surface that is not public (Reels equivalent) turns this flag on and uses it inferred.

Candidate generation (retrieval)

Candidate generation (retrieval) is the stage that gathers posts from multiple sources to hand to ranking. The 2026 pipeline runs the sources in parallel and concatenates the results as is, with per-source caps instead of an allocation ratio between in-network and OON verified (Candidate allocation section). Since the 2026-10-07 commit (Gen4+37), the source that serves a popular posts list built in advance by an offline job is on by default verified (Gen4+37 in the change log). The SID generative retrieval source released in the 2026-10-02–03 commits (Gen4+34–35) is off by default verified (Gen4+34, Gen4+35).

Current (2026-08 Gen4)

As of the Gen4 release, For You has 12 candidate sources in total: 7 internal Phoenix pipeline sources and 5 external For You pipeline sources verified. The evidence is home-mixer/candidate_pipeline/phoenix_candidate_pipeline.rs, for_you_candidate_pipeline.rs, and the EnableXxxSource defaults in home-mixer/params/param.rs.

On the same basis, the retrieval sources confirmed on by default are Thunder, which serves the latest in-network posts, and Phoenix retrieval and SimClusters, which serve OON candidates verified. The SID source and the popular posts source in the table were added later, in the 2026-10-02–03 commits (Gen4+34–35) verified (details below). The table values are as of the Gen4 release, but the rows for these two sources and the cold slice cap of PhoenixSource are items added in later commits.

Source What Gate · default
ThunderSource Latest in-network posts (in-memory, 2-day retention) EnableThunderSource=true (on by default), ThunderMaxResults=1200
PhoenixSource OON candidates found by Phoenix two-tower retrieval (an embedding model split into a user tower and a post tower). Since the 2026-09-18 commit, the cold-start slice is distinguished separately (details below) EnablePhoenixSource=true, PhoenixMaxResults=1000. Cold slice cap PhoenixColdStartMaxResults=200 (since 2026-09-30, Gen4+32)
SimclustersSource SimClusters (revived 2026-08). OON candidates found by cluster similarity EnableSimclustersSource=true
TweetMixerSource Legacy OON aggregator (calls the Gen2 tweet-mixer over thrift) EnableTweetMixerSource=false off by default, TweetMixerMaxResults=800
PhoenixTopicsSource Phoenix retrieval for topic requests Topic requests
PhoenixMOESource Phoenix MoE retrieval EnablePhoenixMOESource
SidSource SID generative retrieval microservice (Gen4+34~35, released 2026-10-02 ~ 10-03, details below) home-mixer-side EnableSidSource=false off by default, SidSourceMaxResults=800, SidSourceMaxSeeds=50, SidSourceMaxPerSeed=100, SidSourceMinPrefixDepth=3 (as of the 2026-10-02 commit)
PopularPostsSource Popular posts list built in advance by an offline job (details below) EnablePopularPostsSource=true, on by default since the 2026-10-07 commit (Gen4+37) (param.rs:944-948). PopularPostsMaxResults=500
CachedPostsSource Redis warm cache has_cached_posts (the inverse condition of all the others)
ScoredPostsSource Runs the entire pipeline above recursively Always
AdsSource Ads EnableAdsSource && !is_preview
WhoToFollowSource Follow recommendations (up to 3 accounts) EnableWhoToFollowModule
PromptsSource Inline/cover prompts EnablePrompts
PushToHomeSource Pins a post that came from a push at position 0 push_to_home_post_id.is_some()

The details of the three sources shortened in the table are as follows:

  • Since the 2026-10-21 commit (Gen4+46), PhoenixSource can send a per-name value model weight map in the retrieval request. The default is an empty string, so it currently sends none verified — sources/phoenix_source.rs:137-138.
    • The parameter is RetrievalValueModelWeights, and the proto field is RetrieveTopKCandidatesRequest.value_model_weights = 17. The server-side code that reads this field is not public verified. Details are in daily 2026-10-22.
  • In the 2026-09-18 commit (Gen4+25), a cold-start slice was wired into PhoenixSource as a first-class path via the dataset_type tag verified (Cold start section).
    • If a response candidate has dataset_type == HOME_COLD_DATASET_TYPE(=13), served_type is ForYouPhoenixRetrievalCold; otherwise it is the existing ForYouPhoenixRetrieval.
    • This slice's cap PhoenixColdStartMaxResults was introduced in Gen4+25 at 0 (off by default) and has been 200 since the 2026-09-30 commit (Gen4+32) verified — params/param.rs:16. It is still 200 in the 2026-10-17 commit (862a123).
  • SidSource calls the SID generative retrieval microservice released in the 2026-10-02–03 commits (Gen4+34–35) verified (Gen4+34, Gen4+35).
    • When the user's positive engagement post IDs are passed as seeds, the service builds candidates in three steps:
      1. Convert the seed into a 6-level code. If the seed post is in the local SID trie, look it up there; otherwise, look it up in the external SidLookupService.
      2. For each seed, pick candidates from the shared-prefix range in order of decreasing depth, from max_prefix_depth down to min_prefix_depth. Ranges already consumed at a deeper level are excluded.
      3. Round-robin interleave the candidate lists of all seeds, dedup, and return the result.
    • Seeds are extracted from user engagement signals by reusing the same function as simclusters_source::post_signal_ids.
    • Each Candidate carries shared_prefix_depth as its score.
    • Response candidates are labeled served_type=ForYouPhoenixRetrievalMoe. This is the same label as PhoenixMOE.
    • The call has a 300ms gRPC deadline, and the connection path has two routes: xDS P2C → DNS fallback.
    • The server polls the parquet snapshot (post_sid_snapshot.parquet, columns post_id/author_id/post_sid) every 30 seconds and reloads it in full.
    • The trie consists of two vectors: by_key(prefix range binary search) and by_post(seed lookup).
    • Server-side limits are max_results=800 / max_per_seed=100 / min_prefix_depth=3 / max_prefix_depth=6 / max_seeds=200, and the hard caps are MAX_RESULTS_CAP=5000 · MAX_PER_SEED_CAP=2000 · MAX_CALLER_LEN=64.
  • PopularPostsSource was created in the 2026-10-03 commit (Gen4+35), and its structure was replaced wholesale in the 2026-10-06 commit (Gen4+36) verified (Gen4+35, Gen4+36).
    • The replaced structure does not call Thunder at request time. It reads the popular posts list (up to 500) built in advance by two offline jobs from Manhattan KV every 60 seconds, removes only the posts the user has already seen (seen_ids), and returns the rest as candidates as is.
    • The first job, popular_authors_job (hourly), picks from a BigQuery snapshot the top 0.005% by follower count among authors who posted in the last 7 days (TOP_POSTING_AUTHORS_FRACTION=0.00005).
    • The second job, popular_posts_job (every 5 minutes), gathers those authors' original posts (excluding replies and retweets) from Thunder. It scores posts from the last 24 hours using the view counts from engagement counts, then trims to 5 per author and 500 overall.
      • The scoring formula is quality = views × (1−e^{−λ·24h}) / (1−e^{−λ·max(age,0.5h)}) (half-life 8 hours).
    • Since the 2026-10-16 commit (Gen4+43), the label is its own served type ForYouPopularPosts; before that it was ForYouPhoenixRetrieval (popular_posts_source.rs:13).
    • It is turned off for cache-reuse requests and in_network_only requests (popular_posts_source.rs:27-31).
    • PopularPostsTopAuthors, PopularPostsMaxPerAuthor, and PopularPostsMaxRepliesRepostsPerAuthor, which existed in Gen4+35, were deleted and moved to job CLI arguments (--popular-posts-per-author=5, --popular-posts-budget=500, --popular-posts-half-life-hours=8).
    • Storage format v1 is a 13-byte header followed by 24 bytes per post (post_id, author_id, quality).

Thunder is an in-network index newly built in 2026. It replaces the Earlybird search index inferred. The evidence is that the roles are the same and references to Earlybird disappeared.

  • Posts are held in DashMap<post_id, LightPost>, and each author has 3 ring buffers (original, reply/retweet, video) verified — thunder/posts/post_store.rs:20-53
  • LightPost has no text, no media, no engagement counts, and no safety labels verified — thunder/kafka/tweet_events_listener.rs:230-248
    • The only fields it holds are post_id, author_id, created_at, in_reply_to_*, is_retweet, is_reply, source_*, has_video, and conversation_id.
  • Ranking inside Thunder is deliberately a single line of recency sorting, because Phoenix re-scores anyway verified — thunder/thunder_service.rs:334-339
  • The default retention period is 2 days verified — post_store.rs:521-526
  • Under overload, it rejects requests immediately instead of queuing them verified — thunder_service.rs:160-171
    • If try_acquire fails, it becomes resource_exhausted.
  • The reply exposure rule is a product policy stated explicitly in code verified — post_store.rs:291-315
    • If the parent is an original post, the reply passes.
    • If the parent is not an original post, the reply passes only when the parent is a direct reply to the conversation root and the reply target is someone the viewer follows.
    • If the parent is not in the store, the reply is simply dropped. So when a thread root older than 2 days expires, all replies under it become invisible.
  • A user's own retweet of themselves is blocked by one line in the hot path verified — post_store.rs:287-289

The retrieval sources that survived from the 2023 generation are tweet-mixer and SimClusters. tweet-mixer is mirrored as off by default, and SimClusters was revived. ⚠ Claim changed (2026-08-13): the canon had long stated explicitly that "SimClusters, TwHIN, UTEG/GraphJet, FRS, Earlybird, Lists, Communities — none of these names appear anywhere in home-mixer/". The Gen4 release brought the simclusters/ sub-repo back as a home-mixer OON retrieval source (EnableSimclustersSource=true, on by default). TwHIN/UTEG/GraphJet/FRS/Earlybird/Lists/Communities are not in Gen4 either verified — home-mixer/params/param.rs, README.md #candidate-sources

The details of the SimClusters core algorithm (SVD pipeline, k, index format, update cycle) need a deep dive. For the simclusters/ sub-repo, only the file list was checked and the individual files were not read. The items that need a deep dive are in the list in daily/2026-08-15.md.

Candidate allocation — per-source caps, not ratios

"In-network 50% / out-of-network 50%" is not a quota.

The 2026 pipeline has no allocator, no ratio parameter, and no global cap verified — candidate-pipeline/candidate_pipeline.rs:257-272

  • It runs the sources in parallel with join_all and simply concatenates the results.
  • A source that errors out silently disappears.

The max_results value each source reads from a FeatureSwitch parameter was released as a production cron mirror in the Gen4 release (2026-08-13) verified — home-mixer/params/param.rs

  • ThunderMaxResults = 1200
  • PhoenixMaxResults = 1000
  • TweetMixerMaxResults = 800. However, it is off by default with EnableTweetMixerSource = false.
  • For PhoenixMOEMaxResults, the corresponding param must be checked.

In the 2026 pipeline, the means of adjusting the in-network versus OON share is a scoring multiplier, not retrieval verified — home-mixer/scorers/ranking_scorer.rs:220-239, 272-275

effective_oon is computed in three branches, and all of its values were released in the Gen4 release verified — home-mixer/params/param.rs:247,269,275

param default condition
OonWeightFactor 0.75 default OON multiplier
TopicOonWeightFactor 0.5 for topic requests
NewUserAgeThresholdSecs 0 new-user routing threshold. A value of 0 seconds means the new-user path is effectively mirrored as disabled inferred. The NEW_USER_OON_WEIGHT_FACTOR param was confirmed to be absent from param.rs
EnableOonRescoreForInNetworkRepliesRetweets true the OON multiplier also applies to in-network replies and retweets

A generalization note is in candidate-allocation.md.

Legacy (2025 Scala, tweet-mixer)

tweet-mixer appeared all at once on 2025-09-03 with 384 files. It has no README and not a single .md file, so every fact has to be confirmed from the code alone verified.

The retrieval families newly introduced in this generation are as follows:

  • 19 new DeepRetrieval-related files appeared (0 in the 2023 snapshot) verified
  • 20 new files that consume SimClusters appeared, and the SimClusters core itself is unchanged from 2023 verified — git show --diff-filter=M c54bec0 | grep -ci simclusters = 0
    • The new files include SimclusterColdPostsCandidateSource.scala.

  • 15 new files that consume Earlybird appeared, and the index itself (src/java/com/twitter/search) did not change verified

How SimClusters, TwHIN, and DeepRetrieval each generate embeddings, build indexes, and do lookups, along with the code defects found in them, is summarized in embedding-retrieval.md.

Ranking

As of the Gen4 release (2026-08-13), Phoenix, the ranking model of X For You, predicts the probability of actions such as like, reply, and report for each candidate post verified(Phoenix section). As of the same release, the score starts from the sum of these probabilities multiplied by per-action weights, and after an offset it applies author-diversity decay, the OON multiplier, and the new-author boost in that order verified(Phoenix section, new-author boost section). Since the 2026-09-24 commit (Gen4+28), the shared crate xai-value-model does this calculation, and home-mixer's ranking scorer file was deleted verified(Phoenix section). In the params of the same release, VMRanker's DPP slate (the bundle of candidates sent out to the user) reordering is also on verified(VMRanker table in the Phoenix section). Since this release, the weight values can be read in the repo as a cron mirror that copies the production defaults daily, and some mirror values changed up to the 2026-10-14 commit (Gen4+41) verified(weights section, Gen4+41 in the change log).

Phoenix (2026, current) — Gen4 release update

Phoenix is a Transformer ported from Grok-1. It puts the user history and the candidates into one sequence and scores them in a single pass. The structure, masks, and parameter distribution are summarized in sequence-transformer-ranking.md.

There are 24 prediction heads by the documentation, divided into 5 categories verified — README.md #scoring-and-ranking (2026-08-13). The table follows this README; weight terms removed or added since then are in the weights table.

category head param symbol (weight)
Engagement (7) favorite · reply · repost · quote · share · share via DM · share via copy link FavoriteWeight · ReplyWeight · RetweetWeight · QuoteWeight · ShareWeight · ShareViaDmWeight · ShareViaCopyLinkWeight
Clicks (6) post · profile · link · photo expand · video open · quoted post ClickWeight · ProfileClickWeight · OpenLinkWeight · PhotoExpandWeight · VideoOpenWeight · QuotedClickWeight
Attention (5) video quality view · dwell · dwell time · click dwell time · active seconds VqvWeight · DwellWeight · ContDwellTimeWeight · ContClickDwellTimeWeight · ContActiveSecs5mResidualNormWeight
Author (1) follow author FollowAuthorWeight
Negative (5) not interested · mute author · block author · report · not dwelled NotInterestedWeight · MuteAuthorWeight · BlockAuthorWeight · ReportWeight · NotDwelledWeight

The click dwell time head and the dwell time head, which deal with dwell time, had their training approach or ranking term changed after the release verified(Gen4+22 in the change log, Gen4+23, Gen4+38).

  • In the 2026-09-16 commit (fad2f71, Gen4+22), the click dwell time head began to be trained as sigmoid BCE (threshold=10s) binary classification verified(Gen4+22 in the change log). The public training code before that had no loss setting for this head verified — 2d4a03c phoenix/xrex grep.
    • The head name is click_dwell_time.
    • The serving head remains a probability [0,1]. _rescale_sigmoid_heads_for_inference skips restoring the original unit through a binary exception.
  • In the 2026-09-17 commit (42266f3, Gen4+23), the ranking term for click dwell was redefined verified(Gen4+23 in the change log).
    • EnableClickDwellLowFavRatePenalty, which had existed since the Gen4 release (47c1bcd), was deleted entirely (param.rs:387-416). This heuristic used 4 tuning params (baseline, alpha, floor, cap) and (fav/baseline)^alpha to lower the dwell prediction when fav was low.
    • A new parameter EnableCdwellOnImpr (off by default) took its place. When on, it computes click_dwell_term = click_dwell_time × click_score. This redefines the click dwell term as expected dwell per impression.
    • ContClickDwellTimeWeight did not change in the mirror.
  • In the 2026-10-08 commit (35650fb, Gen4+38), the training loss of the dwell_time head changed from Tweedie and MAE to CREAD verified — phoenix/xrex/configs/xrecsys.py:272-275, 715-742.
    • The newly enabled CREAD loss trains dwell time as binary classification of whether it exceeds each of 30 log-spaced thresholds (2 seconds up to the cap), then converts back to an expected value.
    • In the default home training config, two CREAD losses were turned on at 0.1 each. The cap is 120 seconds for regular surfaces and 240 seconds for gallery/immersive surfaces.
    • In the same config, the Tweedie (0.1) and MAE (0.1) weights became 0.
    • The serving head name and the ranking weight (ContDwellTimeWeight) are unchanged.

There are 2 more params that contribute to the score but are not in the README categories. The total number of effective weight params is 26.

  • QuotedVqvWeight is the video quality view weight of a quoted post. It is not in the README categories, but the param exists.
  • PostUnexploredWeight is the new-author boost. Details are in the new-author boost section.

The canon's long-standing observation that "the head count splits three ways within the repo (public checkpoint 19 / ranking scorer 22 / VMRanker proto 21)" is a fact up to Gen3. The Gen4 README states 24 by the documentation, and the weight symbols in home-mixer/params/param.rs are also organized as 25 (prediction head) + 1 (post_unexplored heuristic). However, whether the dead 19-field PhoenixScores struct in candidate_pipeline/candidate.rs observed in Gen3 was cleaned up in Gen4 requires a deep dive. verified (documentation) / inferred (whether the code was cleaned up)

The generalized notes on head design are in multi-task-ranking.md.

As of the Gen4 release (47c1bcd), the final score was computed in the following order verified — home-mixer/scorers/ranking_scorer.rs.

  1. Take the weighted sum of 26 weights × P(head). negative_sum is subtracted with its sign flipped.
    • Only for original posts from mutual follows, add BidirectionalFollowReplyWeightBoost=15.0 to the reply weight. The condition is !in_reply_to && !retweeted && is_mutual_follow_author.
  2. Apply offset_score. If the score is negative, it is (score + negative_sum) / total_sum * NEGATIVE_SCORES_OFFSET; if positive, it is score + NEGATIVE_SCORES_OFFSET.
  3. Multiply by author-diversity decay. The k-th appearance of the same author is multiplied by (1-0.25)*0.5^(k-1) + 0.25, so the first appearance is 1.0×.
    • The exponent is the number of times that author has appeared earlier (ranking_scorer.rs:614-615, 635).
    • The settings are AuthorDiversityDecay=0.5, AuthorDiversityFloor=0.25, and EnableAuthorDiversity=true.
  4. Multiply by the OON multiplier OonWeightFactor=0.75. For topic requests, use TopicOonWeightFactor=0.5.
  5. Apply the new-author boost.

The normalize_score normalization stage that existed in the Gen3 code (0bfc279) is not in ranking_scorer.rs of the Gen4 release verified — ranking_scorer.rs:4, 259.

In the 2026-09-24 commit (Gen4+28, 44d37eb), ranking_scorer.rs was deleted, and the weighted sum, offset, author-diversity decay, and OON multiplier calculations moved to the shared crate xai-value-model verified — xai-value-model/scoring.rs.

  • As of the 2026-10-17 commit (862a123), the scorer chain is PhoenixScorer, ImmersiveVideoScorer, VMRanker in that order verified — phoenix_candidate_pipeline.rs:487-488.
    • The chain at the time of the Gen4 release was vec![phoenix_scorer, ranking_scorer, vm_ranker] (phoenix_candidate_pipeline.rs:395-396).
  • As of the same reference, home-mixer's VMRanker scorer first computes a local weighted sum (fuse_heads) and the new-author adjustment, then overwrites them with the score returned by the vm-ranker service verified — home-mixer/scorers/vm_ranker.rs:59-131.

The heuristic that sets the vqv weight to 0 depending on the video length and the querying user's follower count has been in the repo's home-mixer/util/candidates_util.rs since the Gen4 release verified — candidates_util.rs:19-60.

  • The related identifiers are vqv_weight, quoted_vqv_weight, and the MinVideoDurationMs threshold. vqv_weight uses the weight as is when the video length exceeds MinVideoDurationMs and query.user_features.follower_count is not 10,000 or more. It also uses the weight when the follower count is empty (candidates_util.rs:4, 25-38).
  • In the Gen4 release, ranking_scorer.rs:230 called this function.

The VMRanker and DPP settings are now public verified — home-mixer/params/param.rs:579-618. The values in the table are those at the time of the Gen4 release, except VMRankerClusterId, which is the 2026-10-06 value.

The VMRanker service itself has been in vm-ranker/ since the Gen4 release verified — vm-ranker/ranker_service.rs.

  • The same directory has main.rs, dpp.rs (the DPP implementation), and scoring/dpp_model.rs verified — vm-ranker/.
  • The 2026-09-23 commit (Gen4+27) added scoring/value_model.rs, params.rs, and config_sync.rs verified — vm-ranker/.

The 2026-08-18 commit (Gen4+3) newly wired 7 SID (semantic ID) fields into the VMRanker request verified — home-mixer/scorers/vm_ranker.rs:194-206:

VMRanker request field source field meaning
sid_known s.sid_known whether this candidate's SID is known/valid (bool)
sid_k1 / sid_k2 / sid_k3 s.sid_k_l1 / sid_k_l2 / sid_k_l3 codeword of each level of the 3-level hierarchical semantic ID
sid_gap1 / sid_gap2 / sid_gap3 s.sid_gap_l1 / sid_gap_l2 / sid_gap_l3 neighbor gap in each level's codebook (proxy for confidence/sparsity inferred)
  • With these fields passed per candidate source alongside the existing fields, VMRanker can now see not only the collaborative pool rank but also the semantic ID hierarchy position in its item diversity decisions.
    • The existing fields are k, pool_rank, and pool_rank_gap.
    • VMRanker keeps the legacy name but is now responsible for DPP slate reordering.
    • This is the X-side connection corresponding to the SID family observed in Kuaishou HD-Rec/PushDualGen inferred.
  • Why it matters: VMRanker's diversity judgment now has three axes of information: per-candidate-source rank, the 3-level semantic ID codeword, and the neighbor gap.
    • The existence of a 3-level codebook hierarchy (coarse → fine) is itself newly confirmed architecture information.
    • This wiring is where the rank/rerank side consumes the same SID infrastructure as the SID window in Phoenix retrieval. The SID window (video_14day, video_48h, etc.) is in the Gen4+1 entry of the Phoenix training and index section.
  • Undisclosed: The following are not public:
    • The SID codebook definition (vocabulary size and training approach of each level)
    • The exact formula for sid_gap
    • How these fields are used in VMRanker's response logic

New-author boost — the third adjustment factor documented in Gen4

The new-author boost is an adjustment factor that lifts posts from authors whose impressions are below a threshold toward a target position. The README describes it as follows:

"New-Author Boost: posts from authors whose impressions are below a threshold are lifted toward a target position."

The new README states three scoring adjustment factors verified — README.md #scoring-and-ranking.

  1. Author Diversity Decay
  2. Out-of-Network Discount
  3. New-Author Boost

The params that set this boost are in the table below verified — home-mixer/params/param.rs:351-374, #coldstart-threshold.

param default meaning
PostUnexploredWeight 0.02 → home-mixer mirror 0.015 (Gen4+37, 2026-10-07). vm-ranker/params.rs stays at 0.02 additive value of the new-author boost
PostUnexploredWeightInNetworkOnly true applied to in-network only (not attached to OON)
EnableMultiplicativePostUnexplored false additive by default, multiplicative form disabled
MultiplicativePostUnexploredAlpha 0.0 exponent used when the multiplicative form is enabled
ColdStartImpressionThreshold 200 (since 2026-09-30, Gen4+32) The README describes it as targeting authors whose impressions are below the threshold, but the code treats a post as a cold-start slot candidate only when its home impression count is below this value verified

ColdStartImpressionThreshold was lowered from 1000 to 200 in the 2026-09-30 commit (Gen4+32) verified — params/param.rs:459(Gen4+32 in the change log). It is also 200 in the 2026-10-17 commit (862a123).

  • The cold-start slot selector that uses this threshold picks only candidates whose post view_count_on_home is below the threshold verified — author_cold_start.rs:293-294.
  • The Gen4 release code made the same comparison using the candidate post's view_count verified — author_cold_start.rs:179.

The canon's observation in the cold start section that "new items: the 2026 code has no mechanism at all" is a fact up to Gen3. Gen4 documented a new-author (account-level) boost. As of the Gen4 release, there was no boost attached to an individual new post (item level), and the hash embedding collision problem was unchanged verified. The later post-level mechanisms are in the cold start section.

The file's own comment defines the meaning of the weight signs and magnitudes verified:

"These weights reflect a combination of how much an action is valued in ranking and typical propensities of these actions across the X network (e.g. negative feedback is overall rare)."

In other words, the magnitude of report −234 is not "the relative importance of one report" but the product of value × 1/propensity. Here propensity means how often that action typically occurs across the whole X network. Because reports are so rare, a large absolute value is attached.

The 2026-08-14 commit (Gen4+1) stated this interpretation rule explicitly in a code comment and the README verified — home-mixer/params/param.rs:281-306, home-mixer/scorers/ranking_scorer.rs:415-446, README.md #scoring-and-ranking:

"Each weight multiplies the predicted probability of that action (P(favorite), P(repost), …) or a continuous value e.g. watch time -- the weights do not multiply raw engagement counts. One common misinterpretation is that you can read these weight ratios as count equivalences, e.g. the incorrect statement that 'one report cancels 468 likes' -- this is incorrect because the weights apply to the predicted probabilities rather than raw counts. And the baseline probability of a Report is more than 1000x lower than a Like, so it's weighted more to allow the prediction to affect the final ranking at all." — home-mixer/params/param.rs:283-292

The same comment also rejects the misconception that "mass reporting uniformly suppresses reach," for two reasons verified — same comment block.

  1. The score multiplies your predicted probability, so reports from bot accounts mainly affect recommendations for users similar to those bots (personalization) verified — same comment.
  2. Only actions taken on posts served in the Home Timeline count as ranking signals. Reactions that appear from a link shared in a group chat do not affect ranking verified — same comment.

Five caveats of the weights mirror

There are five things to watch when reading this mirror.

  1. The cron sync is a mirror that follows once a day, so it lags. Production changes after the sync time in the header may not be reflected yet. verified
  2. Sign and magnitude must be read with propensity in mind. The file's own comment states "value = worth × 1/propensity". The ratio of absolute values (report −234 is 468× favorite 0.5) is not the relative importance as is.
  3. Since the 2026-09-23 commit (Gen4+27), the weights mirror has been split into two files, and as of the 2026-10-17 commit the weight values differ between the two files.
    • Gen4+27 introduced vm-ranker/params.rs, which holds 56 parameters, so the mirror became two files together with the existing home-mixer/params/param.rs for the home-mixer process verified.
    • The next day (Gen4+28, 2026-09-24), 22 non-weight ranking parameters were deleted from the home-mixer param.rs verified — comparison of param.rs in 1b3fec20 and 44d37eb.
      • The deleted parameters include the author diversity, OON, new-user, weight perturbation, VMRanker DPP, and value model switch families; the only weight is ContActiveSecs5mResidualNormWeight.
    • Per-action weights remain in both files, and as of the 2026-10-17 commit (862a123), five values differ: favorite, video_open, cont_dwell_time, post_unexplored, and not_interested verified — home-mixer/params/param.rs, vm-ranker/params.rs.
    • The shared crate xai-value-model was released as an actual file, so both processes compute the value model with the same code verified. However, each process reads the weights from its own parameter file verified — home-mixer/scorers/value_model.rs:8-51, vm-ranker/scoring/value_model.rs:68.
    • The phoenix training hyperparameters and the botmaker rule constants are still outside the repo. crate::util, which the Gen3 canon treated as outside the repo, has been released as home-mixer/util/ since the Gen4 release verified — home-mixer/lib.rs.
  4. The Phoenix training code is "trainable", not "the same as production". The README states the difference in scale: "a small model can be trained and served end-to-end".
  5. Some botmaker rules are not published to prevent gaming. The README states this explicitly. For some of the labels that visibility-filtering references, the rules are not open.

Practice of documenting parameter changes — introduced in Gen4

The practice of documenting parameter changes as code diffs began in Gen4. docs/BIDIRECTIONAL_BOOST_CHANGE.md is a model for how parameter changes will be documented as code diffs going forward verified:

"Going forward, you'll see future algorithm updates published to this open source repository, and you should be able to understand what changed by checking the diffs."

The same document reproduces the 3-stage rollout of the mutual-follow boost (A/B start → broad rollout → parameter adjustment) with 3 code diffs. No other company (Meta, Netflix, or YouTube) has had an example of this documentation approach so far.

The value of tracking the X commit log daily in this repository grows considerably. What changes in which param in the next commit becomes a lagging indicator of A/B results.

Generation comparison — why the earlier canon stated "values undisclosed"

In Gen1, Gen2, and Gen3 the values were indeed not released, and Gen4 newly opened them.

  • Gen1 (2023 Scala): object ModelWeights at ScoredTweetsParam.scala:151 has 17 parameters. The defaults are 1.0 for 10 and 0.0 for 7, and they are not actual production values. Range bounds (e.g., ReportParam −20000..0) are valid only as relative-scale hints.
  • Gen2 (2025 Scala): Moved to HomeGlobalParams.scala:786, and the parameters grew from 17 to 30. All 30 values were intentionally wiped to default = 0.0. Only relative-scale hints remain.
  • Gen3 (2026-01 Rust): The params:: module itself was dropped from the repo. Symbols such as FavoriteWeight had only call sites and no definition.
  • Gen4 (2026-08 Rust): ⚠ Released the real production mirror as home-mixer/params/param.rs.

The widely quoted "reply 13.5" table is still exactly the 2023-04-05 snapshot. Only favorite 0.5 and retweet 1.0 match the Gen4 mirror, and the rest was overhauled substantially over three years. verified — twitter/the-algorithm-ml projects/home/recap/README.md

  • The values in that table are as follows:
    • Positive items: fav 0.5 / retweet 1.0 / reply 13.5 / good_profile_click 12.0 / video_playback50 0.005 / reply_engaged_by_author 75.0 / good_click 11.0 / good_click_v2 10.0
    • Negative items: negative_feedback_v2 −74.0 / report −369.0

Some constants are restored across generations. Gen3 offset_score is a literal translation of Gen2 Scala RerankerUtil.weightedScoresSum. The Gen2 counterpart of NEGATIVE_SCORES_OFFSET, which was hidden in crate::params in Gen3, is val Epsilon = 0.001. Whether NEGATIVE_SCORES_OFFSET was also exposed in param.rs in Gen4 needs a grep. Details are in multi-task-ranking.md.

In the Gen2 code, X can inject multiplicative Beta-distribution noise seeded per user×date into the ranking weights verified — HeavyRankerWeightsQueryFeatureHydrator.scala, seed Objects.hash(userId, startOfDay). Whether this noise injection was kept in Gen4 needs a deep dive.

Legacy heavy ranker (2023–2025)

The legacy heavy ranker is a structure in which a multi-task neural network predicts engagement probabilities and sorts by their weighted sum. Compared with the 2026 Phoenix, the objective has the same form and the input differs. The legacy ranker uses handcrafted features as input, and Phoenix uses ID embeddings.

In the 2025 generation, two rankers run side by side verified — ScoredTweetsRerankingScoringPipelineConfig.scala:35-39.

  • Navi is the production heavy ranker and has 15 heads verified — home-mixer/.../model/PredictedScoreFeature.scala:294-311.
  • Phoenix is a Transformer rescorer (a model that rescores the scores assigned by the preceding ranker) and has 13 heads. It is attached after Navi through ParamGatedScorer(EnablePhoenixScorerParam, …) and shares the same ModelWeights as Navi verified — PhoenixPredictedScoreFeature.scala:174-189.

The Transformer ranker did not replace the existing heavy ranker in one step. It first joined alongside as a rescorer switched on by a param, and then fully replaced the heavy ranker in 2026. verified — the evidence is that all 8 files were newly created in c54bec0 (git log --diff-filter=A) and the pipeline wiring above.

The 2025 Phoenix call specification is below verified — home-mixer/.../util/PhoenixUtils.scala.

  • Candidates are cut to 1400 (MaxCandidates = 1400 :36). There is also a config value TopLogProbsNum = 50 (:35).
  • Retries are 2, 500ms per attempt, 1 second in total (:119-121). The channel is picked at random again on every attempt (:108-109).
  • Because the response is a logprob (log probability), the probability is restored with math.exp(logProb) (:151-158).
  • Only 5 booleans travel with a candidate: isRetweet, isForYouPage (always true), isPromotedTweet (always false), isReply, isQuote :48-68.

The score combination formula and the full per-generation head lists are in multi-task-ranking.md. This formula does not multiply the negative heads but handles them with a threshold constant penalty, and finally compresses with Epsilon = 0.001.

There is a caveat in the 2025 code. There are two files named PredictedScoreFeature, with different head sets. The 15 in model/ are actually used, and the 17 in product/scored_tweets/scorer/ are legacy. Writing the head list from the latter is wrong. verified — import path in RerankerUtil.scala:4

Grok does not contribute arithmetically to the 2025 ranking score. It enters only through filters (4 kinds, including GrokGoreFilter) and topic tags. No Grok head appears anywhere in PredictedScoreFeatures. verified — repo-wide, ScoredTweetsRecommendationPipelineConfig.scala:543-546

There is no ranking boost for verified authors. All 10 files that reference AuthorIsBlueVerifiedFeature and similar are hydration, logging, caching, or marshalling. However, it does enter as an input feature of the trained model (GizmoduckFeaturesAdapter.scala:12-17). There is no rule-based bonus; the model uses it on its own. verified — repo-wide grep

Re-ranking, diversity, and filters

As of the 2026-10-22 commit (989fb91), X For You has 27 filters: 22 run before scoring and 5 run after candidate selection verified (filters section). From the same commit, a filter that cuts candidates exceeding the Phoenix scoring budget by the same ratio for each source is on by default verified (filters section). As of the Gen4 release, diversity has three layers: author-diversity decay, VMRanker's DPP slate reordering, and conversation dedup verified (diversity section, Phoenix section). Since the 2026-10-14 commit (Gen4+41), VMRanker skips DPP diversity re-ranking by default for topic requests verified (Gen4+41 in the change log). As of the 2026-10-08 commit (Gen4+38), the final arrangement is not in score order: the blender inserts ads, prompts, follow recommendations, and the video carousel (off by default) in turn and pins push-to-home posts at the front verified (final arrangement section).

21 filters (2026-08, Gen4+1) — 18 before scoring + 3 after

As of the 2026-10-22 commit (989fb91), 22 filters run before scoring, in the order below verified — phoenix_candidate_pipeline.rs:411-443. As of the 2026-08-14 commit (Gen4+1), there were 18. The evidence is README.md #filtering and phoenix_candidate_pipeline.rs.

  • IneligibleSubscriptionFilter
  • PreviouslySeenPostsFilter
  • PreviouslySeenPostsBackupFilter
  • PreviouslyServedPostsFilter
  • ViewerMutedKeywordFilter (replaced MutedKeywordFilter in the 2026-08-19 commit (Gen4+4))
  • AuthorSocialgraphFilter
  • Brazil2026ElectionFilter (new in Gen4+1, 2026-08-14)
  • VideoFilter
  • TopicIdsFilter
  • NewUserMinEngagementFilter (new in Gen4, replaced NewUserTopicIdsFilter)
  • InventoryHoldoutFilter (new in Gen4)

As of the 2026-10-17 commit (862a123), the filters that run after selection are 5: VFFilter, AncillaryVFFilter, AncestorVideoFilter, DedupConversationFilter, and VideoCarouselFilter verified — phoenix_candidate_pipeline.rs:518-524.

  • Up to the 2026-08-14 commit (Gen4+1), there were 3, VFFilter, AncillaryVFFilter, and DedupConversationFilter, the same as Gen3 verified.
  • VideoCarouselFilter was added in the 2026-10-08 commit (Gen4+38) and AncestorVideoFilter in the 2026-10-13 commit (Gen4+40) verified — phoenix_candidate_pipeline.rs in 35650fb and e1a0375.

The first 4 of the bullets below are the filters newly introduced in the Gen4 release.

  • OONRetweetReplyFilter filters retweets and replies from accounts the user does not follow, as well as replies without a parent. It is separate from RetweetDeduplicationFilter.
  • OONNsfwSimclustersFilter was introduced together with the SimClusters revival. It filters posts from adult-content accounts that came from the SimClusters source out of the feeds of users who do not follow those accounts.
  • NewUserMinEngagementFilter removes OON posts to be shown to new users that fall below the engagement threshold. It has 6 related params.
    • NewUserMinEngagementThreshold, NewUserMinEngagementFilterMetric, NewUserMinEngagementFilterUseRatio, NewUserMinEngagementFilterMaxAccountAgeSecs, NewUserMinEngagementFilterMaxResurrectionAgeSecs, EnableNewUserMinEngagementFilter
  • InventoryHoldoutFilter holds out inventory at the 3-tier ratios through deterministic user×post hashing, and its params were confirmed in the 2026-09-17 commit (Gen4+23, 42266f3) verified — home-mixer/filters/inventory_holdout_filter.rs
    • The hashing goes through splitmix64-family double mixing and is split into 100-modular buckets.
    • There are 3 params, InventoryHoldoutOriginalsPercent, InventoryHoldoutRepliesPercent, and InventoryHoldoutRetweetsPercent, each clamped with .min(100).
    • The post type is determined by retweeted_tweet_id.is_some() → Retweet and in_reply_to_tweet_id.is_some() → Reply, and anything else is treated as Original. A quoted post is treated as Original.
    • The gate opens when EnableInventoryHoldout=true and at least one of the three values is greater than 0.
    • A retweet is decided against get_original_tweet_id() (the original), so it shares the holdout decision with the original.
  • FavHoldoutFilter was introduced in the 2026-09-17 commit (Gen4+23, 42266f3) and holds out by fav count tier. It is off by default with param EnableFavHoldout=false verified — home-mixer/filters/fav_holdout_filter.rs
    • The tier table is the following 23-tier one:
      • 10K+ fav = 15%, 5K+ = 15%, 3K+ = 15%, 2K+ = 14%, 1.5K+ = 13%, 1K+ = 13%, 750+ = 12%, 500+ = 11%, 300+ = 10%, 200+ = 9%, 150+ = 8%, 100+ = 7%, 75+ = 7%, 50+ = 6%, 30+ = 6%, 20+ = 5%, 15+ = 5%, 10+ = 5%, 7+ = 4%, 5+ = 4%, 3+ = 3%, 2+ = 3%, 1+ = 2%, ≤1 = 0%
    • The holdout decision reuses InventoryHoldoutFilter::is_held_out(post_id, viewer_id, percent) (the same splitmix64 hash), so it is deterministic per viewer.
  • FairShareRankingFilter cuts each served type by the same ratio when candidates exceed the Phoenix scoring budget of 2800. It was introduced in the 2026-10-21 commit (Gen4+46) as off by default, and the switch has been true, so on by default, since the cron mirror of the 2026-10-22 commit (989fb91) verified — params/param.rs:1206-1211
    • The filter itself is home-mixer/filters/fair_share_ranking_filter.rs.
    • Through 2026-10-21, while it was off, the Phoenix request sent only the first 2800 candidates of the candidate list verified. Now, instead of all sources at the back of the list being cut, each source is cut by the same ratio inferred. The evidence is that the budget and the cutoff cap are the same and that a test pins the same ratio per source. Details are in daily 2026-10-22 and daily 2026-10-23.
  • NewUserSoftNsfwFilter was introduced in the 2026-10-22 commit (Gen4+47) as off by default. When on, it removes OON posts carrying a soft NSFW label from the For You feed of users whose account is less than one day old verified — home-mixer/filters/new_user_soft_nsfw_filter.rs
    • The conditions and the label lookup approach are in the new users section of cold start and daily 2026-10-23.

Gen4+1 (2026-08-14, c65aa17) added one new filter.

  • Brazil2026ElectionFilter filters out posts tied to accounts that Brazil's Electoral Court (TSE) acted on in connection with the Brazil 2026 general election, unless the viewer follows the account verified — home-mixer/filters/brazil_2026_election_filter.rs
    • The account list is a FxHashSet<u64> with 665 accounts hardcoded.
    • The fields checked on a candidate are author_id, retweeted_user_id, quoted_user_id, and ancestor_users, and if any one of them is in the set, the candidate is targeted.
    • In the pipeline it sits right after AuthorSocialgraphFilter and right before VideoFilter. Another evidence location is phoenix_candidate_pipeline.rs:356-368.
    • The source materials are the Brazilian Electoral Court open dataset and X's announcement (@XBR, 2026-08-14). The README states: "in accordance with Brazilian electoral law, For You now runs Brazil2026ElectionFilter, which removes posts from accounts reported to Brazil's Electoral Court for the 2026 election, unless the viewer explicitly follows the account."
    • In the 2026-10-14 commit 17c96bf (Gen4+41), the list was cut to 25 accounts tied to candidates in the October 25 runoff (the relevant diff range went from 5,654 lines to 63 lines) verified. It cites TSE official letter numbers in comments as evidence verified — brazil_2026_election_filter.rs:17-74
    • The code leaves @username as a comment next to each account ID ("obfuscated ID + username alongside for transparency"). Examples are 40053694 // @FlavioBolsonaro, 21069302 // @marcelvanhattem, and 48298703 // @eduardopaes.
    • The follow exception is based on the user's personal following graph, so it is symmetric regardless of political spectrum. The decision formula is is_excluded_author(user_id, followed_user_ids) = LIST.contains(user_id) && !followed_user_ids.contains(user_id).
    • The list size is the code constant 665. The code has this unusual comment: "OmarAzizSenador deleted his account at the time this code was written."
    • This filter is the first case in which a jurisdiction filter is observed directly in code. Until now, responses to regulation such as DSA, GDPR, and NetzDG were seen mostly only in regulatory filings (transparency reports). If this code-release practice continues, similar filters can be confirmed in code for each country's election cycle.

The notable points among the filters are as follows:

  • AuthorSocialgraphFilter checks 6 conditions verified — filters/author_socialgraph_filter.rs:8-61
    • mute, block, author blocks me, quoted author blocks me, I block the quoted author, I block the retweet's original author
  • VFFilter is still fail-closed, but since Gen4+18 (2026-09-09, 75d93d9) the basis of the decision moved from matching FilteredReason variants to an explicit Action enum verified — home-mixer/filters/vf_filter.rs:16-21
    • should_drop_action classifies Drop(_), Tombstone, and NotEvaluated as drop, and Allow, Interstitial, Avoid, and Downrank as keep.
    • The upstream StratoVfClient converts non-SafetyResult reasons (mute, block, null-cast, exclusive, etc.) to Drop at the client layer, and converts NotEvaluated inside a SafetyResult to Allow verified — visibility-filtering-client/vf_client.rs:178-187. So on this path, a missing verdict is not dropped.
    • Conversely, the Rust VF client fills posts missing from the response with NotEvaluated, and VFFilter drops them verified — vf_client.rs:360-378. Fail-closed applies to missing results on this path.
    • As of the 2026-10-17 commit (862a123), the two handlings and should_drop_action are the same verified — vf_client.rs, vf_filter.rs.
  • In-network and OON get different safety levels (TimelineHome vs TimelineHomeRecommendations). Ancestor posts and quoted posts always get the stricter one verified — vf_candidate_hydrator.rs:62-67, 76-90
  • TopicIdsFilter is a 572-line file containing about 90 topic constants and a hand-built supertopic hierarchy. This part sits squarely against "remove all handcrafted features". verified — filters/topic_ids_filter.rs:109-515
  • PreviouslySeenPostsBackupFilter is permanently a no-op. The ImpressedPostsQueryHydrator that would fill its input is only constructed, bound to _, and not registered in the pipeline. It runs on every request but filters nothing verified — phoenix_candidate_pipeline.rs:234-236

Gen4+4 (2026-08-19, aad7179) added a mute keyword filter dedicated to the Following pipeline and the quoted-post text hydrator that supports it verified — home-mixer/filters/following_viewer_muted_keyword_filter.rs (65 new lines), home-mixer/candidate_hydrators/quoted_post_text_hydrator.rs (106 new lines). This commit continues the flow in which the Following pipeline branched to VFFollowingCandidateHydrator in the 2026-08-18 commit (Gen4+3).

  • FollowingViewerMutedKeywordFilter was split into a separate file from the existing MutedKeywordFilter (for the For You pipeline).
    • It tokenizes muted_keywords with TweetTokenizer and builds the matcher with MatchTweetGroup.
    • It filters a candidate if any one of three text sources matches: the candidate's tweet_text, quoted_tweet_text, or ancestor_texts.values().
    • This matching is CPU-bound work wrapped in tokio::task::block_in_place.
    • A peculiarity is the possibility that the existing For You filter looked only at tweet_text. The evidence is that the 2026-08-18 commit (Gen4+3) had no quoted-text wiring.
    • The mute targets have now widened to quoted posts and ancestors (reply ancestors). This extension narrows the route of bypassing a mute through quotes or replies.
  • QuotedPostTextHydrator is the hydrator that prepares this filter's input. For the filter to match quoted text, this field must be filled first.
    • For candidates with quoted_tweet_id, it does a bulk lookup with TESClient.get_tweet_core_datas and then fills the quoted_tweet_text field.
    • It removes duplicates with a HashSet and calls gRPC in batches.
  • Why it matters: Now For You and Following use different components in the filter and hydrator stack. Paired with the VF hydrator branch in the 2026-08-18 commit (Gen4+3), the Following pipeline is being rebuilt as a parallel structure rather than a subset of the For You pipeline inferred

Gen4+5 (2026-08-20, d0cef2f) added an "AI trend" feedback context channel to For You.

A second context channel opened alongside the existing topic feedback context (a context label for inferring a user's topics of interest) verified — home-mixer/candidate_hydrators/ai_trend_feedback_context_hydrator.rs (157 new lines). In the pipeline it is wired in right after TopicFeedbackContextHydrator, side by side with it verified — home-mixer/candidate_pipeline/phoenix_candidate_pipeline.rs:424-428. Another evidence location is home-mixer/util/urt/post_marshaller.rs:72-110.

  • The gate is 3-part. The switch EnableAiTrendFeedbackContext=false is off by default, and the other two conditions are !query.is_topic_request() and !query.in_network_only. That is, it does not overlap with topic surfaces or Following surfaces and targets only For You OON candidates.
  • Candidates are filtered by a 4-part standalone original post condition. In other words, the AI trend label is attached only to original posts, not to replies, retweets, posts with conversation ancestors, or targets that a followed account replied to.
    • The condition expression is in_reply_to_tweet_id.is_none() && retweeted_tweet_id.is_none() && ancestors.is_empty() && following_replied_user_ids.is_empty().
  • At most 2 AI trend labels are attached per page, and each trend is attached to only one candidate. This limit is a suppression device to avoid flooding the same label across multiple candidates of the same trend.
    • The selection approach is the top-2 trends and one random candidate per trend.
    • The trend_ids of the candidates are looked up with Strato batch_get_tweet_ai_trend, and the top 2 trends are picked from the frequency histogram (TOP_TREND_COUNT = 2). On a tie, the smaller trend_id takes priority.
    • For each trend, one candidate labeled with that trend is picked at random, and the display name is looked up with Strato batch_get_ai_trend_name.
  • At render time, topic feedback takes priority. In post_marshaller, topic wins if topic feedback exists, and AI trend enters as a fallback only when it does not.
    • Both go out in URT as type ContextType::TOPIC.
    • AI trend fills landing_url = "https://x.com/i/trending/{trend_id}" and TopicFeedbackContext.topic_id is None.
    • That is, tapping the chip goes to the trending surface rather than the topic feedback page.
  • Why it matters: This channel widens the context and signal sources upstream of ranking. The user's reaction of tapping, dismissing, or ignoring this chip becomes a label source for "does this user care about this AI trend".
  • Undisclosed: The following are not public:
    • The definition of AI trend (tweet clustering with Grok? human curation?)
    • The location of the batch_get_tweet_ai_trend upstream pipeline
    • Whether EnableAiTrendFeedbackContext is actually deployed

Diversity

X For You has three layers of diversity mechanisms.

  1. Author-diversity decay was applied inside the ranking scorer at the Gen4 release; since the 2026-09-24 commit (Gen4+28), the vm-ranker service computes it with the shared crate xai-value-model verified (final score calculation order in the Phoenix section).
  2. VMRanker DPP optimizes candidates as a set, and the service itself has been in vm-ranker/ since the Gen4 release verified (VMRanker paragraph in the Phoenix section).
    • Gen4+20 (6bb4594, 2026-09-12) added an optional seed_tweet_id argument.
    • If an embedding exists for this id, the seed is pinned to the first slot of the greedy DPP and filtered out of the final result, so it does not consume the top_k budget while only candidates similar to the seed receive a penalty.
    • In other words, the diversity axis can now extend from within the set to relative to a reference tweet.
    • Which production surfaces carry this field is not yet public.
  3. Conversation dedup keeps only the top-scoring one per thread verified — filters/dedup_conversation_filter.rs:6-48
    • The id that groups a conversation is conversation_id = min(ancestors) or the tweet itself.

The feed goes out without DPP even if the VMRanker call fails. Since the 2026-09-24 commit (Gen4+28), if gRPC fails it emits the local weighted-sum score and counts the failure with the VMRanker.local_score_fallback metric verified — vm_ranker.rs:107-113.

  • Before that (Gen3 to Gen4+27), it returned Err for every candidate, and the pipeline's update_all skipped the Err without logging. As a result, a score-ordered feed lacking DPP diversity went out with no indication verified — candidate-pipeline/scorer.rs (default update_all implementation), vm_ranker.rs:44-66

X made the mechanism that measures how many new topics the feed shows the viewer off by default. In the 2026-10-20 commit (Gen4+45), a path was added that counts the first and second SID levels of posts the viewer recently engaged with as topics and records, as a metric, the share of response posts whose topic is not in that history verified — side_effects/serendipity_stats_side_effect.rs.

  • History topic computation is off because the switch HistoryTopicsEnabled is false by default; when it is on, the metric is measured against a 28-day history verified — params/param.rs:508-529.
  • A switch that sends the same history topics in the VMRanker request was also added, off by default verified — same file. How VMRanker uses this value is not in the public code verified.
  • Since the 2026-10-21 commit (Gen4+46), the same measurement also measures the share of posts in languages the viewer does not use verified — side_effects/serendipity_stats_side_effect.rs. The viewer's languages are those that make up at least 5% of the engagement history, plus the app language. Because the history topics switch is false by default, this measurement is also off verified.
  • Only the metric exists, and there is no code that uses it for re-ranking verified. Given that the measurement was added first, we infer this is preparation to test history-based topic exploration as a diversity goal inferred. Details are in daily 2026-10-21 and daily 2026-10-22.

The 2025 Scala generation worked differently from today. MMR gave a reward for distance and the SimClusters category penalty gave a penalty for the same thing, and the two sat side by side, param-gated. There were six dedup filters. A comparison of the four approaches (decay, MMR, DPP, dedup) and the full per-generation list are in feed-diversity.md.

The final placement is not score order

The blender that handles final placement intentionally disables the framework's sorting verified. The evidence is home-mixer/selectors/blender_selector.rs:25-114. In this file's BlenderSelector, score() returns the constant 0.0 verified. The blender then runs the following stages.

  • Inserts prompts at positions 0..n verified — same file
  • Inserts Who-to-Follow (WTF) at designated positions verified — same file
  • Pins the push-to-home post always at position 0 verified — same file
  • Runs the ads blender. As of the 2026-10-17 commit (862a123), AdsBlenderType picks one of partition_organic_low_risk, safe_gap, multi_risk, and time_gap, and the default has been multi_risk since the 2026-09-01 commit (Gen4+13) verified — blender_selector.rs:55-72, params/param.rs:817
  • Since the 2026-10-08 commit (Gen4+38), inserts the video carousel module, off by default, at the VideoCarouselPosition (default 6th) slot. The execution order is ads blending → prompt → WTF → carousel → push-to-home pinning → frame → survey verified — home-mixer/selectors/blender_selector.rs:72-85, 137-153
