Cold start

Cold start is the question of how recommendations treat users, authors, and posts that have not yet accumulated history or impressions. As of the Gen4 release, the X For You code had mechanisms for new users and new authors, but none for individual new posts verified (sections New users, new-author boost, and New items). Since the 2026-09-30 commit (Gen4+32), the Phoenix retrieval cold slice, which collects new posts with few impressions and likes separately, has been on, and the cold-start slot selector picks only posts with fewer than 200 home impressions verified (section New items). The new-author boost on in-network posts of new authors has been 0.015 in the home-mixer mirror and 0.02 in the VM-Ranker mirror since the 2026-10-07 commit (Gen4+37) verified (change log Gen4+37); Thompson sampling in the cold-start slot selector and the cold-start slice of Phoenix retrieval came in off by default and were turned on together in the commit that tuned the home-mixer cold-start parameters to production values verified.

New users (account level)

New users whose history length is below a threshold are sent to a separate model fleet for both ranking and retrieval verified. The evidence is phoenix_scorer.rs:29-43 and phoenix_source.rs:25-39. The threshold is Phoenix*NewUserHistoryThreshold, and the fleet these users go to is Phoenix*NewUserInferenceClusterId.

  • In the 2026-09-18 commit (Gen4+25), the Phoenix retrieval cold-start slice was wired in as first-class verified — home-mixer/sources/phoenix_source.rs.
    • This slice is distinguished by the dataset_type axis carried in the Phoenix retrieval response.
    • Candidates tagged HOME_COLD_DATASET_TYPE=13 have their served_type mapped to ForYouPhoenixRetrievalCold.
    • record_phoenix_retrieval_cold_stats emits the PhoenixRetrievalColdTweets.* stat block.
    • A separate cap param for this slice, PhoenixColdStartMaxResults, was introduced at 0 (off by default).
    • Unlike the routing above, which splits model fleets by the user's history threshold, this slice splits the candidate set returned by the same Phoenix retrieval RPC using the dataset_type tag.
    • When introduced, it was off by default, so it had no production share.
    • This cap was later turned on at 200 in the commit that tuned the home-mixer cold-start parameters to production values verified — params/param.rs:16.
  • As of the Gen4 release, the new-user routing threshold is NewUserAgeThresholdSecs = 0 verified. Because it is 0 seconds, we infer the new-user path is mirrored as effectively disabled inferred.
    • This param was dropped from the home-mixer param.rs in the 2026-09-24 commit (Gen4+28), and it is also 0 in vm-ranker/params.rs as of the 2026-10-17 commit (862a123) verified.
  • NewUserMinEngagementFilter, the OON engagement-threshold filter new in Gen4, removes OON posts that fall short of the engagement threshold.
  • In the 2026-10-22 commit (Gen4+47), a filter that removes OON posts carrying a soft NSFW (non-explicit sexual content) label for new users was introduced, off by default verified — params/param.rs:804-815.
    • It targets non-topic For You requests from viewers whose account age is under 86,400 seconds (1 day). Followed accounts and the viewer's own posts are not even looked up for labels.
    • If the label lookup fails or the label is unknown, the post is kept (fail-open). Details are in daily 2026-10-23.
  • NEW_USER_OON_WEIGHT_FACTOR, NewUserTopicIdsFilter, and EnableNewUserTopicRetrieval, which existed in Gen3, are not in the Gen4 param.rs. A deep dive is needed.

New authors (account level)

New authors are identified by impression count, and their in-network posts get the new-author boost verified (new-author boost section of ranking). The boost and threshold params were documented in Gen4, and the full set of boost params is in the table in that section.

  • The new-author boost has been 0.015 in the home-mixer mirror and 0.02 in the VM-Ranker mirror since the 2026-10-07 commit (Gen4+37). It applies only to in-network posts.
    • The value documented in Gen4 is PostUnexploredWeight = 0.02.
  • The Gen4 README describes authors whose impressions are below a threshold as "new authors", and the threshold param at that time was ColdStartImpressionThreshold = 1000. The code applies this threshold to the home impression count of the candidate post, not to the author verified (new-author boost section).
    • This threshold was later changed to 200 in the commit that tuned the home-mixer cold-start parameters to production values verified.

Cold-start slot selector

The cold-start slot selector chooses "which candidate fills a slot" within the set of cold-start target candidates. In the 2026-08-14 commit (Gen4+1), this selection approach was split into two branches, greedy max-score and Beta-reward Thompson sampling verified — home-mixer/scorers/author_cold_start.rs:151-190. Thompson sampling was off by default at first, and it has been on by default since the commit that tuned the home-mixer cold-start parameters to production values verified.

The param definitions and the defaults as of Gen4+1 are in param.rs verified — home-mixer/params/param.rs:687-724.

param default as of meaning
EnableColdStartThompsonSampling true commit that tuned the home-mixer cold-start parameters to production values Switch that decides whether to pick slots with Thompson sampling instead of greedy
ColdStartBetaAlpha0 0.75 2026-08-14 commit (Gen4+1) α of the prior Beta(α₀, β₀). Prior observations of likes
ColdStartBetaBeta0 49.25 2026-08-14 commit (Gen4+1) β₀. Prior observations of non-likes. The sum of the two values, 50, is the "prior effective sample size"
ColdStartTsTopK 5 2026-08-14 commit (Gen4+1) Pick the top K by Beta sampling, then tie-break by the actual score
ColdStartImpressionScale 1.0 2026-08-14 commit (Gen4+1) view_count scale. When sampling, n = scale × view_count
ColdStartTrackedIds "" 2026-08-14 commit (Gen4+1) Comma-separated list of account/post IDs. Targets for serving-stats instrumentation

EnableColdStartThompsonSampling is a switch added for A/B. Its default in the 2026-08-14 commit (Gen4+1) is false, and the default is still greedy (current behavior unchanged). That it is off by default matters. At this release point (2026-08-14), the cold start shown to real users is still max-score greedy, and for Thompson only the A/B infrastructure is wired up.

  • Thompson sampling draws one sample per candidate from the posterior, picks the top K, and then picks the candidate with the highest original score among them.
    • For each cold-start candidate i, set n_i = scale × view_count_i and x_i = min(fav_count_i, n_i).
    • The posterior is Beta(α₀ + x_i, β₀ + max(n_i − x_i, 0)), and one sample is drawn from it.
    • In other words, it does Bayesian exploration (uncertainty about which candidate will be good), but the final choice is decided by tie-break on the original score.
  • α₀=0.75, β₀=49.25 set a prior of "roughly 0.75 likes per 50 impressions". The values are meant to let new authors whose measured like rate is higher than this be picked generously.
  • As of the 2026-08-14 commit (Gen4+1), the instrumentation hook record_tracked_ids is an individual observation hook that lets A/B manually watch specific accounts.
    • This hook counts how many times a tweet_id/author_id registered in ColdStartTrackedIds appeared from which source of the cold-start pipeline.
    • The counter is home_mixer.cold_start_tracked_ids_total{id, source}.
  • In the 2026-08-18 commit (Gen4+3), the aggregation key of this instrumentation was simplified verified — home-mixer/scorers/author_cold_start.rs:92-108.
    • The changed function is count_tracked_ids.
    • Previously, tweet_id and author_id were aggregated as separate entries.
    • Afterward, a candidate whose tweet_id or author_id is in the tracked list is counted under its single tweet_id. The separate author_id entry is gone.
    • The tracked-list filter remains, so if the list is empty nothing is counted. The function in the 2026-10-17 commit (862a123) is the same verified — author_cold_start.rs:151-185.
  • In the 2026-09-04 commit (Gen4+16), the caller of record_tracked_ids and the param wiring were confirmed verified — home-mixer/scorers/author_cold_start.rs. This tracked ID observation hook is an always-on observation channel independent of A/B.
    • ColdStartParams::read(query) reads all params at once and puts them in params.tracked_ids.
    • record_tracked_ids(candidates, &params.tracked_ids) is always called regardless of EnableViewerColdStart gating.
  • The same 2026-09-04 commit (Gen4+16) pinned the impression symmetry of the codivert experiment with a regression test verified — same file.
    • A pair of YAML rules was added so that the two arms of the new experiment moe_codivert_viewer split symmetrically as enable_viewer_cold_start_boost=true/false.
    • The experiment params are PhoenixMoeCodivertViewerIsControl and PhoenixMoeCodivertViewerIsTreatment.
    • apply() changed its execution order to call viewer_arm(query) and author_corpus(...) before the enabled gating.
    • Each of the two arms leaves exactly 3 moe_codivert_viewer bucket impressions and 2 moe_exp bucket impressions, which target authors. The tests both_arms_log_the_same_codivert_impressions and both_viewer_arms_log_the_same_author_impressions pin this.
    • Triggered-analysis compares only users who entered the pipeline, while intent-to-treat compares all assigned users. A methodology that guards against the mismatch between the two definitions with a regression test came in as code.
  • In the same 2026-09-04 commit (Gen4+16), the candidate filter of the Treatment arm was narrowed to apply only to Phoenix MoE candidates verified — same file.
    • The condition && is_phoenix_moe(c) was added to cold_start_corpus_eligible(Treatment).
    • As of this commit, the cold-start candidates of a Treatment viewer were only those that are posts by treatment corpus authors and have served_type == ForYouPhoenixRetrievalMoe.
    • The test name also changed to treatment_viewer_cold_starts_treatment_moe_only.
    • Cold start and Phoenix MoE are bundled into one codivert experiment and isolated so that the two effects are not confounded.
    • This MoE condition was removed from the Treatment branch in the 2026-09-17 commit (Gen4+23), and cold_start_corpus_eligible in the 2026-10-17 commit (862a123) has no MoE condition verified — author_cold_start.rs in 42266f3 and 862a123.
  • In the same 2026-09-04 commit (Gen4+16), engagement counts hydration was separated from cold-start gating verified — home-mixer/candidate_hydrators/engagement_counts_hydrator.rs.
    • enable() drops the dependency on EnableViewerColdStart and decides whether to turn on solely by EnableEngagementCountsHydration || is_shadow_traffic.
    • It also removed the !query.has_cached_posts gating of enable(). The has_cached_posts branch on the side that decides per candidate whether to look up remained until the 2026-10-01 commit (Gen4+33) and was removed in the 2026-10-02 commit (Gen4+34) verified — engagement_counts_hydrator.rs:123, same file at 76843a5.
    • The tight coupling of the initial Gen4+1 (2026-08-14) wiring, where cold-start Thompson sampling depended on view_count_on_home and fav_count, is loosened.

New items (post level)

As of the Gen4 release, there was no separate mechanism that boosts a new post itself regardless of its author verified. As of the 2026-10-17 commit (862a123), two mechanisms work on post-level conditions.

  • In the 2026-09-24 commit (Gen4+28), HOME_COLD (13) and HOME_HOT (14) datasets were added to the Phoenix retrieval training data. HOME_COLD keeps only recent posts with fewer than 500 views and fewer than 8 likes verified — retrieval_dataset.py:280-281, cold_pool_filter.py:26-46.
    • The home-mixer has separated retrieval candidates carrying this tag (13) as a cold slice since the 2026-09-18 commit (Gen4+25), and has accepted up to 200 since the 2026-09-30 commit (Gen4+32) verified (current candidate generation).
  • The cold-start slot selector picks one of the original posts whose author has 50,000 followers or fewer, that was posted within the last 2 hours, and that has fewer than 200 home impressions, and raises its ranking verified — author_cold_start.rs:296-309, params/param.rs:507-531.
    • This selector has used the candidate post's impression count as a condition since the Gen4 release, and the threshold then was 1000 (new-author boost section).

The hash embedding of a new post is the value the continually trained table currently holds, and for an ID seen for the first time it is the average of other posts mixed in by hash collisions inferred.

The 2025 Scala code had SimclusterColdPostsCandidateSource.scala. Because SimClusters was revived in Gen4, whether this source is alive in Gen4 simclusters/ needs a deep dive (open questions).

Safety / visibility-filtering / labeling pipeline (released in full in Gen4)

The Gen4 release (2026-08-13) published the whole path by which X creates safety labels and uses them to decide post visibility. According to the Gen4 README, this path has four stages: content understanding, labeling rules, storage, and visibility filtering (VF) verified (4-stage Labeling Path). As of the 2026-10-15 commit, VF uses five SafetyLevels verified (2026-10-15 commit in the change log).

Through Gen3, VFFilter and AncillaryVFFilter were applied fail-closed in home-mixer/. However, who attaches the labels those filters consult, and when and how, was a complete black box. The Gen4 release added 15 new visibility-filtering and labeling sub-repos verified (released source Gen4).

Since the 2026-10-22 commit (989fb91), a reaction post (a post made in reaction to another post; the test file is named reaction_video) inherits the safety label of the original post verified — rules/tweet_rules.rs.

  • If the original has an adult content or violence label, the reaction post is blurred (hidden behind a warning screen), and if the original author's account is private, the reaction post is removed verified — same file.
  • This rule was added only to TimelineHomeHydration among the SafetyLevels, and the golden corpus test pins that it is still allowed as is in TimelineHome verified — rules/golden_corpus/reaction_video.rs.
  • If the original label lookup fails, the reaction post is shown without being hidden. A code comment states that this matches the behavior of Tweetypie verified. Details are in daily 2026-10-23.

4-stage Labeling Path verified — README.md #labeling-path

Stages 1–3 create and store labels, and stage 4 makes decisions with those labels on the request path verified.

Content Understanding → Labeling Rules → Storage → Visibility Filtering

Stage 1 (Content Understanding) is a nearline stage that runs outside the request path. Stage 1 of the README diagram lists six: grox, media-model-proxy, clip, agatha, bdsm, and user-cred-v2 verified. The related sub-repos are in the table below.

Sub-repo Target Role
grox/ Posts, media Grok-based nearline classifier. Also partially released in Gen3
media-model-proxy/ Images, video Serving proxy for NSFW, violence/gore, hate symbols, topics, and known-media matching
clip/ Images, text CLIP embedding model training (input to media classifiers)
adult-content/ Adult media Classifier training and calibration
pnsfwmedia/ Adult media Discriminator combining CLIP embeddings and account scores
agatha/ Accounts Offline batch. Labels based on how other accounts reacted to this account's posts (favorite ratio against blocks and reports), and spam-suspension and adult labels
bdsm/ Accounts Extracts inauthentic/abusive signals from time-series behavior sequences (Rust, proto, training, tests subdirectories)
user-cred-v2/ Accounts Account trust score computed with PageRank over follow and engagement edges

Stage 2 (Labeling Rules) turns events and scores into labels verified.

  • scarecrow/ is a rule runner that runs in response to events, and it embeds botmaker/ as the rule engine verified.
  • botmaker/ is the rule DSL, compiler, and runtime verified.
  • botmaker-rules/ holds the actual rules that scarecrow loads verified. According to the README, some were not released to prevent gaming verified.
  • abuse-enforcement-service/ takes account actions (labeling, challenge, suspension) based on model scores verified.
  • safety-label-user-agg/ aggregates labels of posts owned by an account to the account level verified.

In stage 3 (Storage), labels are written to storage and read on the request path.

Stage 4 (Visibility Filtering) runs on the request path verified — visibility-filtering/rules/registry.rs. The client library is in visibility-filtering-client/ verified.

As of the 2026-10-15 commit (92f0918), there are five SafetyLevels, and the number of rule constant entries per level is as follows verified — visibility-filtering/rules/levels.rs.

SafetyLevel Rule constant entries (as of the 2026-10-15 commit)
FILTER_ALL 1
TIMELINE_HOME 39
TIMELINE_HOME_RECOMMENDATIONS 65
TIMELINE_HOME_HYDRATION 87
IMMERSIVE_EXPANDED_RECOMMENDATIONS 47

Since the 2026-09-22 commit (Gen4+26), the verdict has been a tree split into withhold and display, rather than the three-way Allow/Interstitial/Drop verified — visibility-filtering/models/verdict.rs (Gen4+26 row of the commit summary table).

  • The withhold side is Drop and Tombstone.
  • The display side has media and engagement slots, and a notice slot was added in the 2026-10-06 commit (Gen4+36) verified — verdict.rs (Gen4+36 in the change log).
  • Before that, the 2026-09-09 commit (Gen4+18) changed the verdict axis from FilteredReason to a flat Action enum (Gen4+18 in the change log).

At the Gen4 release (2026-08-13), there were three SafetyLevel policies verified — Gen4 registry.rs.

  • FilterAll drops everything verified.
  • TimelineHome is the policy for following targets and consists of 28 base rules verified.
    • The 28 rules of base_home_rules() consist of 5 account-state rules, 3 viewer-relation rules, 8 tweet-label rules, 4 tweet-state rules, 3 NSFW viewer-gating rules, 1 excluded-tweet rule, and 4 NSFW interstitial rules verified.
  • TimelineHomeRecommendations is the policy for recommendation targets and consists of 54 rules, the 28 base rules plus 26 OON-only rules verified.
    • The 26 OON-only rules consist of 2 DMCA/geo-restricted media rules, 4 NSFW account rules, 9 rules for tweets labeled NSFW/violence/DoNotAmplify/spam, and 11 NSFW/spam/impersonation/deactivated/adult user-label rules verified.

In the Gen4 registry.rs, evaluation ends at the first drop verdict (short-circuit) verified. The OON-only rule group can only drop and issues no interstitial or allow verdict verified. The verdicts are three: Allow, Interstitial(reason), and Drop(FilteredReason) verified. Interstitials are handed off to UI handling, and this repo has no code that draws interstitials verified.

Verifying canon caveat list #1 and #2 (partial)

Both items were partially verified, and each leaves one question that needs a deep dive.

  • VFFilter fail-closed behavior: The Gen3 observation that VFFilter unconditionally drops every FilteredReason variant that has no verdict is still valid. How the visibility-filtering/ sub-repo handles a return without a verdict (error, timeout) needs a deep dive.
  • Different safety levels for in-network and OON: The Gen4 Policies struct exposes the three levels FilterAll, TimelineHome and TimelineHomeRecommendations as they were. Whether the Gen3 rule of applying the stricter level to ancestor and quote posts (vf_candidate_hydrator.rs) still holds in Gen4 needs a deep dive.

Under the Hood transparency tool — introduced alongside Gen4 verified

Under the Hood is a transparency tool where users look up the visibility-impacting labels attached to their own account and posts verified. A daily batch collects the labels, and the serving layer aggregates them verified. X stated that the purpose is to let users audit "why was my post treated this way" by checking against the code in this repo verified.

  • Address: x.com/i/under_the_hood
  • Sub-repo: under-the-hood/

Feedback signals

The X recommendation code uses positive actions such as like, reply and repost and negative actions such as not interested, block, mute and report as feedback signals, and production also counts not dwelling on a post as a negative signal verified. Phoenix's history encoding feeds an action not taken as −1 rather than 0, and masks history entries that have no action at all verified. Already-seen posts are handled in six layers, and the user-side features include demographics such as age and inferred gender verified. In the commit that introduced the vertical video carousel module as off by default, the Phoenix feature that feeds history dwell time as a bucket embedding became on by default verified (change log).

  • Positive signals are actions such as like, reply, repost, quote, click and dwell verified — phoenix/runners.py:233-253
    • The full list is favorite, reply, repost, quote, click, profile_click, photo_expand, video quality view, share (including DM and link copy), dwell, dwell_time and follow_author.
  • Negative signals are not interested, block author, mute author and report, and production counts even not_dwelled (did not dwell) as a negative signal verified — ranking_scorer.rs:83
    • The identifiers of the four actions are not_interested, block_author, mute_author and report.
  • In the history encoding, no action is −1, not 0 verified — phoenix/recsys_model.py:404-432
    • The formula is actions_signed = 2*actions - 1.
    • That is, "did not like this post" enters as an explicit negative signal.
    • However, a history entry with no action at all is masked as a whole entry verified — same file.
  • Already-seen posts are handled in six layers verified — each file in query_hydrators/ and side_effects/
    • The six layers are the seen_ids sent by the client, the impression bloom filter, the server-side served history (last N minutes/M items), the Redis candidate cache, the Phoenix request cache and the URT cursor.
  • Impressions reported by the client are sent back out to Kafka verified — side_effects/publish_seen_ids_to_kafka_side_effect.rs
  • User-side features include demographics such as age, inferred gender and IP location verified — home-mixer/models/query.rs:24-95
    • The fields included are user_age_in_years, user_inferred_gender, ip_location and subscription_level.
    • The topic and starter pack fields are followed_grok_topics[32], inferred_grok_topics[32] and followed_starter_packs[20].
    • user_inferred_gender has a dedicated GenderPredictionGrpcClient.
    • The hydrator-side evidence is phoenix_candidate_pipeline.rs:210-231.

Ads

In the public code, X For You inserts ads between organic posts and decides ad slots by looking at the brand safety grade of the posts next to an ad verified. The default ads blender has been the multi-risk blender since the Gen4+13 commit (2026-09-01, 7ba7768) verified (Gen4+13 in the change log). This blender places no ad next to a HighRisk post, places next to a MediumRisk post only ads whose advertiser allows that context, and gives such ads the MediumRisk slots first verified (Gen4+10 in the change log). As of the 2026-10-15 commit, the V2 verdict switch for the brand safety verdict and the fallback switch that substitutes the author-level label when there is no post-level Grok safety label are both on by default verified (2026-10-15 commit in the change log).

Ads blending and brand safety verdict

The public code contains the entire ads blending. This is the unexpected part of this release.

  • At least 5 organic posts are required before ads can be attached verified — home-mixer/ads/util.rs:10
  • The default ad spacing is {requested: 3, min: 2}, and the minimum requested spacing is 3 verified — ads/util.rs:12-17
  • Ads are inserted only up to half of the "safety gap" verified — ads/partition_organic_blender.rs:35
    • The formula is max_from_safe = safe_count / 2.
  • If the last item is an ad, it is trimmed verified — ads/util.rs:164-198
  • Brand safety is an adjacency verdict. The partition_organic_low_risk blender, the default until the 2026-09-01 commit (Gen4+13), attaches no ad next to MediumRisk or HighRisk posts (has_avoid() treats both tiers as avoid). The multi_risk blender, the default since Gen4+13, first tries to place a BSR-high ad between two MediumRisk posts and, if it fails the overlap check, moves it to a Safe slot verified — multi_risk_blender.rs:68-179. The verdict is made from a hand-written rule cascade plus whether Grok scored the post and whether PTOS reviewed it verified — home-mixer/models/brand_safety.rs:5-13, 15-22, 45-48
    • The 2026-08-24 commit (Gen4+7, d011592) introduced the BrandSafetyVerdict::HighRisk = 4 tier verified — home-mixer/models/brand_safety.rs
      • Five labels previously in medium and the new SOFT_NSFW were promoted to HIGH_RISK_LABELS. v1 and v2 are symmetric.
        • The five are NSFW_HIGH_PRECISION, NSFW_HIGH_RECALL, GORE_AND_VIOLENCE_HIGH_PRECISION, PDNA and EGREGIOUS_NSFW.
      • The NSFW ancestor-inheritance escalation in ads_brand_safety_vf_hydrator.rs changed from MediumRisk to HighRisk.
      • scored_posts_server.rs added the proto HM enum mapping for five V2 labels (downstream exposure begins).
        • The five are GROK_SFA_V2, GROK_NSFA_LIMITED_V2, GROK_NSFA_V2, GROK_NSFA_EXPANDED_V2 and PTOS_REVIEWED.
  • If the quote post lookup fails, the verdict is pessimistically demoted to MediumRisk verified — ads/../ads_brand_safety_hydrator.rs:144-145
  • Gen4+2 (2026-08-17, b089ce6) wired in the V2 verdict function side by side, and Gen4+3 (2026-08-18, 11a71f8) redesigned its semantics a day later.
  • The Gen4+2 original (b089ce6, 2026-08-17) added two label lists for V2, a migration helper and a verification test verified — home-mixer/models/brand_safety.rs
    • MEDIUM_RISK_LABELS_V2 has 16 entries. Compared with V1, GROK_NSFA was renamed GROK_NSFA_V2, GROK_NSFA_EXPANDED_V2 was introduced, and the list includes NSFA_HIGH_PRECISION.
    • LOW_RISK_LABELS_V2 has 3 entries. Compared with V1, GROK_NSFA_LIMITED was renamed GROK_NSFA_LIMITED_V2, and the list includes NSFA_LIMITED_INVENTORY.
    • The migration helper strip_v1_grok_written removes from the input label set, before the V2 verdict, any label that meets both conditions.
      • The first condition is that the label is NSFA_HIGH_PRECISION or NSFA_LIMITED_INVENTORY.
      • The second condition is that the label's botmaker rule id is one of the seven in PROMPT_OWNED_RULES = [1400, 1410, 1420, 1500, 1510, 1610, 1700].
      • That is, the V2 logic ignores labels dual-written by the V1 prompt and decides from pure V2 labels only.
    • The verification test v2_mirrors_v1_across_tier_matrix asserts that the V1 and V2 verdicts must match exactly across 6 label combinations × two tweet_id points in time (before/after PTOS_CUTOFF).
  • The Gen4+3 redesign (11a71f8, 2026-08-18) deleted this helper and added a gate that decides with V2 only when at least one V2-written label is present and otherwise falls back to V1 verified — home-mixer/models/brand_safety.rs
    • strip_v1_grok_written was deleted entirely (even the Cow import was removed). That is, the seven-rule-id PROMPT_OWNED_RULES logic that the canon update folded in yesterday was discarded within a day.
    • A new constant V2_WRITTEN_LABELS was added instead. It has 4 entries: GROK_SFA_V2, GROK_NSFA_V2, GROK_NSFA_LIMITED_V2 and GROK_NSFA_EXPANDED_V2.
    • The new gate checks at the start of compute_verdict_v2 whether any of V2_WRITTEN_LABELS is in the label set. If none is, it falls back to compute_verdict(v1), and if one is, it decides from the pure V2 label set.
    • NSFA_HIGH_PRECISION was removed from MEDIUM_RISK_LABELS_V2, and NSFA_LIMITED_INVENTORY from LOW_RISK_LABELS_V2. That is, once V2 gives a verdict, the V1 heuristic labels are ignored.
    • The new test v2_defers_to_v1_when_v2_has_not_ruled explicitly asserts the decisive case.
      • In particular, for the label set NSFA_HIGH_PRECISION + GROK_NSFA + GROK_SFA_V2, the V1 verdict is MediumRisk and the V2 verdict is Safe.
      • That is, once V2 sends a verdict signal (GROK_SFA_V2 alone), the V2 decision governs and V1's traditional heuristics are ignored entirely.
    • Interpretation: The dual-write migration strategy moved from "filter specific rule ids when V2 decides" to "use the V2 decision if V2 has ruled, otherwise fall back to V1." The latter is much cleaner dual-write semantics. Posts the V2 labeler has not yet reached stay covered by the V1 safety net, and posts it has reached are fully replaced by V2.
    • Undisclosed: When the V1 verdict function will finally be removed, the V2 labeler coverage, and the origin of the four V2_WRITTEN_LABELS labels (a Grok prompt change? a pipeline retraining?)
  • The Gen4+7 commit (d011592, 2026-08-24) introduced the HighRisk tier in the brand safety verdict verified — home-mixer/models/brand_safety.rs
    • A fourth grade, BrandSafetyVerdict::HighRisk = 4, was added on top of the existing Unspecified/Safe/LowRisk/MediumRisk. Because the enum discriminant is assigned 4, the >= comparison in worst_verdict() extends automatically.
    • Five labels were promoted from medium to high. They are NSFW_HIGH_PRECISION, NSFW_HIGH_RECALL, GORE_AND_VIOLENCE_HIGH_PRECISION, PDNA and EGREGIOUS_NSFW. One new label, SOFT_NSFW, is also HighRisk. In both V1 (compute_verdict) and V2 (compute_verdict_v2), the HighRisk check moved to the top.
    • V2 changed symmetrically too. The same five labels were also removed from MEDIUM_RISK_LABELS_V2. V2 originally had NSFW_HIGH_PRECISION, NSFW_HIGH_RECALL, GORE_AND_VIOLENCE_HIGH_PRECISION, PDNA and EGREGIOUS_NSFW.
    • The ads util treats both tiers as avoid. has_avoid() in home-mixer/ads/util.rs was extended to a MediumRisk | HighRisk matches (previously only MediumRisk).
      • That is, in the adjacency verdict, no ad is attached next to a HighRisk post, exactly as with MediumRisk.
      • There is no further action yet, and the severity may be for flagging or logging purposes.
    • Quote adjacency was also promoted. ads_brand_safety_vf_hydrator.rs escalates the verdict to HighRisk, not MediumRisk, when the quoted ancestor post has an NSFW author.
    • Downstream exposure began. Five V2 labels were added to the safety_label_to_proto mapping in scored_posts_server.rs.
      • The five are GROK_SFA_V2, GROK_NSFA_LIMITED_V2, GROK_NSFA_V2, GROK_NSFA_EXPANDED_V2 and PTOS_REVIEWED.
      • These labels are now actually carried out in the feed response proto. Previously, V2 labels were used only in the internal verdict and were not sent downstream.
    • DDG experiment tracking was added. ads_injection_logging_side_effect.rs exposes the EnableAdsBrandSafetyVerdictV2 experiment bucket in logging in the form ddg_experiment_bucket = "experiment_id:bucket".
      • DDG passes to the ads reporting pipeline (presumably Data Dashboard or a similar system inferred), which makes it possible to observe revenue and safety metrics for the V2 experiment group.
      • Why it matters: It indirectly shows that V2 is still at the experiment stage (experiment bucketing). Gen4+2 introduced only the V2 verdict function, Gen4+3 redesigned the semantics, and Gen4+7 put the experiment measurement infrastructure in place.
    • Undisclosed: What follow-up actions the HighRisk tier triggers beyond ads avoid (strong ranker decay, complete blocking of organic impressions, etc.) and the holdout/treatment ratio of the V2 experiment

Ads conversion action expansion — Gen4+6 (2026-08-21, 28e414f)

The Phoenix ranker's ads revenue prediction heads grew by 20 in the 2026-08-21 commit (Gen4+6), and the training loss was reorganized verified. After that, the Gen4+9 commit (2026-08-26, 45b48ba) added three pixel-fire-related heads, and the 2026-09-17 commit (Gen4+23) added 10 each of tier 2 and tier 3 to the delayed conversion actions verified. Since the 2026-10-24 commit (6258a15, Gen4+49), six view-through delayed conversions (conversions that happen late after a user only viewed an ad without clicking) are also trained with late-window twin heads verified (daily).

Before Gen4+6, the ads conversion family effectively had only a few members (install and click-attributed conversions). The Gen4+6 commit expanded it as follows.

20 ActionNames were introduced in the proto verified — phoenix/crates/serving/xai-recsys-proto/proto/recsys.proto

  • 6 MACT kinds × click/view = 12 (171–182) were added.
    • MACT is Mobile App Conversion Tracking. It attributes in-app events after an ad click or impression (purchase, add to cart, level achieved, tutorial completed, sign-up, custom) to the ad.
    • Each event has two versions: click-attributed (MACT_<event>) and view-attributed (MACT_VIEW_<event>).
  • 8 view-through conversions (183–190) were added.
    • The targets are purchase, add_to_cart, checkout_initiated, sign_up, site_visit, session, landing_page_view and upper_funnel.
    • Each is a view-through head corresponding to the existing click-attributed one (ADS_PURCHASE_CONVERSION = 200, etc.).

The engagement metric group changed verified — phoenix/xrex/data/recsys/constants.py

  • Added 12 new MACT mappings and 8 view-through mappings to ads_conversion_engagement_to_action_types.
  • The new metric group ads_slim trains only 3 positive signals, 4 negative signals and non-primary conversion clicks. It is the slim signal combination of the ads ranking line.
    • The positive signals are open link, external link long dwell and video quality view.
    • The negative signals are not interested, block, report and mute.
  • CLIENT_TWEET_SEARCH_QUERY_REFORMULATED was added to NEGATIVE_FEEDBACK_HEAD_INDICES. When a user rewrites the query because they dislike the search results, it is treated as negative feedback. This is in the same direction as the xrecsys_search config.

A delayed feedback training branch was added verified — phoenix/xrex/models/recsys_model.py

There are four new config options. The defaults in the table are as of the Gen4+6 commit.

Option Default Meaning
split_head_training_by_source False Separates delayed feedback samples from fresh samples in the loss mask (engagement heads train on fresh only, conversion heads on delayed only). condition_conversion_on_click=True is an assert precondition. In Gen4+24 (2026-09-18) this option was unified into ads_head_masking and deleted.
train_view_through_heads False Turns on training of the 8 view-through heads. If False, the view-through loss mask is 0. Unified into ads_head_masking and deleted in Gen4+24.
mact_in_app_loss_weight 1.0 Loss weight applied only to the 12 MACT actions. Tunes the training intensity of the ads conversion heads
metric_mask_keys None Filters the training observability metric slices

There are two new batch fields.

  • sample_source (bool) comes from the is_delayed_feedback column of the kafka record. If True, this sample is a conversion delayed re-observation.
  • conversion_keep_mask (bool per-candidate) is the kafka conversionKeepMask column. If False, this candidate is excluded from conversion training.
    • In sequence packing, only all(True) is allowed (when not linked).

The new metric slices are fresh (delayed=0), delayed_clicked (delayed=1 & clicked=1) and delayed_non_clicked (delayed=1 & clicked=0). Because condition_conversion_on_click is kept in delayed training as well, even a delayed sample trains conversion under the condition "was there a click."

In the 2026-09-18 commit (Gen4+24), three options were unified into a single ads_head_masking: bool = False. The three options are split_head_training_by_source, train_view_through_heads and condition_conversion_on_click. The three slice names (fresh, delayed_clicked, delayed_non_clicked) are kept, and a new slice late_split_no_early was added. Sample source is a three-valued categorical (FRESH=0, EARLY_RELABEL=1, LATE_SPLIT=2). The twin head mapping is summarized in Gen4+24 in the change log.

Why it matters: The Gen4+6 commit attached two things to ads conversion prediction at once. One is a large increase in the number of heads (20 introduced), and the other is infrastructure that formally branches delayed feedback training. This is a signal that X ranker training is explicitly aligned with the standard treatment in the ads delayed conversion prediction literature (since Chapelle 2014). Separate from the ranking signal channel, SID and SlateContext extension axes that the canon has folded in through Gen4~+5, the ads revenue prediction stack was added as a new axis.

In Gen4+9 (2026-08-26, 45b48ba), three combined pixel-fire and long-dwell heads were added and conv_asset_ids was wired in verified — phoenix/python/common/xai-proto/proto/recsys.proto (+12)

  • Other evidence files are phoenix/crates/serving/xai-recsys-proto/proto/recsys.proto and home-mixer/models/candidate.rs (+8).
  • Three new ActionNames (191–193) were added.
    • 191 ADS_PIXEL_FIRE is the firing of a conversion pixel (web tracking pixel) that an advertiser planted on their own site or app. It directly predicts web conversion events.
    • 192 ADS_LONG_DWELL_AND_PIXEL_FIRE combines pixel fire and long dwell (staying long on the landing page) with AND. That is, it is the case where the pixel did not merely fire but the user actually stayed long.
    • By the Gen4+6 convention, the prefix P_ of 193 P_LONG_DWELL_AND_PIXEL_FIRE suggests a primary or predicted target family inferred.
  • A ConvAssetIds message was introduced and wired in as the field PredictNextActionsRequest.conv_asset_ids = 18.
    • It consists of three arrays: impressed_time_ms (int64), author_id (int64) and asset_id (int64).
    • It passes to Phoenix serving, along with the request, the history of ad creatives (assets) the user was recently shown.
    • This history is presumably consulted in conversion prediction when an ad asset is reused across several advertisers or when a user saw the same asset several times inferred.
  • Two Option<u32> fields (SlateContext.recon_count_above, recon_gap_above) were added to the home-mixer SlateContext struct.
    • These fields break down the recon reconstruction metrics of served_slate_context.
    • They are not yet reflected on the proto side. The proto has only the field 13 reconCosMilli.
    • The home-mixer local wiring is waiting for the proto migration.
  • Why it matters: This follows Gen4+6's large expansion of the ads conversion prediction heads by 20. Gen4+9 adds three heads that combine pixel fire and long dwell, and creates a channel to carry asset history in the serving request. constants.py and models/recsys_model.py do not yet reflect it. Because only the proto was introduced, the training and serving wiring is a checkpoint to watch in the next commit.

In Gen4+13 (2026-09-01, 7ba7768), the DPA product SID was carried in the serving wire format verified — phoenix/crates/serving/xai-recsys-proto/proto/recsys.proto, phoenix/python/common/xai-proto/proto/recsys.proto

Dynamic Product Ads (DPA) is an ad format in which an advertiser uploads a product catalog and X automatically generates and shows ads tailored to each user. This commit added repeated int32 sid_codes = 8 to the DPA DpaProductInfo. That is, SID codes for ad DPA products are carried in the request payload into the ranker. This is a separate pipeline from the SID of organic posts, which is already carried as post_sids in history_seq and candidate_seq.

In the same commit, reserved 214 to 252 was added to the DiscreteActionName enum; reserving 39 slots in advance appears to secure room for further expansion of ads conversion actions inferred.

Why it matters: Ads DPA ranking has begun to be incorporated into the SID family of signals. Paired with the Phoenix ranker's Gen4+13 SID recon mode, this opens the possibility that ads DPA products and organic posts are represented under the same SID vocabulary. However, this commit alone does not tell us the following three things:

  • Whether the DPA SID codebook is the same as or different from the organic post SID codebook
  • Whether a server-side connection that consumes sid_codes already exists
  • Whether there are A/B results

In Gen4+23 (2026-09-17, 42266f3), delayed conversion attribution was expanded to 3 tiers verified — phoenix/crates/serving/xai-recsys-proto/proto/recsys.proto, phoenix/python/common/xai-proto/proto/recsys.proto

The existing reserved 214 to 252 was narrowed to reserved 234 to 252, and tier 2 and tier 3 were attached at 214-233.

  • 10 Tier 2 actions (214-223) were added.
    • ADS_ATTRIBUTED_KEY_CLICK_CONVERSION_DELAYED_TIER_2·ADS_ATTRIBUTED_CLICK_CONVERSION_DELAYED_TIER_2·ADS_PURCHASE_CONVERSION_DELAYED_TIER_2·ADS_MID_FUNNEL_CONVERSION_DELAYED_TIER_2·ADS_ADD_TO_CART_CONVERSION_DELAYED_TIER_2·ADS_UPPER_FUNNEL_CONVERSION_DELAYED_TIER_2·ADS_WEB_CONVERSION_DELAYED_TIER_2·ADS_SEARCH_CONVERSION_DELAYED_TIER_2·ADS_SIGN_UP_CONVERSION_DELAYED_TIER_2·ADS_CHECKOUT_INITIATED_CONVERSION_DELAYED_TIER_2
  • 10 Tier 3 actions (224-233) are the _TIER_3 symmetric counterpart of the same 10.

Why it matters: The 10 *_DELAYED actions (204-213) introduced by the 2026-09-01 commit (Gen4+12) were expanded to tier 2 and 3 in 16 days verified — recsys.proto:446-455 in 6384ca7. The delayed window is now divided not into one but into three intervals by lag. The delayed feedback literature of the Chapelle (2014) and Yasui&Sakata (2020) line has taken the approach of mitigating propensity bias with per-lag masks, and this change is in the same direction inferred. Which part of the observation window each tier covers and how the loss weights are combined across tiers are not stated in this commit. Whether values like mparams["*_tier_2_loss_weight"] appear in the training config is the checkpoint to watch.

Phoenix training and index (introduced in Gen4)
