Training code, optimizer, and training config

As of the 2026-08-21 commit (Gen4+6), the released flagship ranking config and nano config use the same Muon optimizer recipe as the production home ranker verified. The training config for search ranking was added next to the For You feed config in the 2026-08-19 commit (Gen4+4) verified.

Phoenix can be run end-to-end since the Gen4 release verified — README.md #deployment-related-code.

  • A Cargo workspace, pyproject.toml, QUICKSTART, and a synthetic data generator are included verified — README.
  • The scope the README states is a small model: "a small model can be trained and served end-to-end". As of this README, the production checkpoint, data, and infrastructure are still not public verified — README.
  • Loss and negative sampling details need a deep dive. The optimizer was released in the 2026-08-19 commit (Gen4+4).

In the 2026-08-19 commit (Gen4+4), Phoenix's dense-parameter optimizer changed from Adam to Muon verified — phoenix/xrex/optimizers/recsys/muon.py (240 lines added).

  • The same commit added phoenix/xrex/optimizers/recsys/dense_optim.py (47 lines) and changed the default config in phoenix/xrex/configs/xrecsys.py.

Muon is an optimizer that approximately orthogonalizes gradient momentum with Newton-Schulz orthogonalization. The Muon in this code wraps optax.contrib._muon and became the default dense-parameter optimizer of the Phoenix ranker. The application is hybrid: only matrix-shaped parameters use Muon, and parameters whose names match the patterns below still use Adam.

muon_adam_patterns = "embed,_emb,logits,vocab,norm,table"

In other words, embedding tables, the output logits head, vocab, and norm (layernorm/rmsnorm) stay on Adam. Only the attention and FFN weight matrices of the Transformer body go to Muon. This setup matches the standard Muon hybrid pattern (Keller Jordan 2024 and the Kimi/Moonshot K2 line).

The default config of _home_direct_packed_base() changed as in the table below.

Parameter Value (from Gen4+4) Previous value (Gen3–Gen4+3)
optim "muon" Adam
learning_rate (dense) 7.1e-4 1e-3
emb_learning_rate (moved to the embedding config) 0.2
muon_consistent_rms 0.2 —
muon_matrix_weight_decay 0.014 —
muon_split_fused "qkv:128" (splits the fused QKV projection into 128-dim blocks and orthogonalizes each) —
adam_embedding_weight_decay 0.014 —
b1, b2 0.95, 0.98 —
embedding optim RecsysRowwiseAdagradConfig(learning_rate=0.28, half_life_steps=2500, lazy_decay=True, weight_decay=2.8e-4) rowwise_adagrad (LR 0.2)

The GB300 override was updated in the same direction. The values are Muon, LR 5e-4, half_life_steps=5000, and weight_decay=0.01.

This is the first time the code confirms Muon adoption in a large-scale production recsys training pipeline that this repository has covered. A new observation axis appears: an optimizer that started in LLM training has moved to ranker and retrieval training. An optimizer axis needs to be added to topics/sequence-transformer-ranking.md.

In the 2026-08-21 commit (Gen4+6), the Muon training recipe was formally included in the export verified — phoenix/TRAINING.md.

  • The same commit also changed phoenix/README.md and phoenix/reference/README.md.

The canon's previous statement was: "The dense optimizer of the Phoenix export is standard Optax AdamW; production's tuned RMS-normalized-Adam derivative is undisclosed." Even after muon.py and dense_optim.py were exported in Gen4+4, which introduced Muon, TRAINING.md still said that only AdamW was exported. In this commit, TRAINING.md changed as follows.

Two dense-parameter optimizer families ship in this export:

  • Muon (xrex/optimizers/recsys/muon.py): the production home-ranker recipe — consistent-RMS scaling with decoupled weight decay on the matrix and embedding partitions. The flagship ranking configs and home_direct_packed_nano select it (optim="muon"), so the nano trains with the same dense-optimizer recipe production runs.
  • Standard Optax AdamW: the slot used by the remaining shipped configs (two-tower retrieval, gen-recs, and the legacy ranking presets). ...

— phoenix/TRAINING.md

  • The flagship ranking config and home_direct_packed_nano train end-to-end with the production Muon recipe verified — TRAINING.md. Running the exported nano model as is gives the same Muon training as production.
  • The AdamW arm remains only in two-tower retrieval, gen-recs, and legacy ranking presets verified — TRAINING.md. These are still the export-safe equivalent of production's tuned RMS-normalized-Adam derivative.
  • It also states that three options come with the rowwise AdaGrad for embeddings in flagship and nano verified — TRAINING.md.
    • The three options are accumulator half-life decay, lazy per-row decay, and decoupled weight decay.
    • The emb_optim_config parameter (LR 0.28, half-life 2500 steps) introduced in Gen4+4 has been settled in the canon.
  • The train_step.py entry in reference/README.md was also generalized to "dense optimizer + rowwise-AdaGrad" verified — reference README. The reference training script configures the AdamW arm, while the flagship and nano configs use the Muon recipe.

Why it matters: With this commit, running the exported training Python code as is gives the same training as the production Muon recipe. When Muon entered the code in Gen4+4 (2026-08-19), the canon's understanding was "the code is exported, but the training recipe is still production-specific." The reproducibility documentation has narrowed, but the data and infrastructure are still not public (the README caveat stays).

In the same commit (Gen4+6), the nano config inherits the LR and optimizer settings of the GB300 hardware-specific override verified — phoenix/xrex/configs/xrecsys.py:330-345.

  • _GB300_OVERRIDES itself has existed since the Gen4 release (batch, EP, attention, remat, and LR entries) verified — xrecsys.py:305-313, 368. The optimizer entries were added in the 2026-08-19 commit (Gen4+4).
  • The block below shows the values as of Gen4+6.
  • bs_per_device=512 is 8× the previous bs_per_device=64 of _home_direct_packed_nano. It reflects the HBM headroom of GB300.
  • ep=64 sets expert parallelism to 64-way.
  • attn_impl="cutedsl_ranker_varlen_attn" is a variable-length attention kernel based on NVIDIA CUTLASS/CUTe DSL. It is a new implementation optimized for GB300.
    • This name is not in open-source catalogs, so it may be xAI's own kernel inferred.
  • remat_policy=RematType.SAVE_GB300_RECSYS is a rematerialization policy tuned to the GB300 memory hierarchy.
  • unroll_layer_stack=True compiles the Transformer layer stack unrolled. This leaves room for XLA optimization.
  • checkpoint_every_n=300 saves a checkpoint every 300 steps.

_home_direct_packed_nano inherits the LR, optim_config, and emb_optim_config of this override. Previously nano had its own learning_rate=2e-3, but from this commit it is unified on the GB300 basis.

Why it matters: This is the first case where X exposes a hardware generation transition in code. NVIDIA GB300 (Grace Blackwell 300) is the latest data-center GPU, which began shipping in the second half of 2025, and the successor to Blackwell B200. LLM companies are securing this generation in bulk, and xAI applied it as is to the ranker training and serving pipeline as well. The new fact for the canon is that Phoenix production training runs on GB300. That even nano is tuned to the GB300 config means the export itself assumes a GB300 reproduction scenario.

The remat policy for H100 was added in a later commit verified (Gen4+15 D in the change log).

In the 2026-08-19 commit (Gen4+4), Phoenix expanded to search ranking by introducing the xrecsys_search config verified — phoenix/xrex/configs/xrecsys.py:435-473.

xrecsys_search was added next to xrecsys, the For You feed training config. The main differences from the For You config are as follows:

  • The vocab grew substantially. The search query and click corpus has greater user and item diversity, so the vocab must be larger than the much smaller vocab of the For You config.
    • The values are user_vocab_size=100_000_000, item_vocab_size=100_000_000, author_vocab_size=30_000_000, and ip_vocab_size=10_000_000.
  • The architecture values are num_layers=8, emb_size=2560, emb_table_width=1024, query_heads=20, kv_heads=4 (GQA), history_seq_len=1022, and candidate_seq_len=64.
  • The distribution settings are ep=512, dp=2, fsdp=1, and tp=1. With expert-parallel 512, the EP axis is much larger than in the For You base config, and the MoE routing is also much larger in the search config.
  • There are search-specific flags. use_product_surface=True turns on product surface conditioning, and output_vocab_size=128 expands the actions to 128 kinds.
    • The rest are condition_search_relevance_on_prompt=True, use_dense_action_table=True, and metric_group="search".
  • The training signal uses a separate group, group_id="user_action_sequence_xrecsys", and log_q_correction=True.
  • The training scale is total_samples=1e11, the same as the For You base.

Meaning: Phoenix is expanding from the For You feed ranker to a search surface ranker. This config pairs with two actions renumbered in the proto from 161/162 to 105/106 (CLIENT_TWEET_RELEVANT_TO_SEARCH = 105, CLIENT_TWEET_NOT_RELEVANT_TO_SEARCH = 106) (prediction output schema). Previously the canon understood each surface (For You, Following, search) as a separate codebase. This commit confirms a new fact: unification is under way toward serving both search and feeds with the same Phoenix Transformer architecture, swapping only the per-surface config. The direction matches the "single ranker for search and recommendation" trend of Netflix UniCoRn and GenRec (topics/llm-in-recsys.md).

In the 2026-08-21 commit (Gen4+6), three options were added to the nano config of two-tower retrieval verified — phoenix/xrex/configs/xrecsys_two_tower.py:429-431.

The options went into the xrecsys_two_tower_nano entry of MODEL_CFGS verified — xrecsys_two_tower.py:411-431. This entry does not inherit the combined base, so until then all three keys used the defaults in the model construction code verified — same file, lines 530, 627, 675, 681. In the combined base, the three keys have been False, 80.0, and True since the Gen4 release, and this commit did not change the base verified — xrecsys_two_tower.py:274-275, 318.

  • qk_norm=True
  • attn_logit_cap=-1: turns off logit capping.
  • right_anchored_rope=True: sets the RoPE positional encoding to right-anchored.

A stability trick from LLM training has moved to the retrieval two-tower. Separately, the EVERGREEN retrieval dataset file was drastically reduced from evergreen_video_1825day.parquet to video_4to14day.parquet. The name and the content now disagree, and this may be temporary inferred.

In the same commit (Gen4+6), the retrieval post-embedding computation was split into 65k-row chunks verified — phoenix/xrex/train/trainer_recsys.py _forward_chunked.

maybe_build_retrieval_post_embeddings previously computed a whole shard with a single candidate_tower_forward_jit call. From this commit, on even shards where total_samples % data_world_size == 0, it computes in units of _chunk_rows = min(_shard_rows, 65536). This stabilizes the subroutine as training scale grows with the Muon promotion and the GB300 config.

Prediction output schema and slate context

In the 2026-08-19 commit (Gen4+4), a reward output and a 5-quantile head for link-open probability were added to the Phoenix prediction output schema verified. The path by which home-mixer receives and uses the slate context computed by Phoenix serving was introduced in the 2026-08-20 commit (Gen4+5), and the default of its gate was false verified.

In the 2026-08-19 commit (Gen4+4), a reward head and a link-open 5-quantile head were added to the Phoenix proto verified — phoenix/crates/serving/xai-recsys-proto/proto/recsys.proto.

The Phoenix prediction output schema expanded in two directions.

  1. A RewardOutputs message was added, providing scaffolding for Phoenix to emit a reward value head and a policy logits head alongside the 24 probability prediction heads verified — recsys.proto.
    • A RewardOutputs rewardOutputs = 8 field was added to NextActionDistribution. The two fields of RewardOutputs are values, a scalar array, and policyLogits, the policy logits.
    • optional double rewardRerankSlotProb = 5 was also added to ScoreInfo.
    • It is presumably used for RL-style (actor-critic value+policy) training or reward-model-guided re-ranking slate decisions, and no scorer that consumes this field is connected yet inferred. It is still at the hidden state scaffolding stage inferred.
    • The training code of the page-level RL re-ranker for immersive surfaces, released later, reads the rewardRerankSlotProbSeq column as rl_rerank_prob and uses it as the logged probability of the page RL loss verified — recsys_batch.py:284, page_rl.py:206, 216, 233 (the page-level RL re-ranker commit in the change log).
      • The claim that this column collects the rewardRerankSlotProb field of the serving response rests on the names being the same inferred.
  2. A head was added that predicts link-open probability not as a single scalar but as a distribution of five quantiles (P10/P25/P50/P75/P90) verified — recsys.proto.
    • The five slots PLACE_HOLDER_167/168/169/170/253 were renamed P_OPEN_LINK_P10, P_OPEN_LINK_P25, P_OPEN_LINK_P50, P_OPEN_LINK_P75, and P_OPEN_LINK_P90, respectively.
    • Before this commit, X's prediction heads were of the single-probability or scalar kind. This head is the first time a distribution-shaped prediction entered the ranker.

The same proto change also includes these:

  1. The search relevance actions were renumbered as CLIENT_TWEET_RELEVANT_TO_SEARCH = 105 and CLIENT_TWEET_NOT_RELEVANT_TO_SEARCH = 106 verified — recsys.proto. The old 161/162 remain as *_DEPRECATED. These actions pair with the xrecsys_search config.
  2. SlateContext gained seven SID fields verified — recsys.proto. The fields are sidKnown, sidK1/2/3, and sidGap1/2/3. This aligns, at the proto level, with the 2026-08-18 commit (Gen4+3) that connected SID to VMRanker.

The following questions need a deep dive:

  • In which training loop is RewardOutputs actually filled? In this commit recsys_model.py changed substantially, +265/−25. The key is whether actor-critic heads were added or a reward model is trained separately.
  • Is the link-open 5-quantile a quantile regression or a categorical mixture?
  • Has the xrecsys_search config been deployed to production, or is it still used only for offline training?

In the 2026-08-20 commit (Gen4+5), home-mixer started receiving and using the slate context computed by Phoenix serving verified — home-mixer/models/candidate.rs:26-27, 76-77, 99-118.

  • The remaining evidence is home-mixer/scorers/phoenix_scorer.rs:107-125, home-mixer/scorers/ranking_scorer.rs:700-710, 806-825, 875-895, and home-mixer/params/param.rs:243-249.

The SlateContext.sid* fields added to the Phoenix proto in Gen4+4 were connected to the consumption path of the actual pipeline in this commit. Four places changed at once across three files (candidate.rs, phoenix_scorer.rs, ranking_scorer.rs).

  1. PostCandidate gained a new field served_slate_context: Option<SlateContext>. It is a second storage slot next to the existing slate_context (a value home-mixer computes locally and then caches), and it holds only the slate context that came from the Phoenix response.
  2. A conversion impl between proto and Rust, From<xai_recsys_proto::SlateContext>, was added. This impl renames the proto's sid_k1/2/3 and sid_gap1/2/3 to home-mixer's sid_k_l1/l2/l3 and sid_gap_l1/l2/l3. The "l" stands for level.
  3. PhoenixScorer takes the slate context out of the prediction response and puts it in this field. If the Phoenix prediction response carries a SlateContext along with the 24 candidate scores, it is used as is.
    • The SlateContext at this point contains pool_rank, pool_rank_gap, fatigue, pre_diversity_score, sid_known, sid_k_l1/2/3, and sid_gap_l1/2/3.
    • The code is predictions.candidate_slate_context(&c.get_original_tweet_id()).map(Into::into).
  4. RankingScorer decides which slate context to use through a three-way fallback. The new gate is UseServedSlateContext, and its default is false. The fallbacks apply in order from the top, and both ranking branches (mpn_scoring, diversity) use the same fallback.
    1. If the gate is on and Phoenix sent the slate context for every candidate, it is used as is.
    2. If the gate is off and the Redis cache hits, the stored context is used.
    3. Otherwise, it is computed locally.

Why it matters: This is the first step of a migration that moves the place where the slate context is computed from home-mixer locally to Phoenix serving. At the moment Phoenix produces a prediction, it already knows each candidate's pool rank, fatigue, pre-diversity, and three-level SID information. Therefore, sending these in the serving response instead of recomputing them in home-mixer gains two things:

  • (a) It saves ranker CPU.
  • (b) It can reflect the richer context that Phoenix has. The three SID levels cannot be computed locally by home-mixer.

This matches the direction of the SID connection to VMRanker in the 2026-08-18 commit (Gen4+3). By definition, SID is a Phoenix training artifact and cannot be computed locally; this commit kept UseServedSlateContext off by default, so it only opened the gate, and the actual rollout is planned as a later parameter change. What to watch next is the commit that raises this gate to true. That commit marks the point when the slate context from Phoenix serving reaches production traffic.

In the 2026-08-21 commit (Gen4+6), SlateContext was also added to NextActionDistribution as field #9 verified — phoenix/crates/serving/xai-recsys-proto/proto/recsys.proto.

SlateContext first appeared in Gen4+4 as the field slateContext = 4 of ScoreInfo, the context attached to re-ranking slate decisions, and in Gen4+5 it was connected as PostCandidate.served_slate_context, which home-mixer started using. In this commit, a SlateContext slateContext = 9 field was also added to NextActionDistribution, the per-action prediction distribution of each candidate. That is, a slate context is now attached to each action distribution as well, so from this commit it can be carried in two places, ScoreInfo and NextActionDistribution. The consumption path is not yet connected, and this is at the scaffolding stage inferred.

Ranker input features and SID reconstruction

Three bool input features of the Phoenix ranker have been filled with real values since the 2026-08-14 commit (Gen4+1) verified. These three became default training inputs in the 2026-08-19 commit (Gen4+4) verified. The recon mode, which converts SID codes back into dense vectors and adds them to the ranker input, was released in the Gen4+13 commit (2026-09-01, 7ba7768), but the default at release was the existing learned mode verified. Since the 2026-10-23 commit (Gen4+48), the embedding of the viewer's recent search queries can be carried in the ranker request, but it is off by default verified (bullet below).

In the 2026-10-23 commit (07d159b, Gen4+48), a path was introduced that carries the viewer's recent search queries in the user context of the Phoenix ranker request. It is off by default. verified — query_hydrators/recent_search_queries_query_hydrator.rs

  • It receives up to 16 recent search queries from before the request time from the repository used by the search service, and sends only the 1024-dimension embedding and the timestamp, with the query text removed verified.
  • The same hydrator was added to both the For You candidate pipeline and the score-only pipeline verified.
  • The Phoenix training code in this commit shows no change that reads this field. So it is unknown whether the model has already been trained with this feature inferred. The fact that a test name says "matches training" is a signal that separate training-side data exists. Details are in daily 2026-10-24.

In the 2026-08-14 commit (Gen4+1), three new Phoenix input features were added verified — phoenix/crates/common/xai-recsys/src/util.rs:456-540.

  • phoenix/crates/common/xai-recsys/src/model_config.rs:40 in the same commit is also evidence.
bool feature description
IS_STALE_POST14D If enable_stale_post = true and now - creation_ts > STALE_POST_14D_TTL_SEC, the fav/reply/retweet/quote/view counts of this candidate (and history) are all stamped to 0 and this bool is set to true. In effect, all engagement signals of posts older than 14 days are ignored and the ranker is only told "stale".
IS_AUTHOR_FOLLOWED_BY_VIEWER_SEQ Whether the viewer follows this candidate's author (per candidate and history sequence)
IS_AUTHOR_FOLLOWING_VIEWER_SEQ Whether the candidate's author follows the viewer (detects bidirectional follows)
  • In the code from Gen3 to early Gen4, bool_features was stamped entirely as vec![false; ...], so the input itself had no effect (a "dead field" kind in the canon caveat list). In Gen4+1, three were filled for the first time verified.
    • The evidence is the patch replacing bool_features: vec![false; ...] → bool_features: candidate_bool_features.
  • The stale signal comes in as a pair: count zeroing and a bool set. It is an explicit label telling the ranker that "these counts are low not because the post is unpopular but because it is old and its impressions have stopped." The purpose is likely to mitigate Gen3's snowball problem inferred.
  • The is_mutual_follow boost (reply +15) was a condition hardcoded in the scorer. From this commit, the model receives the follow direction as separate input bools and can learn a similar pattern through training.
  • In the 2026-08-19 commit (Gen4+4), all four features were promoted to train-default ON verified — phoenix/xrex/configs/xrecsys.py:270-290.
    • In the _home_direct_packed_base() default config, the four flags enable_stale_post=True, enable_is_author_followed_by_viewer=True, enable_is_author_following_viewer=True, and enable_engagement_counts=True were raised to the FeaturePrepConfig defaults.
    • The three bools filled in Gen4+1 have been default inputs of the training pipeline since this commit.
    • Separately, only the grpc_recsys dataset type overrides enable_stale_post=False, so the stale-flag stamp is off on the real-time serving path. The reason is presumably that count zeroing can be risky in real time inferred.

In the Gen4+13 commit (2026-09-01, 7ba7768), an SID recon mode was added to the Phoenix ranking model. It is off by default. verified — phoenix/xrex/models/recsys_sid.py (72 lines added).

  • In the same commit, phoenix/xrex/models/recsys_model.py changed by +35/−2.

This commit is the first code release of the path by which X attaches RQ-VAE-family SIDs to the ranker input. It does not replace the retrieval model with SID; it is a path that reconstructs SID codes into input embeddings for the ranker post tower.

_load_sid_decoder(path) reads the tensors below from an offline .safetensors.

  • stages is a stacked residual codebook (RQ-VAE style) of shape (num_levels, codebook_size, code_dim). For each level, stages[l, code_l, :] is picked and summed. The codebook size and number of levels are determined by the artifact and are not hardcoded in the code.
  • dec_w0, dec_b0, dec_w1, and dec_b1 form a 2-layer MLP decoder (relu → linear). It restores an SID sequence to a dense vector.

The recon function reconstruct_entity_sid turns SID codes into ranker input vectors in the order below verified — phoenix/xrex/models/recsys_sid.py.

  • (a) codes = sids - 1 converts 1-based to 0-based, and rows with sids[..., 0] == 0 are marked "missing".
  • (b) For each level, stages[l, code_l, :] is picked to compute the residual sum.
  • (c) It is restored with a 2-layer MLP and relu.
  • (d) It is L2-normalized (eps=1e-12).
  • (e) Missing rows are masked to 0.
  • (f) The decoder is kept fully frozen with stop_gradient.
  • (g) Only one linear projection from recon_dim → target_dim ({prefix}_sid_recon_proj, trainable) is a parameter. The result is returned with its dtype cast to fit the ranker post tower.

The mode is chosen by a config gate verified. Two fields were added to RecsysAggregatedModelConfig:

  • The default "learned" keeps using the existing SID embedding table (a lookup trained inside the post tower).
  • Setting "recon" bypasses the learned SID table. Instead, it builds recon vectors from the SID codes of history_seq and candidate_seq and adds them to the post tower embedding (add).
    • The requirements are the legacy build_inputs path (feature_prep_enabled=False), no sid_hash_level, no sid_cross_attn, and a specified sid_decoder_path.

Why it matters

  • This is the first code release of X's SID line. This commit is the first to show in code how SID codes themselves are turned back into dense features. Until now, X's public SID-related material comprised three items:
    • (a) In Gen4+3 (11a71f8, 2026-08-18), the sid_known, sid_k_l1/2/3, and sid_gap_l1/2/3 fields were connected to VMRanker.
    • (b) In Gen4+4 (aad7179, 2026-08-19), the SlateContext.sid* fields were added to the Phoenix proto.
    • (c) In Gen4+5 (d0cef2f, 2026-08-20), a path was added by which SID is carried in the slate context of the serving response.
  • The decoder is fully frozen. Because it uses stop_gradient and an offline artifact, serving only needs the codebook and MLP matrices deployed, and the only thing trained is the single recon_dim → target_dim projection. Codebook tuning happens only offline, and ranker training does not disturb the codebook.
  • "learned" and "recon" become the A/B axis. That the default is still learned is read as meaning that recon mode's production validity has not yet been verified, or that it is before dial-up inferred. If sid_embedding_mode="recon" appears in a production config in the next commit, it will signal that the X SID pipeline has moved from a "trained table" to "offline codebook + recon at serving time".
  • This path is not a retrieval model. Restoring vectors from the codebook and attaching them to the ranker input increases the density of the candidate representation; it does not replace candidate generation with SID. Its lineage differs from the approach of Kuaishou OneRec and Tencent TGR (radar.md generative retrieval thread), which "treat SID as the autoregressive generation target". As of this commit, X still uses SID as an input signal inside the cascade. A generative retrieval source that uses SID for candidate generation was later released off by default verified (candidate generation section).

This commit also leaves some things undisclosed.

  • Code of the SID training pipeline that builds the artifacts (encoder and VQ training)
  • Measured codebook size and number of levels
  • Whether sid_embedding_mode="recon" is on in production
  • A/B metrics for the learned and recon modes

Phoenix retrieval index

The post index that Phoenix retrieval queries, and the event layer that decides which index a post goes into, were released with Gen4 verified. A post gets a visibility verdict before it enters the index verified. Since the 2026-08-17 commit (Gen4+2), candidates with no likes are also published as indexing events verified.

The Gen4 release also included the Phoenix retrieval index services verified — README.md #retrieval-index.

  • phoenix-rankall/ is the post index that Phoenix retrieval queries. It is updated when events arrive verified — README.
  • phoenix-rankall-strato/ is the event layer that decides which index a post belongs to. This layer consults visibility-filtering first verified — README.
  • In the 2026-08-14 commit (Gen4+1), one SID window, video_14day, was added verified — phoenix-rankall/src/config/mod.rs:177-180.
    • It pairs with the existing video_48h, video_96h, and nsfw_video_48h/168h/14day.
    • A video popularity signal over a 2-week window entered the retrieval SID.
  • In the 2026-10-20 commit (Gen4+45), the hourly video windows video_6h and video_6hto2day were added, so the shortest video window of the SID index went from 48 hours to 6 hours verified — phoenix-rankall/src/config/mod.rs:212-213.

The indexing pipeline is already aligned with the ranking-side visibility rules. A post already carries a visibility verdict before it enters the index. This is an architecture fact that the canon did not know at all through Gen3.

Two indexing gates were removed in the 2026-08-17 commit (Gen4+2) verified — phoenix-rankall-strato/columns/phoenix_rank_all/phoenixRankAllCandidateProcessor.strato.

  • build1FavIndex publishes every candidate from this commit. In other words, the "1fav" index name became a backward compat label, and the actual index holds all incoming candidates.
    • Before the change, only candidates with favoriteCount >= 1 published a "1fav" indexing event to Kafka.
    • After the change, only candidates with favoriteCount == 0 are instrumented with a new counter, 1fav_uec_count_race.
  • buildMMEmbMetadataDump also lost its gate and fetches and dumps three versions of the multimodal embedding for every candidate.
    • Before the change, the same favoriteCount >= 1 gate meant that only candidates with favorites looked up the three versions (v3, v5_1, v6_dev) and dumped them as Kafka metadata.
  • This is a new caveat. The canon's understanding from Gen3–Gen4 that "phoenix-rankall updates the index with a popularity signal" is no longer accurate from this commit. The index name does not imply a filter condition.
  • Why it matters: This is an infrastructure expansion that lets Phoenix retrieval attempt embedding-based matching on long-tail posts too inferred. In the next commit we look at two things: the ratio at which the 1fav_uec_count_race counter is actually observed, and which param gates (Phoenix retrieval top-k, SID window) the index coverage expansion is turned on together with.

In the 2026-08-18 commit (Gen4+3), Phoenix postCreationEventForwarder was migrated to unified posts topic V3 verified — phoenix-rankall-strato/stream_forwarders/postCreationEventForwarder.strato.

  • The same commit also changed phoenix-rankall-strato/columns/phoenix_rank_all/postCreationEventProcessor.strato.
Field Value (since Gen4+3) Previous value
Kafka topic content_understanding_realtime_unified_posts_v3 content_understanding_realtime_unified_posts
Kafka dest /s/kafka/phoenix-kafka-external-bootstrap (separate Phoenix-only cluster) /s/kafka/main-2:kafka-tls (X main Kafka cluster)
Consumer group post_creation_event_v3 (plus a separate develConsumerGroupId = Some("post_creation_event_v3_devel")) post_creation_event
Kafka mapping KeyValue({key = Long, keyEncoding = NativeEncoding, ...}) (postId as the explicit key) ValueOnly (Thrift value only)
Import hydra/sharedConfig content_understanding/sharedConfig
Processor signature Op.execute[(Long, Event), Unit] (prefers the postId that arrives as the key in the tuple) Op.execute[Event, Unit] (parses the postId from inside the event via ctx.arg)
  • This migration moves the shared event stream of the content understanding domain from v1 to v3. It changed in two directions:
    • (a) It raised postId to the Kafka key, so partitioning, dedup, and inverted-index lookup can be purely key-based.
    • (b) It separated the Phoenix retrieval Kafka cluster from X main, so isolation and tuning can be done separately.
  • Moving the import to hydra/sharedConfig is also a signal that the Phoenix family is being brought under hydra infrastructure.
  • With this change, the upstream event path for maintaining the Phoenix retrieval index (build1FavIndex, buildMMEmbMetadataDump) fully moved from X main Kafka to the isolated Phoenix Kafka. It points the same direction as the "indexing gate removal" in Gen4+2. The direction fits if the indexing pipeline's throughput grew and a separate cluster became necessary inferred.
  • Some things are also not public. They are whether a v2 existed (whether it jumped straight from v1 to v3, or this is a third migration going from v2 to v3), the scale of the Phoenix Kafka cluster and the reason for isolation, and when the v1 forwarder is finally shut down.

Training and serving infrastructure

The 2026-08-20 commit (Gen4+5) extracted the core of the embedding table loader into a function not tied to pyo3 verified. The 2026-08-21 commit (Gen4+6) released an option to return memory after hotswap and the interface of xai-o2, the internal object storage verified. The path that exports a trained ranking model as a StableHLO bundle for CUDA serving entered off by default in the Gen4+13 commit (2026-09-01, 7ba7768) verified.

In the 2026-08-20 commit (Gen4+5), emb_table.rs was split into a Python wrapper and a pyo3-free core verified — phoenix/crates/serving/xai-recsys-engine/src/emb_table.rs (+189/−169, essentially a behavior-preserving refactor).

The existing load_tensor was tied to pyo3 types and errors and could not be reused in non-Python contexts. This commit extracted its core into the function below, and the existing load_tensor was redefined as a pyo3 wrapper.

  • load_tensor_into(&str, &str, &[(String, String, usize, usize)], &mut [u8], usize, usize) -> Result<(), String>

Safety was also reinforced.

  • The tokio runtime's unwrap() was replaced with map_err.
  • A prefix.len() < 3 guard (checkpoint path too short: {path}) was added.
  • The modulo check was unified on the is_multiple_of API.

This is refactor preparation for the growing need to load large embedding tables (vocab 100M/100M/30M of Gen4+4 xrecsys_search) in multiple serving and training contexts inferred.

In the 2026-08-21 commit (Gen4+6), a malloc_trim(0) option was added to inference hotswap verified — phoenix/xrex/inference/model_runner.py.

  • The same commit also changed launch_inference.py.

The new CLI option --hotswap_malloc_trim defaults to True. The _malloc_trim_after_swap() method calls libc malloc_trim(0) at the end of every hotswap cycle. The observability metric is checkpoint_reload_step_seconds.labels(step="malloc_trim").

The CLI help reads:

glibc malloc_trim(0) on the coordinator thread after each applied hotswap; returns the cycle's freed pages (glibc slots otherwise ratchet ~196 MiB/cycle). No-op under jemalloc.

Why it matters: This is the first documentation that embedding table hotswap in Phoenix serving has been leaking ~196MiB of RSS per cycle under glibc. Hotswap is long-running infrastructure in production, so the observation is that the accumulated burden was large enough to need this patch.

The same commit (Gen4+6) released the interface of the xai-o2 storage crate verified — phoenix/crates/storage/xai-o2/.

The description in Cargo.toml reads as follows:

Client interface for the xai-o2 (S3-compatible) object storage backend

The crate consists of 3 files:

  • base_client.rs (12 lines) defines the BaseO2Client async trait, whose only method is put(key, data) -> Result<()>.
  • In o2_client_builder.rs (115 lines), O2ClientBuilder provides 15 builder methods.
    • endpoint·bucket·prefix·access_key_id·secret_access_key·allow_anonymous·timeout·io_timeout·retry_max_times(6)·retry_min_delay(1s)·retry_max_delay(32s)·write_chunk_size_mib(8)·write_chunk_concurrency(16)·max_concurrent_write_requests(64)·trace_always
  • lib.rs is 7 lines.

However, in the open-source build, build() always returns the error below.

The xai-recsys-engine crate declares the dependency as xai-o2 = { workspace = true }, but in actual use it must fall back to the standard object_store crate.

Why it matters: This is the first confirmation that xAI has an internal S3-compatible object storage system named xai-o2. The 15 builder params are significant because they are items actually tuned in production. It signals that production checkpoint and data storage attach here inferred.

A new StableHLO bundle export path arrived in the same commit as SID recon mode (Gen4+13). It is off by default. verified — phoenix/xrex/train/recsys_bundle_export.py (634 new lines).

  • In the same commit, phoenix/xrex/train/trainer_recsys.py changed by +53/−0.

The entry point build_bundle(trainer) lowers the ranking model's forward pass with jax.export. The only target is RecsysAggregatedModelConfig, and RecsysGenRecsModelConfig is explicitly unsupported. The export produces three outputs:

  • StableHLO MLIR bytecode (.mlirbc) made with jit(...).lower().as_text(dialect="stablehlo")
  • .jax_export made with jax_export.export(platforms=("cuda",)).serialize()
  • MANIFEST.json

The bundle structure reveals features of the serving architecture:

  • Embedding lookup is outside the exported graph. The forward input merged_embeddings is a tensor that concatenates already looked-up embedding rows.
    • MANIFEST.embedding holds {rows, rows_padded, num_shards, width, dtype, merged_slices, hash_table}, so the serving side knows how to concat the embedding server results.
    • The code reveals that the serving architecture of the X ranker is a split structure: "the embedding server does the lookup, and the GPU server runs StableHLO".
  • There are multiple batch buckets. The default of export_bundle_bs_per_device is "1,2,4". A separate program is lowered per bucket, and at serving time the bucket matching the request batch size is chosen.
  • The target is CUDA only. MANIFEST carries device_kind and compute_capability.
  • seqpack supports only pallas_ranker_varlen_attn. The block-sparse layout of FA4 (cutedsl_ranker_varlen_attn) explicitly raises NotImplementedError.
    • Because the Gen4+6 GB300 config uses attn_impl="cutedsl_ranker_varlen_attn", exporting the GB300 training config as is requires switching the attn kernel to pallas observed. This limit is the break point in the pipeline from GB300 training to GB300 serving observed.
  • Custom-call targets are recorded in the manifest. Because ranker-specific pallas/CUDA kernels are baked into the StableHLO, the serving loader must allow custom calls. The allowed range is widened with jax_export.DisabledSafetyCheck.custom_call(...).
  • sid_num_levels is echoed into the manifest prep_spec. The serving side uses this value to know how many SID levels to put in a batch. This field pairs with SID recon mode.

Four new fields on Trainer turn on and tune the bundle export:

If export_stablehlo_bundle is on but checkpoint_config.copy_port is off, __post_init__ raises ValueError. In other words, export can be turned on only when attached to the copy_port of the checkpoint deployment pipeline (hot checkpoint deployment). With every copy_port deployment, a bundle is shipped to {OUT_PATH}/.{prefix}/export/ as well.

Why it matters

  • X released for the first time code that standardizes the handoff from JAX training to CUDA serving as StableHLO. Until then the canon's understanding was "Phoenix is trained with JAX/Haiku and serving is a separate stack". With this commit, the code confirms that the serving stack takes and runs compiled StableHLO.
  • The explicit separation of embeddings and dense forward is settled as an architecture fact. This accurately supports the canon's understanding that X does not hold the embedding table on a single GPU and looks it up from a separate server (the embedding server and mm_embedding_client.rs). An example of table scale is the vocab 100M/100M/30M of Gen4+4 xrecsys_search.
  • It is off by default. This commit alone cannot confirm whether the production serving pipeline actually consumes StableHLO bundles. If export_stablehlo_bundle=True appears in a production config in the next commit, it will signal that serving has attached to this path.

Some things are also not yet public.

  • Code of the serving loader (the runtime that consumes StableHLO)
  • Detailed conventions for how the embedding server builds the merged_embeddings tensor. The merged_slices schema of MANIFEST.embedding is in the code, but the consumer-side code is not public.
  • Whether this bundle is on in production

The Gen4+13 commit added an Orbax writer that encrypts and stores training checkpoints with envelope encryption. The default is off. verified — phoenix/python/training/xai-checkpointing/xai_checkpointing/orbax_encrypted.py

The linked orbax_encrypted.py is a new 288-line file, and phoenix/xrex/train/misc.py (+5/0) and phoenix/xrex/train/checkpoint_write.py (+6/0) also changed with it verified — same commit.

Envelope encryption encrypts data with a data key (DEK) and then encrypts that data key again with another key.

This writer wraps Orbax PyTreeCheckpointHandler and enforces the following:

  • Every file in a checkpoint must start with a magic header. If even one file lacks the header, the commit is refused verified — same commit.

    • The magic header value is b"XAIENC01".
    • After finalize, assert_all_enveloped(path) walks the checkpoint directory. If it finds a file without a header, it raises RuntimeError("encrypted save left plaintext at rest; not committing: ...").
    • _DEK and _DEK.claim (the DEK file issued by KMS and its claim) are exceptions.

  • Leaves allow only jax.Array; string, dict, and Python scalar leaves are explicitly rejected verified — same commit.

    • The guards are _ArraysOnlyRegistry and _require_array_leaves.
    • This guard removes the arbitrary code execution risk when the serving side loads this checkpoint.

  • The tensorstore KvStore is also replaced with an encrypted wrapper verified — same commit.

    • The option is use_encrypted_kvstore.

  • Metadata is also encrypted verified — same commit.

    • _METADATA, _CHECKPOINT_METADATA, and the sharding metadata are all written with encrypt_write.

  • A process that restored from an encrypted checkpoint cannot save in plaintext (no downgrade) verified — same commit.

    • The new guard is in checkpoint_write.py.
    • Attempting a plaintext save raises ValueError("restored from an ENCRYPTED checkpoint but the orbax writer cannot produce encrypted saves — refusing to downgrade to plaintext saves").

  • CheckpointConfig gained new encryption setting fields verified — same commit.

    • The encryption_context field follows the AWS-KMS encryption-context pattern as is.
    • The default chunk size is 8 MiB.

Why it matters

  • A writer that encrypts training checkpoints at rest entered the code verified. We infer that X uses this writer in production inferred. The basis is that it even includes devices aimed at operational accidents, such as the downgrade-prevention guard.
    • Previously this could only be guessed to be handled at the infrastructure layer (not confirmed in the canon).
    • Now envelope encryption, KMS, and magic header enforcement are in-tree in the xrex training Python code.
    • The source did not state a regulatory framework (SOC2, FedRAMP, GDPR, etc.). It reads as general "data at rest" protection.
  • CheckpointConfig.encrypt defaults to False, and as of the 2026-10-17 commit (862a123) none of the public training configs turns it on verified — phoenix/xrex/train/misc.py:56. So code alone cannot confirm whether production actually uses this writer.
  • The downgrade-prevention guard stands out in particular. It blocks accidentally losing the encrypted state at the code level.
    • It points the same direction as the VF reference_compare harness in Gen4+7, which panics when booted with APP_ENV=prod and so enforced staging-only use.
    • In both cases the policy is fixed in code as a fail-close assertion, not as a config value.

The following is not public:

  • The actual implementation of kms_client (within the file it is passed in from outside)
  • DEK rotation period
  • Actual values used for the encryption context
  • Which KMS is used (AWS, Azure, or in-house)

Grox (LLM annotation) — unchanged from Gen3 (+ threshold raise on 2026-08-14)

Grox is a Grok-based nearline annotation pipeline. The follower threshold that splits reply spam verdicts from reply ranking scoring targets has been 250k since the 2026-09-24 commit (Gen4+28). Replies whose thread root and reply target are both at or below this value receive a spam verdict, and replies where either exceeds it receive reply ranking scoring verified. The threshold started at 15k in the Gen4 release and was raised eleven times; each raise widened the spam verdict targets and narrowed the reply ranking scoring targets verified. The separate spam detection flow was absorbed into the reply ranking flow in the 2026-08-18 commit (Gen4+3) verified. Both thresholds changed after that, and the changed values are in the change log; see the threshold history summary in the commit that raised the coordinated spam threshold from 10k to 30k and the commit that split the reply spam model by thread followers verified.

grox/ produces the slop score, safety labels, topics, reply scores, and multimodal embeddings. In Gen4, grox/ was explicitly placed as Content Understanding stage 1 of the upstream labeling pipeline (safety section). Details are in llm-in-recsys.md.

The 2026-08-14 commit doubled the follower thresholds for reply spam verdicts and reply ranking scoring verified — grox/flows/reply_spam/task_filter.py:17,185.

  • The two threshold constants in grox/flows/reply_spam/task_filter.py changed from 15000 → 30000.
    • TaskSpamFilter.FOLLOWER_COUNT_THRESHOLD_FOR_SPAM_DETECTION: 15,000 → 30,000
    • TaskReplyRankingFilter.FOLLOWER_COUNT_THRESHOLD_FOR_REPLY_RANKING: 15,000 → 30,000

Meaning: replies whose thread root and reply target both have 30k followers or fewer receive a grok spam verdict, and replies where either exceeds 30k receive reply ranking scoring verified — task_filter.py:77-92, 214-225. Doubling the threshold widened the spam verdict targets and narrowed the reply ranking scoring targets. Because the original code constant names carry "spam detection" and "reply ranking", this adjustment is a resource allocation adjustment that decides which replies get grok resources.

The 2026-08-18 commit (Gen4+3, 11a71f8) raised both thresholds again and merged the separate spam detection flow into the reply ranking flow verified — grox/flows/reply_spam/.

  • Both constants went up from 40,000 → 60,000 verified — same commit. This is the third raise, following 30,000 → 40,000 in the 2026-08-17 commit (Gen4+2) (task_filter.py:17, 185 in b089ce6).
    • Only replies whose root and reply target are both at or below 60k become grok spam verdict targets, and the other replies receive reply ranking scoring.
    • The boundary between spam verdicts and reply ranking scoring moved from 40k to 60k.
  • The separate task generator that detected spam over the whole post stream was deleted, and spam detection was absorbed into the reply ranking flow verified — same commit.
    • The deleted generator is PostStreamTaskGenerator. The TOPIC_UNIFIED_POSTS constant (the original, not v3) was also deleted.
    • The remaining ReplyRankingTaskGenerator injects the three plans below together and consumes from the single source TOPIC_UNIFIED_POSTS_V3.
      • PlanReplyRanking (existing)
      • PlanSpamComment (newly absorbed)
      • PlanCoordinatedSpam (newly absorbed)
  • Meaning: the grox spam verdict pipeline was consolidated with a wider range of verdict target accounts (60k and below) and a single flow verified — same commit. The single flow refers to the merge with reply ranking.
    • This change came in the same commit as the Phoenix unified_posts_v3 topic migration (Phoenix training and index section). So the observation follows that grox and Phoenix both moved to the v3 content understanding stream at the same time.

Grox → PtOS Adult Content Cross-Validation (Gen4+2 new, 2026-08-17)

Verdict flow of the adult content judge

A judge layer was added to adult content verdicts to handle verdict disagreement. The grox safety pipeline first released in Gen4 runs the two verdicts in parallel and only logged the result when they differed.

  • The two verdicts are TaskSafetyPtosSafemodelSexNudity (a sex/nudity verdict based on an in-house vision model) and PtOS (a policy-based violation category verdict).
  • In the 2026-08-17 commit (Gen4+2), this logic was split into two files, and a new task was added in which a Grok 4.5 judge re-evaluates when the two verdicts disagree verified — grox/flows/ptos/task_safety_ptos_adult_content_cross_validation.py (162 lines, new)
    • The safemodel task was moved to grox/flows/ptos/task_safety_ptos_safemodel_sex_nudity.py (32 lines moved).
    • The judge class was newly created at grox/flows/ptos/classifier.py:597-608.

The judge task works in four stages:

  1. Compare the two verdicts. The enum CompareOutcome distinguishes BOTH_POSITIVE, BOTH_NEGATIVE, SAFEMODEL_ONLY_POSITIVE, and PTOS_ONLY_POSITIVE. is_disagreement is true for SAFEMODEL_ONLY or PTOS_ONLY.
  2. Check two gates.
    • It runs only in the deluxe flow, and the regular flow only logs. The condition is is_deluxe = ctx.payload.task_type == SAFETY_PTOS_DELUXE.
    • It skips posts that are already NSFW-flagged. The flag is looked up with StratoSafetyPostAnnotationsResultDirectMh.
  3. Call the Grok 4.5 judge. The new class SafetyPtosAdultContentCrossValidationJudge uses ModelName.EAPI_GROK_4_5_X_ALGO.
    • The dedicated circuit breaker has a 50% failure rate, a 600-second window, 600 seconds of recovery, and 5 half-open calls.
    • The system prompt is _strip_thinking_restrictions(adult_content_policy_prompt()). The user message is built with UserRenderer.render(user) and PostRenderer.render(post, include_reply_to=True).
    • The response is parsed with re.compile(r"(.*)<json>(.*)</json>", re.DOTALL) to separate the free-text reasoning from the JSON verdict.
  4. Apply the judge result. If the judge returns AdultContentSexualHard, the original verdict is kept. For any other result, it does three things.
    • It demotes the safetyPolicy.policyType of every AdultContent violation to AdultContentSexualSoft.
    • It writes reason = "Grok 4.5 Cross Validation disagreed" on the demoted violation and leaves it in the audit log.
    • It sets safemodel_sex_nudity.positive to false.

Four points in this design are worth noting:

  • There is only a demotion direction (hard → soft) and no escalation direction.
    • This judge layer works only in the direction of easing over-gating.
    • The code shows a policy direction aimed at reducing false positives rather than false negatives.
  • For a reply, the parent post is also put in as context, so the context "this is a reaction to that post" influences the verdict (include_reply_to=True).
  • In the judge context, the "do not expose reasoning" caution constraint in the original prompt is stripped by _strip_thinking_restrictions() so the reasoning can be seen (for audit purposes).
  • The verdict layers are now three: safemodel, PtOS, and the Grok 4.5 judge. This matches the direction of Gen4's "release of the whole labeling pipeline" trend.

Three questions need a deep dive:

  • Whether this judge layer expands to other categories (violence, hate, spam)
  • How much Grok 4.5 inference cost can be absorbed
  • How the EAPI_GROK_4_5_X_ALGO model differs from the existing EAPI_GROK_4_5_INTERNAL. Presumably the difference is x-algorithm-specific tuning versus a general internal judge.

The 2026-08-18 commit (Gen4+3) improved the logging of this task.

  • The outcome attribute of Metrics.counter(metric) changed from a binary "hard"|"soft" label to the raw policyType.value of the verdict verified — grox/flows/ptos/task_safety_ptos_adult_content_cross_validation.py:128-131
    • Even if the judge returns a policyType other than hard/soft (for example, a finer adult category split), it can now be observed without loss.
    • This is an adjustment to instrumentation granularity, not a change to the verdict logic itself.

Judge models and judged categories over time

With the changes through Gen4+7, X settled on a dual stack that keeps the primary and the judge on different model generations and tunings. The two call sites in the PTOS classifier that called Grok 4.5 internal (the child safety judge and the high-fav deluxe reclassification) moved to Grok 4.6 internal across three commits from 2026-08-19 to 08-21 verified (classifier in 28e414f). Three days later, in the 2026-08-24 commit (Gen4+7), the new judge class also came to use the 4.5 X_ALGO endpoint that the Gen4+2 adult content judge used, and the scope widened to 3 categories verified (classifier in d011592).

From Gen4+4 to +6, the two call sites that used 4.5 internal moved to 4.6 internal, and in Gen4+7 the child safety judge moved to the new cross-validator class and came to use 4.5 X_ALGO. The adult content judge has used 4.5 X_ALGO unchanged since Gen4+2 verified. The flow by commit:

  • Gen4+2 (b089ce6, 08-17): The adult content judge SafetyPtosAdultContentCrossValidationJudge was introduced (when safemodel and PtOS disagree). Its model is EAPI_GROK_4_5_X_ALGO, and this endpoint and its dedicated circuit breaker were also introduced in this commit verified — classifier.py:85, 100, 561.
  • Gen4+3 (11a71f8, 08-18): Refined the metric outcome of the judge above.
  • Gen4+4 (aad7179, 08-19): Attached Grok 4.6 internal with a 10% dial (two sites: high-fav deluxe reclassification and the child safety judge).
  • Gen4+5 (d0cef2f, 08-20): Raised the 4.6 internal dial from 10% to 30%.
  • Gen4+6 (28e414f, 08-21): Switched fully to 4.6 internal at 100%, and 4.5 internal was removed from the code entirely.
  • Gen4+7 (d011592, 08-24): The new cross-validator class also came to use EAPI_GROK_4_5_X_ALGO, which the adult content judge had used since Gen4+2, and the scope widened to 3 categories (child safety, violent media, illegal).
    • The adult content judge is still kept as a separate class (SafetyPtosAdultContentCrossValidationJudge).

If the judge were the same model as the primary, it would amplify the same mistakes, so the rationale of this design is to let the view of a separate model only demote.

The 2026-08-19 commit (Gen4+4) attached Grok 4.6 internal to 10% of traffic and added a cache to skip NSFW reclassification. verified

The verdict stack was refined in two directions.

  • First, it introduced Grok 4.6 to the child safety judge and the high-fav deluxe reclassification verified — grox/flows/ptos/classifier.py (+66/−7)

    • It registered the new model name ModelName.EAPI_GROK_4_6_INTERNAL and attached an EapiSampler instance and a dedicated circuit breaker (_eapi_4_6_internal_breaker).

      • This site is not a judge; it is a path where the first-pass classification of high-fav posts is done with this model instead of the regular sampler verified — classifier.py:461-489.

    • It is an exclusive traffic split that calls 4.6 with 10% probability per request and 4.5 for the rest verified — the code above. It is not dual-write or shadow, which would send the same request to both models.

Why it matters: The PTOS verdict layer is being organized around a traffic split for the 4.5 → 4.6 model switch and a separate cache for the prior classification lookup. Across the three commits Gen4+2 → +3 → +4, this verdict stack is seen being refined daily.

The 2026-08-20 commit (Gen4+5) raised the Grok 4.6 internal dial from 0.1 to 0.3 (3× in one day). verified — grox/flows/ptos/classifier.py:114

Two other places in grox changed in the 2026-08-20 commit (Gen4+5), one day earlier verified — the diff between aad7179 and d0cef2f.

Three days after Gen4+6 removed Grok 4.5 internal completely, the 4.5 X_ALGO endpoint was also used for the new verdict judge (cross-validator). The scope widened to 3 categories.

If it matches, it is kept; if the judge decides NoViolation, it is demoted; if type_mismatch, it is downgraded to ViolentMediaGraphicMedia (the weaker form). The demotion options were refined into three: NoViolation, GraphicMedia, and keep.

  • It keeps the demotion-only principle verified — same commit. This is the same design philosophy as the Gen4+2 adult content judge.
    • The cross-validator cannot produce a stricter verdict than the primary.

In the same commit, the classifier turned on reasoning only for the two categories ViolentSpeech and SuicideOrSelfHarm, and made it include the entire thread when a parent thread exists verified.

  • SafetyPtosPolicyClassifier.build_convo() applies _strip_thinking_restrictions to the prompt only for these two categories (reasoning enabled) verified — same commit.
    • Here the assistant message is left empty so the model can think freely.
    • The set is USE_REASONING_CATEGORIES = {ViolentSpeech, SuicideOrSelfHarm}.
    • Other categories still suppress thinking with THINKING_CONTROL_END (fast and cheap responses).
  • Only for the same two categories, if the post has ancestors, the whole parent thread is rendered as the user message with ThreadRenderer verified — same commit.
    • The set is USE_THREAD_RENDERER_CATEGORIES = {ViolentSpeech, SuicideOrSelfHarm}.
    • The reason is fundamental. A sentence like "I want to die" cannot be judged without the thread context. If the earlier remark was about losing a game, it is harmless; if it is a self-harm support thread, it is serious.
    • Likewise for violent speech, the quote and reply context decide the verdict.
    • For other categories (adult, NSFW media, illegal), the target post itself carries the signal, so thread expansion is not needed.

Changes to the grox reply spam path and LLM input

The grox reply spam pipeline has had a path that writes the reply ranking score back to Strato since the Gen4 release (2026-08-13), and the 2026-08-24 commit (Gen4+7) added regional cache fanout to this path verified(storage module at 47c1bcd, storage module at d011592). As of the 2026-08-28 commit (Gen4+10), grox skips the Manhattan write when the new reply ranking score is not lower than the existing score verified(write task at 24c6094). In other words, the reply ranking score sent out on this path only goes down over time and never goes up verified(write task at 45b48ba).

The 2026-08-24 commit (Gen4+7) also changed three other places in grox.

  • The follower threshold of the reply spam filter and the reply ranking filter rose from 80k to 100k (grox/flows/reply_spam/task_filter.py:17).
    • The two filters are TaskSpamFilter and TaskReplyRankingFilter in grox/flows/reply_spam/task_filter.py.
    • The threshold rose five times in 11 days (15k → 30k → 40k → 60k → 80k → 100k), so the set of accounts covered by spam verdicts kept widening.
    • The increases after Gen4+3 are 1.25–1.5×. The higher the threshold, the more threads of accounts with more followers grok checks with grok, so we infer this adjustment aims to check more spam replies in threads of large accounts inferred.
  • The reply ranking score storage module now also writes the score to two regional caches verified — grox/flows/reply_spam/strato_loader.py (+17/−0).
    • This file and the ReplyRankingScoreStratoLoader class have existed since the Gen4 release (32 lines) verified — same file at 47c1bcd.
    • Since then it has stored the score with StratoReplyRankingScore.put() and emitted an event with StratoReplyRankingScoreV2Kafka.insert().
    • Gen4+7 added one more stage after put(). If score ≤ 1.0, it writes to two regional caches (StratoReplyRankingScoreCacheAtla, StratoReplyRankingScoreCachePdxa) in parallel.
    • If the score exceeds 1.0, the cache fanout is skipped verified — strato_loader.py:20, 34-41. Low-confidence verdicts stay only in the canon (strato), and the serving cache is not polluted inferred.
  • X Spaces (audio) context entered the LLM verdict. The Grok safety judge recognizes posts with an audio space card attached for the first time.
    • A SpaceMetadata class was added to grox/core/data_loaders/data_types.py (a single title as of this commit). A space_metadata: SpaceMetadata | None field was added to Post.
    • post_mapper.py maps it from StratoSpaceMetadata.
    • The grox/core/lm/post.py renderer inserts it into the LLM prompt as \n\nThis post has the following audio space card attached:\nAudio Space title: {title}.
    • It does not listen to the audio content itself, but the space title text becomes input to the verdict. For example, if the topic stated in the space title is adult content or violence, it is reflected in the brand safety verdict.

Gen4+9 (2026-08-26, 45b48ba) added an option to put the follower count and bio into the reply_spam LM prompt and put a monotone-only gate on the Manhattan write. verified

  • The user metadata going into the LM verdict was widened verified — grox/core/lm/post.py (+18/−6), grox/core/lm/thread.py (+25/−4)

    • The previous PostRenderer.render extracted user metadata as a single line, Metadata: <name> @<handle>. It now takes two options, include_follower_count and include_bio, and renders it split as follows:

      User Handle: @<handle>
[User Follower Count: <N>]     # include_follower_count=True
User Name: "<name>"
[User Bio: "<bio>"]              # include_bio=True

    • When ThreadRenderer._render_thread receives the include_follower_count argument, it renders the follower count of every post in the thread. It renders the bio only for post 0 (the original post, the thread root) (include_bio=include_follower_count and post_idx == 0).

    • The follower count is also included for the reply under evaluation (the evaluate target).

    • A header # Reply Author Info\n\nThe user profile and any signals below describe the author of the reply being evaluated (the final post of the thread).\n is prepended to the message. This header tells the LLM explicitly that "this information is about the author of the reply being evaluated."

      • Below the header, UserRenderer.render(post.user) separately renders the name, handle, and bio of the reply author verified — thread.py:25-27, user.py:18-24. So the bios of two people are included: the author of the original post (post 0) and the author of the reply under evaluation.

    • Implications:

      • The follower count was already used as the grox reply_spam gating threshold (100k in Gen4+7), and now the LM verdict itself also references this signal directly.
      • Bio is strong evidence for spam and bot detection, so exposing the profiles of both the original post author and the reply-under-eval author together is expected to raise confidence.
      • The bio content that serves as evidence includes spam hints such as "link in profile", affiliation with political or commercial organizations, and interests.
      • Bios of other thread participants are not included (to prevent context explosion), and only the two authors' profiles are expanded.
  • The reply ranking score sent to Manhattan only goes down over time and never goes up verified — grox/flows/reply_spam/task_write.py (+22)
    • Inside _publish_to_reply_ranking_manhattan, it looks up the existing score with ReplyRankingScoreStratoLoader.fetch_reply_ranking_score(post.id).
    • If the new score is greater than the existing one, it skips the write and increments Metrics.counter("task.write_reply_ranking_manhattan.skipped.count", reason="higher_than_existing"). If it is lower, it writes as is.
    • Implications:
      • If a reply's first verdict comes out low (close to spam), that reply keeps a low score. Even if a new verdict becomes lenient, the serving score is not updated.
      • Conversely, a reply whose first verdict comes out high (lenient) is lowered if a later verdict becomes stricter.
      • This is consistent with the monotone safety direction of the reply spam verdict (once caught as spam, always treated as spam; only normal → spam reclassification is allowed).
      • It eliminates label flapping of the reply ranking score along the time axis at the source, so the ranking of the same reply does not go up and down in the UI or in A/B tests inferred.
      • Label flapping was likely actually observed in the reply ranking channel inferred.

Gen4+10 (2026-08-28, 24c6094) added a Kafka-first storage order and tie skipping, and made the follower count always injected into the coordinated spam verdict. verified

_publish_to_reply_ranking_manhattan was tightened in three ways on top of the monotone-only logic of Gen4+9 verified — grox/flows/reply_spam/task_write.py (+15/−21)

  1. Ties are not written either. The comparison operator changed from > to >=, so it skips if score >= existing.score.
    • Previously, when the new score equaled the existing one, it was written anyway (idempotent write).
    • When exactly the same score is recomputed, it saves the Manhattan put, and no Kafka event is emitted either.
    • The counter name also changed from higher_than_existing to not_lower_than_existing to make the semantics clear.
  2. The Kafka event moved ahead of the Manhattan write. The previous order was save_reply_ranking_score(Manhattan) → save_reply_ranking_kafka_v2(Kafka), and the new order is the reverse: Kafka publish first, Manhattan write second.
    • Reason inferred: Kafka is append-only and can be retried on failure, whereas Manhattan can hit the monotone-only logic and get a not_lower_than_existing verdict, so the retry itself may be skipped. Manhattan is also an upsert with side effects, so it is heavier than a Kafka publish. If Kafka succeeds first, the offline reprocessing pipeline can later recover a Manhattan write failure; if Manhattan succeeds first and the Kafka publish fails, downstream (serving cache warm-back, other consumers) cannot see the new score already reflected in Manhattan. In other words, Kafka-first is the durability order that guarantees consistent observability across the whole system.
  3. The try/except around fetch_reply_ranking_score was removed. Previously, if the fetch failed, it logged a warning and proceeded with existing = None, so it always wrote. Now it raises the exception upward as is, so the flow task is marked as failed and retried.
    • This blocks at the source the incident where a fetch fails silently, the monotone comparison is nullified, and an unexpected write goes through.
    • Defensive exception handling was removed, prioritizing logic correctness.

In the same commit, the follower count option of Gen4+9 was adopted as always on in the coordinated spam verdict verified — grox/flows/reply_spam/classifier_coordinated_spam.py (+5/−1)

  • An argument was added to _to_convo in classifier_coordinated_spam.py. It now calls PostRenderer.render(p, max_media=MAX_MEDIA_PER_POST) with include_follower_count=True.
  • The coordinated spam verdict receives the follower count of each participating account in the thread in the prompt. Bio keeps the include_bio=False default, and only the follower count is included.

Why it matters: The two axes Gen4+9 introduced changed in Gen4+10 as follows. The LM prompt user metadata expansion became always on. Manhattan monotone-only gained consistency through stronger idempotency and the Kafka-first order. The durability contract of the reply_spam verdict stack became much more explicit.

BDSM (abusive account detection from account behavior sequences) — enforcement note generation logic partially released in Gen4+1

BDSM is an account scorer that extracts abuse signals from an account's time-series behavior sequence. As of the c65aa17 commit (Gen4+1), the enforcement note generation logic is partially public verified(commit summary table). The logic for the conditions to create a note and for choosing the bot heads to put in the note is public, while the template string and the tuned verdict thresholds are not public verified(resolution record). The note carries a score for which bot family was triggered and how strongly, but the text explaining which action pattern caused it is not public verified(BDSM section text).

From Gen3 through early Gen4, build_enforcement_note at bdsm/runtime/score_results_sink_focal.py:78 was a stub that only did return None. The Gen4+1 commit released the gate logic and the dominant-head selection logic, leaving only the template string as a "<redacted>" sentinel verified — bdsm/runtime/score_results_sink_focal.py:78-128, bdsm/README.md, bdsm/proto/abuse_inference.proto:98-102.

  • A note is created only for a sequence with 30 or more actions in which some head other than LegitimateUser has a score above 0.5 verified — the three files in the previous paragraph.
    • The action count condition is MIN_ACTIONS = 30, total_actions >= 30, and the score condition is score > 0.5.
  • If the conditions pass, the head with the highest score is chosen as dominant, and the note string carries the names and scores of up to the top 3 heads verified — the three files in the previous paragraph.
    • The note string has the form "<redacted> [model: FollowBot=0.91, also: ReplySpamBot=0.60, LikeBot=0.53]".
    • Which bot family was triggered and how strongly goes out in the note as is, but the text explaining which action pattern triggered it is not public.
  • Seven bot heads were officially released verified — the three files in the previous paragraph.
    • The names are FollowBot, LikeBot, EngagementAmplifier, ReplySpamBot, TweetSpamBot, RTBot, and MultiActionBot.
  • The 9.99 filling the operating point (verdict threshold) in sink_policy.yaml is a sentinel, and the README states this explicitly verified — bdsm/runtime/sink_policy.yaml:5-13.
    • The operating point is a probability in the range [0, 1], so when it is filled with 9.99 it never triggers.
    • This means the gating structure and head names are real, and the tuned real numbers were not released, to prevent gaming.
  • Note that the head score carried in the note is a bot probability, not a "report reviewer decision" verified — the three files in the previous paragraph.
    • abuse-enforcement-service receives this note and decides the actual action (label/challenge/suspension).
    • Related changes on the abuse-enforcement-service (AES) side are in the AES generic_actions passthrough subsection of the change log.

How to read the source — caveat list

This list collects points of caution so that one does not judge "it is in the code, so it is true" when reading X's public source. As of the 2026-08-15 update, weights and constant values are filled in Gen4 xai-org/x-algorithm, and Phoenix can also be fully built, but it is not production scale verified(item 1). The score post-processing utilities and external service client modules that the Gen3 canon regarded as outside the repo are also included in the Gen4 release verified(item 1). In Gen3 code, files not connected to any module and files with syntax broken by literal substitution were also observed verified(items 2 and 3).

  1. xai-org/x-algorithm did not build through Gen3, and Gen4 partly resolved this. ⚠ This item was updated on 2026-08-15.

    • crate::params, missing in Gen3, was filled in Gen4 as home-mixer/params/param.rs verified.
      • This file is 1084 lines and is a production cron mirror of the weights and constants.
      • The canon's Gen3 observation that symbols like FavoriteWeight have only call sites and no definition is resolved verified.
    • crate::util, missing in Gen3, was filled in the Gen4 release as home-mixer/util/ verified — home-mixer/lib.rs.
      • vqv_weight and quoted_vqv_weight are in util/candidates_util.rs:19, 42.
      • score_normalizer, which Gen3 code called, is not in Gen4; the normalization stage itself is gone (Phoenix section).
    • crate::clients was also filled in the Gen4 release as home-mixer/clients/ (19 files) verified — home-mixer/clients/.
    • Phoenix became fully buildable in Gen4 verified.
      • It comes with a Cargo workspace, pyproject.toml, QUICKSTART, and synthetic data.
      • However, the README states explicitly that a small model can be trained and served: "a small model can be trained and served". It is not production scale verified.
    • Whether the neighboring crate (component_library) is still unreleased in Gen4 needs a deep dive.

    Reflecting the changes above, we redefine the character of the repo. Through Gen3 it was "only the shape of the logic released, values and wiring missing", and Gen4 moved to "values released + safety rules released + Phoenix runnable end to end, but the service glue layer still undisclosed". The missing parts are not accidental omissions but still show a consistent character.

  2. In Gen3 (0bfc279) code, the three scorers named in the README were cut off from the module tree. The README wrote "Weighted Scorer / Author Diversity Scorer / OON Scorer", but the actual pipeline was vec![phoenix_scorer, ranking_scorer, vm_ranker] verified — phoenix_candidate_pipeline.rs:299-300 vs README.md:251-255

    • scorers/mod.rs does not declare the three files, and there are 0 external references verified.
      • The three files are weighted_scorer.rs, author_diversity_scorer.rs, and oon_scorer.rs, and the struct names are WeightedScorer/AuthorDiversityScorer/OONScorer.
    • Yet those files contain hardcoded constants, so a reader following the README would mistake unreachable constants for production values verified.
      • An example of a hardcoded constant is p::AUTHOR_DIVERSITY_DECAY.
    • These three are not the only unconnected files. There are 11 .rs files in home-mixer/ not hooked by any mod declaration verified.
      • The 11 files are the following:
        • candidate_hydrators/engagement_counts_hydrator.rs
        • candidate_pipeline/{candidate,candidate_features,query,query_features}.rs
        • query_hydrators/{user_action_seq,user_features}_query_hydrator.rs
        • scorers/{author_diversity,oon,weighted}_scorer.rs
        • side_effects/cache_request_info_side_effect.rs
    • How to tell (Gen3 basis): dead files import crate::candidate_pipeline::{candidate, query}, while the live ranking_scorer.rs imports crate::models::{candidate, query}. Types with the same name exist in both directories, and models/ is current and candidate_pipeline/ is the older generation inferred. This was inferred only from the direction of the connections, and the commit history has no clue.
    • pub(crate) mod is also a declaration. ads/util.rs is hooked in ads/mod.rs:3 by pub(crate) mod util;, so it is live verified.
      • Counting with a regex like ^\s*(?:pub )?mod wrongly judges this file dead verified.
    • In the Gen4 release (47c1bcd), 10 of these 11 files disappeared from the repo, and engagement_counts_hydrator.rs was declared at candidate_hydrators/mod.rs:6 and connected verified. The README of the same release also no longer lists these three scorers verified — README.md.

  3. In Gen3 (0bfc279) code, there were places where string and number literals were mechanically replaced with "". Syntax was not checked, so some files had broken compilation or parsing verified.

    • For example, in grox/classifiers/content/safety_ptos.py:241-244, and is left without an operand, causing a SyntaxError, so the PTOS plan itself cannot be imported verified.
    • grox/tasks/task_summarizer_for_post_embedding.py:14 throws FileNotFoundError at import time, so Grox cannot start at all verified.
    • Neither file exists in the Gen4 release (47c1bcd) verified.

  4. git log --diff-filter=D <commit> shows the deletions of all ancestors, not the deletions of that commit. It would be wrong to conclude from this command's result that "the 2025 refresh deleted DiversityScorer.scala". That file was deleted on 2023-07-07 verified.

  5. If the the-algorithm-ml clone is a shallow clone, every file looks like a "new file". Weight history must not be read from such a clone verified.

  6. has_cached_posts is the most impactful switch, but it is a cache threshold, not a model. When 500 or more posts are stacked in the Redis warming cache, this boolean turns on, and then the retrieval sources and many hydrators turn off verified — cached_posts_query_hydrator.rs:11, 69

    • As of the 2026-10-17 commit (862a123), 25 files in home-mixer have a !query.has_cached_posts gate. These include 8 retrieval sources and 12 candidate hydrators verified — 862a123 home-mixer/ grep. In Gen3 code (0bfc279) there were 18 files.
    • On the same basis, the Phoenix scorer also has a has_cached_posts branch verified — phoenix_scorer.rs:70. EngagementCountsHydrator dropped this gate in the 2026-09-04 commit (Gen4+16) (cold start slot selector).
    • Much of "load more" during scrolling is answered from leftover candidates of the previous request without model inference verified.
    • How large that share is cannot even be inferred. The repo has no clue.

  7. In Gen3 (0bfc279) code, CoreDataHydrationFilter, despite its name, does not actually filter out candidates whose core data lookup failed. This is because the hydrator does not use author_id verified(code) — core_data_candidate_hydrator.rs:108-113, filters/core_data_hydration_filter.rs:13

    • The README describes this filter as "removes posts whose core metadata hydration failed".
    • We regard it as a bug inferred. Given the code flow, another explanation is hard to find.

  8. In Gen3 (0bfc279) code, all failures are silent. There is no framework-level timeout, circuit breaker, or fallback verified — candidate-pipeline/candidate_pipeline.rs:202-218, 266, 419-428

    • Sources and query hydrators that error out disappear verified.
    • If a candidate hydrator errors, the field is left unset verified.
    • Side effects run detached verified.

  9. In Gen3 (0bfc279) code, logging is sampled. The two richest log streams are unrepresentative slices verified — side_effects/reranking_kafka_side_effect.rs:14,29

    • The reranking Kafka log samples 5% in production and keeps only the top 50 verified.
    • The other one is kept only in shadow traffic verified.

  10. In the 2025 Scala code, some comments disagree with the code. Two comments on the low-signal user gate say "< 25 users", but the actual constant is SmallFollowGraphSize = 5. Quoting the threshold from the comments is off by 5× verified — SignalUtils.scala:17-23 vs AllowLowSignalUserGate.scala:12, DenyLowSignalUserGate.scala:12

  11. There is no single value called "ranker score". The 2025 MMR and the 2026 VMRanker both overwrite the score field. When looking at a score in logs or code, check which stage's value it is. This is why the 2026 code keeps weighted_score and score as separate fields verified — DiversityRescoringFeatureHydrator.scala:70, vm_ranker.rs:47-52, ranking_scorer.rs:277-281(both Gen3 code). In the 2026-10-17 commit (862a123), VMRanker also fills the two fields separately (vm_ranker.rs:93-131).

  12. The credibility thresholds in the abuse-enforcement-service rule files are not production values. The follower-count threshold already carried a comment saying "production uses a different threshold, and this value is a mock value to reduce gaming", and the 2026-10-24 commit (6258a15, Gen4+49) added the same comment to the credibility score threshold verified — enforcement_user.yaml. The same commit also deleted the "mirror of the GrowthBook dynamic config" notice on the first line of the post rule file (daily). Unlike the cron mirror, the numbers in the enforcement rules must not be read as production values verified.
