Gen4+14 (2026-09-02, 85ac72a) — home-mixer requests Phoenix backbone scores + scarecrow → XReview intake introduced + VF rules Box<dyn> removed + checkpoint in-envelope derived master key

This commit confirmed in code for the first time that the Phoenix ranker has two layers, a shared backbone and a reranker head. In the same commit, home-mixer started requesting backbone scores at all five feed endpoints, and a path was added for scarecrow's automated detection bots to put reports into the same XReview queue as user reports verified (daily).

This single commit contains the following changes:

  • The two-layer structure of the Phoenix ranker, backbone and head, became visible in the response wire.
  • A new gRPC pipeline lets scarecrow's automated detection bots submit reports to XReview programmatically, posing as user reports.
  • The VF rules refactor, which started in Gen4+11 and turned into data literals in Gen4+13, moved on to phase 2, so policy now sits in rodata rather than on the runtime heap.
  • The checkpoint encryption that Gen4+13 started now supports an in-envelope derived master key, and the encryption_context schema is enforced.
  • The Phoenix retrieval dwell default also changed from short to long.

A. Phoenix backbone scores response forced on the 5 feed endpoints

home-mixer requests backbone scores from Phoenix at all five feed endpoints verified — home-mixer/server.rs. Each endpoint hardcodes query.return_backbone_scores = true right before passing the request to Phoenix. There is no parameter gating. The five gRPC endpoints are ScoredPostsService, ForYouFeedService, the polling variant of ForYouFeed, RankedFollowingFeedService, and FollowingFeedService.

Backbone fields were added to both the request and the response of the Phoenix proto verified — phoenix/crates/serving/xai-recsys-proto/proto/recsys.proto. The request field is returnBackboneScores (#20). The response fields are backboneTopLogProbs (#10, repeated float) and backboneContinuousValues (#11, repeated float). By naming convention, Top corresponds to the top log probabilities of the discrete head and Continuous to the dense regression output.

PostCandidate gained a backbone score field, and the scorer parses the response into two layers verified — home-mixer/models/candidate.rs, home-mixer/scorers/phoenix_scorer.rs. The new field is backbone_scores: Option<PhoenixScores>. predictions.candidate_scores() is the output of the existing reranker head, and predictions.candidate_backbone_scores() is the output of the newly exposed backbone layer. The candidate carries the scores of both layers to the next stage from a single prediction round.

Why it matters This confirmed in code for the first time that the Phoenix ranker has a two-layer structure of a shared backbone and a reranker head. The previous canon had observed two things. From Gen4 it knew the top-level semantics, a "24-document engagement probability Transformer", and the rerankerHeadTag field in Gen4+11 (bc8e5f0) showed "multiple re-ranking heads". This commit confirms that a backbone layer sits below those heads and that its output is exposed as separate response fields. However, backbone_scores is only stored on the candidate, and no downstream consumer appears in this diff. So which of MultiRiskAdsBlender, VMRanker, DPP re-rank, and the attribution logger consumes the backbone logits is the point to watch.

Two other things changed alongside it:

  • The default of the Phoenix retrieval aggregation approach changed from short dwell to long dwell verified. In home-mixer/params/param.rs, the PhoenixRetrievalAggregationType default changed from DENSE_WITH_SHORT_DWELL → DENSE_WITH_LONG_DWELL.
    • This is a mirror commit whose file-header sync time was updated from 2026-09-01T16:42:25Z to 2026-09-02T16:03:45Z, so the value reflects the source catching up with a production feature switch that actually changed within a day.
  • A buffer guard was added to the batch preparation code of Phoenix serving (phoenix/crates/serving/xai-recsys-engine/src/python.rs). A .fill(0) guard and a copy_len > 0 condition were added together for the candidate embedding and search-query embedding slices. They prevent values left in a reused buffer from leaking out and a panic on an empty slice.

B. scarecrow (formerly Botmaker) → XReview intake gRPC pipeline introduced (new canon)

This commit created a programmatic path connecting scarecrow and XReview. It is a gRPC path through which scarecrow's automated detection bots put reports into XReview intake as if they were user reports. scarecrow is X's internal rule-based engine for automated detection and action, and XReview is the user report and moderation queue. scarecrow was inherited from Twitter's old Botmaker, and the com.twitter.botmaker package remains as is.

Two new function units that scarecrow can call were added verified — scarecrow/legacy/XReviewIntakeRegistry.scala (179 lines, new).

  • The action level of CreateXReviewReportProd is PROD_AGENT_WORKFLOW_ACTION.
  • The action level of CreateXReviewReportStaging is NO_ACTION, and it is a dry run.
  • There are 7 arguments: entityType ("post"/"profile"), entityId, userId, reportType (XReview allowlist), botId, optional note, and optional victimId.

The report payload fills the fields of the SubmitReportRequest proto as in the table below verified — scarecrow/legacy/XReviewReportBuilder.scala (59 lines, new).

XReview report key Value Meaning
subject "Botmaker report" Fixed report title
report_surface "x_app" Same surface as user reports
report_type Argument value (e.g., "bystander_impersonation") Discriminator for lane tag routing
report_source "proactive" A bot detection, not a user report ("user")
reporter_id "0" Bot reports have no reporter user id
detection_bot_id Argument value Which bot produced the report
detection_timestamp_ms context.startMillis() Goes into the uniqueness of the content-hash report id
victim_user_id Argument value (optional) Victim user id

Facts worth noting about the schema:

  • entityType is restricted to a "post"/"profile" whitelist. If an invalid value arrives, normalizeEntityType throws an IllegalArgumentException.
  • The XReview server distinguishes user reports from bot reports with the report_source = "proactive" field.
  • The uniqueness of a report is determined by the content-hash report id and detection_timestamp_ms. Even if the same bot detects the same content twice, the reports are separate when the timestamps differ, and XReview later aggregates them as an evidence rollup.
  • report_type is the discriminator for routing (lane tag) that selects the reviewer team inside XReview. The document quoted from scarecrow's own docs says: "Impersonation bots should use bystander_impersonation (lane tags key on that type, not generic impersonation)." If the wrong type is chosen, the lane is assigned wrongly, and the review is delayed or ignored.
  • The XReview connection goes through the shared library useng.common.xreview. This suggests that not only scarecrow but several internal X backends call XReview intake programmatically.

The submitter has 5 observability counters verified — scarecrow/legacy/XReviewReportSubmitter.scala (91 lines, new). The counters are attempted, submitted, skipped, unsupported_entity, and rpc_failed. The submitter attaches to XReview intake over mTLS (the xreview.tls.ca-cert flag) and is a noop in localMode()/personalAccountMode().

Why it matters This commit expanded X's moderation pipeline. The previous canon knew two layers: inline visibility-filtering and grox PtOS labeling. This commit reveals a third layer in code. When scarecrow reports to XReview automatically, XReview collects the reports as an evidence rollup and routes them to a human reviewer lane. It is not a path that filters inline but one that reports and aggregates asynchronously. ⚠ Claim reinforced: previously we understood the handoff from X's automated detection to human review as roughly "grox PtOS → policy service". This commit confirmed in code that one branch of that handoff shares the same XReview queue as user reports. The existence of XReview allowlist types such as bystander_impersonation means the impersonation response line is subdivided by lane.

C. VF rules restructuring phase 2 — Box<dyn Rule> removed, policy as a static table

The VF rule trait and the vector for dynamic dispatch disappeared from the code verified — visibility-filtering/rules/mod.rs (−155 lines). The targets are the Rule trait and Vec<Box<dyn Rule>>. The Rule trait definition, the evaluate_rules function, and 5 related unit tests were all removed.

Policy is now carried in rodata as a static table verified — visibility-filtering/rules/registry.rs. Its form is &'static [&'static [RuleSpec]].

Policies was renamed RuleEngine verified. This struct no longer owns a rule vector and wraps only a NsfwGatingCountries reference, so the new name states explicitly that it is the dispatch layer. RuleEngine::new() does no heap allocation.

The semantics of rule evaluation are unchanged.

  • Drop short-circuits.
  • If a Drop comes after an Interstitial, Drop wins; if there is none, the first one wins.
  • If the result is Allow, decided_by = None.

The composition of 9 home-common slices and 5 recommendation-only slices is the same as in Gen4+13. The new test wired_rule_names_are_unique_and_nonempty verifies that the names of the 15 rule slices are non-empty and do not overlap. The 15 is the 9 home-common and 5 recommendation-only slices plus FILTER_ALL verified — tweet_rules.rs:1130-1157.

Why it matters The direction of the refactor across the four commits from Gen4+11 to +14 is now clear. Rules move from code to data, policy moves from the heap to rodata, and naming is organized around the dispatch view. The next step is to load rule literals from a config file, which would allow changing rules without a code deployment inferred. However, that direction gives up the benefit of static dispatch, so it can only be confirmed by later commits.

D. Checkpoint encryption evolution — in-envelope derived master key + encryption_context enforced + mint_nonce auto-attached

The envelope header format of checkpoint files was defined verified — phoenix/python/training/xai-checkpointing/xai_checkpointing/dek.py.

  • The header is 4096 bytes, and the magic is b"XAIENC01".
  • wrapped_len (big-endian u32) is at offset 28–32, and context_len (u32) is at offset 32–36.
  • If the wrapped field has the form xai-dek1:<salt>:<master>, it is judged the "derived" approach; otherwise it is judged legacy per-file wrapping.

The reader uses the xai_encrypted tensorstore driver directly verified — phoenix/python/training/xai-checkpointing/xai_checkpointing/load.py. Gen4+13 used the xai_kms.KvServe KMS-proxy KvStore, which calls KMS on every IO. Now it unwraps the DEK once and decrypts symmetrically on the local machine. adopt_tree_dek uses the _DEK sidecar if there is one, and otherwise unwraps from the derived master key in the checkpoint file's envelope header, which keeps it backward-compatible.

The writer requires both keys, domain and run, in encryption_context verified — phoenix/xrex/train/checkpoint_write.py. If either is missing, a ValueError is raised. domain is the system domain (e.g., "recsys", "grox"), and run is the training run id. This rule forces the KMS audit log to record which run of which domain unwrapped which checkpoint and when.

mint_nonce = sha256(path) is automatically added to the encryption_context verified. The hash of the checkpoint path goes into the context automatically, so if an attacker copies a checkpoint to another path and tries to unwrap it, KMS rejects it because the context does not match. This uses the standard AWS-KMS encryption-context pattern.

_uses_tensorstore_save no longer enforces encrypt verified — phoenix/xrex/train/trainer.py. The two options were separated. save_checkpoint takes kms_client as an argument and assembles orbax_encrypted.get_encrypted_checkpointer itself. _AsyncCheckpointer waits through wait_until_finished of the orbax_encrypted module, so the flush guarantees completion of the encrypted IO.

Why it matters With this commit, enforced validation on the write path and support for two read-path formats (sidecar and in-envelope) are complete. Because the file format remains in code, audit tools and viewer tools can parse it later. With the KMS-proxy KvStore gone, restore latency drops significantly. When Phoenix loads a checkpoint made of tens of thousands of files, KMS calls drop from tens of thousands to one. However, whether CheckpointConfig.encrypt = True is on by default in the actual training config is still not in this diff either.

E. two-tower training config qk_norm=True, attn_logit_cap=-1

The two-tower training config turned on QK-norm and turned off the attention logit cap verified — phoenix/xrex/configs/xrecsys_two_tower.py. The values changed from qk_norm: False → True and attn_logit_cap: 80.0 → -1 (off). The two keys had been in the combined base as False and 80.0 since the Gen4 release verified — xrecsys_two_tower.py:274-275 at 47c1bcd. The combined base default became the same value 12 days after the 2026-08-21 commit (Gen4+6) put True and -1 into the nano config verified — :429-430 at 28e414f. Because QK-norm bounds the QK dot product, a separate logit cap is no longer needed.

Gen4+15 (2026-09-04, 9b0dc31) — grox thread-level multi-step reply spam classifier introduced + PTOS Illegal category dual setup with Gemma+Grok 4.1-fast + Phoenix serving SID sidecar fully removed + H100 remat policy + FA4 attention variable-length history support + large simplification of VF hydration/safety-label

grox gained a second path that looks at an entire reply thread at once and judges, together as spam, the replies that the same author added under their own replies verified. For the PTOS illegal and regulated behavior category, Gemma now handles the first pass and Grok 4.1-fast acts as the judge, and Phoenix serving uses the history SIDs carried in the request instead of an SID sidecar verified (daily).

A single commit changed 6 areas verified — xai-org/x-algorithm@9b0dc31. It touched 74 files with +1,363/−1,876, so the line count shrank on net.

  • In grox reply_spam, a new pipeline of five files and about 500 lines was added, and a second reply spam verdict path was formally wired in. This path puts the entire reply thread into the LLM and receives back "a list of post indexes in this thread to treat as spam".
  • Grok 4.1-fast (EAPI_GROK_4_1_FAST_X_ALGO) appeared in the PTOS policy judge stack as the cross-validator for the IllegalAndRegulatedBehaviors category. This started an asymmetric assignment against 4.5 X_ALGO (Gen4+7), the judge for the other categories. The same category was also promoted to the Gemma path (USE_GEMMA_CATEGORIES) in the first pass.
  • sid_client.rs (189 lines) and sid_retrieval_runner.py were deleted entirely from the Phoenix serving engine, and the xai-recsys-sid-proto dependency was removed. The SID retrieval sidecar is gone, and history SIDs now arrive directly in the request.
  • SAVE_H100_RECSYS = 32 was introduced in the Phoenix training remat policy. This is the first code signal that training also runs on the H100 generation besides GB300.
  • The FA4 attention kernel (ranker_attention_fa4.py, +139/−75) was rewritten. It now handles variable-length history directly (hist_valid_len, valid_block_upper/lower), and the cache is gone.
  • The hydration and safety_label_source stack of visibility-filtering got thinner overall, with a net reduction of 800+ lines.
    • The reductions are −378 in registry.rs, −206 in safety_label_source/codec.rs, −90 in hydration/mod.rs, and so on.

In addition, the Brazil2026ElectionFilter account list also received minor maintenance (166 account IDs added from a TSE update).

A. grox PlanMultiStepReplySpam — a second reply spam path that feeds the whole thread to Gemma and judges several follow-up replies as spam at once

This commit introduced a second verdict path that runs alongside the existing reply spam verdict. It puts the whole thread into the LLM prompt and has it mark several follow-up replies at once as "these indexes are spam". The existing grox reply_spam pipeline gave a one-shot verdict on a single reply and stored the result. That pipeline received flow unification, a follower threshold raised up to 100k, and a Kafka-first storage order across Gen4+2–+10. The multi_step in the name means the unit of judgment is several reply chains rather than an individual reply.

Six files were introduced (Plan/State/Task/Classifier/Prompt, plus the generators change) verified:

  • grox/flows/reply_spam/task_multi_step_reply_spam.py (206 lines)
  • plan_multi_step_reply_spam.py (29 lines)
  • classifier_multi_step_reply_spam.py (226 lines)
  • state_multi_step_reply_spam.py (13 lines)
  • prompts.py (+5, multi_step_reply_spam_system_prompt)
  • generators.py (+7, PlanMultiStepReplySpam.KEY injected into the two streams ReplyRankingTaskGenerator and ReplyRankingRecoveryTaskGenerator)

The conditions for entering a verdict are set by the entry gating TaskMultiStepReplySpamFilter verified — task_multi_step_reply_spam.py:

  • The target must be a reply. post.ancestors must exist, and none of them may be deleted (None).
  • The authors must exist. The users of the target post, the thread root, and the direct parent of the target post must all be alive.
  • The author must differ from the thread root author. Replies that the original poster adds to their own thread are skipped.
  • If the author is GROK_USER_ID or GORK_USER_ID, it is skipped. Replies posted by Grok/Gork themselves are not verdict targets.
  • The thread depth must be 2 or more. This means the reply chain must have two or more levels. That is, this pipeline is not entered for the single level of "root → first reply".
  • The direct parent's author must be the same as the target post's author. In other words, only a chain in which the same person replies again to their own reply enters. This is the typical self-thread spam pattern.
  • The root author must have 1,000 or more followers ("blast radius"). A verdict is made only when the root is an account with wide exposure. Reply spam under low-exposure accounts is pointless relative to the effort, so it is excluded.
  • If the reply author is a high page-rank v2 user or a grey badge user, it is skipped. Established accounts are out of scope. UserStratoLoader.is_high_page_rank_v2_user and is_grey_badge_user are looked up in parallel with asyncio.gather.

That exactly these 8 axes make up the gating is fixed in the canon. In particular, the sixth axis (the same author replying again to their own reply) explicitly defines the pattern this pipeline aims to catch. That pattern is a reply spam chain that steals root exposure through a self-conversation chain.

The LM prompt is built by MultiStepReplySpamScorer._to_convo verified — classifier_multi_step_reply_spam.py.

  • The system prompt is multi_step_reply_spam_system_prompt(). The README policy is that the original text is excluded from the export to prevent gaming.
  • The human message has two sections.
    • The "Reply Author Info" section renders the user profile of the reply author (UserRenderer.render(post.user)).
    • The "Thread" section lists all posts in the thread, numbered by index in the #### Post N format.
  • The prompt states explicitly that "Post 0 is the root (never flag), and the highest number is the reply being evaluated".
  • If the thread exceeds MAX_THREAD_SIZE = 10, only the first 5 and last 5 remain, and the middle is cut out.
  • The options are include_follower_count=True for each post, include_bio=True for the root only, and max_media=2.

This prompt design is also fixed in the canon. The task does not ask the LM whether an individual post is spam; it asks the LM to extract the set of spam indexes within the thread. The response is JSON with spam_post_indexes: list[int] and reason: str.

The LM is Gemma 2. The setting is model_name = GEMMA_2, and it is called through OaiSampler (grok_sampler/oai_sampler.py). Spam was already in grox's USE_GEMMA_CATEGORIES as of Gen4+9 (45b48ba), and this commit also added IllegalAndRegulatedBehaviors (section B below). The Gemma path appears to be a stack that X is pushing to cut its paid grok API budget inferred. That multi-step reply spam is Gemma-only from the start fits this trend.

Post-processing does not trust the LM output and goes through a 3-step safeguard verified:

  1. _drop_if_newest_reply_not_flagged discards the whole result if the verdict target (the last post of the thread) is not among the candidate indexes the LM returned. The Task entry condition is that "this reaction must be treatable as spam for the pipeline to run", so a result that judges the last reaction as not spam is a consistency violation.
  2. _drop_other_author_posts removes a post if the LM points to a post by another author in the thread as spam. This pipeline targets a chain in which the same author replies to their own reply, so a post by another author appearing in the result is ignored.
  3. _drop_singleton discards the result if it has exactly 1 item. Chain spam by definition targets "several follow-up replies", so a result with only one caught is not a valid result for this pipeline.

The set of indexes remaining after these three filters is the actual spam verdict.

The verdict is stored by TaskWriteMultiStepReplySpamReplyRanking verified:

  • _apply_reply_spam_label(post_id, author_id) is applied to each flagged post. It is the same helper the single-verdict pipeline uses.
  • The score is stored with ReplyRankingScoreStratoLoader.save_reply_ranking_score(..., ReplyRankingScore(score=0.0, reasoning=reasoning[-500:])). The score is forced to 0.0 (lowest confidence), and only the last 500 characters of the reasoning are kept.
  • It emits to v2 Kafka with save_reply_ranking_kafka_v2(..., ReplyRankingScoreKafka(...)).
  • DISABLE_RULES = [DisableTaskForNonProd] skips the write in non-prod. That is, no real label is applied in dev or staging.

The Plan DAG (PlanMultiStepReplySpam) chains tasks in the order filter, media hydration, detection, write verified:

task_multi_step_reply_spam_filter →
  task_media_hydration →
    task_multi_step_reply_spam_detection →
      task_write_multi_step_reply_spam_reply_ranking

The point to notice is that TaskMediaHydration runs only after the filter passes. Media hydration is costly, so it runs only after the filter has cut out a substantial share.

The new Plan joins two existing streams. Both stream generators add this Plan to their own PLANS_TO_INJECT set. One is ReplyRankingTaskGenerator (kafka TOPIC_UNIFIED_POSTS_V3), and the other is ReplyRankingRecoveryTaskGenerator. That is, this multi-step verdict runs in parallel from the same v3 event source, alongside the existing reply ranking, comment spam, and coordinated spam verdicts.

Why it matters This commit added a third axis to reply spam verdicts. That axis is the pattern of one author stealing root exposure through their own reply chain. The previous canon knew two flows. reply_spam judges individual replies, and coordinated_spam judges "repeated replies coordinated by multiple accounts". If coordinated spam is coordination on the account axis, multi-step is chain coordination on the time axis. Because the gating is set at a low threshold of 1k root followers (100k for the single-reply verdict), this pipeline appears to run broadly over threads whose root author has substantial exposure. It also fits the direction of running verdicts on Gemma to cut the grok API budget.

Some things are not yet public.

  • The system prompt original text (excluded from the export per the README)
  • The initial share of traffic on which this pipeline is active (the experiment gating is not in this diff)
  • Initial production metrics (measured values of counters such as multi_step_reply_spam.scored.count)
  • The tuning history of the gating constant (FOLLOWER_COUNT_THRESHOLD_FOR_SPAM_DETECTION = 1000)
  • How often the singleton drop actually fires (whether the LM tends to catch only the first seed of a chain)

B. PTOS SafetyPtosPolicyCrossValidator migrates the IllegalAndRegulatedBehaviors category from Grok 4.5 to Grok 4.1-fast + Gemma also assigned to first-pass (judge and primary axes move together)

The PTOS cross-validation judge starts using a different model per category with this commit verified. The SafetyPtosPolicyCrossValidator introduced in Gen4+7 (d011592) was a single-judge stack. It confirmed all three categories (ChildSafety, ViolentMedia, IllegalAndRegulatedBehaviors) on EAPI_GROK_4_5_X_ALGO. In this commit only IllegalAndRegulatedBehaviors switches its judge to a different model.

Grok 4.1-fast was registered as a judge verified — grox/flows/ptos/classifier.py:

The primary breaker and sample lines of _validate_illegal_and_regulated_behaviors changed. Previously they were _eapi_4_5_x_algo_breaker.guard() and self.eapi_4_5_x_algo.sample(...); now it is self.eapi_4_1_x_algo.sample(...). That is, the judge model for this category migrated from 4.5-X_ALGO to 4.1-fast-X_ALGO. The disappearance of the circuit-breaker guard is also worth noting. 4.1-fast is called directly without a breaker, while 4.5 was wrapped in a breaker. The metric name also changed from ..._cross_model_validate_with_grok_4_5 to ..._cross_model_validate_with_grok_4_1.

Why it matters The code now states explicitly that judge models are assigned per category. ChildSafety and ViolentMedia still use 4.5-X_ALGO, and only IllegalAndRegulatedBehaviors switched to 4.1-fast. The policy is to tune the judge model separately according to each category's difficulty, latency requirement, and judge disagreement characteristics. Given the fast suffix in the name and the direct call without a breaker, 4.1-fast is presumably a model that responds faster than 4.5 and is tolerable. The X_ALGO suffix suggests fine-tuning on the x-algorithm domain inferred.

IllegalAndRegulatedBehaviors was also promoted to the Gemma path at first-pass verified:

Previously only Spam was there. Now Gemma runs as first-pass for two categories.

The probability dial gate of SafetyPtosPolicyClassifier (use_oai_gemma4_dial) was removed verified. The dial value was 1.0 from the Gen4 release until just before this commit (classifier.py:490, 715 at 85ac72a). Previously there was a probability gate: if sample_for_gemma and not self.deluxe and self.use_gemma and random.random() < self.use_oai_gemma4_dial:. This commit removed the gate entirely, and the condition became if sample_for_gemma: ... oai_gemma4.sample(...). That is, categories in USE_GEMMA_CATEGORIES are routed 100% to Gemma, and grok handles only the fallback. When Spam was first introduced as a Gemma candidate in Gen4+9 (45b48ba), it started with a probability dial and was promoted unconditionally 15 days later. This commit adds IllegalAndRegulatedBehaviors, so both categories are now 100% Gemma.

IllegalAndRegulatedBehaviors was added as a target of the classify_policy_for_violation cross-model reclassify verified — grox/flows/ptos/task_safety_ptos_policy.py:

Previously only ViolentMedia took this reclassification path. In other words, IllegalAndRegulatedBehaviors now has a three-layer stack in this order: first-pass Gemma, deluxe cross-model reclassification (which is costly), and the Grok 4.1-fast judge cross-validator.

Why it matters It becomes clear that the PTOS verdict layer is evolving separately per category. Spam has used Gemma first-pass since the Gen4 release (dial 1.0). ChildSafety and ViolentMedia have used the Grok 4.5-X_ALGO judge since Gen4+7. With this commit, IllegalAndRegulatedBehaviors has three layers: Gemma first-pass, the Grok 4.1-fast judge, and reclassification. The dual stack that tunes judge and primary models separately per category continues. The Gemma promotion appears to aim at saving grok budget, and the 4.1-fast judge is lower in latency and cost than the 4.5 judge, which fits the budget-management direction inferred.

C. SID retrieval sidecar removed entirely from the Phoenix serving engine — history SIDs now arrive in the request

The sidecar path through which the Phoenix serving engine looked up SIDs separately was deleted, and history SIDs now arrive in the request verified.

SID sidecar code was deleted from the serving engine and inference code verified — phoenix/crates/serving/xai-recsys-engine/:

  • src/sid_client.rs (−189 lines) had the SemanticIdClient Rust client and the Python binding (PySemanticIdClient) removed entirely.
  • pub mod sid_client; was removed from src/lib.rs.
  • The xai-recsys-sid-proto dependency was removed from Cargo.toml. The same applies to pyproject.toml.
  • The SID client field was removed from the RecsysPredictorImpl and RecsysRetrievalPredictorImpl structs in src/python.rs.
    • The removed field is sid_client: Option<Arc<crate::sid_client::SemanticIdClient>>.
    • The sid_client: Option<&crate::sid_client::PySemanticIdClient> argument that the server_impl macro took was also removed.
  • Five lines of PySemanticIdClient stubs were removed from xai_recsys_engine.pyi.
  • phoenix/xrex/inference/sid_retrieval_runner.py (−17 lines) was deleted completely. It was the Python entry point of the SID retrieval runner.
  • The --sid_endpoint CLI argument and the assignment runner.sid_endpoint = args.sid_endpoint were removed from phoenix/xrex/inference/launch_inference.py.
  • The sid_endpoint: str | None = None field was removed from phoenix/xrex/inference/model_runner.py.
    • The 12 lines in create_server that assembled sid_client = xai_recsys_engine.PySemanticIdClient(...) were also removed.

The semantics that replaced it show in the remaining log verified. The log reads "Parsing history SIDs from the request (sid_num_levels=%d); no sid_endpoint". That is, history SIDs now arrive directly in the request. Previously, when sid_endpoint was set, there was a sidecar path in which the serving engine called a separate SID service to look up the SID codeword for each post_id in the user history. This commit removed that path. It has now migrated to a contract in which upstream (home-mixer and others) already includes the SIDs when it builds the request.

The default of use_pinned_d2h also changed False → True. D2H transfers through CUDA pinned host memory run at ~50 GB/s, versus ~3 GB/s for the JAX default. This saves ~29ms per inference. The option was introduced in Gen4+6, and this commit changed its default.

Why it matters The structure of the Phoenix retrieval SID pipeline was substantially cleaned up. The previous canon knew that phoenix-rankall manages the SID index window (video_14day and others) in Gen4. It also knew that seven SID fields were connected to VMRanker in Gen4+3, and understood the serving engine to have an optional SID sidecar. This commit confirms that the SID sidecar is gone from the serving engine entirely and that SIDs are carried directly in the request. That is, responsibility for SID codeword lookup migrated out of online serving. home-mixer extracts SIDs in advance at the candidate hydration stage and puts them in the request, and phoenix-rankall consumes them as they are. One extra gRPC call per request disappears, and the fault domain of the SID infrastructure narrows.

Some things are not yet public.

  • The name and source of the hydrator that fills SIDs in home-mixer (or the candidate hydration layer)
  • SID codeword storage(Manhattan? Strato?)
  • The point in time of the migration (whether there was a dual-write period under an experiment)

D. H100 policy introduced in Phoenix training remat (first signal that training also runs on H100 besides GB300)

A value for H100 was newly added to the remat policy of Phoenix training verified. The evidence is the enum in phoenix/xrex/models/remat.py:

SAVE_H100_RECSYS was registered with the new value 32. An elif policy == RematType.SAVE_H100_RECSYS branch was added to custom_remat_policy(policy). This branch stores the same name list as GB300 as rematerialization checkpoint targets.

  • The name list is attn_outputs, dense_outputs, dense_outputs_individual, attn, gate_up_proj, dense_up_proj, query_heads_rope, key_heads_rope, cutedsl_attn_outputs, query_heads, key_heads, value_heads, and scalar_stats.

The two policies share the same name list but have separate enum values. This structure leaves open the possibility that different tuning (for example, presets for stored-tensor priority) will later be attached to GB300 and H100 separately.

Why it matters By stating the H100 remat policy in code, this commit left the first signal that X distributes training across two hardware generations, GB300 and H100. The previous canon confirmed that Phoenix production training runs on GB300 when _GB300_OVERRIDES appeared in Gen4+6. Whether H100 is used for training was not mentioned. GB300 is the flagship, and H100 may be for secondary, backfill, or research use inferred. A hardware-specific config block such as _H100_OVERRIDES does not yet exist in this commit. It is a checkpoint to watch in the next commit.

E. Phoenix ranker_attention_fa4 — native support for variable-length history + cache removal

The FA4 attention kernel now handles histories of differing lengths directly, without padding.

The FA4 kernel previously assumed that "history is always filled exactly to a multiple of the tile size (128)" verified — phoenix/xrex/cutedsl/ranker_attention_fa4.py. FA4 is flash attention v4 based on NVIDIA CUTLASS/CUTe DSL. The previous signature was build_dense_block_sparse_layout(batch_size, seq_len, hist_len, num_q_heads) (four arguments, including a batch argument). It is now (seq_len, hist_len, num_q_heads, hist_valid_len). The new argument hist_valid_len takes the actual number of valid history tokens for each item in the batch.

The computation moved from numpy to jax.numpy. Previously, import numpy as np was used to build the layout in advance on the python host and cache it (_DENSE_BS_LAYOUT_CACHE). This time it was rewritten in a JIT-friendly way with jnp.where, jnp.arange, and jnp.broadcast_to, and the cache was removed. The reason is clear. Because hist_valid_len differs per batch, the layout became a function of batch data rather than a deterministic function, and python host caching becomes meaningless.

New fields valid_block_upper and valid_block_lower were added. So that the attention mask can handle partial-history blocks, the upper and lower bounds are computed per batch and passed to the kernel. A partial-history block is a case where the number of actually valid tokens within a history tile is at most the tile size. is_partial = is_hist & (t == n_full) & (has_partial == 1) marks the position of the partial block. full_q_seq and mask_q_seq compute valid token positions as indices in the forward and backward passes respectively.

The signature of ranker_attention_fa4 widened. Two optional arguments, valid_block_upper and valid_block_lower, were added, and when no value is given they fall back to zero-fill. custom_vjp packs and unpacks them as bs_args = (*fwd_bs, *bwd_bs, valid_block_upper, valid_block_lower) so that the new arguments are also included in the gradient computation. input_output_aliases shifted from {12: 0, 13: 1, 14: 2} to {14: 0, 15: 1, 16: 2}. This is because the two new arguments were attached at the front.

Why it matters The FA4 kernel now handles varlen history directly, without needing padding. Previously, short histories (for example, new users) were padded up to the tile size, so the set of positions to attend to grew or the actual attention semantics were likely contaminated. This kernel handles upper and lower bound masking of partial blocks internally, so it computes exact attention without padding. Training and inference accuracy improve for new users and short sessions. In Gen4+6, attn_impl="cutedsl_ranker_varlen_attn" was the attention kernel of the GB300 override. We can understand that varlen semantics as having been extended to the history axis in this commit. A new observation is added to the attn kernel axis of sequence-transformer-ranking.

Gen4+16 (2026-09-04, 902a06f) — symmetric wiring of codivert impressions in the cold-start experiment + treatment viewers restricted to Phoenix MoE candidates + experiment_overrides map and SlateContext.exact_k/exact_gap added to the Phoenix serving contract + devel app_env added to VF dark-traffic mirroring + upcoming VF muted-keyword rule signal

The control and treatment arms of the cold-start experiment now leave the same bucket impressions, and cold-start candidates for treatment viewers were narrowed to Phoenix MoE candidates verified. A per-request experiment param override and two slate metric fields were added to the Phoenix serving request verified (daily).

One commit changed three axes in an interlocking way verified — xai-org/x-algorithm@902a06f. The scale is 25 files, +472/−179.

  • AuthorColdStart::apply reordered its execution order. Now the control and treatment arms leave experiment bucket impressions symmetrically (the codivert pattern).
  • Fields were added to the Phoenix serving request contract. experiment_overrides: map<string, string> is a per-request experiment param override, and SlateContext.exact_k and exact_gap are two optional uint32 metric fields.
  • VF dark-traffic mirroring now recognizes the devel app_env (per-PR preview deployments) in addition to staging.

In addition, CoreFeature.text was explicitly preserved as dead code for the upcoming muted-keyword rule. In the VF stack, a large-scale cleanup from pub to pub(crate) took place.

A. The two arms of the cold-start experiment leave codivert impressions symmetrically verified — home-mixer/scorers/author_cold_start.rs, home-mixer/params/param.rs.

The new params are rust_home_mixer_phoenix_moe_codivert_viewer_is_control and rust_home_mixer_phoenix_moe_codivert_viewer_is_treatment (bool, default false). A symmetric YAML rule was created for the moe_codivert_viewer experiment. The treatment and control arms split symmetrically by enable_viewer_cold_start_boost=true/false. The core reordering is the following sequence.

  • First, ColdStartParams::read(query) bundles the param lookup into one step, and the viewer_arm bucket impression is always left.
  • Next, record_tracked_ids is called.
  • Then, if params.arm != Holdout, author_corpus(...) is called regardless of whether the feature is enabled, leaving the author bucket impression.
  • Only after that does it return early on the enabled gating.

Because it returns after leaving the impressions, the observation log shape of the two arms becomes symmetric. The previous version returned early before leaving impressions when !EnableViewerColdStart.

New regression tests lock in this symmetry.

  • both_arms_log_the_same_codivert_impressions verifies that control and treatment each leave exactly 3 moe_codivert_viewer impressions.
  • both_viewer_arms_log_the_same_author_impressions verifies that both arms leave exactly 2 moe_exp (author-targeted) impressions.

Impression counts are instrumented with the test utility SpyingBucketImpressor (exposed by the experiment SDK). It is a culture observation that X enforces A/B bucket observation symmetry through regression tests.

B. The cold-start treatment candidate filter was narrowed to apply only to Phoenix MoE candidates verified — same file:

Previously it checked only corpus == AuthorCorpus::Treatment. This time the condition && is_phoenix_moe(c) was added, and this condition means served_type == ForYouPhoenixRetrievalMoe. Now the cold-start candidates of a treatment viewer are only those that are posts from treatment corpus authors and also come from the Phoenix MoE source. The test name also changed from treatment_viewer_keeps_treatment_moe_and_cold_starts_treatment_corpus to treatment_viewer_cold_starts_treatment_moe_only. Cold start and Phoenix MoE are now bundled in a single codivert experiment, isolating the two effects so that they are not confounded.

Gen4+17 (2026-09-08, 49815da) — ranking scorer per-head weight perturbation + grox v8-search multimodal embedding stack introduced + ContentFeatures enters the Phoenix wire + PTOS adult leading-frames rescan path + FA4 attention kernel SM80·SM90 forward·backward fully open-sourced

The ranking side gained a mechanism that perturbs per-behavior weights on every request, but the default perturbation magnitude is 0.0, and the post information the ranker receives gained a content-features field verified (items A and C). The safety verdict gained a path that re-examines the first 10 seconds of videos of 30 seconds or longer that have already passed through PTOS, and a search-only embedding pipeline and the release of attention kernel backward code are in the same commit verified (items B, D, E). This commit is covered in the daily.

One commit moved on five axes at once verified — xai-org/x-algorithm@49815da. It changed 78 files, with +10,938/−982 lines.

  • The ranking scorer perturbs the weights of 26 engagement heads on every request by exp(±sigma). The newly added ScoringWeights::perturbed() in home-mixer/scorers/ranking_scorer.rs does this, and the sign is set deterministically by md5(salt:user_id:head).
  • A v8-search embedding stack dedicated to the search surface was added under grox/flows/mm_emb/. It adds 12 new files (+1,026 lines) and modifies 5 existing files (+171 lines).
  • The Phoenix serving proto gained a ContentFeatures message and the TweetInfo.contentFeatures and quotedContentFeatures fields. The values are built by the new file home-mixer/models/content_features.rs (185 new lines) using Twitter's weighted-text rules.
  • grox/flows/ptos/ gained an 8-stage DAG PlanSafetyPtosAdultContentLeadingFrames and an entry filter, which crop the first 10 seconds of a video and re-judge it. To enter, a video must be 30 seconds or longer, must already have passed PTOS without an NSFW verdict, and must also exceed the deluxe fav threshold.
  • phoenix/xrex/cutedsl/ranker_fa4/ gained 6 new files (7,080 lines in total): flash_fwd, flash_fwd_sm90, flash_bwd, flash_bwd_sm90, flash_bwd_preprocess, and ampere_helpers. X.AI released in full its modified SM80/SM90 forward and backward kernels, forked from the original Dao-AILab flash-attention, and the original backward pass is released for the first time here.

Beyond that, phoenix/xrex/utils/aot.py sanitizes CutlassCall device blobs into SHA256 digests to stabilize the AOT cache. copy_port_client.rs checks for MANIFEST.json and picks only checkpoints whose bundling is finished, and quote_hydrator.rs gained parallel MediaInfoCacheClient hydration.

A. The ranking scorer perturbs per-head weights on every request (per-head weight perturbation) verified — home-mixer/scorers/ranking_scorer.rs, home-mixer/params/param.rs.

There are two new params. WeightPerturbationSigma is an f64 with a default of 0.0. WeightPerturbationSalt is a String with a default of "". .perturbed(query) is chained after ScoringWeights::from_params(&query.params). On each request, if sigma > 0, each of the 26 heads is scaled by multiplying weight *= (sigma * perturbation_sign(salt, user_id, head)).exp(). perturbation_sign is a deterministic ±1 set by md5(format!("{salt}:{user_id}:{head}"))[0] & 1. negative_sum, positive_sum, and total_sum are recomputed from the perturbed values in recompute_sums().

The target heads number 26 in total.

  • 18 core positive: favorite·reply·retweet·photo_expand·video_open·click·open_link·profile_click·vqv·share·share_via_dm·share_via_copy_link·dwell·quote·quoted_click·quoted_vqv·follow_author·post_unexplored
  • 3 continuous: dwell_time·click_dwell_time·active_secs_5m_residual_norm
  • 5 negative: not_interested·block_author·mute_author·report·not_dwelled

The sync timestamp in the param.rs header changed to 2026-09-04T16:22:24Z → 2026-09-08T16:24:06Z.

For the same (salt, user_id), the 26 heads get independent signs, and changing the salt reshuffles the per-user assignment entirely. At σ=0.1 the weights are perturbed by about ±10.5%, and at σ=0.3 by about ±35%. This is multiplicative noise that is symmetric in log-space. The mechanism can be read as Bandit-style exploration (gradient-free) or as infrastructure for measuring A/B weight sensitivity on production traffic inferred. Because the default is 0.0, default production behavior is still deterministic.

B. grox gained v8-search, a multimodal embedding stack dedicated to the search surface verified — grox/flows/mm_emb/.

  • There are four Plans:
    • mm_emb_v8_search: real-time, grox-multimodal-embedding-requests-with-summary topic
    • mm_emb_v8_search_for_reply: for replies, content-understanding-...-min-traction-for-grox-multi-modal topic
    • mm_emb_v8_search_backfill and mm_emb_v8_search_backfill_batch: backfill of past posts, grox-multimodal-embedding-backfill topic
  • The embedder is embedder_v8_search.py (113 lines). It looks up the two endpoints RECSYS_V8_SEARCH_EMBED and RECSYS_V8_SEARCH_BACKFILL_EMBED through grox_config.get_embedding_model. It calls embed_openai_async(text, images) through XaiEmbeddingClientHttp (an OpenAI-compatible embed API), with a timeout of 60 seconds. The result is re-normalized with L2. The author's core information is fetched in parallel with StratoUserCore().fetch(user_id) and passed to the renderer.
  • The renderer is renderer_v8_search.py (461 lines). The media budget is 16 frames counting the original and quoted media together (MAX_MEDIA=16), and the number of frames the embedder actually requests is MAX_FRAMES=4. The rendered result consists of the elements below:
    • instruction prefix "Represent this X post (formerly Twitter) for recommendation: capture its topic, intent, key entities, and likely engagement."
    • author block: the follower count in two forms, a human-readable notation and a tier label
    • body: up to 4000 characters, with dangling media URLs removed
    • quoted post (1000 characters), ASR (2000 characters), card title (100 characters), article title (200 characters)
  • The fav threshold for backfill adjusts itself according to throughput. The implementation is adaptive_min_fav.py (63 lines).
    • The controller is AdaptiveMinFav(start=20000, target_qps=5.0, gain=0.3, deadband=0.1, window_s=30.0, floor=0, cap=20000, warmup_s=60.0).
    • This PI controller observes the actual pass QPS and adjusts the fav threshold every 30-second window. It raises the threshold when the pass QPS is above the target and lowers it when it is below.
    • It is a pure PI controller with no side conditions. error = (qps - target) / target, and if |error| ≤ deadband it makes no adjustment. Otherwise it updates with min_fav *= 1 + gain * clamp(error, -1, 1).
    • TaskBackfillFavGate throttles posts with an insufficient fav count, observing them as task.backfill_gate.dropped.count{reason=low_favs}.
    • TaskBackfillPreloadGate skips posts that are already embedded with V8_SEARCH_MODEL_VERSION = "v8_search_1". Only posts that pass are counted in the rate calculation through _min_fav.observe_pass().
  • The fanout is handled by task_backfill_fanout.py (85 lines). BackfillIdBatch.post_ids (a byte-packed <q list in the kafka value) first goes through BackfillConsumerDedup to check whether it is seen for the first time. Then fav counts are hydrated in parallel by BatchedFavHydrator, and Plans run in parallel under the cap of asyncio.Semaphore(FANOUT_CONCURRENCY=240). Exceeding task_timeout raises TimeoutError, and results are recorded as task.backfill_fanout.posts.count{result=executed|failed}.

This stack attaches a vector space dedicated to the search surface, separate from v5 and v8.2. It pairs with the Phoenix xrecsys_search config of Gen4+4. With it, both the search ranking model and its paired search document embedding pipeline are in place. However, the actual model behind the two RECSYS_V8_SEARCH_EMBED endpoints (dim, base architecture, training data) and the connection to the retrieval index are not public.

C. ContentFeatures entered the Phoenix wire format verified — phoenix/crates/serving/xai-recsys-proto/proto/recsys.proto, phoenix/python/common/xai-proto/proto/recsys.proto, home-mixer/models/content_features.rs (185 new lines).

The builders build(candidate: &PostCandidate) -> ContentFeatures and build_quoted(...) are pure functions. TextMetrics::of(text, attachment_urls) follows Twitter's text length counting rules as they are.

  • A URL always counts as 23 characters (URL_WEIGHTED_LEN). This corresponds to the t.co shortener.
  • CJK characters, emoji bases, and punctuation count as 2 characters (outside SINGLE_WEIGHT_CODEPOINT_RANGES).
  • ASCII, basic Latin, and certain ranges count as 1 character.
  • ZWJ and skin-tone modifiers (0xFE0E·0xFE0F·0x1F3FB..0x1F3FF·0xE0020..0xE007F) count as 0 characters.
  • The first media attachment URL is subtracted from the external URL count (external_urls = urls.saturating_sub(attachment_urls)).

Five regression tests pin down these rules:

  • weighted("hello world")=11
  • weighted("日本語")=6
  • weighted("see https://t.co/abc123 now")=3+1+23+1+3
  • weighted("ok 👍🏽")=2+1+2: the skin-tone modifier is 0 characters.
  • weighted("日本\u{3000}語")=4+2+2: the ideographic space also counts as CJK.

media_attachment_url_is_not_an_external_link pins down the distinction between a media URL and an external link.

Why it matters The ranker receives structural signals of the text itself on the wire as first-class inputs. weighted_text_len is a signal for "how full it is / whether it is a pass-through with only a URL attached", newline_count for formatting, and has_url for external navigation. However, this commit has no code in phoenix/xrex/models/recsys_model.py that embeds these fields. They are carried on the wire, but whether training consumes them is something to observe in the next commit.

D. PTOS gained a leading-frames deep rescan path that re-judges whether the beginning of a video contains adult content verified — grox/flows/ptos/plan_safety_ptos_adult_content_leading_frames.py (56 lines), grox/flows/ptos/task_safety_ptos_adult_content_leading_frames_filter.py (81 lines), grox/flows/ptos/constants.py (+15).

PlanSafetyPtosAdultContentLeadingFrames is an 8-stage DAG in the order rate_limit → leading_frames_filter → media_hydration → category_detection → policy_detection → safemodel_sex_nudity → cross_validation → sink_write. The entry filter is a 6-stage gate.

  1. post.user must exist.
  2. post.get_fav_count() >= deluxe_fav_count_threshold must hold. This is the deluxe tier threshold introduced in Gen4+12, for cost control.
  3. post.media or post.quoted_post.media must contain a video of 30 seconds or longer (ADULT_CONTENT_LEADING_FRAMES_MIN_DURATION_SECONDS = 30.0).
  4. A prior PTOS verdict must exist (StratoSafetyPostAnnotationsResultDirectMh.fetch(post_id) is non-null). Only posts that have already passed through the PTOS pipeline once are eligible.
  5. The prior verdict must not be NSFW (prior.safetyBoolMetadata.isNsfw is false).
  6. The prior must have an AdultContent violated policy, or the fav count must be 512 or more (ADULT_CONTENT_LEADING_FRAMES_UNCONDITIONAL_FAV).

For videos that pass, video.crop_seconds = 10.0 (ADULT_CONTENT_LEADING_FRAMES_CROP_SECONDS) is set, so media hydration crops only the first 10 seconds for judgment.

The deluxe tier task types are DELUXE_TIER_TASK_TYPES = frozenset({SAFETY_PTOS_DELUXE, SAFETY_PTOS_SPECIAL_VIDEO, SAFETY_PTOS_ADULT_CONTENT_LEADING_FRAMES}). The new kafka topic is safety-ptos-adult-content-leading-frames.

Why it matters This path follows the special-video path of Gen4+12 and the 3-category cross-validator of Gen4+7, and is the third defense layer aimed at temporal evasion that disguises the first few seconds. The special-video path counters static-overlay evasion, and the cross-validator allows only demotion. The reason isNsfw is false even though the prior has an AdultContent violated policy is that the cross-validator allows only demotion. This path is a second judge that can overturn a demoted verdict again. The unconditional-entry threshold of 512 fav is the scale of a mid-popularity post in production.

E. The SM80·SM90 forward·backward of the Phoenix FA4 attention kernel were fully open-sourced verified — phoenix/xrex/cutedsl/ranker_fa4/.

The changes are 6 new files and 4 modified files.

File Status Lines Role
flash_fwd.py added 1,333 SM80/Ampere forward
flash_fwd_sm90.py added 1,465 SM90/Hopper forward
flash_bwd.py added 1,954 SM80/Ampere backward
flash_bwd_sm90.py added 1,864 SM90/Hopper backward
flash_bwd_preprocess.py added 329 pre-bwd dO·row_sum·softmax_LSE
ampere_helpers.py added 135 SM80 utilities (warp shuffle, register layout)
block_sparse_utils.py modified +412/−314 Rewrite of the block-sparse iterator
ranker_attention_fa4.py modified +273/−130 Refactor of the fwd entry point
ranker_attention_varlen_fa4.py modified +178/−211 Migration and cleanup of Gen4+15 varlen support
mask.py modified +63/−1 AttentionMask extension (for bwd)

The newly added code totals 7,080 lines verified — sum of the per-file added lines in 49815da. The file headers read # Derived from flash-attention (https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention); modified by X.AI Corp. and SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 Copyright 2026 X.AI Corp.. What was open-sourced this time is X.AI's modified fork based on the original Dao-AILab/flash-attention. The phoenix/NOTICE file also gained +198 lines of copyright notices for the flash-attention subcomponents.

The main features of the kernels are as follows:

  • It is based on CuTeDSL (the cutlass Python DSL).
  • It supports asymmetric attention with head_dim != head_dim_v.
  • It supports pack_gqa (Grouped Query Attention).
  • It has the options is_causal, is_local, score_mod, mask_mod, and has_aux_tensors.
  • There are two schedulers, SingleTileScheduler and SingleTileVarlenScheduler (fixed and varlen).

The backward settings are m_block_size=64, n_block_size=128, num_stages_Q=2, num_stages_dO=2, and num_threads=256. The _bs_bwd_seq_at constexpr subtile maps the domain indices of the mask, full, and diag iterators of block-sparse backward. flash_bwd_preprocess.py precomputes dO·row_sum using the softmax_LSE (log-sum-exp) saved in forward.

Why it matters:

  • The original backward pass was open-sourced for the first time. Gen4+15 released the rewrite of forward varlen support, but backward is first here. Backward, which is essential for training, existed only in X's internal repository, and the open-source mirror had released only forward.
  • The wiring on the SM90 (H100) side is confirmed. The SAVE_H100_RECSYS = 32 remat policy in Gen4+15 was "the first code signal that H100 training is running". This commit explicitly contains two SM90 files for forward and backward, so the wiring on the H100 training side is complete. X maintains attention kernels optimized separately for two hardware generations, GB300 (SM100) and H100 (SM90).
  • X chose a strategy of reusing the flash-attention upstream. Rather than writing CuTeDSL from scratch, it forks and modifies the Dao-AILab original. This is a signal that the attention kernel is standardized infrastructure verified by the LLM community, and that X has not departed from that standard.

Not public are the benchmarks of the SM90/SM80 kernels (GB/s, TFLOPS, speedup over baseline) and where the sparse patterns of block_sparse_utils.py are actually used.

Other changes

  • Replaced the CutlassCall device blob with a SHA256 digest, so the JAX AOT cache has a stable cache key for the same CUDA kernel binary and avoids repeated recompilation verified — phoenix/xrex/utils/aot.py (+54/−1).
    • _sanitize_cutlass_calls replaces the module field in the backend_config of the StableHLO stablehlo.custom_call{target=CuteDSLRT_NvJaxCutlassCall} with a SHA256 digest (device_digest:<hex>). This field is an ELF/fatbin byte sequence.
    • cutlass_module_device_digest parses the ELF header and hashes only the device blob section.
    • AOT_CACHE_VERSION also changed "20260705" → "20260904".
  • Serving-side checkpoint discovery now picks only checkpoints whose bundling is finished verified — phoenix/crates/serving/xai-recsys-engine/src/copy_port_client.rs (+207/−9).
    • full_prefixes_newest_first was split out as a helper that returns the prefixes present across the whole channel, newest first.
    • select_bundle_checkpoint picks the newest checkpoint for which export/MANIFEST.json is non-empty on every channel. A newest checkpoint that is still unbundled is skipped with a warn log.
    • download_named_files downloads a specified list of file names atomically.
    • The .mlirbc bundle system (StableHLO export) of Gen4+13 is now fully connected in the serving loader as well.
  • The serving sequence_len is now computed automatically verified — phoenix/xrex/train/recsys_bundle_export.py (+48).
    • _serving_sequence_len back-computes sequence_len - history_seq_len - candidate_seq_len * (1 + num_negatives) - num_global_negatives = prefix_tokens from the training config and checks that it matches num_user_prefix_tokens.
    • Then it overrides the attention kernel size with the serving sequence_len = prefix + history + candidate.
    • model_sequence_len was also added to the MANIFEST.
  • quote_hydrator.rs was extended verified (+142/−12).
    • MediaInfoCacheClient is injected as a new dependency.
    • get_quoted_content looks up the core data and media info of the quoted post in parallel within a 200ms timeout, and caches them in QuickCache<u64, QuotedContent>.
    • This extension is an upstream condition for wiring up ContentFeatures.quotedContentFeatures in Gen4+17.
  • The media info lookup in media_info_hydrator.rs was refactored, and max_video_duration_ms and the like needed for the content features computation are hydrated here verified (+70/−15).
  • The entire file home-mixer/bin/pipeline_components_json.rs was deleted (76 lines) verified. It was likely an offline debugging JSON dump utility inferred.
  • The PTOS reclassification trigger was extended verified.
    • In task_safety_ptos_policy.py (+4/−1), policy detection also handles re-judgment from the leading-frames path.
    • TaskRateLimitSafetyPtosAdultContentLeadingFrames was added to task_rate_limit.py.
  • The Pipeline core signatures were cleaned up in 8 candidate-pipeline files, with no semantic change verified (+103/−38).
  • The proto in VF safety_label_source/proto.rs was slightly expanded verified (+34/−38).
  • image.py (+42/−19), subtitles.py (+3/−1), and video_frames.py (+7/−7) in video_tools were slightly modified verified.
  • A new API was added to the VF client in visibility-filtering-client/vf_client.rs verified (+119/0).
  • The grox reply_spam code was cleaned up verified.
    • This was a small touch-up of the multi-step reply spam pipeline introduced in Gen4+15, and the removed lines are in task_write.py (−17) and task_multi_step_reply_spam.py (−9).

Five things are not public.

  • the actual production σ value of the weight perturbation and the salt assignment logic
  • the dim, base model, and retrieval index connection of the v8-search embedding
  • which ranking heads actually use ContentFeatures, and how
  • benchmark figures for the FA4 SM80/SM90 kernels
