Gen4+18 (2026-09-09, 75d93d9) — VF verdict axis refactor (FilteredReason → Action) + new ad format header-image-prompt-ad + grox preview thumbnail for videos over 30 seconds + broadcast formally enrolled in the PTOS safety pipeline + all multimodal embeddings disabled in the ranking training config

Starting with this commit, visibility-filtering filters candidates by an explicit action value instead of the reason they were filtered out, and the home timeline gained a sixth ad format verified (items A and B). Live broadcasts entered the PTOS safety pipeline, and multimodal post embeddings were turned off in both ranking training configs verified (items D and E). This commit is covered in the daily.

This commit is about +801/−252 lines across 28 files, and five axes moved together verified — xai-org/x-algorithm@75d93d9.

A. The criterion of the VF verdict changed from FilteredReason to Action

TweetVisibility now has an action: Action field as a formal member, in addition to the existing reason: Option<FilteredReason> and safety_labels. The Action variants are Allow, Interstitial, Avoid, Downrank, Drop(DropReason), Tombstone, and NotEvaluated. StratoVfClient derives the action from the FilteredReason received from Strato through action_from_strato_reason. There are four derivation rules:

  • None → Allow
  • Some(SafetyResult) with NotEvaluated → Allow
  • Some(SafetyResult) with other → unchanged
  • Some(other reason) → Drop(DropReason{})

The gRPC path maps the result.action returned by the server as it is, and sets NotEvaluated if it is absent. PostCandidate has a visibility_action: Option<Action> field, and VFFilter::filter splits candidates with should_drop_action (see line 392 in the ranking and filter section above). should_drop_ancillary also decides based on the action of ancestor, quoted, and retweeted posts. FilteredReason::ViewerBlocksAuthor was added as a formal variant verified. It covers the case where the viewer blocks the author, and is the symmetric direction of the existing AuthorBlockViewer. However, no rule code returns this reason yet verified — visibility-filtering-client/vf_client.rs (+130/−62), visibility-filtering-client/models.rs (+7), home-mixer/filters/vf_filter.rs (+27/−69), home-mixer/candidate_hydrators/vf_candidate_hydrator.rs (+159/−23).

⚠ Canon claim updated. The previous canon said: "VFFilter is fail-closed. Every FilteredReason variant other than SafetyResult is an unconditional drop." The new verdict function has entirely different syntax, but the fail-closed character is retained. Non-SafetyResult reasons are already converted to Drop at the client layer, and NotEvaluated is also a drop. Only one thing changed. Downrank and Avoid became explicit keep targets. Previously this was ambiguous depending on the path.

B. The home timeline gained a sixth ad format, header-image-prompt-ad

It follows the existing five formats (promoted-tweet · preroll video · SSP/RTB Trend Takeover · rtb-image-ad · GoogleSDKNativeAd). At the very start, marshal_ad() checks whether AdIndexInfo.header_image_prompt_ad_info: Option<HeaderImagePromptAdInfo> is present, and if so branches to marshal_header_image_prompt_ad. This path marshals the ad as the URT TimelineEntryContent::Item(TimelineItem { content: TimelineItemContent::Message(MessagePrompt { content: MessageContent::HeaderImagePrompt(HeaderImagePrompt { .. }) }) }). The Entry ID format is header-image-prompt-ad-<impression_hex>.

The structure of HeaderImagePrompt consists of the fields below:

  • header_image: MessageImage
  • header_text, body_text
  • header_rich_text (RichText, no entities), body_rich_text
  • primary_button_action: MessageTextAction
  • secondary_button_action: Option<MessageTextAction>

Each button has its own ClientEventInfo (action = "primary_cta" or "secondary_cta") and on_click_callbacks: Option<Vec<Callback>>. The secondary button is attached only when secondary_button_text is non-empty. This format is the first case of an ad on the home timeline that uses the URT MessageContent type, and also the first ad format that supports a secondary CTA. Three tests pin down this contract verified — home-mixer/util/urt/ad_marshaller.rs (+258/−3).

  • header_image_prompt_ad_marshals_to_message_prompt_entry
  • header_image_prompt_ad_emits_secondary_button_when_set
  • header_image_prompt_ad_info_absent_stays_a_tweet_item

C. grox attaches a preview thumbnail to videos longer than 30 seconds

The Video pydantic model gained a preview_image: bytes | None field. The new constants are _VIDEO_PREVIEW_MIN_DURATION_MS = 30_000 and PREVIEW_IMAGE_LABEL = "[Video Preview Thumbnail]". hydrate_video_preview resizes the first frame of a video that passes the 4 gates with resize_tile(bs, tile_size) and stores it. The 4 gates are: convo_video exists, url exists, videoInfo exists, and duration > 30s. The tile size is deluxe_image_tile_size if the video is deluxe (= main_post ∧ is_high_fav), and image_tile_size otherwise. In the LLM input, interleave_storyboard puts the preview before the storyboard as the three elements [LABEL, image_bytes, "\n"] verified. The _image_part chat marshaling also attaches the label text and the image part before the storyboard in the same order verified — grox/core/data_loaders/media_loader.py (+100/−19), grox/core/lm/convo.py (+18).

D. Broadcast (live video) formally entered the PTOS safety pipeline

BroadcastLoader came into the grox media loader from broadcast_tools.broadcast. MediaLoader._get_broadcast_loader() lazily initializes the loader from the X_API_BEARER and BROADCAST_GUEST_TOKEN environment variables. _extract_broadcast_video(broadcast_metadata) extracts frames with BroadcastLoader.load_broadcast(broadcast_id, media_key, max_frames, tile_size, max_duration=crop_seconds). The extracted frames are normalized into Video(convo_video=ConvoVideo(frames, duration=average interval, total_duration=sampled_duration)).

The entry conditions of the PTOS leading-frames filter were restructured. Two of the 6 gates folded into the canon in Gen4+17 changed:

  • The deluxe fav gate (gate #2) was removed. Posts without a prior AdultContent verdict still need fav ≥ 512 (gate #6) to enter verified — task_safety_ptos_adult_content_leading_frames_filter.py:63-67.
  • The broadcast payload was formally added. The old code looked only at long_videos ≥ 30s and skipped with no_long_video if there were none. The new code also computes broadcasts = [p.broadcast_metadata for p in (post, post.quoted_post) if p and p.broadcast_metadata and p.broadcast_metadata.broadcast_id], and a post enters if either exists. At that point broadcast_metadata.crop_seconds = 10.0 is set, and eligible.count gets a media = "both" | "broadcast" | "video" tag.

After the change, there are 5 gates:

  1. post.user exists
  2. a video of 30 seconds or longer, or a broadcast_id, exists
  3. a prior PTOS verdict exists
  4. the prior verdict is not NSFW
  5. prior AdultContent violated policy or fav ≥ 512

Broadcast frames now formally enter the PTOS safemodel sex/nudity payload as well. It is gated by enable_local_broadcast_frame_extraction; when on, _iter_broadcast_videos(post) iterates over broadcast_metadata.video.convo_video.frames. The samples chosen by _sample_uniform(frames, _MAX_FRAMES_PER_VIDEO=8) are appended as ("broadcast_frame", frame) payloads. The constant _FRAME_KINDS = {"video_frame", "broadcast_frame"} makes both kinds count equally when computing has_video and n_video_frames verified — grox/flows/ptos/task_safety_ptos_adult_content_leading_frames_filter.py (+18/−8), grox/flows/ptos/task_safety_ptos_safemodel_sex_nudity.py (+21/−2).

E. Multimodal post embeddings are now turned off in all ranking training configs verified — phoenix/README.md (+3/−3).

The "Multimodal post embedding" row of the nano training config table changed from "v5 on xrecsys_seqpack; off on home_direct_packed" to "off (home_direct_packed and xrecsys_seqpack)". The accompanying note was also updated from "on the xrecsys_seqpack training config" to "and on every registered ranking config". "and on" is a grammatical elision, and read together with the table it means "off everywhere". In other words, multimodal post embeddings were dropped from the training inputs of both registered ranking training configs. The two configs are the flagship home_direct_packed and the seqpack xrecsys_seqpack. Read together with Gen4+17 (one day earlier, 2026-09-08) introducing the v8-search stack, this appears to be an intermediate state: v5 was removed from ranking, and v8-search is not yet connected to a ranking config inferred. We will watch whether v8-search enters a ranking config in the next commit.

F. Other changes

  • Fixed a NUMA CPU affinity bug verified — phoenix/xrex/utils/gpu.py (+32/−3).
    • Added the helpers _parse_cpulist and schedulable_cpus(*nodes) to phoenix/xrex/utils/gpu.py.
    • pin_process_to_local_numa runs numa.memory.set_membind_nodes(node) and then, with os.sched_setaffinity(0, schedulable_cpus(node)), schedules only the node's CPUs excluding isolated CPUs.
    • Previously it claimed the whole node with numa.schedule.run_on_nodes(node), so work could be scheduled onto isolated cores.
  • Deleted six log sites in candidate-pipeline that were gated by the quiet-spans feature verified — xai-org/x-algorithm/candidate-pipeline.
    • One #[cfg(feature = "quiet-spans")] tracing::info!(...) block each was removed from filter.rs, hydrator.rs, query_hydrator.rs, scorer.rs, selector.rs, and source.rs (−40 lines in total).
    • The error log string format also reverted from error!(component=…, error=%err, "source_failed") to error!("{} Failed: {}", self.name(), err). The structured fields are gone and the format regressed to a plain string.
  • The Phoenix inference code changed slightly. The changed lines are xrecsys.py (−1), model_runner.py (+2/−1), and recsys_model.py (+5). It may be code wiring up the consumption of Gen4+17's ContentFeatures, but the diagnosis of this commit alone cannot confirm it inferred.

Five things are not public.

  • Where the rule that actually returns Action::Downrank lives
  • How the rule that returns FilteredReason::ViewerBlocksAuthor is wired up
  • Which of the five ads blenders header-image-prompt-ad enters
  • When v8-search is connected to a ranking config
  • The actual scale of broadcast PTOS re-judgments

Gen4+19 (2026-09-10, fee1d0f) — VF hydration timeout unified (80/100 → 390 ms) + AuthorId fallback cache on TES failure + AuthorLabel 64-bit bitset + gRPC deadline observation + clock-cache primitive introduced (not wired) + new ProductSurface and UserAction constants + two-tower user tower padding segment ID + UTH per-country account takedown batch job

In this commit, the call timeout that VF applies at the Strato layer when calling TES and Gizmoduck grew from 100 ms and 80 ms, respectively, to a single 390 ms verified. Also, even if a TES lookup fails, author-based rules keep being evaluated as long as a cached author id remains, and author labels are reduced to the 11 used in verdicts verified. This commit was covered in the 2026-09-12 daily.

33 files, +1587/−391, with nine axes moving together verified — xai-org/x-algorithm@fee1d0f.

A. The VF hydration timeout was unified. The Strato per-call caller timeout rose from 100 ms for TES and 80 ms for Gizmoduck to a unified 390 ms. pub(crate) const HYDRATION_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_millis(390); was added to visibility-filtering/hydration/mod.rs. The CLIENT_TIMEOUT of the two hydrators, TES and Gizmoduck, moved to this shared constant. Previously, each of the two hydrators had used its own 150 ms local constant since the Gen4 release. The two Strato client config constants in server_deps.rs also follow this value. TES_STRATO_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS (previously 100) and GIZMODUCK_STRATO_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS (previously 80) now refer to crate::hydration::HYDRATION_TIMEOUT.as_millis() as u64 (=390). In other words, the Strato-layer per-call caller timeout for the two backends grew 3–4×. verified — visibility-filtering/hydration/mod.rs, visibility-filtering/hydration/gizmoduck_hydrator.rs, visibility-filtering/hydration/tes_hydrator.rs, visibility-filtering/server_deps.rs.

B. When a TES lookup fails, the author is looked up in the AuthorId fallback cache. This cache is on by default, and its default size is 1 M entries. TesHydrator gained an author_id_cache: Option<FallbackCache<TweetId, u64>> field. fetch_pure_core now returns PureCoreHydration { core: HashMap<TweetId, PureCoreData>, recovered_authors: HashMap<TweetId, u64> } instead of HashMap<TweetId, PureCoreData>. If the TES call result for a tweet is Hydrated::Found(core_data), it records (tweet_id, author_id) in the cache and also fills core. If it is NotFound or Failed, it looks up this tweet's earlier author_id in the cache. The priority with which resolve_candidate consumes this result is raw.request_author_id → core.get(&tweet_id).map(|c| c.author_id) → recovered_authors.get(&tweet_id). In other words, even if TES is down or does not respond, author-side rules (user label, account state) are still evaluated as long as this tweet's earlier author_id is in the cache. In that case only tweet-side rules (NSFW media, takedown reason, etc.) are skipped. The new environment variable VF_AUTHOR_ID_FALLBACK_ENABLED defaults to true and uses is_none_or, so "unset = enabled". The new environment variable VF_AUTHOR_ID_FALLBACK_CAPACITY defaults to 1_000_000. verified — visibility-filtering/hydration/tes_hydrator.rs (+234/−42), visibility-filtering/models/mod.rs (+49/−9), visibility-filtering/config.rs (+14).

C. Author labels were replaced by 11 explicit AuthorLabel variants and a 64-bit bitset. The old HashSet<LabelValue> is gone. UserLabelSet(HashSet<LabelValue>) in models/author.rs became AuthorLabelSet(u64). The new AuthorLabel enum names only these 11 variants: NsfwHighRecall, NsfwHighPrecision, NsfwNearPerfect, NsfwAvatarImage, NsfwBannerImage, SpamHighRecall, AbusiveHighRecall, Compromised, ReadOnly, ImpersonationHighPrecision, DoNotAmplify. These 11 correspond exactly 1:1 to the 11 OON_USER_LABEL_DROPS rules that Gen4+13 (7ba7768) organized as rule constants. AuthorFeatures was promoted to #[derive(Clone, Copy, ...)]. Its size is locked at exactly 16 bytes, and the assert size_of::<Option<AuthorFeatures>>() == 16 pins it. The Gizmoduck hydrator's author_features(user_result, counts) narrows each thrift LabelValue to an Option<AuthorLabel> through the author_label(LabelValue) mapping. Labels that do not map only increment a count. The new metric is vf_author_labels{result="mapped"|"unmapped"}, and a test asserting that the dashboard references this name was added with it. In other words, VF now uses only these 11 labels for verdicts, and the other thrift LabelValue values (e.g., NSFW_TEXT_HIGH_RECALL, NSFW_NEW_USER) are explicitly dropped at input. Previously everything was kept in the HashSet and rules only checked for existence on lookup, so the other values were not used in verdicts but were still held in memory. verified — visibility-filtering/models/author.rs (+49/−13), visibility-filtering/hydration/gizmoduck_hydrator.rs, visibility-filtering/rules/author_rules.rs (+30/−27), visibility-filtering/rules/context.rs.

D. VF observes whether it met the gRPC deadline (filter_tweets_deadline{outcome=within|overrun|absent}) and measures request time split into two phases, hydration and post_hydration. filter_tweets.rs::FilterTweetsEndpoint::filter_tweets parses the grpc-timeout header in the request metadata. The units H/M/S/m/u/n map to hours, minutes, seconds, milliseconds, microseconds, and nanoseconds, respectively. The digits must be 8 or fewer, and any other format becomes None. When the request succeeds, it calls RequestMetricsGuard::record_deadline(grpc_timeout). The behavior of record_deadline splits into three cases.

  • If elapsed <= deadline, it increments the counter with outcome=within and records the remainder in the filter_tweets_deadline_remaining_ms histogram.
  • If the deadline was exceeded, it increments with outcome=overrun and records the excess in filter_tweets_deadline_overrun_ms.
  • If there is no timeout header, it increments with outcome=absent.

The new metric filter_tweets_phase_ms{stage="hydration"|"post_hydration"} observes hydrated_at - started and hydrated_at.elapsed() in filter.rs::FilterTweets::run, respectively. That is, the VF service can now measure the following two things:

  1. How much slack its own latency has relative to the deadline the caller allowed, or how much it overran
  2. How request time is allocated between hydration and the rule engine stage that follows

This added observation and the timeout increase in A read as effectively the same project. verified — visibility-filtering/filter_tweets.rs (+42/−0), visibility-filtering/filter.rs (+6/−1), visibility-filtering/rules/metrics.rs.

E. clock_cache.rs, a 32-way set-associative × 64-shard CLOCK cache primitive, was introduced, but nothing is wired to it yet. The changes are visibility-filtering/clock_cache.rs +446 and the registration pub(crate) mod clock_cache; in visibility-filtering/lib.rs. The top of the file opens with #![cfg_attr(not(test), expect(dead_code, reason = "TODO: no consumer wired yet"))]. The cache has fixed capacity, with u64 keys and V: Copy values. The structure has three layers, in the order shard (64) × set (capacity ÷ WAYS, distributed across shards) × way (32). When insert(generation, key, value) overwrites an existing slot, it checks the stored generation and skips the write if the stored one is newer. If there is no existing slot, it evicts with the CLOCK algorithm. The hand rotates, decaying Referenced → Cold, and inserts into the slot when it finds Cold or Empty. begin_request() assigns each request a monotonic generation, which prevents a later request from reviving a stale cache value. It is a separate primitive from the existing FallbackCache (TinyLFU family, moka::sync::Cache). This cache is a new hot-path cache that handles write throughput and lock contention better, with per-shard mutexes and fixed-slot arrays. Since this commit has no consumer, what to watch is which hydrator's backend it gets wired to in the next commit (TES author-id? Gizmoduck AuthorFeatures? SafetyLabel expiring cache?). verified — visibility-filtering/clock_cache.rs, visibility-filtering/lib.rs.

F. The Phoenix proto gained two ProductSurface values (TREND_PAGE=16, EXPLORE_SPOTLIGHT=17) and UserActionAggregationType::IMMERSIVE_LONG_DWELL=29. The changed files are phoenix/crates/serving/xai-recsys-proto/proto/recsys.proto and phoenix/python/common/xai-proto/proto/recsys.proto. The earlier PLACEHOLDER_16 and PLACEHOLDER_17 were named PRODUCT_SURFACE_TREND_PAGE = 16 and PRODUCT_SURFACE_EXPLORE_SPOTLIGHT = 17, respectively. Proto slots opened for the Trend surface and the Explore Spotlight surface to be formally brought into Phoenix ranking. The two surfaces were added after the 15 surface constants organized in code in Gen4+3, and there is no actual home-mixer wiring yet. In UserActionAggregationType, PLACEHOLDER_29 was also named IMMERSIVE_LONG_DWELL = 29. Separately from the existing IMMERSIVE = 26, it is now possible to split immersive interactions with long dwell time into their own aggregation type. Which sequence pipeline in the nano/flagship training configs consumes this new aggregation is not in this commit. verified — phoenix/crates/serving/xai-recsys-proto/proto/recsys.proto, phoenix/python/common/xai-proto/proto/recsys.proto.

G. The two-tower user tower uses PADDING_SEGMENT_ID at padding positions and HISTORY_SEGMENT_ID at real history positions. It now reflects the mask instead of the previous all-zero. user_tower_segment_ids in phoenix/xrex/models/recsys_two_tower_model.py was extended to take an optional padding_mask: jax.Array | None argument. The previous logic had two branches.

  • If use_history_segment_ids=True, it fills the array entirely with HISTORY_SEGMENT_ID.
  • If False, it uses jnp.zeros.

The new logic, when padding_mask is given, mixes the two values by mask position with jnp.where(padding_mask, HISTORY_SEGMENT_ID, PADDING_SEGMENT_ID). The actual call site of the _pool function now passes user_padding_mask, so the production training path takes this new branch. In other words, the user tower's attention, RoPE, and attention bias are computed with padding positions distinguished from history. It is a correctness fix of the same nature as Gen4+15's variable-length history support in the FA4 attention kernel. verified — phoenix/xrex/models/recsys_two_tower_model.py (+15/−4).

H. Home-mixer's ads injection log now explicitly includes an ads_blender field. home-mixer/side_effects/ads_injection_logging_side_effect.rs looks up the AdsBlenderType parameter (feature-switch) and fills the ads_blender string in the log payload. For RequestType::Following, it does not look up the parameter and uses the hardcoded "following". The AdsBlenderType param is looked up only for the other surfaces. Gen4+10 (24c6094) introduced five ads blenders (safe_gap, partition_organic, partition_organic_low_risk, time_gap, multi_risk). This time, in follow-up, a separate blender label "following" for the Following surface was formally brought into the logging axis. Whether this is a sixth blender, or whether the Following surface takes a separate pipeline outside the five blenders so that the label is attached only in logging, cannot be confirmed from this diff alone inferred. The latter fits the code flow better (skipping the param lookup reads as a signal that the pipeline is different) inferred. verified — home-mixer/side_effects/ads_injection_logging_side_effect.rs (+5/−1).

I. Under-The-Hood gained a daily per-country account takedown batch job, UthPctdAccountTakedownEventsJob, and the UTH label aggregates gained a countryCodes field. under-the-hood/scalding/UthPctdAccountTakedownEventsJob.scala was added with +143 lines. The job joins two datasets. AuditServicePctdActionsScalaDataset is the User-type PCTD action log, and UsersourceScalaDataset holds the takedown reason from the user snapshot. The join result (userId, day, reason, country) is written as daily-partitioned Parquet (daily_account_takedowns/YYYY/MM/DD). The reason priority is LEGAL_REQUEST < BYSTANDER_REPORT < DMCA < UNSPECIFIED. If multiple reasons are found for the same (userId, country), the one with the lower priority value is kept. Cross-DC snapshot access (AllowCrossDC) is allowed. The default reducers is 50, the default usersourceSnapshotMaxAgeDays is 10, and the test user filter is supported through TestUserFilter.isTestUserId. A countryCodes: optional list<string> field (#3) was added to the two structs UthPostLabelAggregate and UthAccountLabelAggregate in uth_serving.thrift. In other words, the UTH transparency tool has started preparing to serve country-level takedown records. It reads as a plan to show users which label was active in which country and when. It pairs with the 16 NSFW-gated countries disclosed in Gen4+12 (2026-09-01, 6384ca7). We will watch whether a per-country filter appears at the UTH URL (x.com/i/under_the_hood). verified — under-the-hood/scalding/UthPctdAccountTakedownEventsJob.scala, under-the-hood/thrift/uth_serving.thrift.

Gen4+20 (2026-09-12, 6bb4594) — VMRanker DPP pins the seed anchor + Phoenix ScoredCandidate log dual-published as Thrift and Proto + VF client discovery migrated to the xDS LDS listener + Phoenix proto LLM-judge search relevance action + Phoenix wire returnLogitsList + CompactAuthorFeatures 8-byte packed (not wired) + VF worldwide takedown rules refined + UTH report monthly cap parameter + Phoenix training Kafka mTLS mode

In this commit, when a request carries a reference post (seed) and its embedding exists, VMRanker's DPP puts the seed into the kernel to reduce the gain of candidates close to it, but does not include it in the result verified. In safety verdicts, bystander reports and legal copyright requests tagged only with a worldwide code are no longer filtered out automatically verified. This commit was covered in the 2026-09-13 daily.

24 files, +1397/−338, with eight axes moving together verified — xai-org/x-algorithm@6bb4594.

A. VMRanker DPP uses seed_tweet_id as a pinned anchor. This seed does not consume the top_k budget. A new field seed_tweet_id was added to RankRequest. dpp_model::rank looks up the embedding store (ctx.store.client) with this id. If the embedding exists, it builds DppInput { id, score: 0.0, embedding, norm, embedding_missing: false } and passes it to the new seed: Option<&DppInput> argument of dpp::rescore. rescore builds a kernel of size total = m + 1 from the top-K candidates and one seed. The first slot of the greedy selection is forcibly pinned to the seed position (pinned_first: Option<usize>). After that, it filters the seed index out of the selection result and returns the rest. That is, the seed sits in the kernel and has its cosine similarity to other candidates computed, which reduces the determinantal gain of candidates close to it. However, it does not appear in the final slate and does not consume the top_k budget. The new metric vm_ranker_dpp_seed_context_total{result="pinned"|"embedding_missing"} counts seed embedding hits and misses separately. The new tests seed_suppresses_near_duplicate and seed_does_not_consume_top_k_budget lock in these two contracts. verified — vm-ranker/dpp.rs (+117/−40), vm-ranker/scoring/dpp_model.rs (+28/−1), vm-ranker/metrics.rs (+8).

Before this commit, VMRanker DPP optimized only within-set diversity (cosine repulsion among top-K candidates), and the home timeline's blender placed that result as is. The seed pin this commit introduced is contextual diversity that "favors candidates dissimilar to the tweet being viewed" inferred. Related tweets on a permalink page, a "more like this" flow for a specific tweet, and alternative slates for thread content read as natural consumers inferred. Which home-mixer pipeline supplies seed_tweet_id is not in this commit.

B. The Phoenix ScoredCandidate log is dual-published in the Thrift PredictionScore BTreeSet format and the Proto LoggedScoredCandidate HashMap format. The Proto side goes to a new Kafka topic. home-mixer/side_effects/phoenix_experiments_side_effect.rs now builds two payloads per candidate and writes them to the two topics concurrently with tokio::join!.

  • The existing Thrift binary ScoredCandidate goes to PHOENIX_SCORES_TOPIC (cluster Aiml).
  • The new proto LoggedScoredCandidate goes to LOGGED_SCORED_CANDIDATES_TOPIC (cluster Phoenix).

prediction_scores in the Proto payload is a map<string, double>. So, unlike the sorted collection of Thrift's BTreeSet<Box<PredictionScore>>, it allows O(1) lookup, and the wire size is also much more compact without a sorted index. The mapping keys keep the phoenix.<cluster_name>.<action_name> naming convention as is. The keys are attached to the 28 engagement heads and the pdwell alias. The constructor, new_mock, and prod assembly code of PhoenixCandidatePipeline were extended to take logged_scored_candidates_kafka_client as the sixth Kafka publisher. The Thrift stream is kept and the Proto stream was attached in parallel. When downstream (the ranking log consumers) switches to Proto is outside this commit. verified — home-mixer/side_effects/phoenix_experiments_side_effect.rs (+207/−54), home-mixer/candidate_pipeline/phoenix_candidate_pipeline.rs (+17/−1).

C. VF moved to finding the TES and Gizmoduck clients through the xDS LDS listener, and unified the Strato constants. Previously, visibility-filtering/server_deps.rs set the gRPC endpoint directly with a datacenter template string (tweet-entity-service.tweet-entity-service.prod.{datacenter}.s2s.twttr.net). It also used each service crate's TESClientConfig and GizmoduckClientConfig. These two are per-service config structs holding the aperture size, penalized peak EWMA / least-request P2C, the readiness probe port, and so on. This commit deleted all of them and replaced them with a common helper, build_xds_strato(XdsStratoParams, deterministic_aperture). The new helper assembles the channel with xai_x_rpc::grpc_client::ChannelBuilder as follows.

Only the TES path attaches a server-side deadline hint with enable_serve_within: true (OpContext.serve_within, round_trip_allowance_microseconds = 10_000). Gizmoduck turns this option off. retry_config: Some(RetryConfig::for_idempotent()) is also set only on the TES path.

This migration changes three things.

  • The service discovery layer moved from a hostname template to going through the xDS LDS (Envoy-family listener name).
  • The separate client-config structs that lived inside the service crates, such as TESClientConfig and GizmoduckClientConfig, are gone. The client assembly logic was absorbed into VF server_deps.rs.
  • The Strato client of the L2 cache warmer now also takes the deterministic_aperture flag.

It can also be read from the viewpoint that the HYDRATION_TIMEOUT unification in Gen4+19 rippled out to here. verified — visibility-filtering/server_deps.rs (+119/−48).

D. The Phoenix proto gained two LLM-judge search relevance actions and the returnLogitsList response format. The following definitions were added to both phoenix/crates/serving/xai-recsys-proto/proto/recsys.proto and its Python mirror.

The two actions extend the xrecsys_search search ranking config from Gen4+4 (aad7179, 2026-08-19). Until this commit, the only search relevance signal was the client signal (a user selecting or skipping a result). This commit adds the LLM judge's relevance verdict as a separate action axis. The natural reading is that the xrecsys_search config uses these two actions as training targets to supervise search relevance prediction inferred. A pipeline in which grox or a dedicated LLM judge feeds relevant/not labels for (query, tweet) pairs must exist somewhere inferred.

returnLogitsList is a response payload format. A new field return_logits_list: bool was added to PredictRequestItem. When this field is on, python.rs::PredictRequestBatch responds as follows instead of using return_log_map (a sparse HashMap<u32, f32>):

That is, the response is a positional list that keeps the order of requested_action_indices. If a requested action index falls outside the model vocab, it is filled with -inf. This compresses what the existing return_log_map sent over the wire as a sparse HashMap into a positional dense array. The key overhead disappears and the order is guaranteed. The two formats are mutually exclusive by design, and if both are on, return_logits_list takes precedence. verified — phoenix/crates/serving/xai-recsys-proto/proto/recsys.proto (+6), phoenix/python/common/xai-proto/proto/recsys.proto (+6), phoenix/crates/serving/xai-recsys-engine/src/python.rs (+19/−6), phoenix/crates/serving/xai-recsys-engine/src/util.rs (+2).

E. VF gained CompactAuthorFeatures, an 8-byte representation packed as a NonZeroU64, but it is not yet wired in. The following code was added to visibility-filtering/models/author.rs:

The layout has three parts:

  • Bit 63: present marker
  • Bits 0–6: 7 account-state flags (is_suspended, is_deactivated, is_protected, is_nsfw_user, is_nsfw_admin, is_erased, is_offboarded)
  • Bits 8–62: 55-bit label bitset

It asserts that the size of Option<CompactAuthorFeatures> is exactly 8 bytes (using the NonZeroU64 niche optimization).

Why it matters: In Gen4+19 (fee1d0f, 2026-09-10), AuthorFeatures was already shrunk to a 16-byte Copy struct. This commit's CompactAuthorFeatures is an 8-byte representation that cuts it in half again. A test that exhaustively verifies the round trip for every label and flag combination was added with it (1<<7 × 1<<11 = 262,144 combinations). Since there is no consumer yet (#[allow(dead_code)]), it appears likely to be adopted in the next commit as a value type for the hydration pipeline or a cache (the clock_cache introduced in Gen4+19 is the most likely candidate) inferred. verified — visibility-filtering/models/author.rs (+94/−2).

F. VF takedown rules now handle worldwide codes separately by reason. visibility-filtering/rules/context.rs extracted the worldwide check of TakedownPredicates::filter_by_country_or_worldwide into a new helper is_worldwide_code(cc) = "xx" OR "xy" (case-insensitive). It also added two exceptions:

  • legal_takedown_country: if TakedownReason::LegalRequest { country_code } carries "xy" (WORLDWIDE_COPYRIGHT_COUNTRY_CODE), it now returns None. That is, LegalRequest{"xy"} no longer triggers the legal takedown rule. The DMCA reason still returns "xy" as the synthetic worldwide code.
  • local_laws_takedown_country: if TakedownReason::BystanderReport { country_code } carries a worldwide code ("xx" or "xy"), it returns None. That is, a worldwide-scale BystanderReport{"xx"} report is no longer dropped by the local laws rule.

Three new test cases (legal_takedown_copyright_code_allows_without_viewer_country, unspecified_takedown_worldwide_drops_without_viewer_country, local_laws_takedown_worldwide_allows_any_viewer) lock in this refinement. This is the first substantive policy relaxation since Gen4+12 (6384ca7, 2026-09-01), which first introduced country-scope handling. Bystander reports and legal-copyright requests that carry only a world-wide scope are no longer dropped automatically. UnspecifiedReason is still dropped when it is worldwide. verified — visibility-filtering/rules/context.rs (+14/−4), visibility-filtering/rules/golden_corpus.rs (+33/−3), visibility-filtering/rules/tweet_rules.rs (+22/−11).

G. The Under-The-Hood report gained a maximum-month cap FS parameter and an employee role. under-the-hood/strato/lib/params.strato exposes a new int parameter under_the_hood_report_max_month_bucket (default 0 = unused). In reportMonthBucket(now, maxMonthBucket) of underTheHoodReport.User.strato, if the cap is greater than 0, the computed calendar month is clamped to that cap. "employee" was added to the userRoles Set next to "birdwatch_team". That is, operators can now lock the displayed month of the UTH report at or below a given value, and the employee role is included among those who can view the report. The month cap appears to be a safeguard that pins the report to the last month with complete data when preparing for a large incident or rollout. verified — under-the-hood/strato/lib/params.strato (+5), under-the-hood/strato/columns/underTheHoodReport.User.strato (+15/−7).

H. Kafka authentication for the Phoenix training pipeline gained an mTLS mode, chosen automatically alongside SASL. phoenix/xrex/data/streaming/kafkaconsumer.py and kafkaloader.py introduced a new KafkaAuth dataclass (mode="mtls"|"sasl"). auto_detect_auth decides the authentication in this order:

  • If the KAFKA_AUTH env var is "sasl", SASL is forced.
  • If ca-bundle.crt, client.fullchain and client.key are all present in KAFKA_MTLS_CERTS_DIR (default /root/client-certs), mTLS is used.
  • If only the client certificate is present and the CA is missing, mTLS is used with the platform CA bundle (/etc/ssl/internal-ca/ca-bundle.crt) or the system truststore as a substitute.
  • If SASL_PLAIN_PASSWORD is present, it falls back to SASL.

The recsys action stream Kafka consumed by Phoenix training can now be reached over mTLS as well as SASL/SCRAM. This code alone does not show which one is adopted in actual operation. verified — phoenix/xrex/data/streaming/kafkaloader.py (+159/−9), phoenix/xrex/data/streaming/kafkaconsumer.py (+96/−40), phoenix/xrex/data/rust_kafka_recsys.py (+23/−5).

LLM_JUDGE_RELEVANT_TO_SEARCH and LLM_JUDGE_NOT_RELEVANT_TO_SEARCH were vacated five days later, in Gen4+23 (42266f3, 2026-09-17). CLIENT_TWEET_LIVE_STREAM_REPLY=107 and RESERVED_108 took their place. Questions about where these two actions connect are now moot.

Gen4+21 (2026-09-15, 2d4a03c) — Three-stage response diversity (pre-heuristic, top10, final) observation side effect + Phoenix ads continuous head ADS_WEB_CT_PURCHASE_VALUE + PurchaseValueBaseline request field + 12 TweetTypeMetrics slate-axis bits (239-244, 315-320) + viewer positive-engagement parser + H100 attn kernel unified with GB300 on the same CUTe DSL + Kafka OTel export 30s → 120s + coordinated_spam follower 10k → 30k

Observation now measures the response slate's diversity side by side at three points: before the heuristic layers, top 10, and final. Slate diversity and author context are also recorded as per-candidate bits verified. On the ads side, a new head regresses on the purchase value after a web click, and on the safety side the follower threshold of the coordinated spam filter rose from 10k to 30k verified (daily).

17 files, +592/−9, with five axes moving together verified — xai-org/x-algorithm@2d4a03c.

A. A side effect now measures the response slate's diversity side by side at three stages.

The new ResponseDiversityStatsSideEffect observes the three stages pre_heuristic, top10 and final in parallel. The default sampling rate is 5%, and it runs at 100% in experiment buckets.

The implementation file is home-mixer/side_effects/response_diversity_stats_side_effect.rs (186 lines, new). This side effect was wired into the Phoenix candidate pipeline as the sixth observation side effect.

There are two activation conditions.

  • The default is DEFAULT_SAMPLING_RATE = 0.05.
  • If the new feature-switch param EnableResponseDiversityStatsExperimentBucket captures an experiment bucket, it runs at 100% in that bucket. Each metric is then emitted with the scope tags ddg=<experiment id> and bucket=<bucket id>.

The three stages cover different ranges.

  • pre_heuristic: merges selected_candidates and non_selected_candidates and takes the top K by weighted_score in descending order. This score is the raw head-weight sum, the value before the DPP, author-decay and OON multipliers are applied. This stage is the counterfactual of "what if the ranker's raw top-K had been served without the heuristic layer."
  • top10: the top 10 of the final slate, sorted by score (post-heuristic).
  • final: the entire slate.

Each stage emits histogram metrics, all with names starting with ResponseDiversity.*:

  • Size: Size
  • Author: UniqueAuthors·UniqueAuthorRatio·MaxAuthorShare, AuthorHhi·AuthorEntropyNorm
  • Source: UniqueSources·SourceEntropyNorm (axis=served_type, retrieval source)
  • Other: InNetworkShare, SidCoverage
  • 3 SID L1 axes: UniqueSidL1·MaxSidL1Share·SidL1EntropyNorm
  • 2 SID L2 axes: UniqueSidL2·SidL2EntropyNorm

It computes HHI (Herfindahl-Hirschman Index, a market concentration measure applied to the slate) together with Shannon entropy normalized as entropy / ln(size). This makes diversity comparable regardless of differences in slate cardinality. verified — home-mixer/side_effects/response_diversity_stats_side_effect.rs, home-mixer/candidate_pipeline/phoenix_candidate_pipeline.rs (+2), home-mixer/params/param.rs (+7/−1).

Why it matters: How much the heuristic layer changes the slate relative to the ranker's raw scores has not been measured until now. The pre_heuristic counterfactual is the first connection that makes this difference measurable.

B. A shared primitive for computing multiset statistics was added.

The new Composition computes multiset statistics (unique, max, HHI, normalized entropy) in O(n). The implementation is in home-mixer/util/composition.rs (63 lines, new). A single Composition::from_keys<K: Hash + Eq>(iter) extracts statistics for any axis (author, served_type, SID L1/L2). It is reused in two places: A's ResponseDiversityStatsSideEffect and the computation of the new bits in C's TweetTypeMetricsHydrator. verified — home-mixer/util/composition.rs, home-mixer/util/mod.rs (+2).

C. 12 bits representing slate-wide and context information were added to the per-candidate bitset.

Slate-axis bits 239-244 and 315-320 were newly defined in the TweetTypeMetrics bitset. Two functions were added to home-mixer/candidate_hydrators/tweet_type_metrics_hydrator.rs (+100/−4):

  • author_diversity_bits(authors: &Composition) -> HashSet<usize> builds the slate-wide bits, which apply identically to every candidate.
  • slate_position_bits(query, candidates) -> Vec<HashSet<usize>> applies differently to each candidate.

In hydrate, the two bit sets are merged by union with each candidate's base bitset, then compressed and stored as the tweet_type_metrics payload. The new predicates are defined in home-mixer/util/tweet_type_metrics.rs (+27).

Slate-wide:

  • UNIQUE_AUTHOR_RATIO_LTE_50_PCT = 239: the slate's unique_ratio ≤ 0.5
  • UNIQUE_AUTHOR_LTE_5/10/15 = 240/241/242
  • SINGLE_AUTHOR_GTE_25_PCT/50_PCT = 243/244

Slate context (traversed in descending score order):

  • AUTHOR_REPEAT_IN_SLATE = 315, AUTHOR_REPEAT_GTE_3_IN_SLATE = 316: turn on from the second and the third-or-later appearance of the same author_id. They do not turn on for the first appearance. What they mark is "which appearance of the same author this tweet is."
  • AUTHOR_NOT_ENGAGED_BY_VIEWER = 317: means the viewer does not follow the candidate's author and that author is also not in the viewer's positive-engagement set.
  • HAS_SEMANTIC_IDS = 318
  • SID_L1_REPEAT_IN_SLATE = 319, SID_L2_REPEAT_IN_SLATE = 320: turn on for the second and later candidates whose SID L1 (L2) prefix is already in the slate.

The new helper is PostCandidate::semantic_id_prefix(levels: usize) -> Option<&[i32]> (home-mixer/models/candidate.rs +8). This helper safely slices the top levels codes from the SID array.

Why it matters: TweetTypeMetrics is an axis for ranking training and serving logs and for offline analysis. So slate diversity, author context and SID context are now logged as per-candidate features and can be referenced in training and modeling. However, this commit has no training config change that actually consumes these bits, so only the channel is open. Actual consumption is something to watch for in follow-up commits. If these bits are promoted to ranker features, it would signal that X's ranker is moving from pointwise to slate-aware scoring. verified — home-mixer/candidate_hydrators/tweet_type_metrics_hydrator.rs, home-mixer/util/tweet_type_metrics.rs, home-mixer/models/candidate.rs.

D. A function was added that extracts the set of authors a viewer has engaged with positively from the viewer's history.

The new function viewer_history::positively_engaged_author_ids extracts the set of positive-engagement authors from an Arrow IPC stream. The file is home-mixer/util/viewer_history.rs (61 lines, new). The function opens the request's ScoredPostsQuery.columnar_scoring_sequence (an Arrow columnar batch of the user's recent interaction history). From it, it collects and returns the authorId of rows where authorId > 0 and at least one of the 18 positive actions below is on in the actionNameMultiHot FixedSizeList.

ServerTweetFav, ServerTweetReply, ServerTweetQuote, ServerTweetRetweet,
ClientTweetClick, ClientQuotedTweetClick, ClientTweetOpenLink,
ClientTweetClickProfile, ClientTweetPhotoExpand, ClientQuotedTweetPhotoExpand,
ClientTweetVideoOpen, ClientTweetVideoQualityView, ClientQuotedTweetVideoQualityView,
ClientTweetShare, ClientTweetClickSendViaDirectMessage, ClientTweetShareViaCopyLink,
ClientTweetBookmark, ClientTweetFollowAuthor

Negative signals such as report, mute, block and not_dwelled, and impression-type signals such as dwell and quality view, are intentionally excluded (video quality view is explicitly positive). This set is a new constant set that appears nowhere else in X's public code. It fixes in code, for the first time, the definition of "an author with whom a relationship was formed through active engagement."

The AUTHOR_NOT_ENGAGED_BY_VIEWER bit in C is the one consumer of this function, but the concept of "an author with an established relationship with the viewer" could be reused in other pipelines (cold start, cold author fatigue decay and so on), so it appears to have been split out as a separate utility inferred. verified — home-mixer/util/viewer_history.rs.

E. The Phoenix proto gained a head that predicts the actual purchase value after an ads web click, and a request field.

The new continuous head is ADS_WEB_CT_PURCHASE_VALUE = 5, and the new request field is PurchaseValueBaseline. This head is the fifth continuous head of the ContinuousActionName enum. The existing four are DWELL_TIME=1, CLICK_DWELL_TIME=2, ACTIVE_SECS_5M_RESIDUAL_NORM=3 and BRIDGE_PROBABILITY=4. The new head's regression target is the purchase value that occurs after a web click-through conversion (CT = Click-Through).

In the same commit, a new field 23 was added to PredictNextActionsRequest:

Each baseline is a tuple of (impression_id, advertiser_account_id, the advertiser's average purchase value in USD over the last 28 days). The Rust helper phoenix/crates/serving/xai-recsys-proto/src/purchase_value.rs (114 lines, new) also came in, and it contains the following three items:

  • is_valid_baseline: the criterion is a positive id and a positive finite USD value.
  • find_baseline(request, impression_id, advertiser_account_id)
  • 5 wire tag stability unit tests: they check whether field 23 = 0xBA 0x01 is independent of returnLogitsList field 22 = 0xB0 0x01 0x01 and whether it is backward compatible with old requests.

Why it matters: If ads ranking has so far predicted only the probability of ad clicks and conversions (including the 20 conversion actions of Gen4+6), the new head takes the value itself as its regression target. The request also carries a per-advertiser 28-day baseline, preparing a connection that would enable residual training. This commit does not state whether it is a direct training target or a baseline offset regression. It appears to be the first serving connection for a value-optimizing auction (the same direction as Meta VBB and Google tCPA/tROAS) inferred. A baseline arriving with every request means a separate offline pipeline updates the advertiser account's 28-day average daily and feeds it into serving requests in parallel, so it is likely that only the baselines of advertisers picked by pre-pruning at request time are attached inferred. verified — phoenix/crates/serving/xai-recsys-proto/proto/recsys.proto, phoenix/crates/serving/xai-recsys-proto/src/purchase_value.rs, phoenix/python/common/xai-proto/proto/recsys.proto.

Gen4+22 (2026-09-16, fad2f71) — Phoenix ads purchase-value loss wired in + new binary continuous loss type (first use = click-dwell BCE, on by default) + XAUC clicked-only metric + silent remap of the user_gender categorical index + H100 attn override flipped to CUTe DSL + VMRanker DSCP + EnableAdsBrandSafetyVerdictV2 rollback + grox reply-spam model split by thread follower count

26 files, +552/−233; five axes moved together verified — xai-org/x-algorithm@fad2f71.

A. The ads purchase-value head now connects through to the training loss, but it is off in the default configuration.

The ADS_WEB_CT_PURCHASE_VALUE Huber ratio loss is now formally wired in (weight default 0, opt-in). In Gen4+21 only the wire (proto, request field, Rust helper) of the ads purchase-value continuous head was opened; this commit connects it through to the training loss. Two functions were introduced in phoenix/xrex/models/loss_recsys.py (+91).

  • purchase_value_valid_mask builds the valid mask as an AND of eight terms.
    • The expression is label_valid & padding & !negative_sample & delayed_mask & has_click & has_purchase & keeper_mask & (isfinite && positive) on ratio·baseline.
    • For a sample to enter the loss, its label must be observed, it must not be padding, and it must not be a negative-sampling sample.
    • The delayed-reward window must also be closed (when delayed_mask is True, the label has converged).
    • The sample must have actually been clicked and actually reached a purchase, and it must be a candidate that is trained on (trained_candidate_mask).
    • Updated in Gen4+24 (2026-09-18): the delayed_mask term narrowed from sample_source > 0 to sample_source == EARLY_RELABEL_STREAM_ID. This loss is not trained on the late-split stream. The stat names were also renamed from purchase-value-* to purchase-value_delayed_clicked-*.
  • purchase_value_loss_compute computes a Huber loss (default delta=1.0). It takes three inputs.
    • raw_ratio: GT ratio
    • pred_ratio: the model prediction
    • baseline_mean_usd: the advertiser's 28-day average
    • It emits seven stats: purchase-value-loss, -valid-count, -weight-sum, -ratio-mae, -target-ratio, -pred-ratio, -baseline-mean-usd.
    • The loss argument is the raw ratio, not raw USD. The training target is the ratio relative to the advertiser's 28-day average. baseline_mean_usd is an offset that arrives with the request and is used only for stat computation.

The loss loop in recsys_model.py (+236/−26) gained a block that runs when purchase_value_loss_weight > 0.

  • It pulls trained_candidate_mask, value_label_valid, and value_baseline_mean_usd from candidate_seq and builds the mask.
  • It takes candidate_continuous_actions[:, :, PURCHASE_VALUE_ACTION_INDEX] (= slot 5) as the raw ratio and candidate_continuous_preds[:, :, 5] as the prediction, and computes the loss.
  • It weights this loss by purchase_value_loss_weight and adds it to continuous_action_loss_total.

The default is purchase_value_loss_weight = 0.0, so it is still off in the default config. Turning it on requires passing mparams["purchase_value_loss_weight"] explicitly.

A new checker, validate_purchase_value, enforces the activation conditions.

  • num_continuous_actions > 5: slot 5 must exist.
  • output_vocab_size > ADS_PURCHASE_CONVERSION: action head 200 must exist.
  • purchase_value_huber_delta > 0 && finite
  • No generic continuous loss may be attached to the same slot. Purchase-value slot 5 is dedicated.

When the purchase-value head is active, the serving activation function is fixed to softplus (positive reals).

Four new fields entered on the wire side (phoenix/xrex/data/recsys/recsys_batch.py +53, parquet_recsys.py +4, feature_config.py +2).

  • PostSeq gained value_label_valid: bool and value_baseline_mean_usd: float32 slots.
  • The Parquet reader _read_value_labels reads the valueLabelValidSeq and valueBaselineMeanUsdSeq columns in pa.list_(dtype, seq_len) format and unpacks them into (batch, seq) arrays.
  • Both columns were registered in the feature list.

With this, the advertiser's 28-day baseline is also injected in parallel per batch at training time. The serving request field purchase_value_baselines was already open in Gen4+21.

Why it matters: Ads ranking has formally entered a value-optimizing auction direction, down to the training pipeline stage. Its training target closely resembles Meta VBB (Value-Based Bidding) and Google tCPA/tROAS. Whether it is actually active will be decided when a mparams["purchase_value_loss_weight"] value appears in a later commit. That the training target is a ratio to the advertiser baseline carries advertiser-scale normalization into the training target itself. This normalization unifies the loss scale of a "10,000 won advertiser" and a "100,000 won advertiser". verified — phoenix/xrex/models/loss_recsys.py, phoenix/xrex/models/recsys_model.py, phoenix/xrex/data/recsys/recsys_batch.py, phoenix/xrex/data/recsys/constants.py.

B. A new continuous loss type was added, and the post-click dwell-time head uses it by default.

The new type binary combines sigmoid, BCE, and a threshold. Its first use is click_dwell_time, with threshold=10s, and training is on by default. ContinuousActionLossConfig.loss_type now accepts binary in addition to the existing {mse, mae, huber, tweedie}. The new field is binary_threshold: float = 10.0. The activation function is forced to sigmoid by an assert. output_cap is meaningless because the output is a probability in [0,1], and an assert forbids it.

The new function binary_threshold_loss_compute binarizes the original continuous value gt_raw to {0,1} against the threshold (gt_binary = (gt_raw > threshold)). It then computes a sigmoid binary cross-entropy. The mask uses the same valid_mask & !negative_sample_mask gating as the existing continuous loss.

The signature of decode_continuous changed to jax.Array → (jax.Array, dict[int, jax.Array]). The second return value, head_logits_by_index, is the plumbing of this commit. Because binary loss needs the raw logit before the sigmoid (computing the sigmoid and BCE together from the logit is numerically stable), it also returns a raw logit tensor for each binary-typed head index. The loss loop consumes these logits through head_logits_by_index[loss_config.action_index]. The return value of the serving forward path (a non-training path) also becomes a 3-tuple, but serving does not use head_logits and discards it.

In the default _home_direct_packed_base of xrecsys.py, two defaults changed.

  1. click_dwell_loss_weight: 1.0: the mparams default was set to 1.0. Before this commit, the public training code (phoenix/xrex) had no click-dwell loss configuration at all verified — 2d4a03c grep. The default training target is now a binary classification of "whether the user dwelled 10 seconds or more within the 60-second window after a click".
    • A new ContinuousActionLossConfig was appended: action_index=CLICK_DWELL_TIME (= 2), metric_name="click-dwell-binary".
    • The remaining settings are loss_weight=mparams.get("click_dwell_loss_weight", 0.0) and loss_type="binary".
    • The binarization and normalization settings are binary_threshold=10.0 and norm_config=NormConfig(norm_scale=60.0).
  2. enable_click_dwell_time: True (feature-prep): the click_dwell_time history feature in the history encoder is now on by default. In recsys_feature_prep.py (+12), when enable_click_dwell_time=True, it normalizes history_seq.continuous_actions[..., 2] (slot 2). The expression is log1p(clip(x, 0, 60)) / log1p(60). It multiplies this value by the hist_click_dwell_time_vec embedding and adds the result to the history vector. The default is click_dwell_time_norm_scale=60.0.

Why it matters: First, the click_dwell_time head now has a training target as a binary classification for the first time. The target is "the probability of dwelling 10 seconds or more". Netflix N-tower and YouTube dwell families keep "whether the user dwelled (binary)" and "dwell time(regression)" as separate heads, whereas X, in contrast, unified them into one head trained as a binary classification. Second, the history encoder now references the actual post-click dwell time in the user history (previously there was only enable_dwell_time). Third, the symmetry between serving and training is shaken. _rescale_sigmoid_heads_for_inference multiplies sigmoid heads by norm_scale to restore the original units. However, the binary loss is explicitly excluded from this rescaling (if loss_config.loss_type == "binary": continue). In serving, this head stays a probability in [0,1]. The ranking scorer multiplies ContClickDwellTimeWeight (param.rs) by this probability. This weight was 0.0 at the time of this commit and became 0.4 in the 2026-09-29 commit (Gen4+31) verified (weight table). verified — phoenix/xrex/models/loss_recsys.py, phoenix/xrex/configs/xrecsys.py (+13/−1), phoenix/xrex/models/recsys_feature_prep.py (+12).

C. An XAUC metric that measures ordering quality among clicked candidates was added.

XAUC is a clicked-only pairwise concordance metric, and the new function is metric_xauc(pred, gt, valid_mask, max_samples=2048). It flat-reshapes the values and reduces them to at most 2048 with stride sampling (stride = max(N // 2048, 1)). It then computes pairwise concordance with a 2048×2048 outer-difference matrix.

  • A valid pair is pair_valid = mask_i & mask_j & (dy != 0).
  • Concordant means sign(dy) == sign(dp); tied means dp == 0 and is weighted 0.5.
  • The metric value is (concordant + 0.5·tied) / pair_valid_count. If pair_valid_count == 0, it returns 0.
  • xauc_mask = _cont_loss_mask & (xauc_gt > 0) uses positive-only samples. That is, it measures ordering quality only among candidates that received a click.
  • The stat name is {metric_name}-xauc-clicked.

For the binary loss type, the xauc gt keeps the original units as clip(gt_raw, 0, norm_scale). It is reconstructed from the pre-binarization value rather than the post-binarization one, to preserve the per-sample rank signal. For binary heads, it additionally emits RCE (relative cross entropy) and ratio-pos.

Why it matters: It measures the ranking quality of continuous heads such as dwell and purchase-value by ordering concordance rather than by the magnitude of the predicted values. In ads value optimization, "the ability to get the order of large revenue right" is more directly tied to auction performance than "the accuracy of the absolute revenue prediction". Because the sampling is strided rather than random, it has a bias that depends on the sequence-packing order. Even so, the budget limit of not computing more than 2048² pairs per training step takes priority. verified — phoenix/xrex/models/recsys_model.py.

D. In serving, sigmoid-head predictions are restored to original units, except for binary heads.

_rescale_sigmoid_heads_for_inference handles this. In the serving forward path, among continuous_action_losses, it multiplies the predictions of heads with activation == "sigmoid" && loss_type != "binary" by norm_scale, restoring the scale before training-time normalization. That is, if a continuous label that was log/scale-normalized in training was regressed with a sigmoid, serving stretches it back to original units. Binary heads are the exception and stay a probability in [0,1]. verified — phoenix/xrex/models/recsys_model.py.

E. The index mapping of the gender categorical embedding changed without notice.

The user_gender index changed from the hardcoded Male=2, Female=1, other=0 to using the proto enum integer as is. The file is phoenix/crates/common/xai-recsys/src/util.rs (+17/−5).

A new regression test, user_gender_is_raw_proto_enum, pins that the three values (Male, Female, Unknown) must match g as i16 exactly.

Why it matters: If the proto Gender enum is UNKNOWN=0, MALE=1, FEMALE=2 (typical proto practice), the embedding indices of Male and Female are swapped. The previously trained embedding table is reinterpreted with misaligned indices, so until retraining, the gender signal in serving has its sign flipped. Also, non-binary values were previously lumped unconditionally into 0, but they now take the index the proto enum defines. The proto definition needs to be rechecked at the open-source mirror point. For a silent embedding index change like this, the open question is whether retraining ran alongside it. Gen4+22 itself is not a code change that forces a training reset to account for this migration, so the actual deployment point is what to watch inferred. verified — phoenix/crates/common/xai-recsys/src/util.rs.

G. DSCP=InferenceCritical was set on the VMRanker gRPC client.

One line, .dscp(Some(Dscp::InferenceCritical)), was added to the LoadBalancedChannel::builder chain in home-mixer/clients/vm_ranker_client.rs (+2/−1). DSCP (Differentiated Services Code Point) is a QoS field in the IP header, used on network paths for traffic classification and prioritization. InferenceCritical first appears in this commit (other clients not confirmed).

Why it matters: This setting tags VMRanker calls with the highest-priority tier of the data-center network, to suppress latency inflation even under congestion. It pairs with the recent cleanup in Gen4+8 that reduced the VMRanker path to a thin layer passing rank server results straight through, and it is evidence that a judgment that VMRanker is "critical to home ranking tail latency" has been deployed inferred. verified — home-mixer/clients/vm_ranker_client.rs.

I. The Grox reply-spam classifier now uses two models depending on the thread follower count, and the task threshold was also raised.

Three changes came together.

  • Constants were added in grox/flows/reply_spam/constants.py (+3).
    • GEMMA_REPLY_SPAM = "oai-gemma4-26b-reply-spam": presumably a dedicated fine-tuned variant.
    • GEMMA_REPLY_SPAM_MIN_FOLLOWERS = 150_000: model routing threshold
    • GROK_GEMMA_FOLLOWER_SPLIT = 180_000: task eligibility threshold
  • In grox/flows/reply_spam/classifier_simple_reply_scorer.py (+22/−4), SimpleReplyScorer has two samplers, oai_gemma4 and oai_gemma4_reply_spam.
    • _sampler(post) looks at the max follower count of the thread root, post.ancestors[0], and the thread tail, post.ancestors[-1]. If this value exceeds 150k, it selects the dedicated oai_gemma4_reply_spam; otherwise it selects the default oai_gemma4.
    • That is, the bigger the thread's reach, the more it is routed to the dedicated fine-tuned model.
  • In grox/flows/reply_spam/task_filter.py (+3/−2), both task thresholds changed 150000 → GROK_GEMMA_FOLLOWER_SPLIT (180000).
    • The targets are TaskSpamFilter.FOLLOWER_COUNT_THRESHOLD_FOR_SPAM_DETECTION and TaskReplyRankingFilter.FOLLOWER_COUNT_THRESHOLD_FOR_REPLY_RANKING.
    • The previous value was 150k from the 2026-09-08 commit (Gen4+17). Compared with 100k in Gen4+7, it is an 80% increase.

It matters that the two thresholds differ.

  • Task eligibility is 180k. Only threads where both the reply target and the thread root have 180k followers or fewer enter the spam verdict pipeline verified — task_filter.py:78-85.
  • The model routing threshold is 150k. The dedicated model is used above 150k.
  • So as of this commit, the dedicated model is used only for threads in the 30k band between the two thresholds (above 150k and up to 180k) verified — classifier_simple_reply_scorer.py:35-45.

Why it matters: The direction is to use a dedicated fine-tuned model on the judgment that reply-spam patterns in large-account threads have a different statistical distribution from ordinary spam inferred. Read together with the coordinated_spam threshold change from 10k to 30k in Gen4+21, the whole spam pipeline is being subdivided toward "handling high-follower and low-follower bands with different models and criteria" inferred. verified — grox/flows/reply_spam/constants.py, grox/flows/reply_spam/classifier_simple_reply_scorer.py, grox/flows/reply_spam/task_filter.py.

J. Grox adds the quoted author's handle and a self-quote marker to the quote-post wording it passes to the LLM.

A by @handle notation and a self-quote marker were added in grox/core/lm/post.py (+10/−1). The thread renderer that feeds the LLM input now improves the opening sentence of a quote post as follows.

  • If the quoted user has a handle, it writes "This Post quotes Post <id> by @<handle>; the quoted content below is embedded within this Post".
  • If the quoter has the same handle as the quoted user, it adds a marker such as "...by @<handle> (this Post's author, quoting their OWN post)".

Why it matters: At the prompt layer, it gives grox judges such as reply spam and PtOS a hint to distinguish semantically between a "quote that is actually a self-quote (self-QT)" and a "quote of someone else". Because self-QT is one of the patterns observed in spam traffic (self-boosting to expand reach), this marker is expected to raise verdict accuracy. verified — grox/core/lm/post.py (+10/−1).

Why it matters: It logs the verdicts AES executed in a state that can be joined with the original score run. It gives a join key to back-reference a policy-violation verdict to a specific score batch and to use when handling verdict reproduction, audit, and rollback. verified — abuse-enforcement-service/service-lib/src/lib.rs.
