Gen4+23 (2026-09-17, 42266f3) — Introduced FavHoldoutFilter; click-dwell scoring redefined from a low-fav penalty to a dwell × click product; cold-start Treatment arm drops the MoE gate and max age 24h→48h; Phoenix proto vacates LLM_JUDGE_* after 4 days and adds CLIENT_TWEET_LIVE_STREAM_REPLY; ads delayed conversion Tier 2/3 (20 kinds) added; VF's own twemcache (2,900 lines) removed and migrated to the unified xai_cache; VF evaluate_tweets RPC and Thrift Action response decoder introduced; UTH daily takedown label reproduction infrastructure

With this commit, home-mixer gained a holdout filter that withholds a post from up to 15% of viewers depending on the post's fav (like) count bucket, and in the slot of the ranking's low-fav penalty it gained an option that multiplies the dwell prediction by the click prediction. Both the new filter and the product option are off by default verified (daily).

The change is +2288/−3627 across 64 files, and the large number of deletions comes from removing the whole VF twemcache subtree (a little over 2,900 lines) verified — xai-org/x-algorithm@42266f3.

A. A new filter, FavHoldoutFilter, was added to home-mixer. The new file is home-mixer/filters/fav_holdout_filter.rs (166 lines, new). This filter is wired in home-mixer/candidate_pipeline/phoenix_candidate_pipeline.rs after InventoryHoldoutFilter. The holdout probability is determined by a 23-tier stepped table of fav count.

If fav_count <= 1, the rate is 0% and the post is shown to every viewer. Above that it rises in steps to a maximum of 15% at 10K+ fav. The holdout decision reuses InventoryHoldoutFilter::is_held_out(post_id, viewer_id, percent). This function computes a 100-modular bucket of (post_id, viewer_id) using splitmix64 double mixing and holds the post out if the value is < percent. In other words, the same post is deterministically held out for the same viewer, and even for the same post only a different subset of viewers is removed. It is off by default with Param EnableFavHoldout=false.

B. The holdout-rate params of InventoryHoldoutFilter were confirmed. An item that had long remained undisclosed was resolved. home-mixer/filters/inventory_holdout_filter.rs references three params: InventoryHoldoutOriginalsPercent, InventoryHoldoutRepliesPercent and InventoryHoldoutRetweetsPercent. The post-kind mapping is retweeted_tweet_id → Retweet, in_reply_to_tweet_id → Reply, and anything else → Original, and a quoted post is treated as Original. The gate opens when EnableInventoryHoldout=true and at least one of the three values is >0. A retweet is judged on the original tweet_id, so it shares the holdout decision with the original.

C. The EnableClickDwellLowFavRatePenalty family was deleted from the ranking score and EnableCdwellOnImpr (dwell × click product) was introduced. The changed files are home-mixer/scorers/ranking_scorer.rs (+10/−32) and home-mixer/params/param.rs. Five fields previously held by ScoringWeights and the five corresponding params were deleted. These fields had existed since the Gen4 release (47c1bcd) verified — param.rs:387-416. The deleted fields are enable_click_dwell_low_fav_rate_penalty and baseline/alpha/floor/cap, and a single enable_cdwell_on_impr: bool took their place.

The previous function low_fav_penalized_click_dwell computed a heuristic penalty that lowered the dwell prediction when the fav rate was low. It was renamed click_dwell_term, and its computation was simplified to click_dwell_time × click_score. The gate observation label also changed gate.click_dwell_low_fav_rate_penalty → gate.cdwell_on_impr. It is off by default with Param EnableCdwellOnImpr=false.

D. Two gates were relaxed together in the Treatment arm of the author cold-start scorer. The changed files are home-mixer/scorers/author_cold_start.rs (+7/−50) and home-mixer/params/param.rs.

  • Previously, ViewerArm::Treatment eligibility was corpus == Treatment && is_phoenix_moe(c). In Gen4+23 the is_phoenix_moe(c) AND condition was dropped, so it now checks only corpus == Treatment.
  • The separate function cold_start_freshness_eligible(arm, c, max_age), which applied an age cap only to the Treatment arm, was deleted. Now apply_cold_start applies the filter duration_since_creation_opt(c.tweet_id).is_some_and(|age| age <= params.max_post_age) to all arms.
  • The default of ColdStartMaxPostAgeSecs was also increased from 86400 → 172800 (24 hours → 48 hours).
  • The regression tests were also cleaned up, with renames.
    • treatment_viewer_cold_starts_treatment_moe_only → _treatment_authors_only
    • treatment_skips_post_older_than_max_post_age → skips_post_older_than_max_post_age
    • control_ignores_max_post_age was deleted.

E. Two LLM_JUDGE_* entries in the Phoenix proto ActionName were vacated after 5 days. The changed files are phoenix/crates/serving/xai-recsys-proto/proto/recsys.proto and its Python mirror. LLM_JUDGE_RELEVANT_TO_SEARCH=107 and LLM_JUDGE_NOT_RELEVANT_TO_SEARCH=108, introduced in Gen4+20 (6bb4594, 2026-09-12), were deleted. CLIENT_TWEET_LIVE_STREAM_REPLY=107 and RESERVED_108 took their place.

Why it matters The direction of porting LLM judge labels as separate actions onto the search relevance axis was readjusted. We infer that it did not carry through to production inferred.

F. Ads delayed conversion attribution was expanded to 3 tiers. In the same proto, reserved 214 to 252 was narrowed to reserved 234 to 252, and 10 kinds each for tier 2 and tier 3 went into 214-233. Details are in the Gen4+23 entry of the ads conversion action section. The lag definitions and loss weights of tier 2 and tier 3 are not stated explicitly in this commit.

G. The VF sub-repo's own twemcache client was removed entirely. Eleven files under visibility-filtering/twemcache/, a little over 2,900 lines in total, were deleted. The top of safety_label_source/twemcache.rs changed from use crate::twemcache::{Key, TwemcacheClient, TwemcacheError, Value} to use xai_cache::{CacheClient, KVCacheError, Key, Value}. The FallbackReason mapping was unified as KVCacheError::Timeout(_) → Timeout, Backpressure → Backpressure, _ → Other. This reads as moving the twemcache protocol that VF maintained itself (including accrual, discovery, host_pool and ring) to the company-wide KV cache abstraction.

H. The VF service gained an evaluate_tweets RPC and a Thrift Action payload decoder. The new file is visibility-filtering-client/evaluated.rs (122 lines, new), and async fns were added to the traits in vf_client.rs and tweet_safety_label.rs. The client test stub returns Err(Status::unimplemented("unused")), and the VF server's evaluate_tweets also returns Err(Status::unimplemented("EvaluateTweets is not served yet")) verified — visibility-filtering/server.rs:50-56, vf_client.rs:958-970. So only the interface is open, and the actual implementation is pending. evaluated.rs defines the following:

The decoding rules are as follows:

  • 64KB payload cap (all four caps of TConfiguration are 64KiB)
  • Compact Thrift protocol
  • No trailing bytes
  • Action::NotEvaluated is rejected

Why it matters The VF response interface has begun to expand toward returning a complete Thrift Action object to the client, not only the sigil enum (FilteredReason) inferred. Read together with the Gen4+20 xDS LDS listener migration, VF is moving from a thin filter to a richer policy verdict service.

I. A daily takedown label reproduction job stack for Under-the-Hood was added. This stack recomputes the audit labels of the Under-the-Hood tool every day and applies them to a Strato column. There are four new Scala files in under-the-hood/scalding/:

  • UthDailyPostTakedownLabelsJob.scala (283 lines)
  • TakedownDeltas.scala (169 lines)
  • TakedownLabels.scala (103 lines)
  • TakedownReplay.scala (80 lines)

The files changed alongside are underTheHoodLabels.strato +164, UthPctdAccountTakedownEventsJob.scala +392/−63, and UthUserMonthMhPublisherJob.scala +140/−34. Because this line is audit tool serving rather than ranking, the canon only mentions it and does not analyze it in detail.

J. A filter that redacts takedown reasons was added. This filter redacts unenforced takedown reasons so that they are not exposed on the read path. The related files are takedowns/gizmoduck/RedactUnenforcedTakedownsFilter.scala (81 lines) and ReadFilters.scala (39 lines). There are also tweet-entity-service/TakedownReasonsTransform.scala (73 lines) and TakedownReasonsColumn.scala (25 lines).

Undisclosed The following are not yet public:

  • The point at which the mirror values of EnableFavHoldout and EnableCdwellOnImpr change, and the bucket definition of the actual deployment experiment
  • Which training config's target head CLIENT_TWEET_LIVE_STREAM_REPLY (107) is added to (home vs. search)
  • The lag-window definitions and training loss weights of delayed conversion tier 2/3
  • When the server-side implementation of the VF evaluate_tweets RPC lands
  • Whether relaxing the cold-start Treatment arm gates was triggered by measured A/B results or is preparation for the next experiment setup

Gen4+24 (2026-09-18, c279172) — Ads delayed feedback training unified under sample-source 3-stream masking; purchase-value loss narrowed to the early-relabel slice; Phoenix wire proto adds EngagementCounts (user×ads window counts, ad×window counts) and SearchLexicalMatch (matched-word fraction, exact phrase) signals; grox introduces a spam-clone detection flow that compares a reference video bundle against candidate videos with a VLM; per-topic cluster/zone override for abuse-enforcement Kafka topics; Phoenix bundle export separates request-vs-template contracts

In ads ranking training, three delayed-feedback settings were merged into one switch that is off by default, and turning it on determines, per head, which of three sample streams (fresh, early-relabel, late-split) is trained on. The purchase-value regression loss was narrowed to train only on early-relabel samples, and grox gained a flow that compares a reference video bundle with candidate videos using a VLM to identify spam clones verified (daily).

30 files changed, +1491/−154 lines verified — xai-org/x-algorithm@c279172.

A. Three config options were merged into ads_head_masking, and sample-source is split into three streams: FRESH, EARLY_RELABEL and LATE_SPLIT. The three config options condition_conversion_on_click, train_view_through_heads and split_head_training_by_source were all deleted and replaced by a single ads_head_masking: bool = False. All three option references were also removed from RecsysAggregatedModelConfig, build_metric_masks and trainer_recsys. When ads_head_masking=True, the new function ads_head_masking_factor(targets, source_id, num_actions) assembles the loss and metric masks by the following rules:

  • Engagement heads (everything except the CT, VT and twin indices) train only on FRESH_STREAM_ID(=0) samples.
  • CT heads (CLICK_CONDITIONED_ACTION_INDICES) train only on EARLY_RELABEL_STREAM_ID(=1) samples that have a click.
  • VT heads (VIEW_THROUGH_ACTION_INDICES) train only on EARLY_RELABEL_STREAM_ID samples that have no click.
  • Twin heads (new ADS_LATE_WINDOW_TWIN_HEAD_INDICES, 10 delayed actions) train only on LATE_SPLIT_STREAM_ID(=2) samples that have a click and no fresh counterpart.

The twin head list is the 10 base *_DELAYED kinds (204-213) that Gen4+12 introduced on 2026-09-01. Tier 2's 214-223 and tier 3's 224-233, newly created by Gen4+23 on 2026-09-17, have not yet been added to the twin list.

The ADS_LATE_WINDOW_TWIN_SUPPRESSOR dictionary, added at the same time, specifies the fresh-stream counterpart index for each twin head. For example, ADS_PURCHASE_CONVERSION_DELAYED → ADS_PURCHASE_CONVERSION and ADS_WEB_CONVERSION_DELAYED → ADS_ATTRIBUTED_CLICK_CONVERSION; note that the suppressor of web-conversion delayed is attributed-click-conversion. ads_head_masking_factor looks up this suppressor value with no_early_counterpart = 1 - targets[:, :, suppressor_index] and multiplies it into the late-split twin mask. If the fresh-stream counterpart has already been observed for the same (user, ad) sample, the late-split twin head is excluded from training to avoid duplicate observation.

The metric slices were also redefined. build_metric_masks lost the condition_conversion_on_click and split_head_training_by_source parameters and takes only ads_head_masking. A new slice late_split_no_early (= mask × late × click × no_early) was added, and the existing fresh, delayed_clicked and delayed_non_clicked remain. verified — phoenix/xrex/models/ads_head_masking.py (67 lines, new), phoenix/xrex/data/recsys/ads_late_window.py (29 lines, new), phoenix/xrex/models/recsys_model.py (+50/−55), phoenix/xrex/train/trainer_recsys.py (+19/−2).

Why it matters A training code path that splits delayed-feedback labeling into three streams (fresh, early, late) was introduced verified. However, ads_head_masking is False by default and no public config in this commit turns it on, so the point at which it was applied to production training is unknown verified — c279172 phoenix/ grep. Of the three booleans, condition_conversion_on_click has existed since the Gen4 release, and train_view_through_heads and split_head_training_by_source were added by Gen4+6 (recsys_model.py in 47c1bcd and 28e414f). In effect, this commit tidied up the fact that the effective combinations of the three booleans are a mapping of a single categorical sample-source; the earlier practice of leaving the 8 view-through kinds out of training with the default train_view_through_heads=False is gone. With ads_head_masking=True, view-through heads are automatically trained on the "no click" slice of the early-relabel stream.

B. The purchase-value loss was narrowed to train only on the EARLY_RELABEL slice. purchase_value_valid_mask was narrowed from sample_source > 0 to sample_source == EARLY_RELABEL_STREAM_ID. The purchase-value regression is not trained on the late-split stream. The loss stat name also changed from purchase-value-* to purchase-value_delayed_clicked-*. The slice scope (clicked samples among delayed samples) was put into the stat name.

The new function purchase_value_smoothed_stats emits EMA-smoothed loss, ratio-mae, target-ratio, baseline-mean-usd, usd-mae and calib. The default smoothing windows are (1 << 28, 1 << 30), which are 2^28 ≈ 268 million samples and 2^30 ≈ 1.07 billion samples, respectively. trainer_recsys._purchase_value_ema_keys keeps a shape=(10,) tensor as EMA state for these two windows. If the shape does not match when the checkpoint is reloaded, it is reinitialized to zeros.

Two new stats are also emitted verified — phoenix/xrex/models/loss_recsys.py (+75/−10), phoenix/xrex/train/trainer_recsys.py (+19/−2).

  • purchase-value_delayed_clicked-usd-mae is the MAE in dollars.
  • purchase-value_delayed_clicked-calib is the sum of predicted ratios ÷ the sum of actual ratios, a calibration against the advertiser baseline.

Because the default purchase_value_loss_weight=0.0 is kept, actual activation is still opt-in verified (same source).

Why it matters The ads revenue regression loss of Gen4+22 was narrowed from the practice of training on everything "inside the delayed observation window" to training on only the "short-delay (early) slice". The late-split slice trains only the twin classification head and does no regression. X ads ranking settled into a two-branch stack. For short-lag observations it trains purchase value as a regression, and for long-lag observations it trains only whether a conversion happened, as a classification.

C. Two new channels, EngagementCounts and SearchLexicalMatch, were added to the Phoenix wire proto. Both channels were applied identically to the two proto mirrors (phoenix/crates/serving/xai-recsys-proto/proto/recsys.proto and phoenix/python/common/xai-proto/proto/recsys.proto).

The EngagementCounts message carries an (action × time-window) count matrix in the request payload.

This message is connected to two slots:

  • PredictNextActionsRequest.user_ads_engagement_counts = 24 is the user's ads engagement history.
  • AdInfo.engagement_counts = 23 is the engagement history of the ad itself.

Server-side training and encoding are not in this commit.

SearchLexicalMatch was attached as TweetInfo.searchLexicalMatch = 38 and carries the following fields:

  • float matchedWordFraction is the fraction of query words that appear in the tweet.
  • bool exactPhrase indicates whether the query string appears as an exact match.

This commit does not state explicitly where xrecsys_search consumes this signal.

Why it matters EngagementCounts is, after ConvAssetIds (ad creative asset ID history) in Gen4+9, the second channel through which recent engagement statistics of a user–ad pair are passed to the ranker as explicit features. SearchLexicalMatch is the first case of a lexical match signal being added as a wire field to the X search ranking line. Instead of the EarlyBird BM25 family, it was simplified to two axes (matched fraction, exact phrase). verified — phoenix/crates/serving/xai-recsys-proto/proto/recsys.proto, phoenix/python/common/xai-proto/proto/recsys.proto.

D. A new flow, safety_ptos_media_injected_adult_infrared_video_spam_detection, was added to the grox safety pipeline. Four new files (146+188+55+44 = 433 lines) were added, and small additions were made to the constants, prompt, rate-limit and generator files. This flow is a streaming task sourced from the Kafka topic safety-ptos-media-injected-adult-infrared-video-spam-detection.

The eligibility filter passes only posts that satisfy all of the following conditions:

  • There is a user.
  • The post or quoted post has a video.
  • It is a high-engagement post whose fav count is at or above media_hydration.deluxe_fav_count_threshold.
  • It has not already been flagged as NSFW.

For posts that pass, the reference video bundle in the blobstore is loaded with MediaReferenceBundleLoader.current("media_injected_adult_infrared_video_spam"). The bundle specification is as follows:

  • Up to 10 videos × up to 10 frames each × up to 2 MiB per frame
  • Refreshed periodically with refresh_interval_s=900 (15 minutes)
  • Identity managed with a 12-character SHA-256 digest

As the VLM, GROK_4_1_FAST_HEDGEHOG_CRITICAL (vision sampler) is called with a 60-second timeout. The prompt interleaves several reference video storyboards and then renders the candidate post with PostRenderer. It then requires a verdict in the format <json>{"violation": bool, "reason": ...}</json>.

If MediaInjectedAdultInfraredVideoSpamVerdict parses successfully and violation=True, the violated policy is added to SafetyPtosState. TaskWriteSafetyPostAnnotationsResultSink sends the result to the safety pipeline sink. verified — grox/flows/ptos/plan_safety_ptos_media_injected_adult_infrared_video_spam_detection.py (44 lines), grox/flows/ptos/task_safety_ptos_media_injected_adult_infrared_video_spam_detection.py (188 lines), grox/core/data_loaders/media_reference_bundle.py (146 lines).

Why it matters For near-duplicate video detection, embedding matching is standard, but instead of embeddings X puts reference storyboard frames directly into the VLM prompt and leaves the visual matching verdict to the VLM. The reference bundle is refreshed from the blobstore every 15 minutes. So when the operations team adds a new clone candidate video to the bundle, it is reflected in verdicts without a separate redeployment. infrared appears to refer to a specific capture mode (for example, adult video clones shot with night vision), but the prompt template that would hold the exact category definition is not public inferred.

E. The request contract and the template contract were separated in Phoenix recsys_bundle_export. A new constant REQUEST_BATCH_KEYS (a set of about 30 batch keys, in the user_*, history_seq.* and candidate_seq.* families) was defined verified — phoenix/xrex/train/recsys_bundle_export.py (+104/−7). _input_spec classifies each batch key into three kinds verified (same file).

  • packing_layout.* is packing_layout.
  • If it is included in REQUEST_BATCH_KEYS, it is source="request" and is filled from the request payload.
  • The rest are source="template". The uniform constant from example_data is baked into the bundle as the fill value.

A non-uniform template raises an error. That is, the request contract and the constant contract of the serving bundle are explicitly separated. verified (same file)

F. Per-topic cluster/zone overrides were added to the Kafka routing of abuse-enforcement-service. Consumer and producer configs can now override the cluster/zone per topic instead of using the service-wide mTLS cluster/zone. The new metric abuse_enforcement_kafka_consumer_start_total{topic,cluster,result} labels the consumer start result at boot time. A filter was also added so that consumer_error_total counts only the set of watched topics, and errors on topics that are not watched do not trigger the watchdog. verified — abuse-enforcement-service/service-lib/src/lib.rs (+390/−56), abuse-enforcement-service/service-lib/src/growthbook.rs (+35/−6), abuse-enforcement-service/service-lib/src/metrics.rs.

G. There was a small cleanup in grox.

  • In _collect_urls, user URLs were pushed behind card URLs. The domain dedup changed from set to dict[str, None], which preserves insertion order. So the order in which domains are exposed in the downstream verdict is stable.
  • In the web_search tool of eapi_sampler, allowed_domains is truncated to the top 5 (MAX_SEARCH_DOMAINS = 5).
  • The name of the reply spam log label changed from "lower than 1000 follower bucket" to "Gemma bucket". This unifies the notation that refers to the Gemma score=0 verdict after the follower two-way routing of Gen4+22.

H. The Brazil2026 election filter was updated for maintenance. Twelve new accounts were hardcoded, and 4 "no live account found" comments were updated. The filter semantics did not change. The practice of updating from TSE dadosabertos continues. verified — home-mixer/filters/brazil_2026_election_filter.rs (+143/−4).

I. The thrift source of Phoenix Cargo moved from a git tag to the crates.io registry. The version is the same at 0.24.0, but a checksum (2b29bdae81cc2dbc498a720e2734e08f26e388c791fca6e95464d41001913714) lock was added, which strengthens supply chain reproducibility. verified — phoenix/Cargo.toml, phoenix/Cargo.lock.

Undisclosed The following are not yet public:

  • When ads_head_masking=True is switched on in mparams (which training config activates it first)
  • When tier 2/3 delayed actions are added to twin masking
  • Where EngagementCounts is consumed (which embedding layer it passes through)
  • Which head or score of xrecsys_search SearchLexicalMatch attaches to

Gen4+29 (2026-09-25, bf7db1b) — VF hydration rewritten as a data-driven Plan/Sources/Execute three-layer design + Hydrator enum 7 → 17 variants + about_this_account/tfe_top_country Strato column added to the hydration budget + 1,493-line single file rules/golden_corpus split into 15 category files + models/region.rs (97 lines) introduced with a 9-region catalog

Hydration in visibility-filtering (the stage that fetches the raw data needed for a verdict from backend services in batches and fills it in) was rewritten from one function per hydrator to execution by a data table and a scheduler. Lookups that use the same input against the same backend are merged automatically into one RPC, and the viewer country is looked up directly from About This Account data and used for the conversation-control country allowed-list verdict verified (daily).

87 files changed, +7,780/−5,759 lines verified — xai-org/x-algorithm@bf7db1b.

A. Hydration was rewritten from a function layer into a data table and a scheduler. Until yesterday (Gen4+28), each hydrator variant had its own function in a separate .rs file, such as conversation_control_hydrator.rs, exclusive_content_hydrator.rs, and socialgraph_hydrator.rs. All of that structure was deleted, and execution moved to the following three files.

  • visibility-filtering/hydration/plan.rs is a new 471-line file. It registers the NodeSpec { source, part, key, label } data of each Hydrator variant through the Hydrator::spec() const fn.
    • Source is the backend, with eight kinds: TesPureCore, TesComposite, TesConversationControl, SafetyLabels, GizmoduckViewer, GizmoduckAuthor, Flock, and ViewerCountry.
    • Part is what is read inside that backend, and has Column, Fields(&[QueryFields]), and Edge(Graph, EdgeDirection).
    • KeyOrigin is the origin of the input key, and has RequestTweets, Viewer, PureCoreAuthor, PureCoreReplyRoot, ExclusiveConversationAuthor, ConversationRoot(&[ConversationControlArm]), and ViewerForCoAllowedList.
    • HydrationPlan::new(level, hydrators) groups the requested hydrator set into (source, input) pairs and merges hydrators with the same backend and the same input dependency into one RPC.
    • Group::fields() builds the union of the field sets, and Group::edges() merges socialgraph edge queries.
    • Three compile-time asserts (inputs_precede_nodes, author_keys_come_from_pure_core, Hydrator::VARIANTS.len() <= u32::BITS) lock the scheduling-order and bitset-width invariants.
  • visibility-filtering/hydration/execute.rs is a new 1,280-line file. HydrationPlan::hydrate(sources, request) schedules the dependency graph with FuturesUnordered. The algorithm proceeds in the following order.
    • Initialize the ready queue with the groups whose input.is_none().
    • Wrap the RPC of each ready group in a Call<'a> future and push it to running.
    • Store the result of a completed group in Store<'a>. The result is a Reply enum (PureCores, Tweets, Controls, Labels, Viewer, Authors, Edges, ViewerCountry).
    • Promote to ready the child groups that had this group as a dependency.
    • Repeat this process.
  • visibility-filtering/hydration/sources.rs is a new 445-line file. The Sources trait defines eight methods, one for each of the eight backends.
    • The methods are pure_cores(tweet_ids), tweets(tweet_ids), conversation_controls(tweet_ids), safety_labels(tweet_ids), viewer(viewer_id, fields), users(user_ids, fields), select_edges(viewer_id, queries), and viewer_country(viewer_id).
    • The ProdSources struct holds TES, composite TES, gizmoduck, socialgraph, about_this_account, safety_labels, PureCoreFallbackCache, and AuthorFallbackCache.

The Hydrator enum grew from 7 variants (Gen4+28) to 17 variants. 13 new names were added and 3, ExclusiveContent, Author, and Relationship, were removed, so the net increase is 10 verified — hydration/mod.rs in 44d37eb and bf7db1b. In the list below, the variants shown in bold are the ones newly added this time. The Hydrators bitset stays a single u32, and an assert checks 17 ≤ 32.

  • PureCore·Tweet·ConversationControl·TweetSafetyLabels·ViewerProfile·AuthorSafety·AuthorLabels·Follows·Blocks·Mutes·MuteRetweets·BlockedByAuthor·BlockedByReplyRoot·SuperFollowsExclusive·RootFollowsViewer·SuperFollowsRoot·ViewerCountry

B. The plan is fixed per SafetyLevel and pinned by golden tests. The plan that RuleEngine::plan(level) builds for each SafetyLevel is locked by golden strings verified plan.rs:422-451. The number of calls per SafetyLevel is as follows verified (same file).

  • filter_all 1 call
  • timeline_home 7 calls
  • timeline_home_recommendations 7 calls
  • timeline_home_hydration 10 calls
  • immersive_expanded_recommendations 7 calls

For example, in the 10-call graph of timeline_home_hydration, each call runs once the following conditions are met verified (same file).

  1. The five calls tes/get_tweet_core_datas, tes/get_tweets_for_visibility, conversation_control/get_conversation_controls, safety_labels/get, and gizmoduck/get_viewer_data start immediately, needing only the request tweet ids and the viewer id.
  2. gizmoduck/get_users runs after pure_core completes. This call looks up the union of the author_safety and labels fields.
  3. blocked_by/batch_check_blocked_by runs after pure_core completes.
  4. exclusive_content/batch_check_super_follows runs after tweet completes.
  5. The call that merges conversation_control/batch_check_followed_by and batch_check_super_follows, and conversation_control/tfe_top_country, run after conversation_control completes.

C. An About This Account client (166 lines) that reads the Strato column about_this_account/tfe_top_country.User was added. AboutThisAccountClient::tfe_top_country(user_id) in visibility-filtering/clients/about_this_account_client.rs returns the weighted top country of a user. This result is fed through the ViewerCountry hydrator into the conversation-control country allowed-list verdict. "About This Account" is the transparency UI at the bottom of an account profile in the X app (account creation date, top country, name change history). VF now consumes that data source directly.

D. rules/golden_corpus was split into 15 files. The 1,493-line single file visibility-filtering/rules/golden_corpus.rs was deleted and split again by policy category into 15 files under visibility-filtering/rules/golden_corpus/. The verdict matrix can now be pinned separately for each category.

  • The line counts per file are age_gating.rs 267, author_state.rs 119, baseline.rs 56, builders.rs 63, conversation_control.rs 257, exclusive_content.rs 61, interstitial.rs 334, mod.rs 173, oon_media.rs 218, oon_tweet_label.rs 133, oon_user_label.rs 234, relationship.rs 122, takedown.rs 224, tweet_label.rs 195, and tweet_state.rs 90.

E. models/region.rs, which groups ISO country codes into 10 regions, was added. visibility-filtering/models/region.rs is 97 lines, with 10 regions and 250 country codes without duplicates verified. If the 16-country NSFW gating of Gen4+12 (2026-09-01) was country-level, region-level rules can now be expressed as well. No rule that actually uses this catalog appears explicitly in this commit.

  • AFR (58 countries), AUS (33 countries), CAS (6 countries: AF·KG·KZ·TJ·TM·UZ), EAS (8 countries: CN·HK·JP·KP·KR·MN·MO·TW), EUR (54 countries), NAM (40 countries), SAM (14 countries), SAS (7 countries: BD·BT·IN·LK·MV·NP·PK), SEA (11 countries: BN·ID·KH·LA·MM·MY·PH·SG·TH·TL·VN), WES (19 countries: AE·AM·AZ·BH·CY·GE·IL·IQ·IR·JO·KW·LB·OM·PS·QA·SA·SY·TR·YE)

F. The rules catalog shrank considerably. The per-file changes are tweet_rules.rs −575 lines (692 → 117), author_rules.rs −160 lines (182 → 22), registry.rs +226/−58, and rule_spec.rs +141/−161. The two-way Verdict tree introduced in Gen4+26 (2026-09-22) (Withheld{Drop|Tombstone}|Shown{media?,engagement?}) and the data-driven RuleClause structure are kept, and the rules themselves appear to be moving further into data. Details will be tracked in a follow-up batch.

G. There were also incidental changes.

  • In home-mixer/filters/brazil_2026_election_filter.rs (+22/−2), the list of accounts under Brazilian electoral court orders, introduced on 2026-08-14, was updated slightly. The basis is TSE Electoral Resolution No. 23.610 Art. 28 §1º-A.
  • 34 lines were newly added at the same time to both mirrors of the Phoenix proto recsys.proto, and phoenix/xrex/models/transformer.py changed by +42/−5 and recsys_model.py by +5/−1. This batch did not track what the new fields are.

Why it matters VF hydration was rewritten with a 24-hour half-life. conversation_control_hydrator.rs (310 lines), introduced yesterday, was deleted today. The pattern introduced yesterday, in which a predicate declares its required hydrators with const fn hydrators() and RuleEngine::hydrators_for(safety_level) combines them, was rewritten as a NodeSpec data table and the execute.rs scheduler. There are three substantive changes.

  1. The interface changed from functions to data. In yesterday's structure, execution was still a separate function or file per hydrator variant, but today execution is data as well. Adding a rule no longer requires writing a new hydrator function; it is enough to add one line to the NodeSpec table.
  2. RPC group merging is automated. Hydrators with the same backend and the same input are merged into one RPC automatically. The gizmoduck SAFETY and LABELS field lookups and the socialgraph 4-edge lookup of Follows, Blocks, Mutes, and MuteRetweets are examples. In X's structure, where the hydration budget concentrates on fan-out services such as gizmoduck and socialgraph, this directly affects P99.
  3. ViewerCountry formally entered the hydration budget. Previously, country information was carried in the request context, but now hydration fills it by looking up the about_this_account/tfe_top_country.User Strato column directly. The backend of the About This Account transparency UI has been attached to the VF verdict path.

Gen4+30 (2026-09-26, 4c5cfe8) — overturn-hold gate introduced in abuse-enforcement (5,270 lines) + VF hydration split into execute/store + safety_label_hydrator.rs and tes_hydrator.rs deleted entirely + wingman follows client introduced + rules registry locked as static Policy + Phoenix ads purchase-value target catalog (event × level, 6 combinations) + Phoenix Cold retrieval channel added to the cold-start arm-gate

An overturn-hold gate was added to the abuse-enforcement service verified — daily. It is the last precheck that, while a hold is active, prevents automated verdicts from re-applying a suspension or label that a human reviewer overturned on appeal. On the feed side, candidates from the Cold channel of Phoenix retrieval started to be shown only in the Treatment arm of the cold-start experiment verified (same daily).

This commit changed 80 files, with +9,130/−2,652 lines verified — xai-org/x-algorithm@4c5cfe8.

A. abuse-enforcement gained the overturn-hold gate as its last precheck.

abuse-enforcement-service/service-lib/src/overturn_hold.rs was added as a new 5,270-line file. Its purpose is to prevent automated verdicts from re-applying a suspension or label that a human reviewer overturned while handling an appeal, for as long as that hold is active. The comment at the top of the file states this purpose directly: "the last precheck before a suspend (or a gated label) is dispatched. It exists so we do not re-apply an enforcement that a human reviewer already overturned on appeal".

The gate consists of a mode, a kind, a remote ledger lookup, and a circuit breaker.

  • There are three gate modes (GateMode::Off | Shadow | Enforce). Shadow only runs the verdict and does not dispatch the action, and Enforce actually blocks.
  • There are two gate kinds: GateKind::Suspend, which prevents re-applying a suspension, and GateKind::Label, which prevents re-applying a label. Suspensions are judged separately as two kinds: temporary (GatedAction::Suspend) and permanent (GatedAction::PermSuspend).
  • Active holds are received from a remote ledger. An HTTP client calls /v1/holds/lookup.
    • The timeouts are CONNECT_TIMEOUT of 200ms and DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS of 200ms, and the tuning range of the latter is 10–5000ms.
    • The positive cache is 60 seconds (up to 3,600 seconds), and the response body cap is 64 KiB.
    • CACHE_MAX_WEIGHT of the moka cache is 100,000, and CONFIG_PUBLISH_INTERVAL, a separate constant, is 15 seconds.
  • The circuit breaker opens when failures reach BREAKER_FAILURES=5, and after opening it waits for DEFAULT_BREAKER_OPEN=10s. If a reachable error (for example, HTTP 5xx) occurs five times in a row, it backs off by REACHABLE_ERROR_BACKOFF=5s.

The gate is wired into the lib.rs of AES (abuse-enforcement-service) at two points verified — abuse-enforcement-service/service-lib/src/lib.rs:166-509.

  • At startup, the gate is built with HoldGate::from_url(cfg.overturn_hold_ledger_url, ..., cfg.overturn_hold_env), and an Arc<HoldGate> is injected into EnforcementCtx.
  • On the execution path, gated_actions(&specs, &cfg) picks and returns the gate-target actions among the dispatch candidates. Also, strip_held_labels(&mut specs, &gate.strip_labels) removes the names of already overturned labels from the spec.

The verdict result has two statuses.

  • STATUS_HOLD_OVERTURNED = "hold_overturned" is the case where the hold was active and the action was actually blocked.
  • STATUS_HOLD_LOOKUP_FAILED = "hold_lookup_failed" is the case where the ledger lookup failed.

The same outcome dict carries five diagnostic keys: overturn_hold_id, overturn_hold_mode, overturn_hold_head, overturn_hold_expires_at, and overturn_hold_labels_stripped. The dedup retention layer also handles the two statuses separately verified — lib.rs:2469-2501. New entries dedup_retention_for(STATUS_HOLD_OVERTURNED) and dedup_retention_for(STATUS_HOLD_LOOKUP_FAILED) were added verified (same file).

B. State management for VF hydration was separated from the execution file into its own file.

State was split out of execute.rs, which had handled both state and execution, into store.rs, and only execution remains in execute.rs. visibility-filtering/hydration/store.rs is new at 339 lines, and the line count change of execute.rs is −141 lines (+394/−535). store.rs defines the Store struct that holds in-flight results during hydration execution.

It has eight Option<...> fields.

  • pure_cores: tweet skeleton
  • tweets: TweetForVisibility
  • controls: ConversationControl arm
  • labels: SafetyLabelMap
  • viewer: ViewerProfile
  • authors: DecodedAuthor
  • edges: Vec<(Hydrators, RawHydrationBatch<Hydrators>)>
  • viewer_country: Arc<str>

Store::keys(origin: KeyOrigin) -> Vec<u64> extracts and resolves the input keys needed by child hydrators for each origin axis. The origin axes include RequestTweets, Viewer, ViewerForCoAllowedList, PureCoreAuthor, PureCoreReplyRoot, and ExclusiveConversationAuthor. The Store::callable: Hydrators field fixes, as a bitset, the hydrators that can run in this request.

In the same commit, two leftovers from the previous day's commit (Gen4+29) were deleted.

  • visibility-filtering/hydration/safety_label_hydrator.rs is −167 lines, and the file was deleted.
  • visibility-filtering/hydration/tes_hydrator.rs is −79 lines, and the file was deleted.

The two files had become unnecessary when the functionality moved to the data-driven scheduler the previous day, but they stayed for a 24-hour grace period and were removed entirely this time.

C. A follows client was added that moves direct socialgraph calls to the wingman path.

visibility-filtering/clients/wingman_client.rs was added as a new 54-line file verified.

The interface is only WingmanClient::batch_exists_intersect(viewer_id, root_author_ids) -> Option<Vec<Exists>>, and it uses IntersectMode::FwdXRev. FwdXRev is a mode that checks the forward (viewer → author) and reverse (author → viewer) directions at the same time. With this mode, "do the reply root author and the viewer follow each other?" is decided in a single RPC. Related code shrank in socialgraph_client.rs (+43/−27). The FOLLOWS_GRAPH=1 constant shows that wingman holds multiple graphs, but graph 2 and later are not confirmed in this release.

visibility-filtering/rules/registry.rs was effectively rewritten completely at +206/−203. The core is the Policy<'a> struct, which holds the rule set for each SafetyLevel. However, this struct and the five statics below already existed in the same form in Gen4+29 (bf7db1b) verified — registry.rs:23-29, 125-170.

RuleEngine::select(level) -> &'static Policy references one of the five statics for each requested SafetyLevel. Policy::with_additional(base, additional) merges two slices to build a derived policy. RuleEngine::wired_rule_names(level) returns the list of rule names wired into a policy verified — registry.rs:346-460. The golden test pins, by assertion, the list that wired_rule_names returns for each of the five registered SafetyLevels verified (same file).

visibility-filtering/rules/metrics.rs was also added as a new 58-line file. Until the previous day, the hydration metrics.rs also handled metrics related to rule verdicts, and as verdicts and hydration were separated, the metrics were separated too.

Why it matters The real headline of this commit is the new overturn-hold gate in abuse-enforcement. The 24-hour half-life pattern of the VF overhaul also continues. safety_label_hydrator and tes_hydrator, which were functions until the previous day, were deleted this time, and the state logic of execute.rs, introduced the previous day, was separated into store.rs.

  1. The priority between automated verdicts and human verdicts is fixed as data. Whenever a suspension spec is created on the automated dispatch path, the last gate that looks up the hold ledger to check "has this action ever been reversed by a human?" and gates on it is now explicit in code.
  2. The reversal of a suspension is treated as persistent state. A hold is a time window with an expiry time (expires_at). During that window, automated actions against a specific target (account or label) are blocked. A human reviewer's approval of an appeal becomes a policy entry meaning "no re-application until time T", not a "one-time reversal".
  3. The follows lookup moved to the wingman path. As direct socialgraph calls move to the wingman path, the fan-out layout of hydration RPCs is reorganized again. The fact that FOLLOWS_GRAPH=1 is fixed as a constant suggests that wingman holds multiple graphs (2, 3, ...), but the rest is not confirmed in this release.
  4. The Phoenix ads purchase-value target is fixed as data. Of the 6 combinations of ValueEvent 3 × ValueLevel 2, 2 REQUIRED and 4 PUBLISHED targets were made explicit. The $100k per-event cap is also fixed in the training and evaluation contract.
  5. Cold retrieval candidates entered the cold-start experiment. The path by which the new Cold channel of Phoenix retrieval flows to the Treatment arm of the cold-start experiment is fixed as data (a matches! pattern).

The server for the remote ledger that the overturn-hold gate in the previous commit (Gen4+30) called was released as a read-only lookup service verified — daily. On the ranking side, the click weight in the home-mixer production cron mirror dropped from 0.4 to 0.3, and the post-click dwell time weight rose from 0.0 to 0.4 verified(same daily).

This commit changed 89 files, with +9,552/−2,325 lines verified — xai-org/x-algorithm@a707cc2.

A. abuse-ledger-service, the server for overturn-hold, was released.

The client overturn_hold.rs introduced in Gen4+30 (2026-09-26) called POST /v1/holds/lookup on a remote ledger. This commit released the full server implementation.

  • The Cargo crate name is xai-abuse-ledger-service.
  • There are 11 files (api.rs, boot.rs, codes.rs, config.rs, lib.rs, main.rs, metrics.rs, pg.rs, repo.rs, sql.rs, tls.rs), totaling +2,282 lines verified — per-file stats of a707cc2.
  • It is a read-only lookup service that combines axum, deadpool-postgres, and rustls.

The lookup API takes a user id and a label list via POST and returns a list of holds verified — abuse-ledger-service/src/api.rs.

  • The path is LOOKUP_PATH = "/v1/holds/lookup", the method is POST, and the header is x-request-deadline-ms verified(same file).
  • The request is {user_ids: Vec<i64>, labels: Vec<String>} and the response is {holds: Vec<Hold>, db_ms: u64} verified(same file).
  • The limits are MAX_USER_IDS = 100 and MAX_LABELS = 32, and empty-string labels are rejected verified(same file).
  • budget(deadline, statement_timeout) uses the smaller of the header value and the statement timeout as the actual DB budget verified(same file).
    • Without the header, it uses statement_timeout + QUERY_DEADLINE_SLACK(100ms).
  • The side endpoints are /healthz, /readyz, and /metrics verified(same file).

The lookup SQL reads only holds that have not been cleared and have not yet expired verified — abuse-ledger-service/src/sql.rs.

  • The table is ledger.enforcement_holds verified(same file).
  • The active condition is cleared_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now() verified(same file).
  • action_kind has two values, 'suspend' | 'label'; Suspend is returned regardless of the label, and Label is returned only when it belongs to the requested label set verified(same file).
  • At startup it validates the column projection schema with CONTRACT_SQL (SELECT ... LIMIT 0), and the health check uses PING_SQL (SELECT 1) verified(same file).
  • The tests assert that none of the three SQL statements contains INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/ALTER/DROP/CREATE verified(same file). The server cannot write verified(same file).

The Hold record carries the target user id, action kind, label, expiry time, reason, and so on verified — abuse-ledger-service/src/repo.rs.

The pg constants are as follows verified — abuse-ledger-service/src/pg.rs.

  • The three pool timeouts are POOL_WAIT_TIMEOUT = 1s, POOL_CREATE_TIMEOUT = 1.5s, and POOL_RECYCLE_TIMEOUT = 500ms verified(same file).
  • QUERY_DEADLINE_SLACK = 100ms is also a constant in this file verified(same file).
  • PgError has 7 variants verified(same file).
    • The variants are BadDsn / Connect{Refused|Auth|Tls|Timeout|Other} / Saturated / Transport / Query{sqlstate,message} / Decode / Timeout.
  • SQLSTATE 57014 (query_canceled) maps to ErrorCode::StatementTimeout verified(same file). 28P01/28000 (auth) map to ErrorCode::AuthFailed verified(same file).
  • At boot, boot::contract_check_until_ok keeps AtomicBool<ready> false until the schema check succeeds, and meanwhile /readyz does not return 200 verified(same file).

TLS is rustls-based mTLS implemented in a separate 348-line file. It parses sslmode=require|verify-ca|verify-full and takes the CA/CRT/KEY paths from separate environment variables. The ledger store is protected by mTLS, and this service sits in the role of a read-only proxy for that store.

B. Tweetypie was added to the VF reference comparison targets.

The comparison targets widened to two values, vf_service | tweetypie. A Reference::{None, VfService, Tweetypie} enum was added in visibility-filtering/reference/mod.rs. The environment variable VF_REFERENCE replaces VF_DUAL_CALL_HARNESS_ENABLED from Gen4+7, and startup fails if the old variable remains. With any value, startup is refused under APP_ENV=prod (staging only).

reference/tweetypie.rs was newly added at 714 lines verified — visibility-filtering/reference/tweetypie.rs. The call target is the Strato column tweetypie/getTweetFields.Tweet, and the request carries GetTweetFieldsOptions { visibility_policy: VISIBILITY_POLICY_USER_VISIBLE, ... }. Tweetypie then returns the response with the tweet-level visibility decision (Action::Allow | Drop(reason)) already attached, and this is diffed against the Rust VF's own verdict. The six constants are listed below.

  • TWEETYPIE_MAX_BATCH_SIZE = 250: batches 250 tweets at a time.
  • MAX_IN_FLIGHT = 32: the semaphore fan-out cap.
  • TWEETYPIE_TIMEOUT = 1500ms
  • SAFETY_LEVEL = SafetyLevel::TimelineHomeHydration: fixes the verdict level requested from Tweetypie.
  • RECORD_CAP_PER_MINUTE = 20: the sample log cap.
  • WEB_CLIENT_APPLICATION_ID = 3_033_300

There are 7 result classes (Allow / BareDrop / Drop / Suppressed / NotFound / Failed / Missing). There are also 7 failure reasons (NoValue / StratoError / RateLimited / DecodeError / RpcError / OverCapacity / TweetypieFailed). Each is a label of the vf_tweetypie_reference_compare metric.

Why it matters Three facts about safety actions, VF verification, and ranking weights overlap in this commit.

  1. The trust layer of the automated suspension policy was physically separated into two services. abuse-enforcement decides dispatch, and abuse-ledger-service makes human reviewers' decisions (overturn) available for read-only lookup. abuse-enforcement queries the ledger only over HTTP (POST /v1/holds/lookup), and it is abuse-ledger-service that connects to ledger.enforcement_holds in Postgres verified — overturn_hold.rs:25, abuse-ledger-service/src/sql.rs:1-11. The latter's SQL consists of only three statements, PROBE_SQL for lookup, CONTRACT_SQL for column contract checks, and PING_SQL for connection checks, and an assert pins that none of the three contains a write verb; in principle, the dispatch path has no write access to the human-verdict store.
  2. The VF reference comparison target widened beyond its own references to the storage layer (Tweetypie). The Rust VF ↔ Scala VF diff is biased toward implementation drift. Tweetypie holds visibility decisions already attached to the tweet itself, so diffing against it catches drift between the "storage-axis decision" and the "serving-axis decision". Fixing the Safety Level to TimelineHomeHydration and refusing to start in prod makes explicit that this harness is a correctness verification tool, not a safety net.
  3. Ranking has begun to trust "clicks" less. ClickWeight 0.4 → 0.3 and ContClickDwellTimeWeight 0.0 → 0.4 flipped together in the same cron sync. In the serving weighted sum, the weight multiplied by the click-dwell head prediction went from 0.0 to 0.4 verified — xai-value-model/scoring.rs:108. We read this as the order in which the head brought into the training loss in Gen4+22 passed verification and came to be used in serving inferred. The direction that "stayed after clicking" fits the production objective better than "clicked" is pinned in code; the exact ×1.1 on Not Interested also strengthens the explicit negative signal.

The hydration stage that fills in the data VF needs for verdicts was rebuilt into a structure that remembers request state per key, and the original post of a retweet is now filled in within a single call verified — daily. In the same commit, the Phoenix retrieval two-tower configuration was organized into a preset catalog, and the home-mixer cold-start parameters changed substantially all at once in the cron mirror verified(same daily).

The commit covers 69 files, +3,306/−1,489 verified — xai-org/x-algorithm@77d431a. It came one day after Gen4+31 (a707cc2). The four-day run from Gen4+29 through +30 and +31 to +32 completes the VF hydration rewrite.

A. The VF hydration Store was rewritten as a Fetcher<V> trait array. The new file visibility-filtering/hydration/fetcher.rs (NEW +113) defines the Fetcher<V> and AnyFetcher traits.

  • Inside is a single HashMap<u64, State<V>>, which holds an enum State<V> { Pending, Landed(Hydrated<V>) } state per key.
  • claim(keys) -> Vec<u64> marks only keys not yet present as Pending and returns only the keys that will actually be sent over RPC. This filters duplicates and also joins with earlier calls (dedup, join with the previous call).
  • land(&[u64], HydrationBatch<u64, V>) fills responses into the claimed keys and fills keys without a response with Hydrated::NotFound.
  • has_incomplete/is_incomplete/has_claimed/is_claimed determine whether a re-call is needed.

The 8 Option<TweetHydrationBatch<...>> fields that visibility-filtering/hydration/store.rs had in the previous day's commit, Gen4+31 (a707cc2), were all replaced by Fetcher<V> this time verified — store.rs:54-84.

  • Each of the 8 Edge variants (Follows / Blocks / Mutes / MuteRetweets / BlockedBy / SuperFollows / FollowedBy / SecondDegree) has one Fetcher<bool>.
  • They are held in the array edges: [Fetcher<bool>; Edge::VARIANTS.len()].

B. retweet.rs was simplified from calling hydrate twice to calling it once and expanding in-flight. evaluate_merging_sources as of Gen4+31 was rewritten verified — retweet.rs (+562/−110).

  • Until the previous day, the original batch was filled first with filter_tweets.hydrate(request). Then retweet source candidates were extracted via source_ids, and a second, separate filter_tweets.hydrate(...) call was sent for sources not in the request batch to build the fetched hydration. Finally, the outcomes of the two results were merged.
  • From this commit, filter_tweets.hydrate_with_retweet_sources(request) is called only once. Internally, the moment pure_cores lands, this call runs store.join_retweet_sources(), attaches to request_tweets those source_tweet_ids of pure_cores that are not yet in the request, and returns Landing::SourcesJoined verified — store.rs:308-330.
  • When the scheduler in execute.rs receives Landing::SourcesJoined, it puts the inputless() groups back into ready, claims new keys only for fetched sources, and sends the expanded batch verified — execute.rs:112-118.
    • inputless() groups are the initial groups with no pure_core dependency.
    • Because the Fetcher's claim filters duplicates, keys already in the request batch are not requested again.

The new metric RetweetSources::{NoSource, InBatch, Fetched} is attached as a label to record_phase verified — filter.rs:62-79. The test each_request_kind_labels_its_phase_samples pins the three cases ([2] → NoSource, [1,2,3,5] → InBatch, [1,2,3,4] → Fetched) verified — retweet.rs:721-738. On the second call (is_first=false), the record_expanded_batch metric is also recorded verified — execute.rs:76-79.

The new file visibility-filtering/treatment.rs (NEW +119) isolates in one place the projection of rules' verdicts into thrift, proto, and metric representations. treatment.rs projects the pure Verdict (Withheld / Shown{media, engagement}) that rules emit into three kinds of downstream representations verified.

  • thrift_action(&Verdict, SafetyLevel) -> Action projects to the thrift action::Action.

  • metric_label(&Verdict) -> &'static str returns a 6-way metric label.

The last sync in the comment header was updated from 2026-09-28T16:00:35Z to 2026-09-29T17:02:52Z verified. This time, six knobs of the cold-start pipeline were adjusted substantially as one set.

  • The Phoenix cold retrieval channel was turned on (0 → 200 posts).
  • The home impression threshold for candidate posts was lowered (1000 → 200). Only posts with fewer than 200 impressions remain, so the targets are narrowed verified — author_cold_start.rs:293-294.
  • The author follower cap was effectively lifted (1000 → 50k).
  • The post age was shortened drastically, from two days to two hours.
  • Exploration was also turned on through Thompson sampling.

This change appears to be the actual production tuning of the HOME_COLD=13 channel, which was introduced in Gen4+28 and incorporated into the cold-start arm-gate in Gen4+30 inferred.

The logic did not change.

Why it matters Four facts overlap in this commit.

  1. VF hydration gained the ability to expand again midway. Across the four commits from Gen4+29 to +32, over five days, the data-driven pipeline skeleton and the retweet.rs module extraction were completed, and this commit added the Fetcher<V> trait, which made the claim idempotent. The moment pure_cores land, a Landing::SourcesJoined flow takes shape that expands request_tweets in flight and resends the inputless group. The pattern of calling hydrate twice was simplified to calling it once and expanding in flight. The NoSource / InBatch / Fetched metrics are captured as labels, so how often expansion batches occur can also be observed. The VF client response was also promoted from Thrift Action to TweetFieldsResultState, so callers can now construct the tweet-service response directly. Isolating the projection of rules results into thrift/proto/metrics in treatment.rs, and tying dashboard.py and six metric labels together with golden tests, completes this simplification.

  2. The Phoenix retrieval two-tower was promoted to a catalog. Until the previous day there was an xrecsys_two_tower.py file, plus small fixes: Gen4+6 put qk_norm=True, attn_logit_cap=-1 and right_anchored_rope=True into the nano config, Gen4+14 changed the base defaults to qk_norm=True and attn_logit_cap=-1, and Gen4+21 changed the H100 attn kernel from pallas_ranker_varlen_attn to cutedsl_ranker_varlen_attn. However, the registry catalog itself was not yet fixed. In this commit, six presets (default, immersive-only and its GB300 version, combined in H100 and GB300 versions, and nano) were fixed in MODEL_CFGS, and the catalog appears to have been migrated so that it connects to the production data pipe inferred. In particular, SID-only (a 6-level codebook hash instead of post embeddings), seqpack, the H100/GB300 hardware presets, and the sharing of two heads between Home and Immersive were organized in one file. Paired with the observation in Gen4+13 that sid_codes was also wired into DPA ads products, the SID vocabulary has greater potential to unify three uses: organic posts, ads DPA, and the retrieval two-tower.

  3. The ads conversion head was differentiated along web/app axes. The delayed feedback split in Gen4+6 and the unified ads_head_masking knob in Gen4+24 moved in this commit from a float multiplier inside the training graph to a boolean mask precomputed by the data loader. This move has two implications:

    • It makes the graph independent of sample_source, which secures compilation stability.
    • By training the web conversion head and the app (MMP) conversion head separately, the sample subsets of the two axes keep_web / keep_app can be used differently.

    In terms of mask semantics, this is an exact refactor that keeps the late-window twin suppression logic and changes only where it is computed. The new mutual-exclusion assert with use_seqpack exists because seqpack breaks the correspondence between candidate slots. With the new ADS_ATTRIBUTED_MACT_MMP_{CLICK, VIEW}_INSTALL = 194, 195 in the proto, there is now a channel for formally incorporating MMP-side app-install conversion into the training head.

  4. Home-mixer cold start was set to production parameters. After the HOME_COLD=13 channel introduced in Gen4+28 was incorporated into the cold-start arm-gate in Gen4+30, this commit fixed the parameters. The Phoenix cold retrieval channel was opened from 0 to 200 posts, and MaxPostAge was shortened drastically from 48h to 2h. FollowerCap was effectively lifted from 1000 to 50k, so the author pool surged. ImpressionThreshold was lowered from 1000 to 200, narrowing the targets so that only posts with fewer than 200 home impressions become cold-start slot candidates. Thompson sampling was also turned on. The combination in effect is extremely strict freshness at 2h with a widely opened author pool. Whether this tuning holds up in the A/B test is the checkpoint to watch at the next cron sync.

Adding nine handles to the Brazil 2026 election filter is list maintenance with no logic change. Deleting Composition.rs is a dedup that follows from reusing the shared candidate-pipeline library.

Gen4+33 (2026-10-01, b79b947) — VF introduced a limited-actions policy system (two files, 703 lines) + gRPC caller-identity logging (126 lines) + LimitedEngagement promoted to a structure that accumulates multiple reasons + a self-restart gate for abuse-enforcement-service config changes (173 lines) + Kafka producer rewired onto the boot config snapshot + phoenix-rankall standalone CLI config module split out (84 lines, SID backfill QPS cap 800k) + VF brazil_election_legal/drop/undesirable labels registered + fallback_cache rewritten with quick_cache sync + OptionsBuilder

From this commit on, VF's verdict response carries not only the restriction reason but also, for each reason, the list of actions to block and localized copy per action, and a single verdict can accumulate multiple restriction reasons verified. This means clients no longer need to maintain their own action mapping and localization. This commit was covered in the daily.

A. VF gained two new files that handle the limited-actions policy and its notice copy.

The new files are limited_actions_copy.rs (NEW +397) and params/limited_actions_policy.rs (NEW +306). treatment.rs, introduced in the previous day's commit, handled projecting the verdict into a Thrift Action, but the Thrift LimitedEngagements payload carried only the reason enum. With these two files introduced in this commit, the payload carries the expansion "reason → action list → localized Prompt".

  • limited_actions_copy.rs loads the localized UI copy bundle verified — limited_actions_copy.rs:1-85.
    • The bundle path is /config/stringcenter/visibility-ltd-actions.json, and the pinned metadata path is /config/stringcenter/_BUNDLE_METADATA.json.
    • The live metadata directory is /usr/local/config/stringcenter/bundles/visibility-ltd-actions.
    • DriftCheck::run() compares bundle_hash between pinned and live and emits the limited_actions_copy_drift_checks{result=match|mismatch|unreadable} counter.
  • A 26-variant enum called LimitedActionType was introduced verified — params/limited_actions_policy.rs:16-43.
    • The variants are Reply · Retweet · QuoteTweet · Like · React · SendViaDm · AddToBookmarks · AddToMoment · PinToProfile · ViewTweetActivity · ShareTweetVia · Follow · ListsAddRemove · MuteConversation · Embed · ViewHiddenReplies · HideCommunityTweet · CopyLink · VoteOnPoll · RemoveFromCommunity · ShowRetweetActionMenu · ReplyDownVote · Autoplay · EditTweet · Highlight · ViewPostEngagements.

    • The keys are limited_actions_policy_limited_actions, limited_actions_policy_copy_namespace, limited_actions_policy_prompt_type, and limited_actions_policy_prompt_learn_more_url.

B. A single restriction verdict can now accumulate multiple reasons.

LimitedEngagement was promoted to a structure that accumulates multiple reasons.

  • This type, which was a single wrapper until this commit, changed to a structure holding one reason and a Vec of the remaining reasons verified — verdict.rs:67-98.
    • Before: LimitedEngagement(pub LimitedEngagementReason)
    • After: { first: LimitedEngagementReason, rest: Vec<LimitedEngagementReason> }
  • The add(reason) method checks for duplicates and then pushes to the Vec, and the reasons() iterator walks first and rest.

Accordingly, the ActionSpec::LimitedEngagement(reason) match branch in rules/registry.rs::collect_specs splits into two cases verified.

  • If engagement is None, it is set anew (LimitedEngagement::new(reason)).
  • If engagement is Some, it is appended (limit.value.add(*reason)).

In other words, if both BlockedViewer and ReadonlyViewer apply to a viewer at the same time, both reasons are carried in the payload. BlockedViewer limits 19 actions and ReadonlyViewer limits 14. Until this commit, the second and later engagement matches were dead code, but from this commit they are actually accumulated. Other reason combinations, such as StaleTweet with BlockedViewer, or ConversationControl with RootAuthorBlockedViewer, work the same way.

A new LimitedEngagementReason::limited_actions_string() const fn maps each reason to a bundle key prefix verified.

  • ConversationControl → "limited_replies"
  • ReadonlyViewer → "readonly_viewer"
  • BlockedViewer → "blocked_viewer"
  • RootAuthorBlockedViewer → "root_author_blocked_viewer"
  • StaleTweet → "stale_tweet"

C. The Thrift projection function takes the limited-actions policy as its third argument.

The signature of the projection layer introduced in the previous day's commit was extended, and treatment.rs::thrift_action takes LimitedActionsPolicies as its third argument verified — treatment.rs:16-20.

Nine symbols were added to the Thrift import.

  • BasicLimitedActionPrompt · CtaLimitedActionPrompt · LimitedAction · LimitedActionCtaType · LimitedActionPrompt · LimitedActionsPolicy · LocalizedMessage · LocalizedMessageLimitedActionPrompt · MessageLink.

On the path where the Verdict is Shown { engagement: Some(..) }, the action list and Prompt are combined for each reason, and the per-action localized Prompt is placed in the LimitedEngagements payload and sent over the wire. This completely replaces the former "payload that passed only the reason enum".

D. VF identifies which service a gRPC caller is by its certificate and records it.

The new VF file caller_identity.rs (NEW +126) extracts the S2S identity from the x509 cert of the gRPC peer and logs it. It emits the new metric vf_requests_by_caller{caller_identity, rpc, deadline} verified — caller_identity.rs:1-56.

  • caller_identity takes the SAN URI of the peer cert (format twtr:svc:<service>:<service>:<env>:<dc>) first, and the CN second if there is none. If neither has the twtr:svc: prefix, it is unknown.
  • rpc is the three-variant enum Endpoint { FilterTweets, EvaluateTweets, GetSafetyLabels }.
  • deadline is present|absent, depending on whether gRPC timeout metadata is present.

The request handlers of the three endpoints call caller_identity::record(Endpoint::XXX, &request) at the very start. The call site is evaluate_tweets.rs:46 and two other places. Three tests fix the identity extraction logic: SAN URI first, CN fallback, and non-S2S cert → None verified.

G. abuse-enforcement-service gained a gate that decides whether to restart itself when the Kafka config changes.

The new file restart_on_config_change.rs (NEW +173) has three board states verified — restart_on_config_change.rs:1-85.

  • Check::Unchanged: there is no change in the watched paths.
  • Check::Invalid: there is a change, but validate(live) failed. It does not restart and only writes an error log.
  • Check::Restart(Vec<String>): there is a change and validate also passed. It returns the list of changed paths.

The JSON pointer paths watched by default are three: /kafka/consumer/topic_labels, /topic_labels, and /kafka/producer. If the override key restart_on_config_change is an array, those paths are used. The state is reported through the CONFIG_RESTART_PENDING{valid=true|false} metric.

H. The Kafka producer is now built from the config snapshot taken at startup.

The Kafka producer binding in abuse-enforcement-service lib.rs (+325/−55) changed to be based on the boot config snapshot. The signature changed from build_kafka_producers(cfg, dynamic_config) to build_kafka_producers(cfg, boot_config) verified — lib.rs:831-840, 1385-1392.

boot_config is a startup-time snapshot captured with dynamic_config.config().unwrap_or(serde_json::Value::Null). When building the producer, it references this Value and extracts the producer spec with kafka_producers_from_config(Option<&Value>). This function is new in growthbook.rs.

The implication of this change is that the Kafka producer reacts only to the boot-time config. Config changes during operation are handled differently by area.

  • The non-kafka area is updated by live reload.
  • The kafka area prompts a service restart through the restart_on_config_change gate.

There is no hot swap.
