Why it matters Four facts overlap in this commit.

  1. The authority to decide "restriction reasons" was pulled into VF. Before this commit, the only information VF put in the engagement axis of the Verdict was a single reason enum. Which of the 26 actions to block and what to show in the UI were left to downstream (home-mixer, clients). From this commit, three things happen inside VF:

    • LimitedActionsPolicies holds the reason → action-list mapping, based on FeatureSwitches.
    • LimitedActionsCopy holds the (action, locale, country) → localized Prompt mapping.
    • treatment.rs::thrift_action combines the two and puts a per-action Prompt list directly into the Thrift payload LimitedEngagements.

    Clients no longer need to maintain their own localization or action-mapping tables, because every decision from reason to action to wording is declared as server-side data. This change pairs with Gen4+32, where treatment.rs was isolated as the rules → thrift/proto/metric projection layer. If the previous day's commit "gathered the wire projection point into one file," this commit "raises the richness of the data passing through that projection point to the UI level." The behavior where the UI buttons a user can press change with operational state (block, conversation control, stale) is now completed as a server-driven declaration.

  2. As LimitedEngagement becomes a structure that accumulates multiple reasons, the situation where one tweet has several restriction reasons at once is modeled explicitly. Before this commit, once rules decided the engagement, the next ActionSpec::LimitedEngagement match was dropped (a dead-code path). From this commit, when rules decide the engagement several times, the reasons are accumulated in a Vec via limit.value.add(*reason). In other words, for a viewer who is both BlockedViewer and ReadonlyViewer, both lists go into the payload and the choice is handed to downstream. BlockedViewer restricts 19 actions and ReadonlyViewer restricts 14, and combinations such as ConversationControl with StaleTweet, or RootAuthorBlockedViewer with BlockedViewer, also become possible. For the UI, there is now a path to answer "why is the Reply button disabled for this viewer and tweet combination" with "both because of BlockedViewer and because of StaleTweet."

  3. abuse-enforcement-service switched to a "boot-time config snapshot" model. Since the Rust reconstruction was released on 2026-09-23, this service had used live config through a DynamicConfig object. From this commit, the Kafka producer binding depends only on a JSON Value snapshot taken at boot. Instead, when the kafka settings (topic, SASL authentication, bootstrap servers) change during operation, the restart_on_config_change module restarts the service to apply the new settings. This approach does three things:

    • It keeps the kafka producer lifecycle simple (no hot swap).
    • It makes config changes clearly visible in logs and metrics (restart events).
    • It provides a fail-safe that does not restart if validate(live) does not pass.

    This restart applies only to changes in core settings; other settings are still applied through the live reload path.

  4. phoenix-rankall exposed an experiment-group identifier and a QPS cap. The CLI config module split looks like an organizational refactor, but two figures are exposed in the process. The first is SCORE_PREFIX = "phoenix.HomeExperiment1Lap7.". It means the Phoenix ranking service publishes scores of a specific experiment group, "Experiment1 Lap7" on the Home surface, to a Kafka topic, and phoenix-rankall consumes only scores with that prefix. The name "Lap7" appears to be an experiment iteration number inferred. The second is SID_BACKFILL_QPS_CAP = 800_000, a QPS cap of 800k for the SID backfill. The SID backfill is not applied to all posts; it is designed to process only posts in a specific window (at most 1 hour, at least 3 minutes). Adding that the number of posts shown per day is in the hundreds of millions to billions gives one picture: the SID embedding table is maintained only for the subset of posts with freshness within the last hour that is covered within the QPS 800k range. Posts outside the freshness window have no SID or remain stale.

The VF brazil_election_legal/drop/undesirable label registration pairs with the previous day's commit expanding the home-mixer Brazil 2026 handle list (2,786 → 2,795). home-mixer filters on the author axis using the handle list, and VF filters on the label axis using signals from the labeling service (Grok or human assignment). In effect, the declaration that the two paths work together during the election period is now stated explicitly in code. The rewrite of fallback_cache.rs is a performance refactor that removes Mutex contention. It results from delegating shard distribution and creation logic to a library.

Gen4+34 (2026-10-02, 76843a5) — generative SID retrieval microservice release (home-mixer SidSource + Phoenix-specific Transformer training config/model/trainer/runner + row-sharded embedding CUDA kernel bundle, 3,180 lines) + Phoenix proto reorganization (LLM_JUDGE_* 108/109 reappear, WEB_CONV_VALUE_USD/RATIO, viewer×advertiser engagement/conversion counts, exclusion bloom-filter axis in the Retrieve request) + outcome label added to VF vf_requests_by_caller + simplified home-mixer cold-start and engagement counts hydrator axes

X released generative SID retrieval in one commit, bundled as a separate microservice, Phoenix-specific Transformer training and serving code, and a home-mixer candidate source verified (daily). The new candidate source is off by default verified (same daily).

This commit changed 105 files, at a scale of +5,227/−756 verified — xai-org/x-algorithm@76843a5. It came one day after the previous commit, Gen4+33 (b79b947).

A. home-mixer was wired to use a dedicated generative SID retrieval microservice as a candidate source.

The new files are sources/sid_source.rs (new, +112) and clients/sid_retrieval_client.rs (new, +246). The call target endpoint is xai-recsys-sid-retrieval.prod.fou.twitter.biz:443.

  • The request sends seed posts, and the response returns a post id and shared prefix depth for each candidate verified — sid_source.rs:60-85.
    • The gRPC request shape is RetrieveRequest { seed_post_ids, max_results, max_per_seed, min_prefix_depth, max_prefix_depth, caller }.
    • The response shape is RetrieveResponse { candidates }, and each Candidate carries post_id and shared_prefix_depth.
  • shared_prefix_depth is passed downstream as an f32 in PostCandidate.retrieval_sources[0].score.

The source turns on only when all five conditions are met verified — sid_source.rs:58-64.

  • EnableSidSource=true
  • !query.is_topic_request()
  • !query.in_network_only
  • !query.has_cached_posts
  • has_post_signals(query)

The last condition, has_post_signals and post_signal_ids, reuses exactly the same functions as SimclustersSource verified — sid_source.rs:14. The two OON retrieval sources branch from the same seed set (the user's positive-engagement posts).

Five parameters were added verified — home-mixer/params/param.rs.

Parameter Default Role
EnableSidSource false Turns on the source itself
SidSourceMaxResults 800 Response cap (tightens the theoretical seeds × per_seed = 50×100 = 5000)
SidSourceMaxSeeds 50 Cap on seed posts in a request
SidSourceMaxPerSeed 100 Maximum result posts per seed
SidSourceMinPrefixDepth 3 Returns only candidates matching 3 or more shared prefix levels out of 6

Candidates from the SID source are labeled with the same ServedType as PhoenixMOESource. The label value is served_type=ForYouPhoenixRetrievalMoe. That is, for downstream scorers and filters, candidates from the two sources are indistinguishable on the label axis.

The SID retrieval client code sets the call deadline and connection path.

  • The gRPC deadline of 300ms is hardcoded (TIMEOUT_MS: u64 = 300, sid_retrieval_client.rs:21).
  • Connection is handled first by an xDS P2C load balancer, with a DNS RotatingChannel (60-second refresh) as the second fallback verified — sid_retrieval_client.rs:120-180.
    • If the build does not finish within 10 seconds or there is no bootstrap, it moves to the second fallback.
    • The discovery authority is xdstp://discovery-*/envoy.config.endpoint.v3.ClusterLoadAssignment/fou-xai-recsys-sid-retrieval.prod.prod:grpc-tls.

The readiness probe is GET /readyz on port 29180. There are two metrics:

  • SidRetrievalClient.retrieve{result=success|timeout|failure, path=xds|dns} labels the call result and path.
  • SidSource.retrieved{type=seeds|retrieved|hydrated} measures the volume at three stages.

B. Phoenix gained training and serving code for a dedicated SID generative retrieval Transformer.

There are four new files: config, model, trainer, and runner.

  • phoenix/xrex/configs/xrecsys_sid_retrieval.py
  • phoenix/xrex/models/recsys_sid_retrieval_model.py
  • phoenix/xrex/train/trainer_sid_retrieval.py
  • phoenix/xrex/inference/sid_retrieval_runner.py

The training config publishes its hyperparameters verified — xrecsys_sid_retrieval.py:11-45, 130-180.

  • The input sequence is 1030 long, combining 1 user prefix token, 1023 tokens of user action history, and 6 tokens of SID target. The candidate sequence length is 64.
  • SID uses sid_num_levels=6 and sid_codebook_size=256, and the theoretical space is $256^6 \approx 2.8 \times 10^{14}$.
    • The remaining SID settings are sid_embed_dim=1024, sid_prediction_hidden_dim=512, sid_level_loss_decay=1.0 (uniform per-level loss weight), sid_hash_level=True, and sid_cross_attn=True.
  • The Transformer has 8 layers and uses GQA 20:4 (query_heads=20, kv_heads=4).
    • The remaining settings are key_size=128, emb_size=2560, attn_logit_cap=80.0 with soft_sign, rotary and causal, widening_factor=2 with gated_mlp=False, and remat WHOLE.
  • The input vocab is user_vocab=0 (unused), item raw vocab=0, item hash vocab 100M, author vocab 30M, action type 60, and continuous action 8.
    • All three axes use double hashing with two hash pairs (linear scale × modulus prime).
    • These figures exactly match the two-tower config released on 2026-09-30. The two models share the same vocab space.
  • The training optimizer is Adam (b1=0.95, b2=0.98).
    • The remaining training settings are weight_decay=1e-3, constant lr=2e-3, batch size per device=128, parallel ep=128·dp=1 (128-way expert-parallel), and max_steps $\approx 3.125 \times 10^9$.
  • The dataset is set to aggregated_kafka, num_kafka_partitions=1024, use_post_sid=True, and multimodal_embedding_type=None.
  • The checkpoint is set to every_n=100 · keep_every_nth=1000 · keep_last_n=10 · verify_checksums=True · replica_axis="replica", and chunked and compressed are both False.

On the model side, there is only one positive action, SERVER_TWEET_FAV verified — recsys_sid_retrieval_model.py:40.

  • Seven hard-negative actions are enumerated explicitly.
    • CLIENT_TWEET_REPORT·_NOT_INTERESTED_IN·_SEE_FEWER·_UNFOLLOW_AUTHOR·_BLOCK_AUTHOR·_MUTE_AUTHOR·_NOT_RELEVANT
  • The SID token embedding consists of a separate table per level and a projection per level.
    • The table is sid_emb_level_{level} with size [256, 128].
    • The projection is sid_emb_proj_{level}, which raises 128 → 1024.

The inference runner sid_retrieval_runner.py holds two separate axes. One is beam search–based SID generation, and the other is reverse resolution from SID to post_id through SidPostIndex/SidBeamResolver.

  • The runner flags beam_width and decode_levels control the beam width and generation depth, respectively.
  • If decode_levels < 6, it stops at the prefix level and returns the set sharing the prefix (prefix retrieval).
  • This pairs with home-mixer SidSourceMinPrefixDepth=3. The server generates 3–6 levels, and a post matched at level 3 can return shared_prefix_depth=3 as its score.
  • _CorpusView exposes post_ids_with_sentinel, author_ids_with_sentinel, and sentinel_idx, and the serving-time corpus is a prebuilt SID trie with a set of post_ids at the leaves, with beam search running over the trie inferred.

This design overlaps in role with the Google TIGER (Rajput et al., Recommender Systems with Generative Retrieval, NeurIPS 2023, paper) · Alibaba PailitaoGR(2025) · Kuaishou OneRec(2025) · Tencent BARGE(2026) · ByteDance GEAR(arXiv 2026-09-30) line of work. Compared with these, the X version has four distinguishing features:

  • It uses 6-level × 256-codebook. TIGER uses 3-level × 256 codebook plus one fourth code to separate collisions verified — arXiv 2305.05065 (paper, 2023).
  • It conditions directly on a 1023-token action history.
  • It passes shared_prefix_depth to the ranking score of the stage above (TIGER uses generation probability).
  • It already shares the vocab design with the two-tower, placing the two retrieval axes in the same user, item, and author embedding space.

C. Phoenix gained a bundle of CUDA kernels for row-sharded embedding tables.

The new directory is phoenix/xrex/cuda/row_emb/, a 12-file bundle with +3,582 lines verified — phoenix/xrex/cuda/row_emb/.

  • Size per file: row_emb_api.cc(+766) · row_emb_comm.cc(+1,104) · row_emb_kernel.cu(+629) · row_emb.py(+290) · row_emb_comm.hpp(+256) · comm_utils.cc(+146) · row_emb_kernel.hpp(+135) · row_emb_common.cuh(+82) · cuda_error_utils.hpp(+68) · comm_utils.h(+57) · comm_utils.py(+47) · __init__.py(+2)

Phoenix's existing async_emb handles embedding tables sharded along the column axis. By contrast, row_emb handles tables sharded along the row axis.

  • If the vocab has N entries, N / group_size rows are loaded on each rank verified — row_emb.py:95-145.
  • Six JAX FFI targets are registered on the CUDA platform.
    • xrex_row_emb_lookup_start · _lookup_done · _stage_update · _rowwise_adagrad_update_start · _rowwise_adagrad_lazy_update_start · _rowwise_adagrad_update_done
  • RowEmbContextHandle bundles the following values.
    • (context_id · group_size · flatten_replicas · tokens_per_rank · emb_width · rows_per_rank · recv_capacity · num_devices_per_node · mesh · table_axis · data_axis)

There are 3 key design decisions.

  1. It splits lookup into two stages to expose the overlap of communication and compute.
    • lookup_start(token_ids, table, gate) returns (table_out, lookup_pin), and lookup_done(pin) returns embeddings.
    • The window between the two FFIs becomes the compute insertion point, and all-to-all overlaps with compute.
    • recv_capacity = min(ceil(tokens_per_rank × recv_factor), tokens_per_rank × group_size) sets an upper bound on the receive buffer in advance.
  2. Rowwise Adagrad is fused in the same two-phase structure as lookup.
    • rowwise_adagrad_update_start updates the table in place (input_output_aliases={0:0, 1:1}), and _update_done returns a completion signal.
    • rowwise_adagrad_lazy_update_start takes last_step and step and lazily updates only the accessed rows. This is a common optimization for sparse embeddings.
  3. The gate axis guarantees the XLA execution order.
    • Every FFI takes gate: jax.Array as an I/O axis to make the side-effect chain explicit. It is a device that keeps XLA from freely reordering.

Validation checks the following conditions:

  • vocab_rows % group_size == 0
  • tokens_per_batch % group_size == 0
  • emb_width % 8 == 0
  • recv_factor > 0
  • table_axis ⊂ data_axis: if it is not contained, a "token shard is not one per rank" ValueError is raised.

Phoenix's recsys_async_emb.py (+112/−36) was rewritten as an adapter layer that accepts both async_emb and row_emb verified.

  • The is_row_sharded(context_handle) branch decides between column and row.
  • table_spec returns P(table_axis, None) for row and P(None, table_axis) for column.
  • That is, the Phoenix async embedding utility was promoted to support both sharding strategies at once.

E. A request-outcome label was added to VF's per-caller request metric.

The change is in VF caller_identity.rs (+90/−15), and the new label axis is outcome. The vf_requests_by_caller metric expanded from yesterday's three labels {caller_identity, rpc, deadline} to four labels {..., outcome} in this commit verified — caller_identity.rs:16-62.

The new test dashboard_generator_pins_the_requests_by_caller_metric pins the dashboard Python script and the Rust constants together. The script's REQUESTS_BY_CALLER_METRIC, REQUESTS_BY_CALLER_NO_DEADLINE_FILTER, and success/non-success filter constants, four in all, are the pass condition of the Rust test. Why it matters

Three facts coincide in this commit.

  1. This is the first commit in which X released generative SID retrieval as three complete parts: a "separate microservice + dedicated Transformer training and serving stack + home-mixer candidate source wiring".
    • So far, X's SID has appeared only indirectly. One appearance was as an input feature of the two-tower item tower (the use_post_sid flag in xrecsys_two_tower.py, released 2026-09-30).
    • The other was phoenix-rankall's backfill QPS cap of 800k (SID_BACKFILL_QPS_CAP = 800_000 in Gen4+33 yesterday).
    • However, no line that generates SIDs directly and returns the result as candidates had been released until now.
    • This release bundles the entire chain into one commit, made up of three parts:
      • It introduced the four files (config, model, trainer, runner) of a dedicated Transformer model (8-layer, GQA 20:4, 1030-length context, 6-level × 256-codebook) on the Phoenix side.
      • It released the gRPC client and request shape of the separate microservice (seed_post_ids, the prefix retrieval axis min_prefix_depth=3) and the shared_prefix_depth score of response candidates. That microservice is xai-recsys-sid-retrieval.prod.fou.twitter.biz.
      • It streams candidates labeled with the same ServedType as PhoenixMOESource through home-mixer SidSource.
    • Because it is off by default with EnableSidSource=false, the checkpoint to watch for real traffic is the day it is turned ON in the FeatureSwitches cron.
  2. Two-tower retrieval and SID generative retrieval are designed not as "replacements for each other" but as "two layers on the same vocab space."
    • The two models share the same user, item, and author hash vocab (100M · 30M · identical double hashing scales/biases). This shows up when comparing the figures in xrecsys_sid_retrieval.py:30-45 with those in xrecsys_two_tower.py, released 2026-09-30.
    • This matters because generative retrieval is expensive on two cost axes, SID generation time complexity (beam_width × decode_levels × codebook size) and corpus-side SID index maintenance. The design appears to be a complementary structure where two-tower first covers the broad recall that ANN can run, and SID retrieval adds supplementary recall on the prefix-sharing axis inferred.
    • With the same vocab, both models could run on a shared embedding table, but the config released at this commit gives each its own table. Whether they are unified into a shared embedding must be observed in the next commit.
  3. The row-sharded embedding CUDA kernel bundle is a two-axis extension of the Phoenix embedding design itself.
    • The 3,582-line row_emb was not added solely for the generative retrieval model. However, in the context of this commit bundle, the natural reading is that the huge-vocab embeddings that SID generative retrieval requires (100M · 30M · 6-level × 256 codebook) are the trigger.
    • The existing async_emb is column-sharded and the new row_emb is row-sharded, and a shared adapter (recsys_async_emb.py) selects one of the two sharding strategies. In effect, this provides a place to choose the optimal sharding per model.
    • two-tower can run with column-shard for each of the user and item towers, but in the SID generative model each token references only its own vocab range along the generation axis, so row-shard yields a more compact communication pattern inferred.

The reappearance of the LLM_JUDGE_* actions is a separate thread. Two actions that had vacated their slots 15 days ago reappeared with renumbered IDs (107/108 → 108/109). This indicates that the direction of "carrying the LLM judge on the action axis and consuming it as one of the training targets" has resurfaced after readjustment. The numbers changed because CLIENT_TWEET_LIVE_STREAM_REPLY permanently took slot 107 in between, and 108 was also vacated and then reused. No consumer in a model training config or on the wire appears in this commit; only the proto claimed the slots. Which head weight and which config's target list they enter is a checkpoint to watch in the next window.

Gen4+35 (2026-10-03, b412112) — SID retrieval serving crate released (xai-recsys-sid-retrieval, a new 7-file Rust crate, parquet snapshot polling + 6-level trie + round-robin interleave) + home-mixer PopularPostsSource introduced (top-K popular authors → Thunder in-network lookup → OON supplement) + ads brand safety V2 verdict flipped to on by default (false → true) + author Grok label fallback introduced (EnableAdsAuthorBrandSafetyFallback, off by default) + VF staging replay subsystem introduced (visibility-filtering/staging/* 2,350 lines, recording · replay_corpus · capture · serve) + Phoenix row-emb checkpoint restore utility (row_embedding_restore.py 488 lines) + Phoenix gRPC server latency metric split out (grpc_server_latency.rs 361 lines)

With this commit, a server crate that receives real requests and responds has been attached to the semantic ID-based candidate search, for which only training code and a client had been released verified. home-mixer gained a source, off by default, that supplements out-of-network recommendations with recent posts from popular authors, and the mirror default of the ads brand safety V2 verdict switch changed from false to true verified (daily).

148 files changed, with a change scale of +9,128/−2,356 verified — xai-org/x-algorithm@b412112. It comes one day after the previous commit, Gen4+34 (yesterday's 76843a5).

A. A new Rust crate phoenix/crates/serving/xai-recsys-sid-retrieval/ that serves generative SID retrieval has been added, with 7 files and 1,062 lines. Yesterday's release (76843a5) brought the Phoenix-side training config, model, trainer, and runner and the home-mixer-side SidSource client. However, the server code that would receive real requests and return responses was missing. Today that slot was released verified — phoenix/crates/serving/xai-recsys-sid-retrieval/.

Per-file sizes are src/service.rs:208 · src/index.rs:223 · src/loader.rs:170 · src/http_api.rs:109 · src/main.rs:115 · src/seed_sids.rs:114 · src/metrics.rs:79. There is also a separate proto crate xai-recsys-sid-retrieval-proto (sid_retrieval.proto:46).

The proto defines one RPC, a request message, a candidate message, and a seed source enum verified — sid_retrieval.proto:

The index ties each SID to one integer key and holds them in two vectors with different sort orders verified — src/index.rs:5-110:

  • SID_LEVELS = 6, BITS_PER_LEVEL = 8. So each level's code range is 0–255, and the full SID is packed into a single 48-bit u64 key. pack_full_key stacks the levels from the top level down using left shifts.
  • It maintains two IndexedPost {key, post_id, author_id} vectors.
    • by_key is sorted by key in lexicographic order, and within the same key by post_id in descending order. It is used for prefix range search.
    • by_post is sorted by post_id ascending. It is used for binary search when converting a seed post to its SID.
  • prefix_range(key, depth) preserves only the top d levels at depth d and returns a [lo, hi) range with the lower levels cleared to 0 or filled. It pulls the posts within that range from by_key using partition_point.

Search collects candidates going from deep prefixes to shallow ones verified — src/index.rs:138-193:

This algorithm has three properties:

  • Each post is emitted "only once, at the deepest prefix level it shared." A post matched at depth 6 is not picked again at the levels of depth 5–3.
  • Within the same depth, posts with a larger post_id (= more recent) take priority.
  • The seed post itself is filtered out by the global excluded set (with multiple seeds, seed₂ does not get mixed into seed₁'s results).

When there are multiple seeds, the candidate lists of the seeds are drawn alternately in round-robin (seed 1 → seed 2 → ... → seed N → seed 1 → ...) while duplicates are removed globally verified — src/index.rs:196-222. It stops when it reaches max_results or there are no more candidates to draw. As a result, position bias is evened out so that it does not skew toward a particular seed.

The snapshot loader periodically checks the parquet snapshot path and reloads the entire index when the path changes verified — src/loader.rs:1-170:

  • The input is an Arrow Parquet file (post_sid_snapshot.parquet) with three columns: post_id: int64, author_id: int64, and post_sid: list<int64>. The record batch size is BATCH_SIZE = 65_536.
  • The timestamp is taken from the filename suffix (*_<unix_ts>.parquet), and it falls back to mtime if parsing fails.
  • watch_snapshots(path, poll_interval, index, ready_tx) calls canonicalize(path) every 30 seconds (default) and reloads everything if the path changed. The new index is built in tokio::spawn_blocking. On success it is atomically swapped via ArcSwapOption<SidIndex>, and ready_tx.send(true) raises /readyz to initial-ready.
  • pack_full_key(row_codes) returns None if len != 6 or any single code falls outside 0..=255, and the skipped counter increments. That is, invalid SIDs are silently dropped.
  • The metric function record_index_load(index, elapsed_s) emits the sid_index_posts gauge, sid_index_skipped_posts, and the sid_index_load_seconds histogram together.

The SID of a seed post is looked up first in the local trie, and if it is absent, an external lookup service is queried verified — src/seed_sids.rs:1-114:

  • If the seed post_id is in the local trie, the code of that trie entry (valid_depth=6) is used as is.
  • If not, it does a batch lookup against a separate gRPC service SidLookupService (xai-recsys-sid-proto, endpoint set by the --sid-endpoint flag).
  • SidLookupService is, in effect, the lookup service that was deleted as an internal sidecar of the Phoenix serving engine in Gen4+15 (2026-09-04, 9b0dc31), now reappearing as a separate external service.
  • The moka cache has 2 million entries and a TTL of 6 hours. If codes.is_empty() in the response, the seed is classified as Missing.

The service layer cleans up the seeds and then finds SIDs by source verified — src/service.rs:68-112:

  • It dedups seed_post_ids in the request and keeps only up to max_seeds (default 200).
  • For all seeds it tries lookup(post_id) in the local trie, and batch-calls SidLookupService.lookup(missing) only for the missing ones (in parallel). Then it classifies each seed into one of three paths (Index / SidService / Missing) and emits it as a metric label.
  • The request path has 5 metrics verified — src/metrics.rs:35-71.
    • sid_retrieval_requests_total{caller, result} counter
    • sid_retrieval_seeds_total{source} and sid_retrieval_sid_service_lookups_total{result} counters
    • sid_retrieval_candidates_per_request{caller} and sid_retrieval_request_latency_seconds{caller} histograms

The defaults of the main.rs flags are verified — src/main.rs:26-52:

  • Ports: --grpc-port=9090, --http-port=8080
  • Snapshot: --snapshot-path=post_sid_snapshot.parquet, --snapshot-poll-secs=30
  • SID lookup: --sid-endpoint=http://localhost:50051, --sid-timeout-ms=200, --sid-cache-size=2_000_000
  • Request caps and defaults: --max-seeds=200, --default-max-results=800, --default-max-per-seed=100, --default-min-prefix-depth=3, --default-max-prefix-depth=6

B. home-mixer added a new source that supplements OON recommendations by feeding the top-K popular authors into the Thunder in-network lookup as "fake following". The added files are sources/popular_posts_source.rs (+116), util/popular_authors.rs (+229), and clients/popular_authors_store_client.rs (+79), all of them new.

PopularPostsSource operates in this order verified — popular_posts_source.rs:68-115:

  1. The source is enabled when !has_cached_posts && !in_network_only && EnablePopularPostsSource==true.
  2. It calls PopularAuthorsCache.maybe_spawn_refresh(now_ms) to start a background refresh. The refresh runs only when needed, and a single token-held AtomicBool prevents duplicate runs.
  3. top_author_ids(top_k) picks the author_ids of the top K (default 1000).
  4. It sends GetInNetworkPostsRequest { user_id, following_user_ids=[top K authors], max_results=500, per_author_limits: {3, 0}, exclude_tweet_ids=seen_ids, algorithm=ThunderAlgorithm, debug=false, is_video_request=false } to Thunder. Thunder treats those K authors as if the user follows them and returns posts from its in-network post store in recency order.
  5. Response posts are tagged with the label served_type=ForYouPhoenixRetrieval and returned as PostCandidate. This label is the same as PhoenixSource's label.

PopularAuthorsCache holds a popular-author snapshot and updates it periodically verified — util/popular_authors.rs:135-223:

  • It consists of RwLock<Snapshot>, AtomicBool refreshing, and Arc<dyn PopularAuthorsStore>.
  • The refresh interval is authors.is_empty() ? 60 seconds : 60 minutes. It is a common pattern that retries aggressively only when the cache is empty.
  • The store's byte format is version=1(1B) + updated_at_ms(8B BE) + count(4B BE) + [author_id(8B BE), follower_count(8B BE)] * count verified — util/popular_authors.rs:64-104. That is, 1,000 authors take 13 + 16,000 = 16,013 bytes, all stored under one Manhattan key.
  • sort_by_followers sorts by follower_count in descending order (ties by author_id ascending).
  • The metrics are the PopularAuthorsCache.Refresh{result=ok|error} counter and the PopularAuthorsCache.LoadedAuthors gauge.

Five parameters were introduced verified — home-mixer/params/param.rs:

Parameter Default Role
EnablePopularPostsSource false Turns the source itself on
PopularPostsTopAuthors 1000 How many of the top authors from the KV store go into the "virtual following"
PopularPostsMaxResults 500 Cap on the Thunder response
PopularPostsMaxPerAuthor 3 Max posts for 1 author
PopularPostsMaxRepliesRepostsPerAuthor 0 Replies/retweets are excluded from the source entirely

By design, this source reuses the ForYouPhoenixRetrieval label (= PhoenixSource's label). So to downstream scorers and filters it looks like "additional OON candidates returned by Phoenix two-tower retrieval." However, the mechanism is not embedding similarity but a "global popularity centroid of the follow graph." It is effectively a global fallback for cold start/exploration on the follow graph. It is a typical global popularity backfill pattern, used "so that Thunder responds with something even if the user follows no one" or "to fill the gap when other OON sources cannot return results because user engagement signals are too few" inferred.

Why it matters

Three facts coincide in this commit.

  1. The "actual server crate" was attached today to the three axes of yesterday's released generative SID retrieval (home-mixer source, Phoenix model/trainer, proto). Until yesterday only the training recipe and the home-mixer source skeleton existed, and the server was empty. The xai-recsys-sid-retrieval crate released today states the following three things explicitly, so this server's actual query complexity can be measured from released code alone:

    • It is a fully static index that reloads everything from the parquet snapshot every 30 seconds. There are no real-time upserts; the pattern is to push in batches the code table that the model extracted.
    • It uses a 6-level trie packed into a 48-bit u64 key and partition_point-based range search.
    • It uses an algorithm that trims recall with reverse depth order and round-robin interleave.

    EnableSidSource=false is still the default, so the checkpoint to watch is the day it is turned ON in the FeatureSwitches cron for real-traffic use.

  2. PopularPostsSource reuses the Thunder in-network index from a "global popularity" angle and mixes its results, under the ForYouPhoenixRetrieval label, with Phoenix two-tower retrieval responses. In the 2026-10-16 commit (Gen4+43) the label was split into ForYouPopularPosts, so the description below holds only until then. It is interesting that it was designed not to be distinguishable from PhoenixSource by label. To scorers and filters it appears as "Phoenix retrieval returned K more," so at upper ranking stages it blends in with the same distribution as PhoenixScore. Mechanically, it is not embedding-based retrieval. It is a retro approach that puts the global popularity centroid of the follow graph into Thunder as "virtual following." EnablePopularPostsSource=false is still the default, so the point at which it is actually turned on is the checkpoint to watch in the next window.

  3. Both ads-side changes expand "SFA (Suitable For Advertising) labeling from post level → author level". It is no coincidence that the EnableAdsBrandSafetyVerdictV2=true switch and the introduction of EnableAdsAuthorBrandSafetyFallback arrived together. The direction is to use the author's past label pattern as a fallback for posts that do not yet have a post-level Grok label. This is a signal that it aims to complement, through author-level aggregation, the situation where Grok classifier coverage is sparse at the post level (especially for new posts) inferred.

Gen4+36 (2026-10-06, e62790c) — Added 3 "post-open dwell seconds" terms to the ranking value model (video continuation · per-user video continuation · profile visit secs, default weight 0) + rewrote PopularPostsSource as two view-count-based offline jobs + added "Under the Hood" pipeline trace response + added NOTICE level to VF verdicts

In this commit the ranking value model gained three expected-dwell-time terms that multiply a probability head by conditional dwell seconds, but all weights are 0, so serving is not yet affected verified. The popular-posts source now reads a global list that an offline job picked by view count, instead of calling Thunder on every request verified (daily).

The commit changed 103 files, at +6,916/−1,393 verified — xai-org/x-algorithm@e62790c. It came three days after Gen4+35 (b412112, 2026-10-03). The cron mirror sync time moved from 2026-10-02T16:00:41Z to 2026-10-05T16:00:50Z.

A. The value model gained three conditional expected-dwell-time terms. verified — xai-value-model/scoring.rs:61-63, 111-128, 141-158:

  • Phoenix proto ContinuousActionName gained HOME_PROFILE_VISIT_SECS = 0 and HOME_VIDEO_CONTINUATION_SECS = 3 verified — recsys.proto:594-599. Number 0 was held by INVALID_CONTINUOUS_ACTION_NAME and number 3 by ACTIVE_SECS_5M_RESIDUAL_NORM.
  • The two heads are multiplied with probability heads. That is, it is an expected-value decomposition: "probability of opening × seconds of continued viewing after opening." The existing cont_dwell_time and cont_click_dwell_time put the head value directly into the weighted sum verified (the apply(scores.dwell_time, ...) line in the same function).
  • set_user_video_continuation computes Σ P(open)·secs / Σ P(open) over all candidates in the request and assigns the same value to every candidate verified. As a result, this term does not change the ranking among candidates; it scales the coefficient of P(video_open) up or down per user inferred. The basis is that the value is constant across candidates, so the term takes the form weight × user_secs × P(open).
  • The cron mirror defaults for the three new weights (VideoContinuationWeight, UserVideoContinuationWeight, ProfileVisitSecsWeight) are all 0.0 verified — vm-ranker/params.rs. In home-mixer, weights_for fixes all three at 0.0 verified — home-mixer/scorers/value_model.rs:37-39. Therefore the only path that can actually turn them on is the VM-Ranker service.
  • home-mixer's extraction of the two heads from the Phoenix response is also behind EnableHomeExcursionScores (default false) verified — home-mixer/scorers/phoenix_scorer.rs:109-117, 141-153. The training-side aggregation type DENSE_WITH_LONG_DWELL_HOME_EXCURSION = 30 took the PLACEHOLDER_30 slot verified — recsys.proto:1815.
  • "home excursion" appears to be a name for the time spent after leaving the home feed for a video or profile inferred. The basis is that the head names all have the HOME_ prefix and are multiplied with the paired probability heads (video_open, profile_click).
  • In the README's Phoenix prediction list, the Attention line dropped active seconds and gained video continuation seconds · profile visit seconds verified — README.md:341.
  • The post_unexplored (new-author boost) term has so far been attached only to in-network candidates. Turning on PostUnexploredIncludeOutOfNetwork (default false) attaches it to OON candidates too verified — xai-value-model/scoring.rs:85-90.

B. PopularPostsSource was rewritten to read a view-count-ranked list built by offline jobs, instead of querying Thunder at request time. verified — home-mixer/sources/popular_posts_source.rs, home-mixer/util/popular_posts.rs:36-87, home-mixer/popular_posts_job.rs:21-178, home-mixer/util/popular_authors.rs:11, 25-40:

  1. popular_authors_job runs on a default 3600-second cycle. This job reads a follower-ranking snapshot from the BigQuery table twttr-bq-timelines-prod.pulse.popular_posting_authors and picks (number of authors active in the last 7 days × 0.00005) authors, which is the top 0.005%. It rejects a snapshot older than 30 hours (--popular-authors-max-snapshot-age-hours=30).
  2. popular_posts_job (default 300-second cycle) groups those authors 20 at a time and collects posts through Thunder GetInNetworkPostsRequest (50 per author, at most 1,200 per request). It drops replies and retweets (is_original).
  3. For posts within 24 hours, it fetches view_count from the engagement counts service, 500 at a time.
  4. The score is quality = views × (1 − e^{−λ·24}) / (1 − e^{−λ·max(age_h, 0.5)}), where λ = ln2 / 8. It assumes the view rate halves every 8 hours and extrapolates the views so far to 24-hour cumulative views inferred. The basis is that the denominator is the fraction accumulated by the post's age and the numerator is the fraction accumulated by 24 hours.
  5. It keeps the top 5 per author and the top 500 overall, writes them to Manhattan, and reads them back to check that generated_at_ms matches.
  6. The serving source refreshes the list every 60 seconds, takes PopularPostsMaxResults (500) items, and returns them excluding only seen_ids. List age is reported with the PopularPostsSource.ListAgeSecs gauge.

The Gen4+35 parameters PopularPostsTopAuthors (1000), PopularPostsMaxPerAuthor (3) and PopularPostsMaxRepliesRepostsPerAuthor (0) were deleted verified. Because the only per-user personalization input is seen_ids, this source is a global popular list verified. The default is still off.

C. A new "Under the Hood" response was added. verified — home-mixer/util/under_the_hood.rs, home-mixer/scored_posts_server.rs:

  • If ScoredPostsQuery.is_under_the_hood_request is true, the response carries a pipeline trace and per-post scores.
    • The trace contains per-stage latency, input, kept and removed counts, and filter rate.
    • Per-post scores contain weighted_score, the name of the value model used (vm_ranker/weighted), and a map of per-head Phoenix scores.
  • Each stage and component carries a public repository code URL of the form https://github.com/xai-org/x-algorithm/blob/main/home-mixer/... (code_url).
  • The default of the flag EnableUnderTheHood is false.
  • Given that the response embeds public repository links, it appears to be a feature that shows users or internal debugging screens "why this post appeared" inferred. The surface where it is displayed is not in this repository.

D. VF verdicts now have four levels. verified — README.md:205-232, visibility-filtering/models/verdict.rs. NOTICE (shows the post as is and attaches a notice) was added to ALLOW, INTERSTITIAL and DROP. The internal representation is SoftIntervention { policy: AppealablePolicy, level, proactive, appeal_submitted }. For home-mixer, as with an interstitial, the post stays in the feed. In the same commit VF introduced article_client.rs, trusted_friends_client.rs and community_source.rs (community post hydration). The evaluation result was also split into Evaluation::{Complete, Partial, NotFound, Failed}.

E. Values and settings also changed. verified — home-mixer/params/param.rs:

  • RetrievalCandidatesKafkaMaxCandidates changed from 200 to 100,000. It is the cap for logging retrieval candidates to Kafka. Effectively, the cap was lifted so that all candidates are logged inferred.
  • VMRankerClusterId changed from "Experiment6" to "Experiment1".
  • Phoenix training gained the H100 remat policy SAVE_H100_QKV_ATTN_FFN = 34, and the condition that prevented using num_microbatch > 1 together with use_row_emb was deleted verified — phoenix/xrex/models/remat.py, phoenix/xrex/train/trainer_recsys.py.

Why it matters

  • X's value model has so far been "weighted sum of probability heads + continuous-value heads as is." This time, an expected-dwell-time decomposition of probability × conditional expected seconds appears in code for the first time. The weights are 0, so serving is not yet affected verified.
  • The profile_click weight has been 0.0 since the Gen4 release (weight table above). The code does not reward the profile-click probability itself, but creates a separate path that rewards the time spent after the click inferred. The basis is that the same probability head is used only as a factor in the product.
  • Within three days of its release, the definition of PopularPostsSource changed from "latest posts of popular authors" to "posts of popular authors with a fast view rate." The Thunder call in the request path is gone, so the cost became constant verified.

Gen4+37 (2026-10-07, 78460ca) — PopularPostsSource on by default + new-author boost 0.02 → 0.015 (home-mixer mirror) + corrected lexical-match features of search ranking negative samples + optional per-layer activation L2 regularization for Transformer + cleaned up VF NotFound verdict path

In this commit the global popular-posts source was turned on by default, so a source whose only personalization input is the list of already-seen posts entered the default path for For You's out-of-network candidates for the first time verified. The same day, the home-mixer mirror's new-author boost dropped from 0.02 to 0.015 verified (daily).

The commit changed 22 files, at +775/−681 verified — xai-org/x-algorithm@78460ca. It came the day after Gen4+36 (e62790c, 2026-10-06). The cron mirror sync time moved from 2026-10-05T16:00:50Z to 2026-10-06T16:00:58Z.

A. PopularPostsSource is now on by default. verified — home-mixer/params/param.rs:944-948: EnablePopularPostsSource changed from false to true. The source is enabled when !has_cached_posts && !in_network_only && EnablePopularPostsSource verified — home-mixer/sources/popular_posts_source.rs:27-31. It was also listed for the first time in the README's candidate source table and OON description as "A shared list of popular recent posts, initially from the most-followed active accounts" verified — README.md. The source structure (two offline jobs, view-count extrapolation score, up to 500 items) is the same as in the Gen4+36 section.

B. The new-author boost was lowered. verified — home-mixer/params/param.rs:384-388: PostUnexploredWeight changed from 0.02 to 0.015. The parameter of the same name in vm-ranker/params.rs:91-95 is still 0.02 verified — vm-ranker/params.rs. The home-mixer value is the one weights_for uses in the local weighted sum verified — home-mixer/scorers/value_model.rs:28. Since Gen4+28, home-mixer computes the local score first and refines it with a VM-Ranker RPC, so for requests the RPC answers, the VM-Ranker value of 0.02 may be the final one inferred. This is the first observed case of the two mirrors holding different values.

C. The lexical-match features of search ranking negative samples were corrected. verified — new phoenix/xrex/data/recsys/negative_word_match.py (51 lines), recsys_batch.py:1476-1488:

  • apply_negative_sampling builds negatives from other users in the batch. If there is a search query, it builds the two blocks below and drops pairs whose query-embedding cosine similarity is 0.9 or higher. Negative slots get the ClientTweetRecapNotDwelled label verified — same file apply_negative_sampling.
    • Block (1): another user's post and my query
    • Block (2): my post and another user's query
  • Post features are all copied from post_src, so the two features computed for the original query remained as they were on negatives paired with a different query verified (the copy code and this correction code). The two features are exactPhraseSeq (exact match of the query phrase) and matchedWordFractionSeq (fraction of query words matched).
  • With search_negative_clear_word_match (default False) on, the two features of negative slots are cleared to 0 verified. If the flag is on and the new columns lexicalTextSeq, lexicalQuerySeq and lexicalAuthorSeq exist, the features are recomputed against the newly paired query with the external library xai_search_lexical_match.search_lexical_match verified.
  • Before the correction, negatives in block (2) kept a feature saying "strongly matches the query" while receiving an irrelevant label, so the model was probably trained to trust the lexical-match features less inferred. The basis is that the features and labels were systematically mismatched.

D. An optional per-layer activation L2 regularization for the Transformer was added. verified — phoenix/xrex/models/transformer.py, recsys_model.py:664, 3827-3830: it collects the mean squares of each layer's attention output and FFN output (attn_loss, ffn_loss, reflecting the padding mask) and adds per_layer_l2_weight × (ffn-loss + attn-loss) to the regularization loss. The default is 0.0. In the same file, four loss-input construction functions (_candidate_inputs and others) were merged into one, loss_inputs_and_normalizers, and the sharding constraint changed to with_sharding_constraint_unless_manual. This appears to be a refactor with no change in training behavior inferred.

E. The VF NotFound verdict path was cleaned up. verified — visibility-filtering/evaluate_tweets.rs, visibility-filtering-client/evaluated.rs: Evaluation::NotFound is removed from the verdict targets and goes to Outcome::Failed. On the client side, the VF verdict overwrites the tweetypie result only when it is Found; Filtered, NotFound and Failed keep their original state.

Why it matters

  • The source introduced in Gen4+35 and rewritten as an offline global popular list in Gen4+36 was turned on by default four days after Gen4+35. A source whose only personalization input is seen_ids entered the default path for For You OON candidates for the first time verified. These candidates also pass through the Phoenix ranker, so ranking decides whether they are shown inferred. The basis is that the source only creates PostCandidate and assigns no score.
  • The same day, the new-author boost was cut by 25%. In effect, the correction for new authors was reduced on the day the popular-author list came in. Whether the two changes are part of the same experiment cannot be confirmed from the code inferred.

Gen4+38 (2026-10-08, 35650fb) — Introduced vertical video carousel module in For You (off by default) + ranking dwell_time training loss Tweedie/MAE → CREAD (on by default) + history dwell-time bucket embedding + Mixture-of-Logits (MoL) and multiple user query head options with CUDA serving kernel in two-tower retrieval (off by default) + cold-start exclusion for topic requests

With this commit, a vertical video carousel module entered the For You feed, off by default, and this module picks videos by video-open probability instead of the value model score. The ranking model's dwell-time head is now trained with the CREAD (classification per threshold, then restoration) loss in the default configuration verified (daily).

The change scale is 173 files, +15,160/−2,465 verified — xai-org/x-algorithm@35650fb. The cron mirror sync time moved from 2026-10-06T16:00:58Z to 2026-10-07T16:00:42Z, and the only values that changed in the mirror are three new parameters. A large part of the increase is third-party CuTe DSL utilities (phoenix/xrex/cutedsl/quack/*, about 3,000 lines) and VF hydration and replay code. This section covers only the parts related to feed behavior. Items that "need a deep dive" are left in the open questions section.

A. A vertical video carousel module was added to For You. verified — home-mixer/util/video_carousel.rs, selectors/top_k_score_selector.rs:10-27, filters/video_carousel_filter.rs, params/config.rs:17-19, 35-36:

  • The module turns on under three conditions: RequestType::ForYou, EnableVideoCarousel (default false), and a fatigue gate. Fatigue is judged by whether VideoCarouselFatigueMinutes (60 minutes) have passed since the last VIDEO_CAROUSEL_MODULE impression time in the served history verified — query_hydrators/served_history_query_hydrator.rs:52-57, 110-126.
  • Selection happens in two stages.
    • In stage 1, TopKScoreSelector picks the top 50 by score (TOP_K_CANDIDATES_TO_SELECT). Then, from the remaining candidates, it picks up to 30 more (VIDEO_CAROUSEL_EXTRA_CANDIDATES) that are videos, are not replies, and have a video_open_score, in order of predicted video_open probability, and marks them video_carousel_extra.
    • In stage 2, these candidates pass through the VF and conversation dedup filters together. Then the last filter, VideoCarouselFilter, removes the extra candidates from the main feed.
    • The carousel candidate pool is "ranks 36 and below among the top 50 (skip(RESULT_SIZE=35)) + the removed extras."
  • From the pool, only vertical videos (width-to-height ratio < 1.0) are kept and up to 5 are picked in video_open order. If there are fewer than 3, no module is created.
    • The width-to-height ratio is filled from TES media metadata by the new VideoAspectRatioHydrator.
  • The blender inserts the module at the 6th slot (VideoCarouselPosition) and records it in the served history as a VIDEO_CAROUSEL_MODULE entry. The URT header string key is VideoCarouselModule.header, and the English value in the test is "Videos for you" verified — util/urt/video_carousel_marshaller.rs.
  • Carousel videos appear designed not to overlap with the top 35 shown in the main feed inferred. This is because the carousel candidate pool consists only of ranks 36 and below plus the extras. However, we did not check this time whether the final response size is cut at exactly 35.
  • Carousel selection uses the single-head probability of video_open, not the value model weighted sum verified. It is the first module to fill slots with an objective separate from main feed ranking inferred. The existing WTF, prompts and frames were separate candidates that did not use post ranking.

B. The ranking dwell_time training loss changed to CREAD, and it is on by default. verified — phoenix/xrex/configs/xrecsys.py:272-275, 687-742, models/loss_recsys.py cread_loss_compute, models/recsys_model.py _decode_cread:

  • In _home_direct_packed_base(), dwell_tweedie_loss_weight and dwell_mae_loss_weight became 0.0, and dwell_cread_loss_weight and dwell_cread_immersive_loss_weight became 0.1. Previously, Tweedie (power 1.5, cap 300) and MAE were each hardcoded at 0.1.
  • For each of its 30 thresholds, the CREAD head learns "does dwell exceed this threshold" with sigmoid BCE. The thresholds are log-spaced from 2 seconds up to the cap, and the last value is the cap. The reconstructed value is computed as Σ σ(logit_k) × (bin width)_k. A Huber loss in raw units (δ=5 s, weight 0.5) is added on top.
  • The CREAD loss is split in two by surface. The general surface has a cap of 120 seconds and excludes PRODUCT_SURFACE_GALLERY_PAGE. The immersive (gallery) surface has a cap of 240 seconds.
  • A feature that feeds history dwell time as a bucket embedding using the same threshold scheme is also on by default verified — models/recsys_feature_prep.py:180-184, 885-910, configs/xrecsys.py:301-304.
    • The settings are enable_dwell_bucket_table=True, a cap of 240 seconds and 30 thresholds, with linear interpolation between two adjacent buckets.
  • CREAD is a method Kuaishou published for predicting video watch time (arXiv 2401.07521, 2024, paper). The name and structure (classification and restoration) of the X code match the paper verified. Instead of the paper's core error-adaptive interval design, the X code uses fixed log spacing verified (cread_log_thresholds).

C. Options for MoL and multiple query heads were added to two-tower retrieval (off by default). verified — phoenix/xrex/models/recsys_two_tower_model.py:523-598, 1629-1665, 2214-2224, phoenix/xrex/cuda/mol_epilogue/__init__.py, configs/xrecsys_two_tower.py:699-743:

  • With user_query_heads=K, the user sequence output is attention-pooled with K learned query vectors to make K user vectors. Each head has its own recency decay coefficient (recency_gamma).
  • With mol_item_components=L, a low-rank adapter is applied to the item embedding to make L normalized component vectors. The K×L cosine values are combined by a weighted sum through a small MLP gate (softmax) to produce the final score. There is also a mol_conditioned_gate option that adds user and item embedding bias to the gate.
  • The (K×L, hidden) combinations the serving CUDA epilogue kernel supports are {(4,32), (8,16), (8,32), (16,16)}, and it supports only up to 512 users per request.
  • Four contrastive loss options were added in the same commit, all off by default.
    • A fixed temperature
    • Masking of false negatives, where the same post in a batch is used as a negative
    • Logit offset for posts of the user's own negative actions
    • User weighting based on the number of positives
  • None of the 6 presets turns on MoL or query heads verified (grep of the configs directory). Whether current production retrieval is dot-product-based or MoL cannot be determined from this code inferred. The experiment configs are not public.

D. Other changes

  • Topic feed requests (requests with topic_ids) are excluded from author cold-start promotion verified — home-mixer/scorers/author_cold_start.rs:384-386.
  • Lookup table functions for the first 2-digit and 3-digit Semantic ID prefixes were added to Phoenix embeddings. The 3-digit one reduces the row count by hashing verified — phoenix/xrex/models/recsys_sid.py:32-79. We did not check whether this function is actually wired up.
  • A path was added for the ads blender to collect dropped ads into query.ad_drops (home-mixer/ads/drops.rs, 87 lines). VF introduced a 345-line user-location (geo/service/userLocation) client and a 528-line hydration exchange.rs verified. Whether this is a policy change needs a deep dive.

Why it matters

  • For You gained a video-only slot, and that slot is filled by video_open probability, not by value model score verified. Because it is still off by default, we treat it as being at the experiment stage inferred. The cron mirror default is false.
  • On the ranking side, the default training approach of the dwell-time head changed verified. Together with the Gen4+31 increase of ContClickDwellTimeWeight from 0 to 0.4, it suggests continued tuning of the dwell-time signal inferred.

Gen4+39 (2026-10-09, cb45b55) — Added feed request context (FeedRequestContext) and cursor direction fields to the ranking request proto + retuned the H100 home ranker training preset (batch 512, 2 microbatches, packing that removes empty candidate slots) + a candidate-region FA4 attention kernel

This commit added two fields to the Phoenix ranking request that carry feed request context such as app launch, refresh, and scroll down, but no public code at the commit reads these fields. Most of the remaining changes fix the preset and sequence packing for training the home ranker on H100 verified (daily).

The change spans 16 files, +1,228/−218 verified — xai-org/x-algorithm@cb45b55. Only the cron mirror sync time changed, from 2026-10-07T16:00:42Z to 2026-10-08T16:00:35Z, and no mirror value changed verified. Most of the changes are Phoenix ranker training-efficiency code. The reference commit for line numbers in this section is cb45b55.

A. Two request context fields were added to the Phoenix ranking request PredictNextActionsRequest. verified — phoenix/python/common/xai-proto/proto/recsys.proto:27-50, 175-176 (the same holds for the serving crate's xai-recsys-proto/proto/recsys.proto):

  • feed_request_context (field 25) records how this feed request was triggered. It has 14 values.
    • They include app launch (LAUNCH), return to foreground (FOREGROUND, FOREGROUND_TRUNCATE), pull to refresh (PULL_TO_REFRESH), manual refresh, screen navigation (NAVIGATE), viewport-based refresh, polling, background fetch, timeline gap filling (GAP), right after signup (SIGNUP), own thread, and AUTO.
  • feed_cursor_direction (field 26) is one of the first request (INITIAL), fetching newer posts upward (TOP), scrolling down to fetch more (BOTTOM), and gap (GAP).
  • Both enums had been defined in the proto since an earlier commit but were not used in any message. This commit connected them to the Phoenix ranking request message for the first time verified (the diff only adds two field lines).
  • At the commit, no code in the public tree reads these fields verified. Even grepping all of phoenix/xrex and home-mixer, the enum names and field names appear nowhere outside the proto. So it is not yet possible to tell whether they are used as ranking features or only for logging inferred.

B. The H100 home ranker training preset was retuned. verified — phoenix/xrex/configs/xrecsys.py:324-345, 427-432:

  • The home_direct_packed preset is _home_direct_packed_base() merged with _H100_OVERRIDES. This time bs_per_device went from 256 to 512, ep (expert parallelism) went from 256 to 128, and num_microbatch=2 was added. One microbatch (the approach of splitting a step's batch, computing the parts sequentially, and summing the gradients) is 256 users.
  • use_async_emb, seqpack_drop_empty_candidates, and overlap_step_host_work became True. remat_policy=SAVE_H100_QKV_ATTN_FFN and unroll_layer_stack=True entered the H100 override. muon_ns_shard_group_size=8 was added to the Muon optimizer.
  • The learning rate (7.1e-4) and checkpoint_every_n (150) are unchanged. The GB300 preset (bs_per_device 512, ep 64) did not change.

C. Sequence packing that removes empty candidate slots was introduced. verified — phoenix/xrex/data/recsys/sequence_packing.py:171-203, 579-754, phoenix/xrex/train/trainer_recsys.py:172-195, 291-292, 404-470, 2033-2060:

  • The previous packing reserved a fixed number of token positions per user, equal to the number of candidate slots. The new layout rounds up only the candidates actually filled for each user to a multiple of 16 (CANDIDATE_TOKEN_ALIGN) and gathers them in a "candidate region" at the end of the sequence.
  • The per-user candidate token budget is one of the stages [32, 128] of seqpack_candidate_tokens_per_user. At each step, all processes agree on the required maximum through a distributed KV store (max_over_processes, 2-hour timeout). Then the smallest stage above that value is chosen. As the budget grows, the mean of the history length distribution (mean_len 510) is reduced to keep the total token count the same.
  • If even the largest stage cannot cover the needed tokens, candidates are dropped from the training batch within the user, starting from the later slots. The number dropped is recorded in the train/seqpack_dropped_candidate_slots metric. A warning is logged if the last stage (128) is smaller than the total number of candidate slots.
  • The candidate-region attention kernel ranker_candidate_attention_fa4 was introduced (369 lines). This kernel is a FlashAttention-family CuTe DSL kernel and supports only SM90 (H100) verified — phoenix/xrex/cutedsl/ranker_candidate_attention_fa4.py:31, 295. Each candidate token sees only the history key range of its own user (candidate_key_starts, candidate_key_counts).
  • To account for the reduced padding tokens, the summary values of the attention and FFN auxiliary losses and the active L2 loss are multiplied by the token count ratio, which keeps them on the same scale as the old layout verified — phoenix/xrex/models/transformer.py:761-781.

D. Other changes

  • mentioned_users (a list of mentioned-user metadata) was added to the grox Post data type verified — grox/core/data_loaders/data_types.py:711, 862-866. No classifier reads this field yet verified (grep over all of grox).

Why it matters

  • A path now exists for the ranking model to receive "whether this request is a refresh or a scroll down" verified. The same user is likely to respond with different probabilities right after opening the app and after scrolling deep into the feed, so the next step may be to use this value as a context feature inferred. The only evidence is that the fields were added to the inference request message.
  • B and C are training-efficiency changes that do not alter serving ranking results inferred. The model structure and loss definition are unchanged; only the packing approach changed. However, candidates are dropped from training when the budget is exceeded, so the training data distribution may differ slightly inferred.
  • A GB300-specific override came first in Gen4+6, but this time an H100-specific kernel and default preset tuning were added. We infer that home ranker training continues to run on H100 as well inferred. This is because the default preset name home_direct_packed uses the H100 override.

Gen4+40 (2026-10-13, e1a0375) — Changed three home-mixer cron mirror weights (favorite 0.5 → 0.6, video_open 0.07 → 0.02, cont_dwell_time 0.004 → 0.006) + a third dwell-based head ld (weight 0.75) for two-tower retrieval and installed-apps feature off + introduced the conversation-screen reply ranker reply_two_tower_v2 + a react_with_video term in the value model (weight 0) + video carousel author and SID dedup (off by default) + the ZERO_FAV retrieval dataset

This commit raised the like and dwell time weights in the home-mixer cron mirror and lowered the video open weight from 0.07 to 0.02, but the VM-Ranker mirror keeps its previous values. The combined retrieval preset also gained a dwell-based head, so the home retrieval objective widened from like to like plus dwell verified (daily).

The change spans 179 files, +26,532/−5,971 verified — xai-org/x-algorithm@e1a0375. The cron mirror sync time went from 2026-10-08T16:00:35Z to 2026-10-12T16:00:33Z. More than half of the increase comes from abuse-enforcement-service (about 10,000 lines) and the visibility-filtering refactor (about 9,000 lines changed). This section covers only the parts related to feed behavior. The reference commit for line numbers is e1a0375.

A. Three weights in the home-mixer cron mirror changed. verified — home-mixer/params/param.rs:320, 341-346, 401-406:

Parameter Before After
FavoriteWeight 0.5 0.6
VideoOpenWeight 0.07 0.02
ContDwellTimeWeight 0.004 0.006
  • In the VM-Ranker mirror, the values under the same names (the same feature switch keys) remain 0.5, 0.07, and 0.004 verified — vm-ranker/params.rs:3, 12-17, 54-59. This is the second case of the two mirrors diverging, after PostUnexploredWeight in Gen4+37.
  • The judgment in the Gen4+37 section applies unchanged. For requests that the VM-Ranker RPC answers, the VM-Ranker value may be the final one inferred. home-mixer first computes a local weighted sum and refines it with VM-Ranker (Gen4+28).
  • The direction is "reduce the share of video open probability and increase the share of like and dwell time" verified (the values themselves). It is notable that this runs opposite to Gen4+38, which made the carousel fill by video_open probability. It may be a division of labor in which the main feed reduces the push toward opening videos and sends videos separately to the carousel slot inferred. The only evidence is that the two changes are 6 days apart, and the carousel is still off by default.

B. A third dwell-based head ld was added to two-tower retrieval. verified — phoenix/xrex/configs/xrecsys_two_tower.py:251-300, phoenix/xrex/models/recsys_two_tower_model.py:93-120, 1916-1920, 2385-2412, 2527-2541:

  • The candidate heads of _xrecsys_two_tower_combined_base() went from 2 (home, immersive) to 3 (home, immersive, ld). The positive action of the ld head is the single CLIENT_TWEET_RECAP_DWELLED, and its negatives use the same list as home.
  • The serving score is w_fav × 〈u, home embedding〉 + w_ld × 〈u, ld embedding〉. The combined preset uses w_fav=1.0 and w_ld=0.75.
    • The post embedding table doubles in width, so a home slot and an ld slot sit side by side in one row (num_table_slots=2).
    • A single user vector scores each of the two slots separately and takes the weighted sum (score_over_slots). The dot product, MoL, and int8 paths all work the same way.
  • The positive of the home head has been the single SERVER_TWEET_FAV since Gen4+32. With this change, the home retrieval objective of the combined preset widened from "like" to "like + 0.75 × dwell" verified (config values).
  • ld appears to stand for long dwell inferred. The positive action is named RECAP_DWELLED, and "Recap" was the internal name Twitter used for the ranked home timeline. The dwell decision threshold is not in the public code.
  • In the same base, enable_user_installed_apps changed from True to False verified (line 259). The list of apps a user has installed is no longer used as a user tower feature. The immersive-only base (line 344) is still True.
  • Whether xrecsys_two_tower_combined is the production home retrieval preset cannot be confirmed from the public code inferred. The evidence is that, among the six presets released in Gen4+32, it is the only one that trains home and immersive together.

C. The conversation-screen reply ranker reply_two_tower_v2 was introduced. verified — phoenix/xrex/configs/xrecsys_reply_two_tower_v2.py (79 lines), phoenix/xrex/models/recsys_reply_two_tower_v2_model.py (1,077 lines), phoenix/crates/common/xai-recsys/src/reply.rs (680 lines):

  • This model scores up to 64 reply candidates of one post (the focal post) per user. The serving registration file calls this model "reply-ranker" verified — phoenix/xrex/inference/reply_services.py.
  • Its scale is much smaller than the home ranker.
    • It has 1 Transformer layer, emb_size=256, history 127, a vocab of 20 million each for users and items, 5 million for authors, and 16 SID levels.
    • The loss is the action multi-hot with a negative feedback weight of 10.0 and a dwell time Tweedie loss (weight 0.02).
  • Unlike home Phoenix, it uses many hand-engineered features.
    • Reply-side features include the reply's like, reply, repost, quote, and view counts, and the author's follower count and verification status.
    • Also included are whether the original post's author liked the reply, whether the original post's author replied, whether it is the author's own reply, the reply section, and cumulative report, block, and mute counts.
    • The grox reply score (grox_score, the 1001 offset divided into 26 buckets of 25) is also included.
    • On the focal post side, the like, reply, and view counts, the author's follower count, and whether the viewer is the original post's author are included.
  • The grox score appears to be the reply ranking score that ReplyRankingTaskGenerator, covered in this document's "Grox" section, assigns with Grok inferred. Apart from the name (grox_score) and the 1001 offset encoding, this diff has no link connecting the two pieces of code.
  • No code in home-mixer calls this ranker verified. The 17 home-mixer files changed in this diff contain no reply ranker call. We infer that the conversation screen is handled by a service different from the For You feed inferred.

D. A react_with_video term was added to the value model (weight 0). verified — xai-value-model/scoring.rs:136, home-mixer/params/param.rs:395-400, vm-ranker/params.rs:102-107:

E. Other feed-related changes

By its name, it is a retrieval channel that collects only posts with zero likes inferred. The code that fills the channel is not public.

However, the place it fills is the ad index request (AdIndexRequest), and the Phoenix ranking request is still not filled in this diff verified — sources/ads_source.rs, grep over the whole diff.
